  {
    "id": 5031,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 5031,
        "brand_name": "Erin",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/f5fzDmMWR55T0McX4hrNcY8Dyf177aC9EKraU4mCVlvmxOMWaW.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/p25B3GRVvB7NenJExQzKgdHFSHakvlvVRI2a3cLDGL4jKXT35o.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Jb9KuqCAfFwdx8tlwOVYo9Q6HCZy8zw1yOFRUX5edyMzTpofQY.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Drospirenone, ethinylestradiol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Contraceptive. For women who experience hormone-related fluid retention and resulting symptoms, and with acne and seborrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Take one tab daily at the same time for 21 consecutive days. Start subsequent pack after 7-day tab-free interval. <b>No preceding hormonal contraceptive use:</b> Start on day 1 of menstrual bleeding. May start on days 2-5 but a barrier method is recommended during the first cycle. <b>Changing from combined hormonal contraceptive (COC), vaginal ring, or transdermal patch:</b> Start on the day after last tab of previous COC or on the day of removal of the last ring or patch of cycle pack. <b>Changing from progestogen-only-method or progestogen-releasing intrauterine system:</b> May switch any day with additional use of barrier method for first 7 days of tablet-taking. <b>Following 1<sup>st</sup> trimester abortion:</b> May start immediately. <b>Following delivery or 2<sup>nd</sup> trimester abortion:</b> Start at day 21-28. Use additional barrier method for the first 7 days of tablet-taking when starting later."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Presence or history of venous or arterial thrombotic/thromboembolic event (e.g., DVT, pulmonary embolism, MI) or cerebrovascular accident. Presence or history of prodrome of thrombosis (e.g., TIA, angina pectoris). High risk of venous or arterial thrombosis. History of migraine with focal neurological symptoms. DM with vascular involvement. Severe hepatic disease with persistent abnormal liver function. Severe renal insufficiency or acute renal failure. Presence or history of liver tumors (benign or malignant). Known or suspected sex-steroid influenced malignancies (e.g., of genital organs or breasts). Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Known or suspected pregnancy. Rare hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of arterial and venous thrombotic and thromboembolic diseases (e.g., MI, DVT, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accidents); DM, SLE, hemolytic uremic syndrome, chronic inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis), sickle cell disease; benign or malignant liver tumors; chloasma; spotting or breakthrough bleeding. May increase risk of cervical or breast cancer. Patients with renal impairment or present or history of hypertriglyceridemia; hereditary angioedema. Discontinue if migraine frequency or severity increases; HTN or acute/chronic liver function disturbances occur; cholestatic jaundice recurs. Avoid sun or UV exposure in women prone to chloasma. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Emotional lability, depression/depressive mood, decreased and loss of libido, migraine, nausea, breast pain, unscheduled uterine bleeding, genital tract bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Enzyme inducers (e.g., phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, St. John’s wort), HIV/HCV protease inhibitors, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, ciclosporin, lamotrigine, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, potassium-sparing diuretics, aldosterone antagonists."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 3 mg/30 mcg."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 536,
          "name": "DKT Health, Inc."
        },

  {
    "id": 3132,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3132,
        "brand_name": "Ervex 150",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YGsjksxPGxQd93kYudqmSuOgvxCBu8enQ72SqDOKCMNs67RX4o.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Fnl5uGO4lzdTNoxGF1giibmqMvpqjIw70fBBN5CtVm45v0hGlz.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/K7lqEUfjdkRo1LaeQdqsiu6xcXS0CEAqgvHQ09Yta41AGqIAkj.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Erlotinib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Protein Kinase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after failure of at least one prior chemotherapy regimen."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>NSCLC</b>: 150 mg daily, taken 1 hr before or 2 hrs after meals. <b>Pancreatic cancer</b>: 100 mg, taken 1 hr before or 2 hrs after meals. May be reduced by 50 mg steps, if necessary, max 450 mg when used with rifampicin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pulmonary toxicity, MI or ischemia, CVA, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rash, diarrhea, GI disturbances and bleeding, fatigue, alopecia, stomatitis, pruritus, dry skin, paronychia, conjunctivitis sicca, epistaxis, and abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, rifampicin, ciprofloxacin, ciclosporin, verapamil, antacids, PPIs, H<sub>2</sub>-receptor antagonist."

            "content": "For major depressive episodes, social anxiety disorder (SAD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and panic disorder with or without agoraphobia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Major depressive episodes, GAD and OCD:</b> 10 mg daily, may be increased to max 20 mg. <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia:</b> 5 mg for the 1<sup>st</sup> week before increasing to 10 mg daily, may be further increased up to max 20 mg daily. <b>SAD:</b> 10 mg once daily, may be decreased to 5 mg or increased to max 20 mg daily. Elderly: &frac12; of usually recommended dose and lower max dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with non-selective, irreversible MAOIs, and reversible MAO-A inhibitors. Patients with known QT interval prolongation or congenital long QT syndrome. Use of medicinal products known to prolong QT interval. Childn and adolescents &lt;18 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Paradoxical anxiety, previous diagnosis of epilepsy, history of mania/hypomania, and diabetes. Patients with bleeding, CHD, angle-closure glaucoma or history of glaucoma, bradycardia, recent acute MI or uncompensated heart failure. Discontinue if seizure develops for the 1st time or increased seizure frequency. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to general anesthesia to facilitate tracheal intubation during routine and rapid sequence induction and to provide skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery. Adjunct in ICU to facilitate intubation and mechanical ventilation. <b>Childn:</b> Adjunct to general anesthesia to facilitate tracheal intubation during routine induction and to provide skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tracheal intubation:</b> 0.6 mg/kg (standard), then adequate intubation conditions are established within 60 secs. <b>Tracheal intubation during rapid sequence induction:</b> 1 mg/kg, then adequate intubation conditions are established within 60 secs; if a dose of 0.6 mg/kg is used, it is recommended to intubate the patient 90 secs after administration. <b>Maintenance:</b> 0.15 mg/kg; in case of long-term inhalational anesthesia, reduce dose to 0.075-0.1 mg/kg. <b>Continuous infusion:</b> 0.6 mg/kg loading dose; once neuromuscular block starts to recover, start administration by infusion (infusion rate adjusted to maintain twitch response at 10% of control twitch height or maintain 1-2 responses to train of four stimulation). Infusion rate to maintain neuromuscular block under IV anesthesia: 0.3-0.6 mg/kg/hr; For inhalation anesthesia: 0.3-0.4 mg/kg/hr. This may vary from patient to patient. <b>Childn:</b> Intubation dose during routine anesthesia and maintenance dose same with adult dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Not for facilitating tracheal intubation conditions during rapid sequence induction in childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Ventilatory support is mandatory until adequate spontaneous respiration is restored. History of reactions to other neuromuscular agents (e.g. suxamethonium). Concomitant use of corticosteroid therapy. Patients with hepatic and/or biliary tract disease, renal failure, neuromuscular disease, poliomyelitis, myasthenia gravis or myasthenic (Eaton-Lambert) syndrome, obesity, burns, hypokalemia, hypermagnesemia, hypocalcemia, hypoproteinemia, dehydration, acidosis, hypercapnia, cachexia, severe electrolyte disturbances, altered blood pH. Surgery under hypothermic conditions. Factors which could cause residual curarization after extubation in the post-op phase (e.g. elderly >65 yrs, drug interactions, or patient conditions). Concomitant use with suxamethonium. Conditions associated with prolonged circulation time (e.g. CV disease, old age  & oedematous state). Risk of medication errors. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Injection site pain or reaction, changes in vital signs, prolonged neuromuscular block, tachycardia, hypotension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Halogenated volatile anesthesia, anticholinesterase inhibitors, suxamethonium, long-term use of corticosteroids, aminoglycosides, lincosamide, polypeptide antibiotics, acylamino-penicillins, diuretics, quinidine and quinine, Mg and lithium salts, CCBs, local anesthetics (e.g. lidocaine IV, bupivacaine epidural), phenytoin, beta-blockers, carbamazepine, protease inhibitors (e.g. gabexate, ulinastatin). Nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers."

            "content": "Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), erosive esophagitis, <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> infections and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Prevention of stomach ulcers in patients taking NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>GERD</b>: 20 or 40 mg/day for 4-8 weeks. <b>Childn 1-11 yrs</b>: 10 mg/day. <b><i>H. pylori</i> infections</b>: 40 mg/day in combination with amoxicillin and clarithromycin for 10 days. <b>Prevention of NSAID-induced ulcers</b>: 20-40 mg daily for 6 months. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 40 mg twice daily. Take 1 hr before meals, swallow whole and do not crush or chew. Patients with difficulty swallowing can open the cap and mix pellets with applesauce."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, nausea, gas, decreased appetite, constipation, dry mouth, and abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diazepam, warfarin, clopidogrel, ketoconazole, atazanir, and erythromycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 40 mg (P36.20)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 441,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 441,
        "brand_name": "Crestor",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rosuvastatin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Adjunct to diet when response to diet and exercise is inadequate. Reduce total mortality and risk of major cardiovascular (CV) events (CV death, stroke, MI, unstable angina, or arterial revascularization) in patients with increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular (CV) disease based on present CV disease risk marker (e.g. elevated hsCRP level, age, hypertension, low HDL-C, smoking, or family history of premature coronary heart disease. Reduce elevated LDL-C, total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides, ApoB, nonHDL-C, VLDL-C, VLDL-TG, LDL-C/HDL-C, TC/HDL-C, nonHDL C/HDL-C, ApoB/ApoA-I ratios and increases ApoA-I and HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and non familial) and mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson Types IIA and IIb); reduce TC and LDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, as an adjunct to diet and other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g. LDL apheresis), or alone if such treatments are unavailable. Treatment of primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson Type III hyperlipoproteinemia); isolated hypertriglyceridemia (Fredrickson Type IV hyperlipidemia). Slow or delay the atherosclerosis progression. <b>Childn and adolescents 6-17 yrs:</b> Reduce TC, LDL-C and ApoB in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses given once daily at any time of day, with or without food. Usual dose range is 10-40 mg, individualized based on the goal of therapy and patient response. If necessary, dose can be adjusted at 2-4 week intervals. <b>Primary hypercholesterolemia (e.g. HeFH), mixed dyslipidemia, dysbetalipoproteinemia, isolated hypertriglyceridemia, treatment of atherosclerosis, and prevention of CV events:</b> Initially 10 mg; 5 mg once daily for special populations; 20 mg for severe hypercholesterolemia (e.g. HeFH), or those with aggressive lipid targets. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia:</b> Initially 20 mg. <b>HeFH - Childn 10-17 yrs:</b> 5-20 mg; <b>6-9 yrs:</b> 5-10 mg. <b>Severe renal or hepatic impairment:</b> Max 10 mg. <b>Asian patients:</b> Initially 5 mg once daily. <b>Genotypes c.521CC or c.421AA:</b> Max 20 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic impairment, excessive alcohol consumption, history of liver disease, pre-disposing factors for myopathy (e.g. renal impairment, advanced age, hypothyroidism), or increased plasma levels. May induce effects on skeletal muscle (e.g. myalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis); immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy clinically characterized by persistent proximal muscle weakness and elevated serum creatinine kinase during treatment or upon discontinuation; increased risk of myositis and myopathy when used with ciclosporin, fibric acid derivatives (e.g. gemfibrozil), nicotinic acid, azole antifungals, and macrolide antibiotics; increases in HbA1c and serum glucose levels and may exceed threshold for diagnosis of DM, primarily in patients at high risk for developing DM. Concomitant use with OATP1B1 and BCRP inhibitors (e.g. ciclosporin and certain protease inhibitors including combinations of ritonavir with atazanavir, lopinavir, and/or tipranavir). Temporarily withhold in patients with conditions suggesting myopathy or risk of renal failure from rhabdomyolysis (e.g. sepsis, hypotension, major surgery, trauma, severe metabolic endocrine, electrolyte disorders, or uncontrolled seizures). Discontinue treatment if CK levels are marked elevated (>10 x ULN) or if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected; induce or aggravate myasthenia gravis or ocular myasthenia. Asian population. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, myalgia, asthenia, constipation, dizziness, nausea, abdominal pain, DM."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir, ciclosporin, darolutamide, regorafenib, atazanavir/ritonavir, simeprevir, velpastavir, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir/dasabuvir, grazoprevir/elbasvir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, lopinavir/ritonavir, clopidogrel, gemfibrozil, eltrombopag, darunavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir, dronedarone, itraconazole, ezetimibe, erythromycin, baicalin, antacids containing aluminum and magnesium, fusidic acid, warfarin, fenofibrates/fibric acid derivatives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg (P32.50), 10 mg (P71.00), 20 mg (P85.75), 40 mg (P111.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 20,
          "name": "AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals (Phils.), Inc."
        },

          },

            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 300 mg daily on an empty stomach. <b>Childn</b>: 5 mg/kg daily. Max 300 mg daily. Intermittent therapy: 10 mg/kg 3x a week or 15 mg/kg 2x a week.           "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YTrlAOPEmnoi9dDCLepHeaIQYvIrvW9JX7oIsnQUdQbv7jAmaf.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cyproterone acetate, ethinylestradiol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of severe acne that has not improved after long-term use of oral antibiotics; excessive hair growth on the face and body (moderately severe hirsutism). Oral contraceptive in women requiring treatment for the androgen-dependent skin conditions above."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab daily starting on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual cycle for 21 days, followed by 7 tab-free days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with or history of conditions relating to thrombosis (e.g. DVT, pulmonary thrombosis, heart attack), stroke, conditions that may be 1<sup>st</sup> sign of heart attack (e.g. angina pectoris) or stroke (e.g. TIA or small reversible stroke), migraine (accompanied by visual symptoms, speech disability, or weakness/numbness in any body part), cancer that may grow under the influence of sex hormones (e.g. of the breast or genital organs), liver tumor. DM with blood vessel damage. Pancreatitis. Jaundice or severe liver disease. Unexplained vaginal bleeding. Men. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid stopping treatment prematurely. Smoking. Patients with DM, high BP, valve or heart rhythm disorder, superficial phlebitis, varicose veins; family history of thrombosis, heart attack or stroke, breast cancer; migraine, epilepsy; history of high level of cholesterol and triglycerides; liver and gallbladder disease, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, PCOS, SLE, HUS, sickle cell disease, angioedema, and hirsutism. Overweight. Development or worsening of hearing loss, porphyria, herpes gestationis, Sydenham's chorea during pregnancy or previous use of sex hormones preparations. Patients with chloasma should avoid exposure to sunlight or UV rays. Surgery or long period of immobilization. Contains lactose.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, abdominal pain, weight gain, headache, depressive and altered mood, breast tenderness and pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Primidone, phenytoin, barbiturates, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, rifampicin, rifabutin, nelfinavir, nevirapine, efavirenz, ampicillin, tetracyclines, griseofulvin, St. John's wort, cyclosporine, lamotrigine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2 mg/35 mcg x 21s (P525.75)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Indicated in adults and adolescents &ge;16 yrs for symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis, and pain and signs of inflammation associated with acute gouty arthritis; Short-term treatment of moderate pain associated with dental surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>OA:</b> 30 mg once daily, may be increased to max 60 mg/day. <b>RA, ankylosing spondylitis:</b> 60 mg once daily, may be increased to max 90 mg/day. Down-titrate to 60 mg once daily when patient is clinically stabilized. <b>Acute gouty arthritis:</b> 120 mg once daily for 8 days. <b>Post-op dental surgery pain:</b> 90 mg once daily. Max duration: 3 days. <b>Hepatic impairment</b> - Mild (Child-Pugh score 5-6): Max 60 mg once daily; Moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9): Max 30 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding. Patients taking aspirin, NSAIDs, COX-2 inhibitors and experiencing bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, angioneurotic edema, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score &ge;10), renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), IBD, CHF (NYHA II-IV), HTN (BP >140/90 mmHg), established IHD, PAD, and/or cerebrovascular disease. Childn and adolescents < 16 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of GI complication with NSAIDs, history of GI disease. Risk factors for CV events. Hepatic and renal impairment. Fluid retention, history of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, edema, HTN. Women attempting to conceive. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, alveolar infection, edema, fluid retention, dizziness, headache, palpitations, HTN, bronchospasm, constipation, flatulence, heartburn, diarrhea, dyspepsia, epigastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, esophagitis, oral ulcer, increased ALT or AST, ecchymosis, asthenia, fatigue, flu-like disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, diurectics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aspirin, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, lithium, oral contraceptives, rifampicin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 60 mg, 90 mg, 120 mg."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4082,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4082,
        "brand_name": "Cyramza",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/aJlz0c2V2Uzsqp1qXF6MpIMfHhRzvwR2bjzLzILGFhaGfSuA3b.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/s7LURNS4jBHJK4Z6vJpZ5vZPx8J8FG9gbKXrucwQ0SnRxgw7UN.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nzMc1KA2GFwSEeFZGRA0hz4vZ5sBqF8sKMCStYNZiNEhVE4Zzj.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ramucirumab",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Monoclonal Antibodies, Antineoplastic"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with paclitaxel or as monotherapy when combination with paclitaxel is inappropriate, for treatment of adults with advanced gastric cancer or gastro-esophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma with disease progression after prior platinum and fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy. In combination with FOLFIRI (irinotecan, folic acid, and 5-FU) for treatment of adults with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) with disease progression on or after prior therapy with bevacizumab, oxaliplatin, and fluoropyrimidine. In combination with erlotinib for first-line treatment of adults with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with activating epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations. In combination with docetaxel, for treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with disease progression after platinum-based therapy. Monotherapy for treatment of adults with advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who have serum-alpha fetoprotein of &ge;400 ng/mL and previously treated with sorafenib."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion over approx 60 mins. <b>Gastric CA and GEJ adenocarcinoma - Monotherapy:</b> 8 mg/kg every 2 weeks; <b>Combination with paclitaxel:</b> 8 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of 28-day cycle, prior to paclitaxel 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over approx 60 mins on days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycle. <b>CRC:</b> 8 mg/kg every 2 weeks prior to FOLFIRI. <b>NSCLC – Combination with erlotinib:</b> 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Determine EGFR mutation status prior to initiation of treatment. <b>With docetaxel after platinum-based therapy:</b> 10 mg/kg on day 1 of 21-day cycle prior to docetaxel 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion on day 1 of 21-day cycle; <b>For East Asians:</b> Initially docetaxel 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 1 of 21-day cycle. <b>HCC:</b> 8 mg/kg every 2 weeks. <b>Premedication:</b> Give H1 antagonist (e.g. diphenhydramine) prior to infusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Tumor cavitation or tumor involvement of major vessels in patients with NSCLC."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic and severe renal impairment. Arterial thrombolic events, gastrointestinal perforations, severe bleeding, pulmonary hemorrhage in NSCLC, HTN, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, aneurysms and artery dissections, impaired wound healing, symptoms of cardiac failure, fistula, proteinuria, stomatitis, elderly patients with NSCLC, sodium-restricted diet.   Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Use effective contraception and avoid lactation during and up to 3 months after last dose. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, peripheral edema, HTN, abdominal pain, headache, proteinuria, fatigue/asthenia, neutropenia, epistaxis, stomatitis, infections, alopecia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate for solution for infusion 10 mg/mL x 10 mL, 50 mL."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 221,

            "content": "<b>Prevention of deficiency - Adults</b>: 25,000 IU per month (1 amp), higher doses may be required in certain situations; <b>Childn 1-18 yrs</b>: 25,000 IU (1 amp) every 6 weeks; <b>0-1 yr</b>: 25,000 IU (1 amp) every 8 weeks. <b>Treatment of deficiency – Adults</b>: 50,000 IU per week (2 amps) for 6-8 weeks followed by maintenance therapy of 1,400-2,000 IU per day; <b>Childn 0-18 yrs</b>: 25,000 IU (1 amp) once every 2 weeks for 6 weeks followed by maintenance therapy of 400-1,000 IU per day. <b>Adjunct to specific therapy for osteoporosis - Adults</b>: 25,000 IU per month (1 amp). Taken with meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hypercalcemia and/or hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis and/or nephrocalcinosis, serious renal impairment, hypervitaminosis D, pseudohypoparathyroidism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment, receiving treatment for cardiovascular disease, sarcoidosis, receiving treatments containing vit D, food and milk enriched with vit D, sun exposure. Risk of renal stones with concomitant calcium supplementation. Increased risk of fractures in elderly. Pregnancy (max 2,000 IU per day) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticonvulsants (e.g. phenytoin), barbiturates, hepatic enzymes inducers; thiazide diuretics; glucocorticoids; drugs containing digitalis and other cardiac glycosides; ion exchange resin (e.g. cholestyramine, colestipol, orlistat) or laxative (e.g. paraffin oil); actinomycin, imidazole antifungal agents."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral solution 25,000 IU/mL."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/CPIrEItBGs5SBXg8OTRjFzrtjDyk94Z9lnq7JomMvM4WCI0nym.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levothyroxine sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-Hypothyroidism Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of benign euthyroid goiter in patients with normal thyroid function. Prophylaxis of relapse after surgery for euthyroid goiter, depending on the post-op hormone status. Substitution therapy in hypothyroidism. Suppression therapy in thyroid cancer. <b>25 mcg, 50 mcg, and 100 mcg:</b> Concomitant therapy with medication against hyperthyroidism. <b>150 mcg, 100 mcg or 200 mcg:</b> Thyroid suppression testing."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment of benign euthyroid goiter and prophylaxis of relapse after surgery of euthyroid goiter:</b> 75-200 mcg/day. <b>Hypothyroidism - Adults:</b> Initially 25-50 mcg/day. Maintenance: 100-200 mcg/day; <b>Childn:</b> Initially 12.5-50 mcg/day. Maintenance: 100-150 mcg/m<sup>2</sup>/day. <b>Suppression therapy in thyroid cancer:</b> 150-300 mcg/day. <b>Concomitant therapy with medication against hyperthyroidism:</b> 50-100 mcg/day. <b>Neonates and infants with congenital hypothyroidism:</b> 10-15 mcg/kg per day for the first 3 months. Taken at least 30 mins before first meal. Tab may be crushed and mixed with some water. <b>Thyroid suppression test - 100 mcg tab or 200 mcg:</b> 200 mcg/day, given 2 and 1 weeks prior to test; <b>150 mcg tab:</b> 75 mcg/day,  given 4 and 3 weeks prior to test; 150 mcg/day, given 2 and 1 weeks prior to test. Take a single daily dose in the morning half an hour before breakfast."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Untreated adrenal insufficiency, untreated pituitary insufficiency, untreated thyrotoxicosis, acute MI and acute myocarditis or acute pancarditis. Combination therapy of levothyroxine and an anti-thyroid agent for hyperthyroidism is not indicated during pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients at risk of psychotic disorders. Exclude or treat thyroid autonomy, CV insufficiency, angina pectoris, arteriosclerosis,  HTN, pituitary insufficiency, or adrenal insufficiency before thyroid hormone therapy or suppression testing. Postmenopausal women with hypothyroidism and an increased risk of osteoporosis. Coadministration with orlistat. Not to be used for weight reduction or with certain substances and sympathomimetic amines for weight reduction. Avoid drug-induced hyperthyroidism in patients with coronary insufficiency, heart failure, and  tachycardiac arrhythmias. Galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Biotin may interfere with interpreting results of thyroid function test that are based on biotin/steptavidin interaction. Monitor hemodynamic parameters upon treatment initiation in very low birth weight preterm neonates. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Irregular or rapid heart rate, chest pains, headache, muscle weakness or cramps, face flushing, fever, vomiting, disorders of menstruation, increased pressure in the head with eye swelling, trembling, restlessness, sleep disturbances, sweating, weight loss and diarrhea. Allergic reactions, particularly of the skin. Angioedema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antidiabetic drugs, coumarin derivatives, protease inhibitors, phenytoin, salicylates, dicoumarol, furosemide, clofibrate. orlistat, sevelamer, tyrosine-kinase inhibitors, ion exchange resins. Aluminum and iron-containing drugs, calcium salts. PTU, glucocorticoids, beta-sympatholytics, iodine-containing contrast media, amiodarone, sertraline, chloroquine/proguanil, PPIs. Hepatic enzyme inducers (e.g. barbiturates, carbamazepine). Estrogen. Soy products. Biotin-containing products on laboratory test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mcg, 50 mcg, 100 mcg, 150 mcg."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Uterine Relaxants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "To delay imminent preterm birth in pregnant adult women with: regular uterine contractions of at least 30 secs duration at a rate of &ge;4 per 30 mins; a cervical dilation of 1-3 cm (0-3 for nulliparas) and effacement of &ge;50%; a gestational age from 24 until 33 completed weeks; and a normal fetal heart."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 6.75 mg/0.9 mL IV bolus injection over 1 min, immediately followed by continuous infusion of 300 mcg/min for 3 hrs, then 100 mcg/mins for up to 45 hrs. Max duration of 48 hrs, and max dose of 330.75 mg. Re-treatment: 6.75 mg/0.9 mL IV bolus injection, followed by 37.5 mg/5 mL concentrate for solution for infusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Gestational age &lt;24 or &gt;33 completed weeks. Premature rupture of the membranes &gt;30 weeks of gestation. Abnormal fetal heart rate. Antepartum uterine hemorrhage requiring immediate delivery. Eclampsia and severe preeclampsia requiring delivery. Intrauterine fetal death. Suspected intrauterine infection. Placenta previa. Abruption placenta. Any other conditions of the mother or fetus in which continuation of pregnancy is hazardous."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired hepatic function. Monitor uterine contraction and fetal heart rate during use, and blood loss after delivery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea and vomiting, headache, dizziness, flushes, tachycardia, hypotension, hyperglycemia and injection site reaction."
          },

        "content": "Dienogest",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Start on any day of the menstrual cycle. 1 tab daily without break, preferably at the same time each day; must be taken continuously regardless of any vaginal bleeding. When pack is finished, start the next pack without interruption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active venous thromboembolic disorder. Present or history of arterial and CV disease (e.g. MI, CVA, IHD), DM with vascular involvement. Severe hepatic disease as long as liver function values have not returned to normal; liver tumors (benign or malignant). Known or suspected sex hormone-dependent malignancies. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Serious uterine bleeding. May experience changes in bleeding pattern, Risk for osteoporosis and changes in bone mineral density. History of chloasma, depression. Hereditary problems of galactose intolerance. Discontinue if there is a presence or suspected arterial or venous thrombotic event. Monitor any irregularity or anomaly of the breast.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Weight increase, depressed mood sleep, disorder nervousness, less of libido altered mood, headache, migraine, nausea, abdominal pain, flatulence, abdominal distension, vomiting, acne, alopecia, back pain, breast discomfort, ovarian cyst, hot flushes, uterine/vaginal bleeding (e.g. spotting), irritability, asthenic conditions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, St. Johnn’s worth) and HIV/HCV protease inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2 mg x 28 (P1,533.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Other Bone Metabolism-Affecting Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture; to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "210 mg, given as 2 SC inj in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, once every month for 12 doses. After completion of therapy, transition to an antiresorptive osteoporosis therapy is required to preserve bone mass."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Uncorrected hypocalcemia. MI or stroke within the preceding year."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) or receiving dialysis; high CV risk; risk factors for osteonecrosis of the jaw. Atypical femoral fracture. Correct hypocalcemia prior initiation of therapy. Adequately supplement patients with calcium and vit D. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Viral URTI, arthralgia. Hypersensitivity, rash, dermatitis, urticaria, angioedema, erythema multiforme. Headache, cough, neck pain, muscle spasms, peripheral edema, inj site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) 105 mg/1.17 mL pre-filled syringe."

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fosfomycin"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute bacterial cystitis, acute episodes of recurrent bacterial cystitis, acute bacterial urethro-vesical syndrome, and aspecific bacterial urethritis. Relevant asymptomatic bacteriuria (pregnancy). Post-op urinary tract infections (UTI). Prophylaxis of UTI during surgery and trans-urethral diagnostic maneuvers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Acute uncomplicated UTI (cystitis, non-gonococcal urethritis)</b>: 1 sachet once a day. <b>Prophylaxis of UTI after surgery or transurethral diagnostic maneuvers</b>: 1 sachet 3 hrs before surgery, then 1 sachet after 24 hrs of 1<sup>st</sup> dose. <b>Elderly, bedridden patients, recurrent infections, infections requiring high doses of antibiotics</b>: 2 doses administered at a 24-hr interval. Dissolve contents in half glass of water (&ge;50 mL) and drink before bedtime, after emptying bladder. Take on empty stomach, 1 hr before or 2 hr after food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;10 mL/min). Patients who have undergone hemodialysis. Childn &lt;12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Persistent symptoms may result from inflammation and do not necessarily indicate therapeutic failure. Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Vomiting, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Metoclopramide, drugs that induce GI motility (e.g. betanechol, cisapride, domperidone, laxatives)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Granules for oral solution 3 g (P472.50)."
          }

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab/Granules:</b> Treatment of respiratory disorders associated with productive cough and thick viscous hypersecretion (e.g. acute bronchitis, chronic bronchitis and its exacerbation, pulmonary emphysema, cystic fibrosis, bronchiectasis). <b>Powder for oral soln:</b> Secretolytic therapy in acute and chronic bronchopulmonary diseases accompanied by impaired formation and transport of mucus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab -</b> Adults: 1 tab (dissolved in 250 mL water) once daily, preferably in the evening. <b>Granules -</b> Adults and childn >14 yrs: 1 sachet (dissolved in 100 mL water) once daily. Treatment duration - Acute disorders: 5-10 days. Chronic disorders: Several months. <b>Powder for oral soln -</b> Adults and adolescents >14 yrs: 1 sachet 2-3 times daily; Adolescents and childn 6-14 yrs: 1 sachet twice daily. All doses to be taken dissolved in a glass of water, after meals. Treatment duration: Max 5 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Powder for oral soln:</b> Patients with active ulceration. Childn < 2 yrs."

        "content": "Dexketoprofen trometamol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of moderate to severe acute pain, when oral administration is not appropriate (e.g. post-op pain, renal colic, and lower back pain)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "May be administered by slow IM injection, IV infusion (10-30 mins), and IV bolus (not &lt;15 secs). 50 mg every 8-12 hrs, intervals may be reduced to every 6 hrs if necessary. Max 150 mg/day. <b>Hepatic (Child-Pugh score 5-9) and renal (CrCl 50-80 mL/min) impairment:</b> 50 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active or suspected peptic ulcer or hemorrhage, history of recurrent peptic ulcer or hemorrhage or chronic dyspepsia, GI bleeding or other bleeding disorders, history of NSAID-induced GI bleeding or perforation, Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis, severe heart failure, moderate to severe renal dysfunction (CrCl &lt;50 mL/min), severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 10-15), hemorrhagic diathesis and other coagulation disorders. Patients in whom aspirin and NSAIDs precipitate asthma attacks, bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, cause nasal polyps, urticaria or angioneurotic edema. Not for neuraxial (intrathecal or epidural) administration. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of allergic conditions, GI disease, esophagitis, gastritis or peptic ulcer, HTN and/or mild CHF. Concomitant use with other NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitors, oral corticosteroids, warfarin, aspirin, heparin, and other coumarins. Discontinue when GI bleeding or ulceration occurs. Consider combination with protective agents (e.g. misoprostol or PPIs). Patients with uncontrolled HTN, CHF, IHD, PAD, and CVD, renal and hepatic impairment, hematopoietic disorders, SLE or mixed connective tissue disease; receiving diuretics; who could develop hypovolemia. Childn and adolescents. Elderly. Women attempting to conceive. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> trimester).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, injection site pain, inflammation, bruising or hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other NSAIDs, warfarin, heparin, corticosteroids, lithium, methotrexate, hydantoins and sulfonamides. Diuretics, ACE inhibitors, aminoglycosides, ARBs, pentoxifylline, zidovudine, sulfonylureas. Beta-blockers, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, thrombolytics, anti-platelet agents, SSRIs, probenecid, cardiac glycosides, mifepristone, quinolones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV/IM) 50 mg/2 mL."

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults (&ge;18 years) with type 2 DM as an adjunct to diet and exercise. Monotherapy for patients unable to take metformin due to intolerance and who require additional glycemic control. Add-on therapy in combination with other glucose-lowering agents, including insulin when existing therapy plus diet and exercise are inadequate. For initial combination for use with metformin in patients whose glycemic control is inadequate with diet and exercise alone and who are unlikely to respond sufficiently to metformin monotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy and add-on combination therapy:</b> 10 mg once daily. Combination with insulin or an insulin secretagogue, such as a sulfonylurea. <b>Initial combination therapy:</b> 10 mg dapagliflozin + 500 mg metformin once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment (GFR < 25 mL/min), hepatic impairment, at risk of volume depletion or hypotension, diabetic ketoacidosis, type 1 DM. Fournier’s gangrene, UTI, CKD, lower limb amputations. Patients with hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Vulvovaginitis, balanitis, UTI. Hypoglycemia, dizziness, rash, back pain, dysuria, polyuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Thiazide and loop diuretics. Insulin and insulin secretagogues (e.g. sulfonylurea). 1,5-anhydroglucitol assay."

  {
    "id": 4575,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4575,
        "brand_name": "Exprogest",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Progesterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Progesterone replacement during the course of complete deficits in women with non-functioning ovaries (ovum transplant). Luteal phase supplementation during in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles; spontaneous or induced cycles in case of hypofertility or primary or secondary sterility due to dysovulation. Threat of abortion or prevention of repetitive abortions due to luteal insufficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Progesterone replacement for women with non-functioning ovaries (ovum transplant)</b>: As adjunct to estrogen therapy, start with 100 mg/day on days 13 and 14 of transfer cycle, then 200 mg/day (100 mg in the morning, 100 mg at night) from days 15 to 25. From day 26 and in case of pregnancy, increase dose by 100 mg/day weekly to reach max 600 mg/day divided into 3 doses, maintained until day 60. <b>Luteal phase supplementation - IVF cycles</b>: 400-600 mg/day, from HCG injection until 12<sup>th</sup> week of pregnancy; <b>Spontaneous or induced cycles (in cases of hypofertility or primary/secondary sterility due to dysovulation)</b>: 200-300 mg/day for 10 days from day 17 of cycle. In case of absence of periods or pregnancy, resume treatment as soon as possible. <b>Threat of abortion or prevention of repetitive abortions due to luteal insufficiency</b>: 200-400 mg/day divided into 2 doses. Caps are to be inserted deep into the vagina."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Allergy to peanut or soya. Patients with undiagnosed genital bleeding, severe liver dysfunction, liver tumors, suspected or confirmed breast or genital organ neoplasia, active or history of thromboembolic diseases, cerebral hemorrhage, porphyria. Contraindications related to estrogens when used for HRT in conjunction with estrogen. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not a contraceptive. Patients with history of venous thrombosis. Carefully examine uterine bleeding before initiation of dose. May aggravate metabolic and thromboembolic risks; discontinue if ocular disorders (e.g. reduced vision, diplopia, retinal vascular lesions), VTE or thrombotic events, or severe headaches occur. Should be used for threatened or recurrent abortion only if corpus luteum secretion is insufficient. Assess medical and family history before initiating or restarting treatment; adapt physical exams and regular check-ups to patient’s needs. Regular period-like bleeding may occur upon withdrawal in women with an intact uterus; if withdrawal bleeding is absent, endometrial hyperplasia should be ruled out. Breakthrough bleeding and spotting may occur during the 1<sup>st</sup> few months of treatment. Regular endometrial monitoring is recommended in long-term treatment (&gt;5 yrs). May cause reduction in glucose tolerance. Contains soya bean lecithin. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Irregular menstruation, amenorrhea, metrorrhagia, headaches."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP450-3A4 inducers e.g. barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenylbutazone, spironolactone, griseofulvin, ampicillin, tetracyclines, St. John’s wort. CYP450-3A4 inhibitors e.g. ketoconazole. Insulin and other antidiabetic agents. Liver and/or endocrine function tests."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Vaginal softgel capsule 200 mg (P50.00)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of multiple myeloma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults &ge;18 yrs: 16 mg/kg IV infusion. <b>Infusion rate</b>: 50 mL/hr increased by 50 mL/hr every hr (in absence of infusion-related reactions) up to max rate 200 mL/hr. <b>Monotherapy for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma or in combination with lenalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone (4-week cycle) for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) or for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma</b> -  Weeks 1-8: Weekly, total 8 doses; Weeks 9-24: Every 2 weeks, total 8 doses; Week 25 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. <b>In combination with bortezomib, melphalan and prednisone (6-week cycle) for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for ASCT</b> -  Weeks 1-6: Weekly, total 6 doses; Weeks 7-54: Every 3 weeks, total 16 doses; Week 55 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. Administer bortezomib 2x weekly at weeks 1, 2, 4, 5 for 1st 6-week cycle, then once weekly at weeks 1, 2, 4, 5 for 8 more 6-week cycles. <b>In combination with bortezomib, thalidomide, and dexamethasone (4-week cycle) - Induction:</b> Weeks 1-8: Weekly, total of 8 doses; Weeks 9-16: Every 2 weeks, total of 4 doses. Then stop for high dose chemotherapy and ASCT. <b>Consolidation:</b> Weeks 1-8 (reinitiation): Every 2 weeks, total of 4 doses. <b>In combination with bortezomib (3-week cycle) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma</b> - Weeks 1-9: Weekly, total 9 doses; Weeks 10-24: Every 2 weeks, total 5 doses; Week 25 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. See full prescribing information for premedication and post-infusion regimen and management of infusion-related reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Infusion-related reactions. Neutropenia/thrombocytopenia may be induced. Interference with indirect antiglobulin test (indirect Coombs test) and serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation tests. HBV reactivation. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and for 3 months after treatment. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infusion reactions, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, peripheral edema, fatigue, back pain, asthenia, pyrexia, urinary tract infection, bronchitis, nasopharyngitis, pneumonia. Decreased appetite, muscle spasms, peripheral sensory neuropathy, dyspnea, cough. Anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphopenia. Arthralgia, pain in extremity, musculoskeletal chest pain."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate for solution for IV infusion 20 mg/mL x 5 mL (P22,384.82), 20 mL (P110,000.00)."

            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - CML-CP: 100 mg; Accelerated, myeloid, or lymphoid blast (advanced) phase CML or PH+ ALL: 140 mg. <b>Adolescents and childn</b> - Ph+ CML-CP, Ph+ ALL - &ge;45 kg: 100 mg; 30-< 45 kg: 70 mg; 20-< 30 kg: 60 mg; 10-< 20 kg: 40 mg. Recalculate dose every 3 months based on changes in BW, or more often if necessary. Max 2 yrs, and additional 1 yr post-transplantation in patients that receive subsequent stem cell transplantation. All doses taken once daily at approx same time each day. Adjust dose based on patient response and tolerability (except in childn with Ph+ ALL). Taken with or without meal. Swallow whole; do not crush or chew. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and dose escalation for childn with Ph+ CML-CP."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic impairment; required to take antiplatelets or anticoagulants; at risk for QT prolongation; risk factors or history of CV disease; galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose-malabsorption. May induce myelosuppression; bleeding; fluid retention (e.g. pleural effusion); pulmonary arterial HTN; QT prolongation; cardiac adverse reactions; thrombotic microangiopathy; hepatitis B reactivation; epiphyses delayed fusion, osteopenia, growth retardation, gynecomastia. Perform CBC weekly for the 1<sup>st</sup> 2 months, then monthly thereafter in adults with advanced phase CML or Ph+ ALL; every 2 weeks for 12 weeks, then every 3 months thereafter in patients with CML-CP; prior to start of each block of chemotherapy and every 2 days until recovery during consolidation blocks of chemotherapy in childn with Ph+ ALL; HBV infections tests prior treatment. Evaluate signs and symptoms of CV disease prior to therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 10 kg BW or < 1 yr. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. Use contraception. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infection; pneumonia, URTI/inflammation, herpes virus infection (including CMV), enterocolitis infection, sepsis; myelosuppression (including anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia); febrile neutropenia; appetite disturbances, hyperuricemia; depression, insomnia; headache; peripheral neuropathy, dizziness, dysgeusia, somnolence;  visual disorder, disturbances, blurring, reduced acuity, dry eye; tinnitus; CHF/cardiac dysfunction, pericardial effusion, arrhythmia, palpitations; hemorrhage; HTN, flushing;  pleural effusion, dyspnea; pulmonary edema or HTN, lung infiltration, pneumonitis, cough; diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain;  GI bleeding, colitis, gastritis, mucosal inflammation, dyspepsia, abdominal distension, constipation, oral soft tissue disorder; skin rash; alopecia, dermatitis, pruritus, acne, dry skin, urticaria, hyperhidrosis; musculoskeletal pain;  arthralgia, myalgia, muscle weakness, musculoskeletal stiffness, muscle spasm; peripheral or facial edema, fatigue, pyrexia; asthenia, pain, chest pain, generalized edema, chills; weight gain or loss; contusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

H<sub>2</sub> antagonists (e.g. famotidine), PPIs (e.g. omeprazole), antacids (e.g. aluminum hydroxide/magnesium hydroxide), CYP2C8 substrates (e.g. glitazones)."

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-protozoals"

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab/IV infusion</b>: Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op infection due to anaerobic bacteria, particularly Bacteroides spp. and anaerobic streptococci. Treatment of septicemia, bacteremia, peritonitis, brain abscess, necrotizing pneumonia, osteomyelitis, puerperal sepsis, pelvic abscess, pelvic cellulitis, and post-op wound infection from which pathogenic anaerobes have been isolated. Treatment of <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> infection associated with peptic ulcer as part of triple therapy. <b>IV infusion</b>: Treatment of intestinal and extraintestinal or invasive amebiasis including amoebic liver abscess. <b>Tab</b>: Urogenital trichomoniasis (symptomatic and asymptomatic), amebiasis, giardiasis, balantidiasis, <i>Blastocystis hominis</i> infection. Vaginal infections (including bacterial vaginosis), acute ulcerative gingivitis, acute dental infections (e.g. acute pericoronitis and acute apical infections). Anaerobically-infected leg ulcers and pressure sores."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IV infusion</b>: Administer by slow IV infusion (30-60 mins) at a rate of 5 mL/min. <b>Adults – Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infections</b>: Initial loading dose 15 mg/kg completed 1 hr before surgery, followed by 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs after initial dose; or 500 mg pre-op and at 8 and 16 hrs after initial dose. <b>Treatment of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic microorganisms</b>: Initial loading dose 15 mg/kg, followed by maintenance 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs for 7-10 days. Max 4 g every 24 hrs. <b>Treatment of intestinal and hepatic amebiasis</b>: 400-800 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days. <b>Childn - Treatment of infections caused by anaerobes, trichomoniasis, Gardnerella vaginitis, amebiasis, giardiasis, pseudomembranous colitis, prophylaxis in colon surgery and part of combination therapy for <i>H. pylori</i></b> – Infants and childn: 15-30 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. &gt;7 days with &gt;2 kg BW: 30 mg/kg every 12 hrs; &gt;7 days with 1.2-2 kg BW: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs;&lt;< 7 days with &gt;2 kg BW: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs; &lt;7 days with 1.2-2 kg BW: 7.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs;  0-4 weeks with &lt;1.2 kg BW: 7.5 mg/kg every 48 hrs. <b>Tab – Treatment of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic microorganisms – Adults</b>: 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs. or 500 mg every 8 hrs. Max 4 g/24 hrs. <b>Childn &lt;12 yrs</b>: 7.5 mg/kg every 8 hrs or 20-30 mg/kg as single dose. May be increased to 40 mg/kg daily depending on severity of infection. Duration of treatment: 7-10 days or longer for serious bacterial infections. <b>Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infections – Adults</b>: 500 mg. <b>Childn &lt;12 yrs</b>: 20-30 mg/kg as single dose given 1-2 hrs pre-op. Initiate 48 hrs before surgery, repeated every 8 hrs. <b>Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i></b>: 20 mg/kg for 7-14 days as part of a combination therapy. Max 500 mg twice daily. <b>Urogenital trichomoniasis – Adults and adolescents</b>: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2,000 mg as single dose. <b>Childn</b> 15-30 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. <b>Bacterial vaginosis – Adults and adolescents</b>: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2,000 mg as single dose. <b>Amebiasis – Adults and adolescents</b> -  Acute intestinal amebiasis: 750 mg 3x daily; Amebic liver abscess: 500 mg or 750 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days; <b>Childn</b>: 15-30 mg/kg/day every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. <b>Giardiasis – Adults and adolescents</b>: 2,000 mg once daily for 3 days, or 500 mg twice daily for 7-10 days; <b>Childn</b>: 15-30 mg/kg/day every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. <b>Acute ulcerative gingivitis – Adults and adolescents</b>: 200-250 mg 3x daily for 3 days. <b>Balantidiasis and <i>B. hominis</i> infection – Adults and adolescents</b>: 750 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active neurological disorders, history of blood dyscrasia, hypothyroidism, hypoadrenalism. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) in patients with trichomoniasis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor regularly if administered for &gt;10 days. Patients with active or chronic severe peripheral and CNS disease. Candidiasis. Sodium retention; patients receiving corticosteroids or predisposed to edema. Hepatic and renal impairment, history of blood dyscrasias. May develop pancreatitis. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."

                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },

                  "title": "X",

                }

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "CV, dermatologic or hypersensitivity, endocrine or metabolic, GI, genitourinary or reproductive, hematologic, hepatic, musculoskeletal, nervous system, respiratory effects. Fever, thrombophlebitis, sharp, unpleasant, metallic taste, glossitis, tongue discoloration/furry tongue, transient vision disorders, tinnitus."

        "content": "Decitabine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), including previously treated and untreated, de novo and secondary MDS of all French-American-British subtypes (refractory anemia, refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts, refractory anemia with excess blasts, refractory anemia with excess blasts in transformation, and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia), and intermediate-1 and -2, and high-risk International Prognostic Scoring System groups."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Single IV infusion use only. May be premedicated with antiemetics. <b>Treatment regimen - option 1:</b> 15 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs every 8 hrs for 3 days, repeated every 6 weeks. If hematologic recovery (ANC &ge;1,000 mcL and platelets 50,000 mcL) from previous treatment cycle requires >6-< 8 weeks: Delay dosing for up to 2 weeks and temporarily reduced to 11 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 8 hrs (33 mg/m<sup>2</sup>/day, 99 mg/m<sup>2</sup>/cycle); 8-< 10 weeks: Assess for disease progression (by bone marrow aspirate). If no disease progression, delay for up to 2 more weeks and reduce dose to 11 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 8 hrs, then maintained or increased in subsequent cycles. <b>Option 2:</b> 20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 1 hr daily for 5 days, repeated every 4 weeks. If myelosuppression is present, delay subsequent cycles until there is hematologic recovery. <b>Non-hematological toxicity:</b> treatment should not be restarted until toxicity is resolved. See product insert for dilution and administration."

              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Phenylpropanolamine</b>: Central nervous system stimulant effects, cardiovascular stimulant effects, hypertensive crisis, tachyphylaxis. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Minor gastrointestinal disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Dextrometorphan</b>: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors, amiodarone, haloperidol, propafenone, quinidine, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, thioridazine, Central nervous system depressants. <b>Phenylpropanolamine</b>: Sympathomimetic agents, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, cyclopropane. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Warfarin or coumarin, isoniazid, anticonvulsants."

        "brand_info": [

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Erosive reflux esophagitis. NSAID-induced gastric duodenal ulcers and upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. Pathological hypersecretory conditions (e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and idiopathic hypersecretion). Cap: Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with low dose aspirin (75-325 mg) therapy. Helicobacter pylori. associated peptic and duodenal ulcers. Maintenance of homeostasis and prevention of rebleeding of gastric and duodenal ulcers following treatment with esomeprazole IV."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs weighing &ge;35 kg</b>: 1 tab thrice a day. Max 30 mg/day. Max treatment duration is 1 week."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with GI bleeding, obstruction, perforation or conditions where stimulation may be dangerous. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment, significant electrolyte disturbances, conditions where the cardiac conduction intervals are impaired or could be affected and underlying cardiac diseases as congestive heart failure, when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Prolactin-releasing pituitary tumor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "QT prolongation; torsades de pointes. Risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Patients with current or history of cardiac disease; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia; ventricular arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, QTc prolongation, torsades de pointes; somnolence, headache, convulsion, extrapyramidal disorder, depression, dizziness; loss of libido, anxiety, agitation, nervousness, akathisia; dry mouth, diarrhea; anaphylactic reactions; urinary retention; rash, pruritus, urticaria, angioedema; galactorrhea, breast pain, breast tenderness, gynecomastia, amenorrhea, irregular menstruation, breast swelling, lactation disorder; oculogyric crisis; abnormal liver function test, increased blood prolactin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "QT-prolonging drugs; potent CYP3A4 inhibitors; sustained release and enteric-coated formulations; bromocriptine; antacids, antisecretory drugs, opioid analgesics (e.g. morphine, codeine), and anticholinergics; systemic azole antifungals, macrolides, SSRIs, HIV protease inhibitors, CCBs, amiodarone, aprepitant, nefazodone; atropine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Delayed-release capsule 20 mg (P44.34), 40 mg (P66.04). Lyophilized powder for injection (IV) 40 mg (P714.15)."
          }
