          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder (SAD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Given orally as single dose in the morning or evening. <b>Adults</b> - <b>Depression:</b> 50 mg daily, increased as needed in increments of 50 mg at intervals of at least a week to max 200 mg/day; <b>OCD:</b> 50 mg daily; <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, SAD, and PTSD:</b> Initially 25 mg daily, increased after 1 week to 50 mg daily, may be further increased as needed in increments of 50 mg at intervals of at least a week to max 200 mg/day; <b>PMDD:</b> Initially 50 mg daily either throughout the menstrual cycle or during luteal phase only, may be increased by 50 mg each menstrual cycle up to max 150 mg daily for continuous dosing or 100 mg daily during the luteal phase only, reduce to the lowest effective level for maintenance once the optimal therapeutic response is obtained. <b>Adolescents</b> - <b>OCD:</b> 50 mg once daily. <b>Childn 6-12 yrs</b> - <b>OCD:</b> 25 mg once daily, increase doses as needed similar to adult dose however consider the lower BW of childn to avoid excessive dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with MAOIs; 14 days should elapse after discontinuation before initiating treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hepatic or renal impairment. Seizures. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }

            "content": "BP disturbance, tachycardia, abnormal vision, vomiting, abdominal pain, arthralgia, myalgia, liver failure. Neurological, genitourinary and skin disorders. Childn with OCD: headache, insomnia, agitation, anorexia, and tremor."

          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For contraception and treatment of menorrhagia, secondary amenorrhea, and mild to moderate endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Contraception and menorrhagia:</b> Single vial within first 5 days of cycle or first 5 days after giving birth.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. History or current high risk of arterial disease. Hormone-dependent neoplasms. Hepatic impairment. Porphyria. Pregnancy."
          },

            "content": "GI disturbances, changes in appetite, weight, breast, and libido, fluid retention, edema, acne, allergic skin rashes, mental depression, urticaria, hair loss, hirsutism, fatigue, drowsiness/insomnia, fever, headache, PMS like symptoms, irregular menstrual bleeding, anaphylaxis, inj site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminoglutethimide, antidiabetics, ciclosporin."

        "brand_name": "Depo-Medrol",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Methylprednisolone acetate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "IM: Primary, secondary, or acute adrenocortical insufficiency; congenital adrenal hyperplasia; hypercalcemia associated with cancer; non-suppurative thyroiditis. Adjunct therapy for short-term administration in rheumatic disorders. During an exacerbation or as maintenance therapy in selected cases of collagen diseases. Dermatologic diseases. Control of severe or incapacitating allergic conditions intractable to adequate trials of conventional treatment. Severe acute and chronic allergic and inflammatory processes involving the eye. Gastrointestinal, respiratory, hematologic diseases. Palliative management of neoplastic diseases. Induces diuresis or remission of proteinuria in the nephrotic syndrome, without uremia, of the idiopathic type or due to lupus erythematosus. Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis. Tuberculous meningitis with subarachnoid block or impending block when used concurrently with appropriate anti-tuberculous chemotherapy; trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement. Intra-synovial or soft tissue administration: Adjunctive therapy for short-term administration in rheumatic disorders. Intralesional administration: Keloids, localized hypertrophic, infiltrated, inflammatory lesions of lichen planus, psoriatic plaques, discoid lupus erythematosus, necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum, granuloma annulare, lichen simplex chronicus (neurodermatitis) alopecia areata; may also be useful in cystic tumors or an aponeurosis or tendon (ganglia). Intrarectal administration: Ulcerative colitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Rheumatoid and osteoarthritis (Intra-articular injection) - Large joints:</b> 20-80 mg; <b>Medium joints:</b> 10-40 mg; <b>Small joints:</b> 4-10 mg. In chronic cases may be repeated at intervals ranging from 1 to 5, or more weeks depending upon the degree of relief from initial injection. <b>Ganglion, tendinitis or tenosynovitis, epicondylitis:</b> 4-30 mg. <b>Local effect in dermatologic conditions:</b> 20-60 mg injected into the lesion; <b>Large lesions:</b> Distribute doses from 20-40 mg by repeated local injection. <b>Patients with adrenogenital syndrome:</b> Single dose 40 mg IM injection every 2 weeks. <b>Maintenance of patients with rheumatoid arthritis:</b> 40-120 mg weekly IM injection. <b>Dermatologic lesions benefited by systemic corticoid therapy:</b> 40-120 mg IM injection at weekly intervals for 1-4 weeks. <b>Acute severe dermatitis:</b> Single dose 80-120 mg IM injection, relief may result within 8-12 hrs. <b>Chronic contact dermatitis:</b> Repeated injection at 5- to 10-day intervals. <b>Seborrheic dermatitis:</b> Weekly dose of 80 mg. <b>Asthmatic patients:</b> Following IM injection of 80-120 mg, relief may result within 6-48 hrs for several days to 2 weeks. <b>Patients with allergic rhinitis (hay fever):</b> 80-120 mg IM injection followed by relief of coryzal symptoms within 6 hrs for several days to 3 weeks. <b>Adjunct in treatment of some patients with ulcerative colitis (Intrarectal injection):</b> 40-120 mg as retention enemas or by continuous drip 3-7 times weekly for periods of 2 or more weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections. For use by intrathecal, epidural and IV routes of administration. Administration of live attenuated vaccine in patients receiving immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Dermal/subdermal changes may form depressions at injection site. Precaution in intra-synovial and IM injection against injection or leakage into the dermis. Septic arthritis. Avoid local injection of steroid into previously infected joints or unstable joints. Increase susceptibility or mask signs of infection and new infections, decrease resistance and inability to localize infection. Do not use intra-synovial, intrabursal or intratendinous administration for local effect in presence of acute infection. Use of corticosteroids in active TB should be restricted to those cases of fulminating or disseminated TB. Monitor patients with latent TB or tuberculin reactivity, during prolonged corticosteroid therapy, these patients should receive chemoprophylaxis. Kaposi’s sarcoma. Septic shock. Allergic reactions. Prolonged periods may result in HPA suppression. Acute adrenal and drug-induced secondary adrenocortical insufficiencies. Steroid \"withdrawal syndrome\". Patients with Cushing’s disease, hypothyroidism, pre-existing diabetes, psychic derangements, seizure disorders, myasthenia gravis, epidural lipomatosis in long-term use at high doses. Prolonged use may produce posterior subcapsular cataracts and nuclear cataracts (in childn), exophthalmos, or increased IOP, ocular herpes simplex (possible corneal perforation), central serous chorioretinopathy. Existing CV risk factors, patients who have or may be predisposed to thromboembolic disorders, HTN. GI ulcers, non-specific ulcerative colitis, diverticulitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, active or latent peptic ulcer. Hepatobiliary disorders. Patients with disorders of neuromuscular transmission or in patients receiving concomitant therapy with anticholinergics, osteoporosis. Renal insufficiency. Elevation of BP, salt and water retention, and increased excretion of potassium. Should not be used to treat traumatic brain injury. Pheochromocytoma crisis. Intracranial pressure and pancreatitis in childn and infants in high doses. Should not drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Intrathecal/epidural: Arachnoiditis, functional GI disorders/bladder dysfunction, headache, meningitis, paraparesis/paraplegia, seizure, sensory disturbance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. isoniazid, aprepitant, fosaprepitant, antifungals, protease inhibitors, diltiazem, oral contraceptives, ciclosporin, macrolide antibiotics, grapefruit juice. CYP3A4 inducers e.g. rifampin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin. Neuromuscular blockers, anticholinesterases, antidiabetics, aminoglutethimide, aspirin, potassium-depleting agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sterile aqueous suspension for injection 40 mg/mL."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For contraception. Treatment of menorrhagia, secondary amenorrhea, and mild to moderate endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IM injection. <b>Contraception and menorrhagia:</b> 150 mg/mL within first 7 days of cycle or within first 4 weeks after giving birth or delay until 6 weeks after giving birth if breastfeeding. <b>Secondary amenorrhea:</b> 5-10 mg daily for about 5-10 days until 2 days before menstruation. <b>Mild to moderate endometriosis:</b> 50 mg weekly or 10 mg every 2 weeks for at least 6 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. History or current risk of arterial disease and thromboembolic disorders. Cerebrovascular disease. Hormone-dependent neoplasm. Hepatic impairment especially severe porphyria. After recent evacuation of hydatidiform mole. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Bone density loss. Not recommended as long-term (&gt;2 yrs) contraceptive method unless other options are inadequate. Breast cancer, vaginal bleeding, fluid retention. Patients with asthma; cardiac or renal impairment; type 2 DM, history of depression; epilepsy, HTN, hepatic dysfunction, migraine, past ectopic pregnancy, masking of climacteric conditions that reduce bone mineral that may cause osteoporotic fractures. Discontinue use in sudden partial or complete loss of vision, onset of proptosis, diplopia especially if there is papilledema or retinal vascular lesions on examination.  May affect plasma, urinary steroid, gonadotropin levels, sex-hormone binding globulin concentrations, coagulation test values for prothrombin, protein-bound iodine and T3 uptake values.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rise in BP, headache, fatigue, dizziness. PMS, irregular menstruation. Changes in libido, appetite and weight; cystitis-like syndrome. Nervousness. Backache, hirsutism, loss of scalp hair. Erythema multiforme, erythema nodosum. Hemorrhagic eruption, itching. Chloasma, injection site reaction, anaphylaxis/anaphylactoid reaction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antibiotics that induce liver enzyme production. Barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, griseofulvin, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, St. John’s wort, topiramate. Aminoglutethimide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension for injection (IM) 150 mg/mL x 2 mL."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Contraception. Treatment of menorrhagia, secondary amenorrhea and mild to moderate endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Contraception and menorrhagia:</b> Given as single dose 150 mg/3 mL within the 1<sup>st</sup> 7 days of cycle or within 1<sup>st</sup> 4 weeks after giving birth (delay 6 weeks after giving birth if breastfeeding). Can also administer any day as long as the patient is not pregnant and use a back-up method (e.g. condoms) for the next 7 days to avoid pregnancy. <b>Secondary amenorrhea:</b> 5-10 mg daily IM for 5 to 10 days until 2 days before expected onset of menstruation. <b>Mild to moderate endometriosis:</b> 50 mg weekly or 100 mg every 2 weeks IM for at least 6 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, porphyria, history or current high risk of arterial disease, hormone-dependent neoplasms, severe hepatic impairment, recent evacuation of hydatidiform mole, suspected pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cardiac or renal impairment, epilepsy, asthma, past ectopic pregnancy, history of depression, diabetes, HTN, migraine, thromboembolism, fluid retention. Wait six weeks after giving birth before the administration medroxyprogesterone.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances; changes in appetite or weight. Fluid retention; edema. Acne; chloasma (melasma); allergic skin rashes; urticaria. Mental depression. Changes in libido; breast changes (e.g. discomfort or occasionally gynecomastia); hair loss; hirsutism; fatigue; drowsiness or insomnia; fever; headache. Altered menstrual cycles or irregular menstrual bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminoglutethimide, antidiabetic drugs, ciclosporin. Enzyme-inducer antibacterial drugs."
          },

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Topical Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of all dermatomycoses due to molds and other fungi (e.g. <i>Trichophyton</i> species) or yeasts (<i>Candida</i> species) e.g. ringworm (tinea) infections (e.g. athlete’s foot), paronychia, pityriasis versicolor, erythrasma and intertrigo; skin diseases showing secondary infection with these fungi; <i>Candida</i>, nappy rash, vulvitis, and balanitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply cream thinly to the affected area 2-3x daily and rub in gently. If feet are infected, wash and dry feet thoroughly, especially between toes, before applying cream. Duration of treatment: 1 month for dermatophyte infections; 2 weeks for candidal infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Not for nail or scalp infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Contains cetostearyl alcohol. May cause damage to latex contraceptives. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Allergic reactions, syncope, hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria, blisters, discomfort or pain, edema, erythema, irritation, peeling or exfoliation, pruritus, rash, stinging or burning."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Cream 10 mg/g (1%) x 5 g, 10 g, 20 g."

  {
    "id": 4506,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4506,
        "brand_name": "Fazef",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefazolin sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "First Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of serious infections due to susceptible organisms, including respiratory tract, urinary tract (UTI), skin and skin structure, biliary tract, bone and joint, and genital infections; septicemia and endocarditis; peri-op prophylaxis. Treatment and prevention of streptococcal infections, including prophylaxis of rheumatic fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>Moderate to severe infections:</b> 500 mg-1 g every 6-8 hrs; <b>Mild infections caused by susceptible G(+) cocci:</b> 250-500 mg every 8 hrs; <b>Acute, uncomplicated UTI:</b> 1 g every 12 hrs; <b>Pneumococcal pneumonia:</b> 500 mg every 12 hrs; <b>Severe, life-threatening infections (e.g. endocarditis, septicemia):</b> 1-1.5 g every 6 hrs. <b>Peri-op prophylaxis:</b> (1) 1 g IV/IM given 30 mins-1 hr before surgery; (2) 500-1 g IV/IM during surgery; (3) 500 mg-1 g IV/IM every 6-8 hrs for 24 hrs post-op. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl 35-54 mL/min: Full doses every 8 hrs; 11-34 mL/min: Half of usual dose every 12 hrs; 10 mL/min: Half of usual dose every 18-24 hrs. <b>Childn</b> - <b>Mild to moderate infections:</b> 25-50 mg/kg in 3-4 divided doses; <b>Severe infections:</b> 100 mg/kg. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl 70-40 mL/min: 60% of normal daily dose in divided doses every 12 hrs; 40-20 mL/min: 25% of normal daily dose in divided doses every 12 hrs; 20-5 mL/min: 10% of normal daily dose every 24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of allergy to penicillins. Discontinue when allergic reaction occurs. Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, history of GI disease (colitis), poor nutritional state; receiving protracted course of antimicrobial therapy, previously stabilized on anticoagulant therapy. Premature infants and neonates. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, oral candidiasis, vomiting, nausea, stomach cramps, anorexia and pseudomembranous colitis, anaphylaxis, eosinophilia, itching, drug fever, skin rash, SJS, neutropenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, thrombocythemia, transient increase in SGOT, SGPT and alkaline phosphatase, genital and anal pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid. False positive for glucose in urine with Benedict’s solution, Fehling’s solution, or Clinitest tabs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection 1 g."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 214,
          "name": "The Cathay Drug Co., Inc."
        },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Febuxostat",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antigout Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of chronic hyperuricemia in conditions where urate deposition had already occurred (including a history, or presence of, tophus and/or gouty arthritis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Initially 40 mg once daily. Recommended dose is 40 mg or 80 mg once daily. If serum uric acid is &gt;6 mg/dL after 2-4 weeks: 80 mg once daily. <b>Mild hepatic impairment</b>: 80 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with IHD or CHF; alteration of thyroid function. Acute attacks (gout flares). Conditions where rate of urate formation is increased (e.g. malignant disease and its treatment, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome); xanthine deposition. Concomitant use with mercaptopurine/azathioprine. Organ transplant recipients. Monitor liver function. Patients with galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Gout flares, liver function abnormalities, diarrhea, nausea, headache, rash, and edema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Mercaptopurine, azathioprine, CYP2C8 substrates (e.g. rosiglitazone), theophylline, glucuronidation inducers and inhibitors (e.g. naproxen), CYP2D6 substrates (e.g. desipramine)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 40 mg (P21.00), 80 mg (P30.00)."
          }
        ],

    "detail": {

        "id": 4587,
        "brand_name": "Feiba",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6bueJsTLboaFhWwXh6nHSTnXn8vpof9jZnNab1kMswuwA6vw71.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OOgYTgJwkfzUW1nzYKZOWla63HGZE9UiqDENde2usurYul5pm4.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kPwlwLKPwjiVSumuH6p45MgQRI2fyCvvajEakw5NXLZXkeC3s6.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Factor VIII inhibitor bypassing activity",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hemostatics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of bleeding in hemophilia A patients with inhibitors; in hemophilia B patients with inhibitors, if no other specific treatment is available; in non-hemophiliacs with acquired factor VIII inhibitors. Prophylaxis of bleeding in hemophilia A patients with inhibitors at high risk or with history of significant bleeding. Also used for long-term therapy, in combination with factor VIII concentrate, to achieve complete and permanent elimination of the factor VIII inhibitor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Reconstituted soln conc: 50 U/mL. Usual dose: 50-100 U/kg. Max 100 U/kg BW single dose and 200 U/kg BW/day. Max infusion rate of 2 U/kg BW/min. <b>Spontaneous bleeding - Joint, muscle, and soft tissue hemorrhage</b> - Minor to moderately severe: 50-75 U/kg BW every 12 hrs. Severe (e.g. retroperitoneal hemorrhages): 100 U/kg BW every 12 hrs. <b>Mucous membrane hemorrhage</b>: 50 U/kg BW every 6 hrs, if bleeding does not stop, may be increased to 100 U/kg BW. Max 200 U/kg BW/day. <b>Other severe hemorrhages</b>: 100 U/kg BW every 12 hrs, may be administered every 6 hrs in individual cases. Max 200 U/kg BW/day. <b>Surgery</b> - Pre-op: Initially, 100 U/kg BW then 50-100 U/kg BW after 6-12 hrs. Post-op: 5-100 U/kg BW every 6-12 hrs. Max 200 U/kg BW/day. <b>Prophylaxis of bleeding in hemophilia A patients with high inhibitor titer - After failed immune tolerance induction (ITI) or when ITI is not considered</b>: 70-100 U/kg BW every other day, may be increased to 100 U/kg BW/day or decreased gradually. <b>During ITI</b>: May be administered concomitantly with factor VIII, in 50-100 units/kg BW twice daily, until factor VIII inhibitor titer has decreased to &lt;2 Bethesda Unit."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Acute thrombosis or embolism (including MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of CHD, liver disease, DIC, arterial or venous thrombosis, post-op immobilization, and other risk factors for thromboembolic events, liver damage. Emicizumab-exposed patients. May induce hypersensitivity reactions, thrombotic and thromboembolic events (including DIC, venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, MI, stroke); increased bleeding tendency, or increased risk of thrombosis. May cause an initial anamnestic rise in inhibitor levels.  Concomitant use with rFVIIa increases risk of developing a thromboembolic event. Discontinue if clinically significant changes in BP or pulse rate, respiratory distress, coughing, or chest pain occur. In vitro tests (e.g. aPTT, WBCT, TEG) may not correlate with clinical outcomes, so increasing dose to normalize them is strongly discouraged due to risk of DIC. If treatment response is inadequate, consider conducting a thrombocyte count or use of another bypassing agent. Consider appropriate vaccination (hepatitis A and B) for patients regularly receiving human plasma-derived products. Contains approx 40 mg sodium per vial. Elderly. Childn and neonates. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity, headache, dizziness, hypotension, rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Recombinant factor VIIa, antifibrinolytics, or emicizumab. May interfere with serological tests for red cell antibodies (e.g. Coombs test) and hepatitis B surface antibodies."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for solution for IV infusion 500 U."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1325,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1325,
        "brand_name": "Dexilant",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dexlansoprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Healing of all grades of erosive esophagitis (EE). Maintenance of healed EE and relief of heartburn. Treatment of symptomatic non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs - Healing of EE:</b> 60 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks; <b>Maintenance of healed EE and relief of heartburn:</b> 30 mg once daily - <b>Adult</b> for 6 months; <b>childn 12-17 yrs</b> for up to 16 weeks. <b>Symptomatic non-erosive GERD:</b> 30 mg once daily for 4 weeks. <b>Moderate hepatic impairment:</b> 30 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks. Capsule may be opened and administered with applesauce; or water via oral syringe or NG tube (&ge;16 French) in patients who have trouble swallowing."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Rilpivirine-containing products."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Presence of gastric malignancy. <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. May increase risk of osteoporosis-related fractures of hip, wrist, or spine. Vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency, hypomagnesemia. Risk of fundic gland polyps. Discontinue if acute tubulointerstitial nephritis is suspected; severe cutaneous adverse reaction, cutaneous lupus erythematosus, and SLE occur. Monitor magnesium and calcium levels prior to initiation of and periodically during treatment in patients with pre-existing risk of hypocalcemia. Temporary withdraw for &ge;14 days prior CgA measurements. Childn < 2 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, URTI, vomiting, and flatulence."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antiretrovirals, warfarin, methotrexate, digoxin, tacrolimus, St. John’s Wort, rifampicin, iron salts, erlotinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, mycophenolate mofetil, ketoconazole, itraconazole, CYP2C19 or CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors. Interactions with investigations for neuroendocrine tumors, secretin simulation test, urine tests for tetrahydrocannabinol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Delayed-release capsule 30 mg, 60 mg."
          }
        ],

        },

      "data": {
        "id": 2798,

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5XIRxBoytEm8DPM39vStSLIilcGpJsAHezpRmTlHKClxPDVVZx.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/X7mjh5SoaYTF9hsyW0F4HozoL8VfLHRotWm44QggZ0RTzm5rLF.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DjlBSaJuVyz7kiwVfRyDdkQ9oRCxbwrtal9tGEkCZAl2cJhYpe.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Biguanides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus, particularly in overweight patients when dietary management and exercise alone does not result in adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially, 500 mg or 750 mg once daily with evening meal. Initial dose should be equivalent to the daily dose of immediate release tab. After 10-15 days, adjust dose based on blood glucose measurements. <b>Max recommended dose - 1 g</b>: 2 tabs. <b>750 mg</b>: 3 tabs. <b>500 mg</b>: 4 tabs. Doses to be taken once daily with evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on four 500 mg tabs once daily, consider two 500 mg tabs twice daily with breakfast and evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on three 750 mg tabs once daily, consider one 750 mg tab with breakfast and two tabs with evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on two 1 g tabs once daily, consider 1 tab during breakfast and 1 tab during evening meal."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe destabilization of diabetes (ketoacidosis or precoma); renal and hepatic insufficiency; severe infection; dehydration due to persistent or severe diarrhea, recurrent vomiting; conditions at risk for tissue hypoxia (heart failure, recent MI, respiratory insufficiency, shock). Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for lactic acidosis. Discontinue 48 hrs before an elective surgery or X-ray with iodinated contrast media and not reinstituted until 48 hrs after and renal function is evaluated as normal. Concurrent intake of alcoholic beverages. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, taste disturbance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Glucocorticoids (systemic and local routes), tetracosactides, beta-2 agonists, danazol, chlorpromazine at high doses. Diuretics (loop diuretics). ACE inhibitors. NSAIDs. Anticoagulant. Cimetidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 500 mg, 750 mg, 1 g."
          }
        ],

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 358,
        "brand_name": "Diamicron",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gJlTxCZhNPyGfmS0YKWtmyOjBPg3UI2IvKcwDZP059kIXQMOyG.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jejpbFNmgAEuYIbJMYhmb5unOb4UQQAnoF27UH0G2bffMvJyqw.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pmxtUuvefgKqIoz86tnOznB8Fz16ug6wyQAOuIjozcgdcx4Y4u.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gliclazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Sulfonylureas"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment for adults with type 2 diabetes in cases where dietary measure have failed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults < 65 yrs:</b> Initially 1 tab/day. Adjust dose according to patient's response and in steps of 1 tab at a time, at least 14 days should separate successive steps in the dose. Maintenance: 1-4 tabs daily (usually 2 tabs/day); <b>>65 yrs:</b> Initially &frac12; tab/day, can be increased accordingly. Monitor blood glucose closely. <b>Patients who are malnourished or showing markedly poor general state of health; with irregular calorie intake; renal or hepatic impairment:</b> Start at lowest dose, then increase accordingly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with type 1 diabetes; diabetes pre-coma and coma, diabetic ketoacidosis; severe renal or hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with miconazole. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Ensure adequate carbohydrate intake. Patients with G6PD deficiency; porphyria; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption. Concomitant use with fluoroquinolones, especially in elderly. Increased risk of hypoglycemia in patients who refuse or unable to cooperate; with malnutrition, irregular meal intake; physical exercise and carbohydrate intake imbalance; renal and severe hepatic impairment; certain endocrine disorders (e.g. thyroid disorders, hypopituitarism, adrenal insufficiency); concomitant use with other medicinal products. Blood glucose control may be affected by St. John’s Wort preparations, fever, injury, infection, or surgery. Monitor blood glucose closely. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia. GI disturbances (e.g. abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, diarrhea, constipation)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenylbutazone (systemic), alcohol; other antidiabetics (e.g. insulins, acarbose, metformin, thiazolidinediones, DPP-4 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists), beta-blockers, fluconazole, ACE inhibitors, H2-antagonists, MAOIs, sulfonamides, clarithromycin, NSAIDs. Danazol; chlorpromazine (>100 mg daily), glucocorticoids (systemic, local, intra-articular, cutaneous, rectal), ritodrine, salbutamol, IV terbutaline; St. John’s Wort. Fluoroquinolones; anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 80 mg x 60s (P487.50)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/1DU7lIjyb7QIxjD1m3XxZ9YPMmTpoPLjZuFXKd3ZkwIroFWT4C.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/lvarAhWUGZ31ax3toKiiIBrid7VApvH5hyhQzkYglZxP3Xof01.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Loperamide HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antidiarrheals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control and symptomatic relief of acute non-specific or chronic diarrhea associated with inflammatory bowel disease. Reduction of number and volume of discharge in patients with ileostomies and colostomies."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Acute diarrhea</b>: 2 caps followed by 1 cap after each LBM. Discontinue if no improvement after 2 days. Max 8 caps/day. <b>Chronic diarrhea</b>: 2 caps followed by 1 cap after each LBM, then reduce dose to meet individual requirements. <b>Average daily maintenance dose</b>: 2-4 caps daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Constipation. Abdominal swelling or pain. Diarrhea due to infections. Acute dysentery. Pseudomembranous colitis, active ulcerative colitis, meningitis, or history of liver disease. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Replace fluid and salt loss with ORS and/or by drinking plenty of fluids. Patients with AIDS.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dry mouth, abdominal pain, distention or discomfort, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, flatulence, dyspepsia, constipation, epigastric pain, paralytic ileus, and toxic megacolon."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ritonavir. Quinidine. Oral desmopressin. Itraconazole or ketoconazole. Gemfibrozil. Drugs that slow down peristalsis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 2 mg (P8.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 677,
          "name": "Unilab Consumer Health"

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For relief of symptoms of diarrhea with bloating, pressure and cramps, gassiness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b>: 2 caps after the first loose stool; 1 cap after each subsequent loose stool; but not &gt;4 caps in 24 hrs. To be taken on an empty stomach (1 hr before or 2 hrs after meal)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with swollen abdomen, abdominal pain in the absence of diarrhea, acute dysentery, pseudomembranous and acute ulcerative colitis, bacterial enterocolitis. Patients with conditions associated with constipation; in which constipation should be avoided (e.g. infectious diarrhea), or slowing of the intestines should be avoided due to the possible risk of developing ileus, megacolon, and toxic megacolon."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not take more than the recommended. Replace fluid and salt loss with ORS and/or by drinking plenty of fluids. Risk for loss/depressed level of consciousness, tiredness. Patients with AIDS or HIV; liver impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;12 yrs; with compromised blood-brain barrier.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, constipation, headache, abdominal cramps, dizziness, dry mouth, dysgeusia, vomiting, flatulence, dyspepsia, drowsiness, fatigue, urinary retention, difficulty urinating, abdominal pain, distension, or discomfort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Loperamide: Ritonavir, quinidine, quinine, clarithromycin or erythromycin, itraconazole or ketoconazole, gemfibrozil; antidepressants, cold and allergy medications; oral desmopressin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 2 mg/125 mg (P18.00)."
          }

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute and maintenance treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults and adolescents 12-17 yrs. Management generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, social phobia and post-traumatic stress disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>MDD – Adults</b>: Initially 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 20 mg after minimum of 1 week. <b>Adolescents</b>: 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 20 mg after minimum of 3 weeks. <b>GAD</b>: Initially 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 20 mg after minimum of 1 week. <b>Elderly, patients with hepatic impairment</b>: Initially 5 mg for the first 2 weeks, may be increased to 10 mg/day depending on patient’s response. <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia</b>: Initially 5 mg, may be increased by 10 mg daily. Max 20 mg daily. <b>Switching to or from a MAOI</b>: At least 14 days should elapse between discontinuation of or switch to MAOI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with MAOIs or pimozide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Withdrawal symptoms. Increased risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in childn and adolescents with MDD and other psychiatric disorders. Serotonin syndrome. Hyponatremia or SIADH may occur. Patients with history of mania, seizure disorder, diseases or conditions that produce altered metabolism or hemodynamic response. Angle-closure glaucoma in susceptible patients. Concomitant use of NSAIDs, aspirin or other drugs that affect coagulation. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;12 yrs (with MDD) and &lt;18 yrs (with GAD). Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, nausea. Decreased/increased appetite, weight increased; anxiety, restlessness, abnormal dreams, decreased libido, anorgasmia in females; insomnia, somnolence, dizziness, paresthesia, tremor; sinusitis, yawning; diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, dry mouth; increased sweating, arthralgia, myalgia; ejaculatory disorder, impotence in males; fatigue, pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other CNS drugs, alcohol, lithium, sumatriptan, ketoconazole, CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g. omeprazole, esomeprazole, fluvoxamine, lansoprazole, ticlopidine) or cimetidine, desipramine, metoprolol. NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P50.85), 20 mg (P67.25)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Treatment of hypertension. May be used alone or concomitantly with other antihypertensive agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Initially 5 mg once daily, may be increased to max 10 mg once daily after at least 2 weeks. <b>Elderly</b>: Initially 2.5 mg once daily, dose increase should be made with particular caution. <b>Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: Initially 2.5 mg once daily, dose increase should be made only after critically weighing the effects and side effects.           {

            "content": "Hypersensitivity.             "content": "Flushing, headache or tinnitus."
          },
          {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yKzZPetOVNGtd8dzGbGqzzsllct6pkxOS2v20vXpJa64b8o006.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0vRiMDVRRFdPrwKq0m5ytSAPfXZoodbhk2L9j789HaAxeK7fuy.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fenofibrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fibric Acid Derivatives & Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet for the reduction of LDL-C and total cholesterol, triglycerides and apolipoprotein B, and increase HDL-C in adult patients with primary hypercholesterolemia or mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson types IIa and IIb). Treatment of hypertriglyceridemia (Fredrickson types IV and V) and secondary hyperlipoproteinemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "160 mg once a day with meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal dysfunction, patients on dialysis, active liver disease, hepatic dysfunction including primary biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormality, preexisting gallbladder disease, presence of gallstones. Known photoallergy or phototoxic reaction with fenofibrate or ketoprofen. Chronic or acute pancreatitis. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver and renal function. May cause myopathy, cholelithiasis, pancreatitis, VTE disease, hematologic changes, skeletal muscle effects. Patients with predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Paradoxical decreases in HDL-C levels. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abnormal elevation in serum transaminases (ALT and/or AST), epigastric distress, flatulence, abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, erythema, pruritus, urticaria, muscle pain and weakness, arthralgia, headache, dizziness, insomnia, decreased libido, hair loss, and weight loss."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Coumarin anticoagulants, immunosuppressants (ciclosporin, tacrolimus), HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, bile acid sequestrants/bile acid resin, colchicine and glitazones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 160 mg (P39.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Y6sHd1LIhjUEy2qvxdn2NsH9YdkwKKF9rAAdFwrBNOjrTfc4yp.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XYGwpwFXv1lXxAwYJUbeqY4LKHFXzCKMKR6T4xHpIu0Pr3vV6w.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/G3aDAmvfH34wp0yVdF0ppuzknXGaRMUVcVD6dBbD6xHMie9RDB.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Doxylamine succinate, pyridoxine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiemetic/Antivertigo"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of nausea and vomiting of pregnancy in women who do not respond to conservative management."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Start with 2 tabs at bedtime on day 1; continue dosage if symptoms are adequately controlled. If symptoms persist into the afternoon of day 2, take 2 tabs at bedtime on day 2, then 3 tabs (1 in the morning, 2 at bedtime) on day 3. If symptoms continue on day 3, increase to 4 tabs on day 4 (1 in the morning, 1 mid-afternoon, 2 at bedtime). Max 4 tabs/day. Take on an empty stomach."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Porphyria. Concomitant use with MAOIs and potent inhibitors of CYP450 isoenzymes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Gradually taper dose at time of discontinuation. Patients with hyperemesis gravidarum; increased IOP, narrow-angle glaucoma, stenosing peptic ulcer, pyloroduodenal obstruction, bladder-neck obstruction; asthma or other breathing disorders (e.g. chronic bronchitis and pulmonary emphysema); hepatic and renal impairment; epilepsy; long QT syndrome. Hypokalemia or other electrolyte disturbances. History of drug use disorders. Avoid direct exposure to sunlight. Concomitant use of CNS depressants including alcohol; ototoxic drugs. May aggravate dehydration and heat stroke. May interfere with allergy skin testing. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Childn. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence. Dizziness, increased bronchial secretion, dry mouth, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticholinergic agents (e.g. TCAs, MAOIs, neuroleptics), sedatives, alcohol, sodium oxybate, ototoxic drugs (e.g. aminoglycosides), photosensitizing medications (e.g. amiodarone, quinidine, imipramine, doxepin, amitriptyline, griseofulvin, chlorpheniramine, piroxicam, furosemide, captopril), drugs that prolong the QT interval (e.g. antiarrhythmic drugs), CYP450 inhibitors. False positive in urine screening tests for methadone, opiates, and phencyclidine phosphate. Allergy skin testing. <b>Pyridoxine</b>: Hydroxyzine, isoniazid, penicillamine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Delayed-release tablet 10 mg/10 mg (P220.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 2820,
    "detail": {

      "data": {
        "id": 2820,
        "brand_name": "Dicorate ER 500",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Divalproex sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fatty Acid Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorder; monotherapy and adjunct of simple and complex partial seizures in adults and childn &ge;10 yrs. Prophylaxis of migraine headaches in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily. Swallow whole.  <b>Migraine - Adults:</b> Initially 500 mg for 1 week, increased to 1,000 mg; <b>Elderly:</b> Reduced dose. <b>Simple and complex absence seizures - Adults and childn &ge;10 yrs:</b> Initially 15 mg/kg, increased at 1-week intervals by 5-10 mg/kg until seizures are controlled or side effects preclude further increases. Max 60 mg/kg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with urea cycle disorders, hepatic disease, or significant hepatic dysfunction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients receiving multiple anticonvulsants, with congenital metabolic disorders, severe seizure disorders accompanied by mental retardation, organic brain disease, epilepsy, history of hepatic disease. Concomitant use with other CNS depressants (e.g. alcohol). Hepatic failure, hyperammonemic encephalopathy, thrombocytopenia, CNS depression. Discontinue treatment if pancreatitis occurs. Evaluate urea cycle disorder prior therapy in patients with history of unexplained encephalopathy or coma, protein load-associated, pregnancy-related or post-partum encephalopathy, unexplained mental retardation or history of elevated plasma ammonia or glutamine, cyclical vomiting and lethargy, episodic extreme irritability, ataxia, low BUN or protein avoidance, family history or signs of UCD or unexplained infant deaths (particularly males). Perform liver function, platelet counts, and coagulation tests prior to therapy and at frequent intervals, especially during the 1<sup>st</sup> 6 months. May cause false interpretation of urine ketone test, alter thyroid function tests, and stimulate HIV and CMV virus replication under certain experimental conditions. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 10 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, tremors; nausea; asthenia; thrombocytopenia; weight gain or loss; amnesia, ataxia, dizziness, headache, nystagmus, paresthesia, speech disorder; tinnitus; abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting; alopecia, ecchymosis, pruritus, rash; increased or decreased appetite; gait disturbances, peripheral edema; abnormal dreams, affect lability, confusion, depression, insomnia, nervousness, abnormal thinking; amblyopia, diplopia; infection; injury."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone, CYP450 inhibitors (e.g. antidepressants), aspirin, felbamate, rifampin, amitriptyline/nortriptyline, clonazepam; diazepam, ethosuximide and other anticonvulsants, phenytoin, lamotrigine, barbiturates, tolbutamide, warfarin, zidovudine, lorazepam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 500 mg x 30s (P1,386.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        },

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Adapalene",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Acne Agents & Cell Stimulants & Proliferants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of facial acne vulgaris; acne on chest or back. <b>3 mg/g:</b> Treatment of facial skin photoaging. Helps minimize the signs of photo-damaged skin which may include wrinkles and hyperpigmentation e.g. blemishes, related to sun exposures, and when used together with appropriate skin care and sunlight avoidance programs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply a thin film of the product to face acne-affected areas once a day at bedtime and after washing. Ensure that the affected areas are dry before application."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue if irritation occurs. Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, angles of the nose or mucous membranes. Do not apply to broken (cuts and abrasions) or eczematous skin. Avoid waxing the treated skin. Concomitant use of other potentially irritating topical products (e.g. medicated or abrasive soaps and cleaners, soaps and cosmetics that have a strong drying effect, products with high concentrations of alcohol, astringents, spices, or lime). Combination with preparations containing sulfur, resorcinol, or salicylic acid. Avoid exposure to excessive sunlight or UV irradiation. Childn < 12 yrs. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C. <b>3 mg/g:</b> Patients < 35 yrs with facial photoaging.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin irritation, dry skin, burning sensation, erythema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other topical retinoids or drugs with a similar mode of action, astringents, peeling agents, abrasive cleansers, strong drying agents. Preparations containing sulfur, resorcinol or salicylic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Cream 1 mg/g (0.1%) x 30 g (P2,690.00). Gel 1 mg/g (0.1%) x 15 g (P2,005.00), 30 g (P2,740.00). 3 mg/g (0.3%) x 30 g (P3,265.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 2644,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2644,
        "brand_name": "Diflucan",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fluconazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Cryptococcosis, including cryptococcal meningitis and infections of other sites (e.g. pulmonary, cutaneous); used as maintenance therapy to prevent relapse of cryptococcal disease in patients with AIDS. Systemic candidiasis, including candidemia, disseminated candidiasis and other forms of invasive candidal infections; Patients with malignancy, in ICU, receiving cytotoxic or immunosuppressive therapy, or with other factors predisposing to candidal infection. Mucosal candidiasis; Prevention of relapse of oropharyngeal candidiasis in patients with AIDS. Genital candidiasis. Vaginal candidiasis, acute or recurrent, and prophylaxis to reduce the incidence of recurrent vaginal candidiasis (three or more episodes a yr). Candidal balanitis. Prevention of fungal infections in patients with malignancy who are predisposed to such infections as a result of cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Dermatomycosis, including tinea pedis, tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea versicolor, tinea unguium (onychomycosis), and dermal Candida infections. Deep endemic mycoses in immunocompetent patients, coccidioidomycosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, sporotrichosis and histoplasmosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>Cryptococcal meningitis and cryptococcal infections:</b> 400 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day followed by 200-400 mg once daily, duration of treatment will depend on clinical and mycological response for cryptococcal infections, at least 6-8 weeks for cryptococcal meningitis. <b>Prevention of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in patients with AIDS:</b> After receiving full course of primary treatment, may administer a dose of 200 mg once daily. <b>Candidemia, disseminated candidiasis and other forms of invasive candidal infections:</b> 400 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day followed by 200 mg once daily, may be increased to 400 mg daily. <b>Oropharyngeal candidiasis:</b> 50-100 mg once daily for 7-14 days, treatment can be continued for longer periods in patients with severely compromised immune function. <b>Atrophic oral candidiasis associated with dentures:</b> 50 mg once daily for 14 days administered concurrently with local antiseptic measures to the denture. <b>Other candidal infections of mucosa except genital candidiasis:</b> 50-100 mg once daily for 14-30 days. <b>Prevention of relapse of oropharyngeal candidiasis in patients with AIDS:</b> After receiving full course of primary treatment, may administer a 150 mg once-weekly dose. <b>Vaginal candidiasis, <i>Candida</i> balanitis:</b> 150 mg single oral dose. <b>Reduce incidence of recurrent vaginal candidiasis:</b> 150 mg once-monthly dose, ranges from 4-12 months. <b>Prevention of candidiasis:</b> 50-400 mg once daily based on patient's risk for developing fungal infection; For patients at high risk of systemic infection (e.g. patients anticipated to have profound or prolonged neutropenia): 400 once daily started days before onset of neutropenia and continued for 7 days until neutrophil counts &gt;1000 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>. <b>Dermal infections:</b> 150 mg once weekly or 50 mg once daily, for 2-4 weeks, tinea pedis may require treatment for up to 6 weeks. <b>Tinea versicolor:</b> 300-400 mg may be needed in some patients may be sufficient; alternate dosing regimen 50 mg once daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>Tinea unguium:</b> 150 mg once weekly, continue treatment until uninfected nail grows in. <b>Deep endemic mycoses:</b> 200-400 mg once daily for up to 2 yrs may be required (11-24 months for coccidioidomycosis, 2-17 months for paracoccidioidomycosis, 1-16 months for sporotrichosis, 3-17 months for histoplasmosis). <b>Childn</b> - <b>Mucosal candidiasis:</b> 3 mg/kg once daily, loading dose of 6 mg/kg may be used on 1<sup>st</sup> day. <b>Systemic candidiasis and cryptococcal infections:</b> 6-12 mg/kg once daily. <b>Suppression of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in childn with AIDS:</b> 6 mg/kg once daily. <b>Prevention of fungal infections in immunocompromised patients at risk as a consequence of neutropenia following cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy:</b> 3-12 mg/kg once daily. <b>Infants &lt;4 weeks old:</b> 1<sup>st</sup> 2 weeks of life, same mg/kg dosing as childn, administered every 72 hrs, during weeks 3 and 4 of life, same dose given every 48 hrs. <b>Renal impairment:</b> Initial loading dose of 50-400 mg; CrCl &le;50 mL/min and no dialysis: 50% of recommended dose; Hemodialysis: 100% of recommended doses administered after each hemodialysis. <b>IV</b> - Infusion rate: Not exceeding 10 mL/min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to fluconazole, any of the ingredients, or related azole compounds. Co-administration of terfenadine, other drugs known to prolong QT interval and are metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g. cisapride, astemizole, erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with liver and renal dysfunction. Discontinue treatment if signs or symptoms consistent with liver disease develop; patients who develop abnormal liver function tests during therapy should be monitored. Discontinue treatment if rash develops in a patient treated for a superficial fungal infection; patients with invasive/systemic fungal infections who develop rashes should be monitored, discontinue if bullous lesions or erythema multiforme develop. Patients with hypokalemia, advanced cardiac failure, other proarrhythmic conditions, and concomitantly treated with CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 substrates. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp-lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C for single low dose (150 mg); Category D for high chronic doses (400-800 mg/day).",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache; abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting; increased ALT/AST, blood alkaline phosphatase; rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cisapride, terfenadine, astemizole, pimozide, quinidine, erythromycin; amiodarone; hydrochlorothiazide, rifampicin; alfentanil, amitriptyline, nortriptyline, amphotericin B, anticoagulants, azithromycin, short-acting benzodiazepines, carbamazepine, CCBs, celecoxib, ciclosporin, cyclophosphamide, fentanyl, halofantrine, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, losartan, methadone, NSAIDs, olaparib, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, prednisone, rifabutin, saquinavir, sirolimus, sulfonylureas, tacrolimus, theophylline, tofacitinib, vinca alkaloids, vit A, voriconazole, zidovudine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 50 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg. Solution for injection (IV) 2 mg/mL x 100 mL."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 111,
          "name": "Pfizer, Inc."
        },
        "class": "human",

            "content": "<b>Oropharyngeal candidiasis in patients with AIDS:</b> 150 mg once weekly. <b>Vaginal candidiasis:</b> 150 mg once monthly. <b>Candida balanitis:</b> 150 mg as single oral dose. <b>Prevention of Candidiasis:</b> 50-400 mg once daily. <b>Derma infection (e.g. Tinea pedis, corporis, cruris and candidal infection):</b> 150 mg once weekly. <b>Tinea versicolor:</b> 300 mg once weekly for 2 weeks. <b>Use in renal impairment – CrCl >50 mL/min:</b> Normal dosage regimen.
