          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wt9Z13Z4RY2jVscXuOmwiMXjTmEuYuZdFrTdBAKGrH7tSSurYn.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Iron, folic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anemia Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) during pregnancy, lactation, and in anemia due to post-partum hemorrhage. Prevention of IDA."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment IDA:</b> 1 cap 2x daily for 3-5 months until normalization of Hgb is achieved. Continue therapy afterward for several weeks to replenish iron stores. <b>Prevention:</b> 1 cap once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Iron overload (e.g. hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis), iron utilization disturbances (e.g. lead anemia, sideroblastic anemia, thalassemia), and all anemias not caused by iron deficiency (e.g. hemolytic or megaloblastic anemia due to vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Reconsider treatment if therapy does not succeed (Hgb increases by about 2-3 g/dL after 3 weeks). Patients receiving repeated blood transfusions. May mask vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency; exclude the possibility of vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency prior to therapy. Childn < 12 yrs. Elderly. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Stool discoloration. Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, epigastric discomfort, abdominal distension, constipation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Iron:</b> Parenteral iron preparations. <b>Folic acid:</b> Phenytoin or other antiepileptics/anticonvulsants, chloramphenicol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg/550 mcg (P21.00)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/b5n70pSrueFDHQHwQMamhpj5doCi0kfPVpIzuoB08FeMmXRcgK.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/73Pi8ggXt65NhH1E0Zkj86d9hSatfMBtL9g5nRBFsdnU3KKk0E.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "<b>Per 1 mL drops:</b> Iron 15 mg, folic acid 10 mcg, vitamins B<sub>1</sub> 10 mg, B<sub>6</sub> 5 mg, B<sub>12</sub> 25 mcg. <b>Per 5 mL syr:</b> Iron 30 mg, vitamins B<sub>1</sub> 10 mg, B<sub>6</sub> 10 mg, B<sub>12</sub> 50 mcg",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anemia Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anemia in infants and childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Drops - Prophylactic dose:</b> Childn 1-7 yrs: 1 mL once daily; Infants 6-12 months: 0.75-1 mL once daily; 4-6 months: 0.5 mL once daily; Term infants: 1 mg/kg/day. Max 15 mg/day. Start no later than 4 months, and continue at least through 1<sup>st</sup> yr of life; Preterm infants: 2 mg/kg/day. Max 15 mg/day. Start no later than 2 months, and continue at least through 1st yr of life. <b>Therapeutic dose:</b> 3 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. Childn 1-7 yrs: 1 mL thrice daily; Infants 6-12 months: 0.75-1 mL thrice daily; 4-6 months: 0.5 mL thrice daily. <b>Syr - Supplemental dose:</b> Equiv to RDA 10-15 mg/day. Childn 2-12 yrs: 2.5 mL once daily. <b>Therapeutic dose:</b> 3 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. Childn 7-12 yrs: 5 mL thrice daily; 2-6 yrs: 2.5 mL thrice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Primary hemochromatosis, peptic ulcer, regional enteritis, or ulcerative colitis. Patients receiving parenteral iron or blood transfusions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not used to treat hemolytic anemias unless iron deficiency also exists. Do not use therapeutic doses for >6 months.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, temporary staining of teeth, darker stools."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids, chloramphenicol and iron salts, carbidopa, levodopa, methyldopa, penicillamine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral drops 15 mL (P168.00). Syrup 120 mL (P374.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1812,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1812,
        "brand_name": "Digox",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xPs3QyZ7K5V0KA6y3B3XPTAJqTsuvk6GIe47Zzbh5XgY1CHgFg.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/N6sM0x61CipT3eVwTnHHrMZxoVVkP6hv9SwRbg18DQXGAMrHzW.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mVQIwTFwK7NRUeb8oKyw0rarxSXYqFNBchn7mBxQQMVsFnzSzu.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Digoxin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Cardiac Glycosides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of supraventricular arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation, and in heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Total loading dose:</b> 750-1,500 mcg may be given during the initial 24-hr period, either as a single dose or in divided doses every 6 hrs if rapid digitalization is required. <b>Patient with mild heart failure:</b> Loading dose may not be necessary and digitalization may be achieved more slowly with doses of 250 mcg once daily or twice a day. <b>Maintenance dose:</b> 125-250 mcg daily but may range from 62.5-500 mcg daily. <b>Renal impairment:</b> Reduce dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (unless there is severe cardiac failure), Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or other evidence of accessory pathway (especially if accompanied by atrial fibrillation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with partial heart block, sinus node disorders, acute myocarditis (e.g. rheumatic carditis) in acute MI, advanced heart failure, and severe pulmonary disease. Electrolyte imbalance, hypokalemia, hypercalcemia. Dialysis. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, anorexia, diarrhea, abdominal pain, headache, facial pain, fatigue, weakness, dizziness, drowsiness, disorientation, mental confusion, bad dreams, visual disturbances. May aggravate heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that cause electrolyte disturbances, thiazides, loop diuretics. Corticosteroids, beta2 agonists (salbutamol), amphotericin B, sodium polystyrene sulfonate, carbenoxolone. Calcium salts, CCBs. Beta-blockers. Drugs that affect P-gp."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 250 mcg (P5.08)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hTzox8HEPH0AZDmyxL1gdQ2jSXllm52Xdf1hPmz17mc3QGmaZc.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Carvedilol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of hypertension (HTN) and angina pectoris. Adjunct to standard therapy in symptomatic heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: Initially 6.25 mg twice daily, increase after 1-2 weeks to 12.5 mg twice daily. May be further increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks to 50 mg once daily or in divided doses if necessary. Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily. <b>Angina pectoris</b>: Initially 12.5 mg twice daily, increase after 2 days to 25 mg twice daily. <b>Heart failure</b>: Initially 3.125 mg twice daily, taken with food. If tolerated, double the dose after 2 weeks to 6.25 mg twice daily, then increase gradually at intervals of not < 2 weeks. Patients weighing >85 kg: Max 50 mg twice daily; < 65 kg: Max 25 mg twice daily. Monitor patients for 2-3 hrs after initiation and after each dose increase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Unstable/decompensated heart failure, clinically manifest hepatic impairment, marked fluid retention or overload requiring IV inotropic support, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), severe bradycardia (&lt;50 bpm, sick sinus syndrome (including SA block), severe hypotension (SBP &lt;85 mmHg), cardiogenic shock, metabolic acidosis, history of bronchospasm or asthma, or other obstructive lung disorders. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Bradycardia, hypotension, heart failure/fluid retention, non-allergic bronchospasm, diabetes and hypoglycemia, PVD, renal function deterioration, hepatic injury, anesthesia and major surgery. Thyrotoxicosis. Phaeochromocytoma. Prinzmetal’s variant angina. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, allergy fatigue, fever, hypovolemia, malaise, edema, flu syndrome, pain in extremities.  Heart failure, heart block and bronchospasm. Fatigue and coldness of extremities. Bradycardia, hypotension/postural hypotension, fluid overload, syncope, AV block, palpitation, angina pectoris (including chest pain), cardiac failure, hypertension, peripheral ischemia, tachycardia, bundle branch block, myocardial ischemia, peripheral circulation disturbances (e.g. cold extremities, peripheral vascular disorder, exacerbation of intermittent claudication, Raynaud's phenomenon)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Clonidine, ciclosporin, digoxin, amiodarone, anesthesia, verapamil, diltiazem. Inhibitors of CYP2D6 (e.g. quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone), catecholamine-depleting agents (e.g. reserpine and MAOIs), insulin or oral hypoglycemics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 6.25 mg (P7.25), 25 mg (P12.50)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ukPXYPcLKHgGy4bbYcyqnKp8vFHWu59VtjGgXxw7klihbaBo0B.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/piD5GUvMPR5U9VaqoDYwtdsOAEUvCaTRdn7eG8TqLeGwAa110p.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Phenytoin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hydantoins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of generalized tonic-clonic (grand mal) and complex partial (psychomotor, temporal lobe) seizures and for the prevention and treatment of seizures occurring during or following neurosurgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap - Adults with no previous treatment:</b> 300 mg daily in 3 equally divided doses. Maintenance: 300-400 mg daily in 3-4 equally divided doses, may increase up to 600 mg daily if necessary. <b>Non-emergency oral loading dose – Adults:</b> 1 g divided into 3 doses (400 mg, 300 mg, and 300 mg) at 2-hr intervals. Normal maintenance dosage is then instituted 24 hrs after the loading dose, with frequent serum level determinations. <b>Seizures – Childn:</b> Initially 5 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 equally divided doses with subsequent individualized dosage to max 300 mg daily. Maintenance: 4-8 mg/kg; <b>Childn >6 yrs and adolescents:</b> may require 300 mg/day. <b>Susp – Adults with no previous treatment:</b> 5 mL three times daily, may increase to 25 mL daily if necessary. <b>Seizures – Childn:</b> Initially 5 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 equally divided doses with subsequent individualized dosage to max 300 mg daily. Maintenance: 4-8 mg/kg; <b>Childn >6 yrs and adolescents:</b> may require 300 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to phenytoin or other hydantoins. Co-administration with delavirdine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not effective for absence (petit mal) seizures. Not indicated for seizures due to hypoglycemic or other metabolic causes. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Suicidal ideation or behavior. Cases of bradycardia and asystole/cardiac arrest. Hypersensitivity syndrome or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms. Serious dermatologic reactions. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema occur. Hepatic injury. Hematopoietic complications occasionally. May produce confusional states, rarely irreversible cerebellar dysfunction and/or cerebellar atrophy. Porphyria. May affect bone mineral metabolism. Good dental hygiene to minimize development of gingival hyperplasia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Oral contraceptives. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anaphylactoid reaction, anaphylaxis; nystagmus, ataxia, slurred speech, decreased coordination and mental confusion; Dizziness, vertigo, insomnia, transient nervousness, motor twitching, headache, paresthesia and somnolence; sensory peripheral polyneuropathy (long-term therapy); coarsening of facial features, enlargement of lips, gingival hyperplasia, hypertrichosis and Peyronie’s disease; acute hepatic failure, toxic hepatitis, liver damage, vomiting, nausea and constipation; hematopoietic complications; SLE, polyarteritis nodosa, immunoglobulin abnormalities; scarlatiniform or morbiliform rashes, bullous, exfoliative or purpuric dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis; taste perversion; bone fractures and osteomalacia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol intake, analgesic/anti-inflammatory agents, halothane, antibacterial agents, anticonvulsants, antifungals, capecitabine, fluorouracil, benzodiazepines, CCBs, cimetidine, fluvastatin, estrogens, tacrolimus, tolbutamide, omeprazole, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, sertraline, ciprofloxacin, rifampin, vigabatrin, antineoplastics, sucralfate, antiretrovirals, theophylline, reserpine, folic acid, diazoxide, St. John’s Wort, anthelmintics, teniposide, theophylline, warfarin, ciclosporin, furosemide, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, hormones, neuromuscular blockers, methadone, oral hypoglycemics, antidepressants, vitamin D."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P36.57). Adult suspension 125 mg/5 mL x 120 mL (P770.15)."
          }
        ],

        },

      "success": true,

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Diltiazem HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of unstable angina pectoris including angina due to coronary artery spasm or following myocardial infarction and hypertension (HTN). Management of chronic stable angina (classic effort-associated angina) in patients who cannot tolerate beta-blocks and/or nitrates or who remain symptomatic. Prevention of graft failure following kidney transplantation. Monotherapy or in combination with antihypertensives for treatment of HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IHD (exertional angina pectoris due to atherosclerotic coronary artery disease or angina pectoris at rest due to coronary artery spasm):</b> Initially 120 mg/day in divided doses, before meals and at bedtime, increased gradually in divided doses 2-4x daily at 1-2 day interval until optimum response is obtained. Optimum dose: 180-360 mg/day. Max 480 mg/day in some cases. <b>Hypertension:</b> Initially 120-240 mg/day in divided doses, before meals and at bedtime. Usual dose: 240-360 mg/day. <b>Kidney transplantation:</b> Initially 120 mg/day in two divided doses. May be increased to max 360 mg/day in three divided doses depending on patient’s BP. Optimum dose: 180-360 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Sick sinus syndrome and 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block, except in the presence of a functioning ventricular pacemaker. Hypotension (< 90 mmHg systolic). Acute MI. Pulmonary congestion. Concomitant use with lomitapide. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; CHF. Cardiac conduction, symptomatic hypotension, acute hepatic injury. Discontinue if dermatological reactions persist. Childn. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dizziness, 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block, sinus bradycardia, flushing, nausea, rash, joint swelling, asthenia, fatigue, edema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lomitapide, beta-blockers, ivabradine, H2-antagonists, digitalis, anesthetics, ciclosporin, carbamazepine, erythromycin, warfarin, rifampin, lithium, statins, sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "<b>Dilzem:</b> Tablet 30 mg, 60 mg. <b>Dilzem SA:</b> Tablet 90 mg. <b>Dilzem OD:</b> Sustained-release tablet 120 mg. <b>Dilzem SR:</b> Sustained-release tablet 180 mg."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of inflammatory manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses when complicated by secondary infections due to organisms sensitive to gentamicin such disorders include: psoriasis, contact dermatitis (dermatitis venenata), atopic dermatitis (infantile eczema, allergic dermatitis), neurodermatitis (lichen simplex chronicus), lichen planus, eczema (including nummular eczema, hand eczema, eczematous dermatitis), intertrigo, dyshidrosis (pompholyx), seborrheic dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, stasis dermatitis, anogenital and senile pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply twice daily, in the morning and at night."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for ophthalmic use; prolonged use.           },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute and chronic corticosteroid-responsive musculoskeletal and soft tissue conditions, allergic conditions, dermatological conditions, collagen diseases, neoplastic diseases, adrenogenital syndrome, ulcerative colitis, regional ileitis, sprue, podiatric conditions (for example, bursitis), blood dyscrasias, and nephrotic syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Systemic therapy</b>: 1-2 mL in most conditions and repeated as necessary. Administer as deep intramuscular injection in the gluteal region."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Intravenous or subcutaneous use. Systemic fungal infections, hypersensitivity, intramuscular administration in idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, and injection into unstable joints, infected areas, or intervertebral spaces. Immunization procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Dose adjustments in serious infection, surgery, or injury. Patients with ocular herpes simplex, existing emotional instability or psychotic tendencies, nonspecific ulcerative colitis, impending perforation, abscesses or pyogenic infection, diverticulitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, active or latent peptic ulcer, renal insufficiency, hypertension, osteoporosis, myasthenia gravis, hypothyroidism, tuberculosis. Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura. Pregnancy and lactation. <a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a> Category: C but D in the first trimester.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."

          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fluid and electrolyte disturbances, muscle weakness, muscle mass loss, tendon rupture, peptic ulcer, impaired wound healing, skin atrophy, convulsions, vertigo, headache, menstrual irregularities, posterior subcapsular cataracts, negative nitrogen balance, mood swings."

            "title": "Drug Interactions",

                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tremors, restlessness, anxiety, insomnia/sleeplessness, nervousness, dizziness, increased BP, palpitation, arrhythmia, weakness, respiratory distress, pallor. Sleepiness, drowsiness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sympathomimetics and general anesthesia; antidepressants; adrenergic-blocking agents; other medicines for cough, cold, or allergy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral drops 2.5 mg/0.5 mg per mL x 10 mL (P125.00). Syrup 5 mg/1 mg per 5 mL x 60 mL (P136.00), 120 mL (P203.75)."
          }
        ],

          {

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/1ANwUEbqBZNjBmyacQmYFng7H5NPcpjG7dvbx0cVBpYCBp6uCZ.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/RopOJDsGG4wPqVNNCAhwMhCdspSKxdG6OtJLaacEnPeeTnY4F2.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Hydrochlorothiazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Thiazide & Thiazide-like Diuretics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of edema associated with heart failure and renal and hepatic disorders; hypertension either as monotherapy or with other antihypertensives. Treatment of edema accompanying premenstrual syndrome. Prevention of water retention associated with corticosteroids and estrogens, treatment of diabetes insipidus, and prevention of renal calculus formation in patients with hypercalciuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer doses in the morning. <b>Edema:</b> 25-100 mg, up to 200 mg once daily in severe cases. Reduce dose daily or intermittently to 25-50 mg. <b>Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus:</b> Initial dose of up to 100 mg once daily. <b>HTN:</b> 25-50 mg once daily alone or with other antihypertensives. Initial dose of 12.5 mg may be sufficient."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with CrCl < 30 mL/min and severe renal impairment or anuria, Addison's disease, preexisting hypercalcemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment, existing fluid and electrolyte disturbances, severe heart failure. May precipitate attacks of gout in susceptible patients. Hyperglycemia and may aggravate or unmask DM. Patients with liver cirrhosis, taking digitalis or its glycosides. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Metabolic disturbances (high dose). Electrolyte imbalances and its signs (e.g. hypochloremic alkalosis, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia; hypomagnesemia). Anorexia, headache, dizziness, photosensitivity reactions, impotence, and yellow vision. Hypersensitivity reactions. Cholestatic jaundice, pancreatitis, and blood dyscrasias including thrombocytopenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Digitalis glycosides, astemizole, terfenadine, halofantrine, pimozide, sotalol. Competitive muscle relaxants. NSAIDs, corticosteroids, corticotropin, beta-2 antagonists (salbutamol), carbenoxolone, amphotericin B, or reboxetine, other antihypertensives, diuretic, barbiturates, opioids, norepinephrine, lithium salts, allopurinol, tetracycline, alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 12.5 mg (P4.80), 25 mg (P5.80)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YBvnc0emk3UQJGxtj75ZwmAePMnTGxVqtox92z7l7Y6iRgiEpd.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dobutamine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inotropic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "To increase contractility of heart in acute heart failure, as in cardiogenic shock and myocardial infarction. During cardiac surgery and positive and expiratory pressure ventilation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute heart failure:</b> 2.5-10 mcg/kg/min. Occasionally, 0.5-40 mcg/kg/min is required. <b>Alternative to exercise in cardiac stress testing:</b> 5 mcg/kg/min infused for 8 mins. Then increased by increments of 5-20 mcg/kg/min infused for 8 mins before the next incremental increase up to 40 mcg/kg/min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis, arrhythmias, marked ST segment depression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not mix with any alkaline solution. Monitor ECG, BP, pulmonary wedge pressure and cardiac output. Cardiogenic shock complicated by severe hypotension, hypovolemia. Correct hypovolemia before treatment. Pregnancy & Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased heart rate, BP, ventricular ectopic activity, angina or chest pain, palpitation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Nitroprusside, beta-blockers, general anesthetics, sodium bicarbonate or any alkaline solution."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 50 mg/mL x 5 mL (P607.87)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1248,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1248,
        "brand_name": "Docetax",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MdIVvRNoPQ2Q1c3JlkeHdlGelKj2jGoJ1swIWBXabe9Htb1Qzk.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/N1kFyIA0gJ7Cx29DKds0mfD9Z29lR28AX3CdN61ktHcm51EsCJ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TtPIgS4YbJZIM1e0mP71rZ4YValoIbwRE8XW1KIlHX7VMaaeyz.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Docetaxel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Taxanes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjuvant treatment of patients with operable, node-positive breast cancer in combination with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in patients who have not previously received cytotoxic chemotherapy in combination with doxorubicin, or after failure of anthracycline or alkylating agent-containing chemotherapy as monotherapy or in combination with capecitabine; metastatic breast cancer whose tumors overexpress HER2 and without prior chemotherapy in combination with trastuzumab. Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after failure of prior chemotherapy as monotherapy; unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC without prior chemotherapy in combination with cisplatin; metastatic ovarian cancer after failure of 1<sup>st</sup> line or subsequent therapy; androgen-independent (hormone-refractory) metastatic prostate cancer in combination with prednisone or prednisolone; metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma, including adenocarcinoma of gastroesophageal junction without prior chemotherapy in combination with cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU); recurrent and/or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN) after failure of previous chemotherapy as monotherapy. Induction treatment for locally advanced SCCHN in combination with cisplatin and 5-FU."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Premedicate all patients with oral corticosteroids (e.g. dexamethasone) 16 mg/day (i.e. 8 mg twice daily) for 5 days starting 1 day before docetaxel administration. <b>Adjuvant treatment of operable node-positive and negative breast cancer</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> after doxorubicin 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup> and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. <b>Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of prior chemotherapy</b> - Monotherapy: 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks. Combination therapy: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks with doxorubicin 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. <b>HER2 overexpressing breast cancer</b> - Combination therapy: 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks with trastuzumab administered weekly. <b>Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of prior anthracycline-containing chemotherapy</b> - Combination therapy: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks combined with capecitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice a day for 2 weeks followed by 1-week rest period. <b>NSCLC</b> - After failure of prior platinum-based chemotherapy: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks as single agent.  Patients who have not previously received chemotherapy: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> immediately followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 30-60 mins every 3 weeks. <b>Prostate cancer</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks. Administer oral prednisone/prednisolone 5 mg twice a day continuously from day 1 and through each cycle. Premedicate with oral dexamethasone 8 mg at 12, 3, and 1 hr before docetaxel infusion. <b>Gastric cancer</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as 1- to 3-hr IV infusion (both on day 1). Starting at the end of cisplatin infusion give 5-fluorouracil 750 mg/m<sup>2</sup> per day as a 24-hr continuous infusion for 5 days. Repeat treatment every 3 weeks. <b>SCCHN</b> – Induction chemotherapy followed by radiotherapy: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 1 hr (day 1) followed by 5-FU 750 mg/m<sup>2</sup> per day as continuous IV infusion for 5 days (day 1-5) initiated after cisplatin infusion. Regimen is administered every 3 weeks for 4 cycles. Radiotherapy should be received after completion of chemotherapy. Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> followed by cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as a 30-180 min IV infusion (day 1) followed by 5-FU 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> per day as continuous IV infusion for 4 days (days 1-4). Regimen is administered every 3 weeks for 3 cycles. Chemoradiotherapy should be received after chemotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to docetaxel or polysorbate 80. Neutrophil counts &lt;1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>. Patients under disulfiram treatment; with severe liver impairment. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Abnormal liver function. Patients with bilirubin &gt;ULN, AST and/or ALT &gt;1.5x ULN concomitant with AP &gt;2.5x ULN; severe fluid retention; at risk for treatment-related acute myeloid leukemia. Possible irreversible infertility (men). Elderly. Childn &lt;16 yrs. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. GI effects. CV effects. Fluid retention. Dermatologic effects. Neurologic, hepatic, musculoskeletal, respiratory, ophthalmic, and otic effects."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, terfenadine, ketoconazole, erythromycin, troleandomycin, doxorubicin, vinorelbine, vinblastine, and nifedipine. Dexamethasone, phenobarbital, and clofibrate. Topotecan. Trastuzumab, carboplatin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 20 mg/0.5 mL (P6,787.45), 80 mg/2 mL (P25,374.68)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3399,
          "name": "Bio-Onco, Inc."
        },

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of mild to moderate aches and pains due to dental pain; headache; muscular aches; common cold, flu, or sore throat; menstrual cramps; earache; pain after vaccination or surgery. Relief of inflammation from arthritis, non-serious arthritic conditions, and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (RA). For fever reduction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Recommended dose: 5-10 mg/kg BW/dose. <b>Pain and/or fever -</b> Childn 7-12 yrs: 10 mL; 3-6 yrs: 5-10 mL; 1-2 yrs: 5 mL. All doses given every 6-8 hrs. <b>Juvenile RA:</b> 7.5-12.5 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 doses/day. Shake well before use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with aspirin or other NSAIDs. Bronchospasm, angioedema, nasal polyps, or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs. Patients with stomach ulcers, bleeding, or other stomach problems (e.g. IBD). Severe heart, liver, or kidney (CrCl < 30 mL/min) disease. Conditions with increased tendency for active bleeding. Dehydration, SLE, dengue fever. Heart surgery (right before or after)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with heart problems, history of stroke. or at risk of these conditions; history of stomach, liver, or kidney problems; blood clotting disorder; asthma; connective tissue disease. Do not use for >3 days. Childn 12-18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Constipation, decreased appetite, diarrhea, dizziness, dyspepsia, otitis media, fever, fluid retention, bloating or flatulence, headache, heartburn, indigestion, itching, stomatitis, nausea, nervousness, rash, tinnitus, pharyngitis, stomach cramps or pain, swelling, vertigo, and vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aspirin and other NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, antacids, antihypertensives, diuretics, anticoagulants, thrombolytic agents, cardiac glycosides, cholestyramine, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, corticosteroids, SSRIs, antiplatelets, Ginkgo biloba, lithium, methotrexate, medicines affecting liver enzyme, antidiabetic agents, probenecid, quinolones, zidovudine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension 100 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P96.25)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Management of moderate to severe pain."
          },
          {

            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;16 yrs:</b> 1-2 tabs every 4-6 hrs as needed. Max 8 tabs daily. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min):</b> Dosing should not exceed 2 tabs every 12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotics, narcotics, centrally acting analgesics, opioids or psychotropics.           },

            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with history of anaphylactic reaction to codeine and other opioids. Patients with acute, severe bronchial asthma, risk of respiratory depression; sleep apnea; increased intracranial pressure or head injury. Patients who are CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolizers. Concomitant use with CNS depressants, including alcohol. History of substance abuse or mental illness. Drug dependence and potential for abuse. Severe hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/rZLiZMbNQ63ocIhBNBN4T0tELodpBxLLQyVdRwve3eAcypaWwI.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Mefenamic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx/Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic relief of mild to moderate pain including headache, dental pain, post-op and postpartum pain, primary dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia. Symptomatic relief of musculoskeletal and joint disorders including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents &gt;14 yrs - 250 mg</b>: 1-2 tabs every 8 hrs as needed; <b>500 mg</b>: 1 tab every  8 hrs as needed. <b>Relief of dysmenorrhea and premenstrual syndrome - 250 mg</b>: 1-2 tabs every 8 hrs while symptoms persist (\"period pains\" and other associated symptoms). Do not take for &gt;7 days unless directed by a doctor; <b>500 mg</b>: 1 tab every 8 hrs while symptoms persist (\"period pains\" and other associated symptoms). Do not take for &gt;10 days unless directed by a doctor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to mefenamic acid, aspirin, or any other NSAIDs. Currently taking aspirin or other  NSAIDs. Bronchospasm, asthma, angioedema, urticaria, nasal polyps or allergic-type reaction after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs. History of stomach ulcers, bleeding, or perforation, or other stomach problems e.g. IBS. Severe heart, liver or kidney disease. Recurrence of diarrhea. Bleeding in the brain or other bleeding disorders. Hyperkalemia. Dengue fever. Right before or after heart surgery.  Childn and adolescents &lt;14 yrs. Pregnancy (last trimester) and lactation. <b>500 mg</b>: Treatment of peri op pain in CABG surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "<b>250 mg</b>: May cause severe allergic reaction or severe stomach bleeding. Long-term use may increase risk of heart attack or stroke. Elderly suffering from dehydration and kidney disease. <b>500 mg</b>: Patients with CV disease or risk factors for CV disease, IHD (e.g. MI, and/or angina),  cerebrovascular disease (e.g. stroke, CVA, TIA and/or amaurosis fugax), and/or CHF, SLE and mixed connective tissue disorder, epilepsy. Risk for serious GI events in elderly patients. Frail or debilitated patients. Elderly with impaired renal, hepatic, and cardiac function. Patients with hypertension, fluid retention or heart failure, history of GI disease. Not a substitute for corticosteroids. Long-term use may result in renal papillary necrosis and other renal injury. Can cause serious skin adverse effects, e.g. SJS and TEN; worsens headaches if prolonged use. Borderline elevations of 1 or more liver tests. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, gross bleeding/perforation, heartburn, nausea, GI ulcers (gastric/duodenal), vomiting, abnormal kidney function, anemia, dizziness, edema, elevated liver enzymes, headache, increased bleeding time, pruritus, rashes and ringing in the ears (tinnitus)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aspirin, salicylates or other NSAIDs (e.g. ketorolac, ibuprofen, naproxen) including COX-2 inhibitors (e.g. celecoxib, etoricoxib). Corticosteroid, SSRI and antiplatelet agents (e.g. clopidogrel, cilostazol). Aminoglycosides (e.g. amikacin, gentamicin, neomycin, tobramycin). Antacids (e.g. magnesium hydroxide). Antihypertensives (e.g. ACEIs, ARBs, and diuretics). Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin). Cardiac glycosides (e.g. digoxin). Ciclosporin and tacrolimus. Lithium and methotrexate. Medicines affecting liver enzymes. Oral hypoglycemic agents, sulfonylureas (e.g. gliclazide, glipizide, glimepiride). Mifepristone. Probenecid. Quinolone antibiotics. Zidovudine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 250 mg (P17.64), 500 mg (Rx) (P33.96)."
          }

        "content": "Methyldopa",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Centrally-Acting Antihypertensives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Initially 250 mg 2-3x a day in the 1<sup>st</sup> 48 hrs, then adjust daily dose depending on response. Start dose increase in the evening to minimize sedation. Maintenance: 0.5-2 g/day in 2-4 divided doses. Max 3 g/day. <b>Elderly</b>: Initially 125 mg 2x a day then increase slowly. Max 2 g/day. <b>Childn</b>: Initially 10 mg/kg in 2-4 divided doses. Max 650 mg/kg or 3 g/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute hepatitis and active cirrhosis, liver disorders previously associated with methyldopa therapy, pheochromocytoma. Patients taking MAOIs. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of previous liver disease or dysfunction, severely impaired kidney, history of hemolytic anemia, parkinsonism, mental depression, porphyria, cerebral atherosclerosis. Perform blood counts, Coombs’ test and liver function test before initial therapy and at periodic intervals. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Contains FD& C yellow #5 (tartrazine) that may cause allergic reaction.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sialoadenitis, blood and lymphatic system disorders, hyperprolactinemia, psychic disturbances, reversible mild psychoses, or depression, decreased libido, nervous system disorders, bradycardia, angina pectoris, myocarditis, pericarditis, AV block, orthostatic hypotension, nasal congestion, GI disorders, liver disorders, rash, TEN, lupus-like syndrome, mild arthralgia, breast enlargement, gynecomastia, amenorrhea, lactation disorder, erectile dysfunction, ejaculation failure, asthenia and edema (weight gain)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other antihypertensives, anesthetics, lithium, MAOIs, amphetamines, other CNS stimulants, TCAs, iron hematinic, and oral contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 250 mg (P17.64)."
          }

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Prokinetic Drugs & Antiflatulents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Short-term treatment of nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, esophageal reflux, reflux esophagitis, gastritis, speeding barium transit in follow-through radiological studies, and diabetic gastroparesis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Nausea and vomiting - Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs (weighing &ge;35):</b> 10 mg, max: 3x daily. <b>Symptomatic management of non-ulcer dyspepsia:</b> 10 mg, max: 4x daily. Max duration: 1 week. Taken 15-30 mins before meals. <b>Renal impairment:</b> 1-2x daily depending on the severity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. QTc-prolonging drugs. Patients with existing prolongation of cardiac conduction intervals, significant electrolyte disturbances, bradycardia, or cardiac diseases. Do not use when GI stimulation might be dangerous (e.g. GI hemorrhage, obstruction, perforation, or immediately after surgery). Neonates."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Chronic use or routine prophylaxis of post-op nausea and vomiting. Elderly with cardiac disease history. Increased risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death especially in patients >60 yrs, patients taking >30 mg daily, and concomitant use with QT-prolonging drugs or CYP3A4 inhibitors. Discontinue treatment when signs and symptoms associated with cardiac arrhythmia occur. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Galactorrhea, breast enlargement and soreness, reduced libido. Dry mouth, thirst, headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Bromocriptine, antimuscarinics, opioid analgesics, levodopa, CYP3A4 inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P11.75)."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/s3JHpuzS9zGHC1TlbRyHcmM2tr6SV7H41AAwguPKtXHu59NDji.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Doxycycline hyclate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Tetracyclines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Sexually transmitted diseases (STD), urinary tract infections (UTI), respiratory tract infections (RTI), gastrointestinal tract (GIT) infections, systemic infections, infections caused by <i>E. coli, Enterobacter aerogenes, Shigella</i> spp. and <i>Acinetobacter </i> spp.; as alternative to penicillin for uncomplicated gonorrhea, syphilis, yaws, listeriosis, anthrax, Vincent's infection, actinomycosis infections caused by <i>Clostridium</i> spp. Adjunctive therapy in acute intestinal amebiasis, severe acne, refractory periodontitis and periodontal abscess. Prophylaxis of malaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs on 1<sup>st</sup> day. Maintenance 100 mg/day once daily. <b>Management of more severe infections (chronic UTI)</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs. <b>STD (Chlamydial cervicitis)</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. <b>Early syphilis for non-pregnant patients allergic to penicillin</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 14 days. <b>Syphilis of &gt;1 yr duration in patients allergic to penicillin</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 4 weeks. <b>Uncomplicated gonococcal infections</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs or 300 mg immediately followed in 1 hr by a second 300 mg. Duration: 7 days. <b>Uncomplicated urethral, endocervical, or rectal infection, non-gonococcal urethritis</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. <b>Acute epididymo-orchitis</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs for at least 10 days. <b>Acne vulgaris</b>: 100 mg once daily for 12 weeks. <b>Traveler's diarrhea</b>: 200 mg (as single dose or 100 mg every 12 hrs) on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of travel followed by 100 mg daily throughout stay in the area. <b>Cholera</b>: 300 mg as single dose (treatment and prophylaxis). <b>Leptospirosis</b> – Treatment: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days; Prophylaxis: 200 mg on weekly basis throughout stay in the area and 200 mg upon completion of the trip. <b>Tick and louse-borne relapsing fevers and louse-borne typhus</b>: Single dose of 100 or 200 mg depending on severity. Prophylaxis of scrub typhus: 200 mg as single dose. <b>Malaria</b> – Treatment of chloroquine-resistant of falciparum malaria: 200 mg daily for at least 7 days; Prophylaxis: 100 mg daily 1-2 days before travel to malarious areas, continue daily during travel in these areas and 4 weeks after leaving said areas. <b>Refractory periodontitis in adults and periodontal abscess (if allergic to beta-lactam)</b>: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Myasthenia gravis. SLE. Infants and childn &lt;8 yrs (except for use as an alternative treatment for inhalational anthrax post-exposure). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May cause permanent teeth discoloration, esophageal irritation and ulceration, increase in BUN, photosensitivity, tissue hyperpigmentation, autoimmune syndromes, bulging fontanelles in infants, porphyria, superinfections; Fanconi-like syndrome, lupus erythematosus-like syndrome with use of deteriorated tetracyclines. <i>C. difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Patients with obstructive esophagic pathology. Avoid exposure to direct sunlight during treatment. Use for treatment of venereal disease. Hepatic impairment. Periodic assessment of organ system functions is recommended during prolonged therapy. Long-term or repeated use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms e.g. fungi. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",

        "content": "Doxorubicin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anthracycline Antibiotics in Chemotherapy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute lymphoblastic leukemia and acute myelogenous leukemia. Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the breast, bladder carcinoma, bronchogenic carcinoma and neuroblastoma. Metastatic thyroid carcinoma. Carcinoma of the endometrium, testes, prostate, cervix, head and neck, and plasma-cell myeloma. Active against carcinoma of the ovary when administered with cisplatin and cyclophosphamide. Administered for carcinoma of the breast and small (oat)-cell carcinoma of the lung with other cytotoxic drugs. Wide range of sarcomas including osteogenic, Ewing’s and soft-tissue sarcoma. Hodgkin’s disease in combination with ABVD. Non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas in combination with BACOP."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Single agent</b>: 60-75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as single IV injection at 21-day intervals. <b>Combination with other chemotherapy drugs</b>: 40-60 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as single IV injection every 21-28 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Persistent myelosuppression, hepatic impairment, myocardial insufficiency, recent MI, severe arrythmias. Previous treatment with max cumulative doses of doxorubicin, daunorubicin, epirubicin, idarubicin, and/or other anthracyclines and anthracenediones. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients should recover from acute toxicities of prior cytotoxic treatment before beginning treatment. Do not mix with heparin and other medicines. Use of contraceptives are advised. Hepatic impairment. Myelosuppression. May cause amenorrhea, oligospermia or azoospermia. Monitor serum total bilirubin.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "ECG abnormalities, sinus tachycardia, tachyarrhythmias, AV and bundle branch block, asymptomatic reductions in LVEF, CHF; leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, hemorrhage, neutropenia, nausea, vomiting, mucositis, stomatitis, esophagitis, abdominal pain, diarrhea, anorexia, dehydration, alopecia, local toxicity, rash or itch, skin changes, red coloration of urine, malaise, asthenia, fever, infection, sepsis or septicemia, chills, shock."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IV) 50 mg."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/BJekWcrJ4iIkjJEicOCsqMvXlzElIdc8G7gNnrgKbChzQpATiP.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/8uG4yY1AqaFqldJnjW4c5nnm3doWZDklpppFMdrjKbRxBVenbQ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Doxycycline hyclate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Tetracyclines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of the following infections: Rocky Mountain spotted fever, typhus fever, Q fever, rickettsial pox, and tick fevers; respiratory tract infections (RTI); lymphogranuloma venereum; psittacosis; trachoma; inclusion conjunctivitis; uncomplicated urethral, endocervical, or rectal infections; non-gonococcal urethritis; relapsing fever; chancroid, plague, tularemia, cholera, <i>Campylobacter fetus</i> infections, brucellosis, bartonellosis, granuloma inguinale; urinary tract infections (UTI); anthrax. Infections caused by <i>Escherichia coli</i>, <i>Enterobacter aerogenes</i>, <i>Shigella</i> spp., <i>Acinetobacter</i> spp. As alternative treatment to uncomplicated gonorrhea, syphilis, yaws, listeriosis, Vincent’s infection, actinomycosis, and infections caused by <i>Clostridium</i> spp., when penicillin is contraindicated. As adjunct to amebicides in acute intestinal amebiasis; severe acne."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 100 mg every 12 hrs on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment, followed by a maintenance dose of 100 mg/day; more severe infections: 100 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Uncomplicated gonococcal infections (except anorectal infections in men):</b> 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. Alternative single visit dose: 300 mg stat, followed by 300 mg 2<sup>nd</sup> dose after 1 hr. <b>Uncomplicated urethral, endocervical, or rectal infection, nongonococcal urethritis caused by <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>:</b> 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Syphilis</b> - Early: 100 mg twice daily for 2 weeks; More than 1 yr duration: 100 mg twice daily for 4 weeks. <b>Acute epididymo-orchitis caused by <i>N. gonorrhea</i> and <i>C. gonorrhea</i>:</b> 100 mg twice daily for at least 10 days. <b>Prophylaxis of malaria:</b> 100 mg daily beginning 1-2 days before travel, continued daily during travel and for 4 weeks after. <b>Inhalational anthrax:</b> 100 mg twice daily for 60 days. <b>Childn weighing < 45 kg</b> - Severe or life-threatening infections: 2.2 mg/kg every 12 hrs; less severe disease: 4.4 mg/kg given in 2 doses on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, followed by a maintenance dose of 2.2 mg/kg. <b>Prophylaxis of malaria:</b> 2 mg/kg once daily beginning 1-2 days before travel, continued daily during travel and for 4 weeks after. <b>Inhalational anthrax:</b> 2.2 mg/kg twice daily for 60 days. <b>&ge;45 kg:</b> Adult dose. Should be given with plenty of fluids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May result in overgrowth of non susceptible organisms, including fungi. Avoid excessive sunlight or artificial UV light exposure. Not used to treat viral infections. Perform laboratory evaluation of organ systems, including hematopoietic, renal, and hepatic studies, periodically. Concomitant use of isotretinoin. Absorption is reduced when taken with calcium, bismuth subsalicylate. Childn &le;8 yrs. Women of childbearing age. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI, and skin effects, renal toxicity, immune system. Hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, eosinophilia. Bulging fontanels in infants; intracranial HTN in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, penicillin; antacids containing aluminum, calcium, or magnesium, and iron-containing preparations; bismuth subsalicylate; barbiturates, carbamazepine, phenytoin; methoxyflurane; oral contraceptives. May interfere with fluorescence test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P17.50)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3490,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3490,
        "brand_name": "Drenex",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0NP1kN9Zp6NyPy3xxCWvatqHIbG8EIrKIwTcRUXuCtpjFJvDfG.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cPHS2vhzdIkoRLjKZWTLvCNTJHPSKKri5E0vrBTI8Kp7YQBOTM.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5TM00ipBu2D6hDZYhLj2oklOjtpMSGkD6B6rJy7cQVKebPsQ79.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dexamethasone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of cerebral edema associated with primary or metastatic brain tumor, craniotomy, or head injury; endocrine, dermatologic, ophthalmic, respiratory, hematologic, neoplastic, and GI diseases; tuberculosis (TB) meningitis with subarachnoid or impending block when used concurrently with appropriate anti-TB chemotherapy, acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis, trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement. Control of severe or incapacitating allergic conditions intractable to adequate trials of conventional treatment. Adjunct therapy for short-term administration in rheumatic disorders. Treatment of exacerbation or maintenance of collagen diseases. Palliative management of leukemias and lymphomas in adults. Induction of diuresis or remission or proteinuria in nephrotic syndrome, with or without uremia of the idiopathic type, or that due to lupus erythematosus. Diagnostic testing of adrenocortical hyperfunction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 0.75-9 mg/day. <b>Childn:</b> 0.02-0.3 mg/kg/day given in 2-4 divided doses. <b>Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis:</b> 30 mg daily for 1 week, then 4-12 mg every other day for 1 month. <b>Acute, self-limited allergic disorders or acute exacerbations of chronic disorders -</b> Day 1: 4-8 mg IM; Days 2-3: 3 mg orally in 2 divided doses; Day 4: 1.5 mg orally in 2 divided doses; Days 5-6: 0.75 mg orally once daily. <b>Cerebral edema:</b> 1-3 mg thrice daily as a replacement for parenteral dexamethasone. <b>Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting -</b> Low emetic risk: 8 mg as a single dose before chemotherapy on day 1; Moderate emetic risk: 8 mg single IV dose before chemotherapy on day 1, then 8 mg once daily on days 2-3 without aprepitant, or 12 mg as a single dose before chemotherapy on day 1 with aprepitant; High emetic risk: 12 mg as a single dose before chemotherapy on day 1, then 8 mg once daily on days 2-4. <b>Suppression Test - Test for Cushing's syndrome:</b> 1 mg at 11 PM, then blood is extracted for plasma cortisol determination at 8 AM the following morning or 0.5 mg every 6 hrs for 2 days, then determine urine-free cortisol and 17-hydroxycorticosteroid excretion. <b>Test for distinguishing Cushing's syndrome due to pituitary ACTH excess from Cushing's syndrome due to other causes:</b> 2 mg every 6 hrs for 2 days then 24-hr urine-free cortisol and 17-hydroxycorticosteroid excretion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections, GI ulcer, osteoporosis, DM, HTN, acute or chronic infections. Concomitant use with prophylactic immunization. Patients with renal impairment or history of psychotic illness. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with adrenal insufficiency; hypothyroidism, cirrhosis; latent TB or tuberculin reactivity; HTN, CHF, renal impairment, MI; myasthenia gravis, peptic ulcer, diverticulitis, recent intestinal anastomoses, nonspecific ulcerative colitis; postmenopausal stage; debilitated patients. Concomitant use with live, live attenuated (including smallpox vaccine), killed or inactivated vaccines. Kaposi's sarcoma; increased susceptibility to or may mask symptoms of infections; posteriour subcapsular and nuclear cataracts (particularly in childn), exophthalmos, increased IOP; edema, potassium loss, hypokalemic alkalosis, HTN, CHF; acute myopathy, mental disturbances, aggravation of emotional instability of psychotic tendencies; peptic ulcer; protein catabolism. Elderly. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Decreased carbohydrate tolerance, development of cushingoid state, glycosuria, hirsutism, hyperglycemia, increased requirements for insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents in diabetes, manifestations of latent DM, menstrual irregularities, secondary adrenocortical and pituitary unresponsiveness, growth suppression in childn, CHF, fluid retention, HTN, hypokalemic alkalosis, potassium loss, sodium retention, bradycardia; cardiac arrest, arrhythmia, or enlargement; circulatory collapse, fat embolism, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in premature infants, myocardial rupture following recent MI, edema, pulmonary edema, syncope, tachycardia, thromboembolism, thrombophlebitis, vasculitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Barbiturates, phenytoin, ephedrine, carbamazepine, rifampicin; CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, macrolides); indinavir, erythromycin, and other CYP3A4-metabolized drugs; oral contraceptives and estrogen; aspirin; warfarin; potassium-depleting agents (e.g. diuretics, amphotericin B; anticholinesterase agents; antacids; insulin, oral antidiabetic agents; thalidomide; indomethacin; aminoglutethimide; cholestyramine; ciclosporin; digitalis glycosides; ephedrine; toxoids, live or inactivated vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 3 mg (P30.25)."
          }

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xMbuCoIf6Bz7rNDiUhT4F75godj01OIjWXSn5Lwmaaa41jEuTB.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/N6WdKc4O0zE86EpnVJc3EJWRQKl1vBb7k9gSLxaLRD36NWGJqQ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wjnHvRXRWlkhByYhP1YF986aJNlBpL19mPveQcpxqybroLzOVm.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ipratropium bromide, salbutamol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticholinergic Anti-Asthmatic & COPD Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of reversible bronchospasm associated with obstructive airway diseases (e.g. bronchial asthma). Adjunct in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on a regular inhaled bronchodilator who continue to have evidence of bronchospasm and who require a 2<sup>nd</sup> bronchodilator."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults, including elderly, and adolescents >12 yrs -</b> Usual dose: 1 pulmoneb every 6-8 hrs; Treatment of acute attacks: 1 pulmoneb for prompt symptom relief, may be increased to 2 pulmonebs in severe cases; Maintenance: 1 pulmoneb. <b>Childn 2-12 yrs:</b> 3 drops/kg/dose. Max 2.5 mg every 6-8 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy or tachyarrhythmia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not mix with other drugs in the same nebulizer. Patients with cystic fibrosis; narrow-angle glaucoma; CV disorders including coronary insufficiency, cardiac arrhythmias or HTN; convulsive disorders; hyperthyroidism; DM; unusually responsive to sympathomimetic amines; prostatic hypertrophy, bladder-neck obstruction; hepatic or renal disease; severe airway obstruction where concomitant therapy with steroid, xanthine derivatives, or diuretics may result in hypokalemia. Cardiac arrest following severe, acute asthmatic crisis and hypoxia; paradoxical bronchospasm; increased IOP, angle-closure glaucoma; temporary pupillary dilation, narrow-angle glaucoma, eye pain or discomfort, blurred vision, visual halos or colored images in association with red eyes from conjunctival and corneal congestion. May interfere with uterine contraction during labor and delivery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Ipratropium:</b> Increased risk of mortality and/or CV events. <b>Salbutamol:</b> Decreased plasma potassium concentrations.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngeal or respiratory, CV neurological, GI, endocrine or metabolic, musculoskeletal, connective tissue and bone disorder, dermatologic, ophthalmic, GUT, and otic effects. Viral infection, local irritation, unusual taste/taste perversion, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic agents, non-potassium-sparing diuretics. <b>Ipratropium:</b> Anticholinergics. <b>Salbutamol:</b> Beta-blockers, MAOIs, TCAs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for nebulization 500 mcg/2.5 mg per 2.5 mL (P47.75)."
          }
        ],
