  {
    "id": 603,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 603,
        "brand_name": "Cipromet",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7Ufoy3TClLjSweHDbVa7jiRtFwOe9EFWtIkwJljhODW6JwX1au.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cyRgoIntmmWKQtLWHQ1CTLfgH41fO58FsdA4tIQmCBkrfXpIxL.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YHo2aLwFDHG8Dbv3X2WZQ6fxy4tlDuhKLHKRdTEk0IQkg7gEPh.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ciprofloxacin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Uncomplicated and complicated infections caused by ciprofloxacin sensitive pathogens. Infections of respiratory tract, urinary tract, abdominal cavity, diarrhea & typhoid fever, middle ear (otitis media), paranasal sinuses (sinusitis), eyes, kidneys and urinary tract, genital organs (adnexitis, gonorrhea, prostatitis), abdominal cavity, skin and soft tissues, bones, and joints. Sepsis, infections in patients with reduced host defense and selective intestinal decontamination in immunosuppressed patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Infections of the kidneys, urinary tract, and abdominal cavity:</b> 250-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days. <b>Infections of the respiratory tract, bone and joints, skin and soft tissues:</b> 500-750 mg twice daily. <b>Infectious diarrhea and typhoid fever, otitis media, sinusitis, bacterial prostatitis:</b> 500 mg twice daily. <b>Acute uncomplicated gonorrhea and cystitis:</b> 250 mg single dose. <b>Other infections:</b> 500 mg twice daily for 7-14 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn and adolescents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Severe and persistent diarrhea during or after treatment may mask symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis. Patients with epilepsy and history of CNS disorders. May cause tendinitis; elderly previously treated with glucocorticoids. Photosensitivity; avoid direct exposure to excessive sunlight or UV. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, headache, restlessness, rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Iron, sucralfate, antacids or highly buffered drugs (e.g. antiretrovirals) containing magnesium, aluminum or calcium. Theophylline, ciclosporin, warfarin, glibenclamide, probenecid, metoclopramide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P39.58)."
          }
        ],

          "name": "Metro Pharma Philippines, Inc."

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Treatment of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) due to G(-) bacteria e.g. exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), broncho-pulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis or in bronchiectasis, pneumonia; URTI e.g. chronic suppurative otitis media; acute exacerbation of chronic sinusitis; urinary tract infections (UTI); genital tract infections e.g. epididymo-orchitis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID); infections of the GIT (e.g. traveler’s diarrhea); intra-abdominal infections; infections of the skin and soft tissue; malignant external otitis; infections of bone and joints; inhalation anthrax (post-exposure prophylaxis and curative treatment). Management of neutropenic patients with fever due to bacterial infection. <b>Childn and adolescents</b>: Broncho-pulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis; complicated UTI and pyelonephritis; inhalation anthrax (post-exposure prophylaxis and curative treatment)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – LRTI, URTI</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-14 days. <b>Malignant external otitis</b>: 400 mg 3x daily for 28 days up to 3 months. <b>UTI – Complicated and uncomplicated pyelonephritis</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-21 days. <b>Prostatitis</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 2-4 weeks (acute). <b>Epididymo-orchitis and PID</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for at least 14 days. <b>GIT and intra-abdominal infections – Diarrhea caused by <i>Shigella</i> spp. and severe traveler’s diarrhea</b>: 400 mg twice daily for 1 day. <b>By <i>Shigella dysenteriae</i></b>: 400 mg twice daily for 5 days. <b>By <i>Vibrio cholerae</i></b>: 400 mg twice daily for 3 days. <b>Typhoid fever</b>: 400 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Intra-abdominal infections due to G(-)</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 5-14 days. <b>Infections of the skin and soft tissue</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-14 days. <b>Bone and joint infections</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for max 3 months. <b>Neutropenic patients with fever suspected to be due to bacterial infections</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily continued over the entire period of neutropenia. <b>Inhalation anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis</b>: 400 mg twice daily for 60 days (from <i>B. anthracis</i> exposure). <b>Childn – Cystic fibrosis</b>: 10 mg/kg BW thrice daily for 10-14 days. Max 400 mg. <b>Complicated UTI and pyelonephritis</b>: 6-10 mg/kg thrice daily for 10-21 days. Max 400 mg. <b>Inhalation anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis</b>: 10-15 mg/kg twice daily for 60 days (from <i>B. anthracis</i> exposure). Max 400 mg. <b>Renal impairment</b> – CrCl 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 200-400 mg every 12 hrs. &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 200-400 mg every 24 hrs. <b>Hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis</b>: 200-400 mg every 24 hrs (after dialysis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant administration of tizanidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not suited for treatment of severe and mixed infections with G(+) and anaerobic pathogens, streptococcal infections (e.g. <i>S. pneumoniae</i>). Patients with history of tendon disease/disorder related to quinolone treatment; myasthenia gravis. Patients with family history of aneurysm disease, or diagnosed with pre-existing aortic aneurysm and/or dissection (e.g. Marfan syndrome, vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Takayasu arteritis, giant cell arteritis, Behcet’s disease, HTN, known atherosclerosis). Avoid direct exposure to either extensive sunlight or UV irradiation during treatment. Patients with known risk factors for prolongation of QT interval. Concomitant use of drugs known to prolong QT interval e.g. Class IA and III anti-arrhythmic, TCAs, macrolides, antipsychotics). Uncorrected electrolyte imbalance (e.g. hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), cardiac disease (e.g. heart failure, MI, bradycardia). May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, transient increase in transaminases, rash, injection and infusion site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs known to prolong QT interval, probenecid, tizanidine, methotrexate, theophylline, caffeine or pentoxifylline (oxpentifylline), phenytoin, ciclosporin, vit K antagonists, ropinirole, lidocaine, clozapine, sildenafil, zolpidem."
          },

Max 750 mg/dose. <b>Renal impairment</b> – CrCl 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs. &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs. Patients on hemodialysis: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs (after dialysis). Patients on peritoneal dialysis: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs."

Treatment of advanced transitional cell bladder cancer in combination with cisplatin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion over 30 mins but not more than 60 mins and not more frequent than once a week. <b>Adults - Ovarian cancer</b>: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; carboplatin should be administered after, on day 1 consistent with a target AUC of 4 mg/mL/min. <b>Breast cancer</b>: Gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered on day 1 over approximately 3 hrs as IV infusion before the administration of gemcitabine. <b>NSCLC – Monotherapy</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> repeated once a week for 3 weeks, followed by a 1-week rest period. The 4-week cycle is then repeated. <b>Combination therapy - 3-week schedule</b>: Gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV administered on day 1 after gemcitabine infusion. <b>4-week schedule</b>: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 21-day cycle; cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV administered on day 1 after gemcitabine infusion. <b>Pancreatic cancer</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> repeated once a week for up to 7 weeks, followed by a 1-week rest period. Subsequent cycles should consist of injection once a week for 3 consecutive weeks out of every 4 weeks. <b>Bladder cancer – Monotherapy</b>: 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle. This 4-week cycle is then repeated. <b>Combination therapy</b>: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle; cisplatin 70 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered on day 1 following gemcitabine or day 2 of each 28-day cycle.             "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver function. Impaired renal function. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Rifampicin</b>: Hepatic impairment, pre-existing liver disease, alcoholics and hyperbilirubinemia.             "content": "<b>Rifampicin</b>: Facial flushing, itching, rash. Flu syndrome of fever, chills, bone pains, shortness of breath and malaise. GI disorders. Pseudomembranous colitis.           },

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of mild to moderately severe pain, with or without accompanied inflammation (e.g. musculoskeletal trauma, post-op pain and post-dental extraction, pain associated with post-partum cramping, and dysmenorrhea)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Rheumatic disorders:</b> 550-1,100 mg as single dose or in 2 divided doses. <b>Dysmenorrhea and acute musculoskeletal disorders:</b> 550 mg initially, then 275 mg every 6-8 hrs. Max: 1,375 mg/day after the 1st day. <b>Acute gout:</b> 825 mg initially, then 275-500 mg every 8 hrs. <b>Migraine:</b> 825 mg, may be followed by 275-550 mg after at least &frac12; hr.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to aspirin or other NSAIDs. History of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF (NYHA Class II-IV). Previous or active peptic ulceration. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with cardiac, liver, and renal disease. Temporarily discontinue therapy 48 hrs before adrenal function tests. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal discomfort, epigastric distress, headache, nausea, vertigo, tinnitus, peripheral edema."
          },
          {

            "content": "Hydantoins, anticoagulants, sulfonylureas, furosemide, beta-blockers, probenecid, methotrexate."

            "content": "Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs: 2 inhalations twice daily."

          {

          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with pulmonary TB, severe CV disease disorders (e.g. heart rhythm abnormalities), DM, untreated hypokalemia or thyrotoxicosis, history of DM.             "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."

  {
    "id": 4488,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4488,
        "brand_name": "Forgram",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/BxtlnVACZALBKFsE9hydpW7qf69MueqqiuKRUaY0NapueqLnjq.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/PLITde29B2xkmSyaZoxBa5OercIMb4usMNgryGriPga45woWkp.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Mmc4NL92a9bYs3U4Av5vxdZW3sNqRd6CbWxK9daSiTEKodUusl.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ceftriaxone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of the following infections due to susceptible organisms: lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) including pneumonia; acute bacterial otitis media; skin and skin structure infections, complicated and uncomplicated urinary tract infections; uncomplicated cervical/urethral, pharyngeal, and rectal uncomplicated gonorrhea; pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), bacterial septicemia, bone and joint infections, intraabdominal infections (e.g. peritonitis, infections of the biliary and gastrointestinal tracts), meningitis. Peri-op prophylaxis for the reduction of post-op infections in patients undergoing contaminated or potentially contaminated surgical procedures and in patients for whom infection at the operative site would pose a serious risk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via IV injection for 2-4 mins, IM injection, or IV infusion for 30 mins (doses >50 mg/kg). <b>Adults:</b> 1-2 g once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Max 4 g/day; <b>LRTI including pneumonia:</b> 1 g IV once or twice daily in combination with other anti-infectives; <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 250 mg IM single dose; <b>PID:</b> 250 mg IM single dose, followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, with or without oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily; <b>Surgical prophylaxis:</b> 1 g IV single dose, administered &frac12;-2 hrs before surgery; For cholecystectomy: 1-2 g IV single dose, administered &frac12;-2 hrs before surgery; <b>Meningitis:</b> 2 g IV twice daily for 7- 21 days. <b>Renal and hepatic impairment:</b> Max 2 g/day. <b>Childn -</b> >12 yrs weighing >50 kg: Adult dose. Childn and infants 15 days-12 yrs: 20-80 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Neonates &le;14 days: 20-50 mg/kg IV for 60 mins once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. <b>Childn and neonates &le;12 yrs - Skin and skin structure infections:</b> 50-75 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Max 2 g/day; <b>Acute bacterial otitis media:</b> 50 mg/kg IM single dose. Max 1 g; <b>Serious infections other than meningitis:</b> 50-75 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses twice daily. Max 2 g/day; <b>Meningitis:</b> 100 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily for 7-21 days. Max 4 g/day. Childn < 50 kg with uncomplicated gonococcal vulvovaginitis, cervicitis, urethritis, epididymitis, pharyngitis, or proctitis: Single 125 mg IM. <b>Treatment duration -</b> Usual: 4-14 days. Complicated infections may require longer treatment; Most infections except gonorrhea: At least 48-72 hrs after the patient becomes asymptomatic or evidence of bacterial eradication has been obtained; Infections caused by <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i>: At least 10 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Neonates (especially premature) with hyperbilirubinemia or jaundice. Infants &le;28 days who require or expected to require treatment with calcium-containing IV solns, including continuous calcium-containing infusions (e.g. parenteral nutrition)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics. Patients with history of cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia; history of GI disease, particularly colitis; renal or hepatic impairment, poor nutritional state; those receiving a protracted course of antimicrobials or previously stabilized on anticoagulants. Concomitant use with calcium-containing IV solns, including continuous calcium-containing infusions (e.g. parenteral nutrition). Gallbladder disease including sonographic abnormalities; seizures; fall in prothrombin activity may occur. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms. Monitor blood levels of patients with severe renal impairment and those with both renal and hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>IM:</b> Do not inject >1 g at a single site.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

          },
          {

            "content": "Patients with hepatic and moderate renal impairment, active or recent urolithiasis; episodes of transient orthostatic hypotension.           },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wnb6Q1KlX0JFOQug022c0zCTmCfJ430BGS07wvMxkmqMp4udjc.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Q7AyME4jvlS4z391I6Rb282KGrGNrLRXQWykxLmwtgvUenaOwn.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fluorouracil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of advanced colorectal carcinoma, alone or in combination with leucovorin. As an adjunct to surgery in women with breast cancer, in combination chemotherapy. Management of gastric, primary hepatic, pancreatic, uterine (particularly cervical), ovarian, and bladder cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IV injection</b>: Initially 12 mg/kg once a day for 4 consecutive days, then 6 mg/kg on days 6, 8, 10, and 12 unless toxic reaction occurs before then; no therapy on days 5, 7, 9, and 11. Discontinue on day 12 even if no toxicity occurs. Alternatively, 15 mg/kg as single IV injection once a week throughout the course. Max 800 mg/day. <b>IV infusion</b>: 15 mg/kg (but not &gt;1 g per infusion) diluted in 500 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose given once daily at a rate of 40 drops/min over 4 hrs. Infusion may be repeated on successive days until first GI or hematological side effects appear or a total of 12-15 g has been given. Alternatively, daily dose may be infused over 30-60 mins or given as continuous IV infusion over 24 hrs. <b>Intra-arterial infusion</b>: 5-7.5 mg/kg/day administered as a 24-hr continuous drip infusion. <b>Maintenance therapy</b>: Repeat initial therapy at intervals of 30 days after the last dose of the previous course. Alternatively, 10-15 mg/kg once a week when toxicity from the initial course of therapy has subsided. Max 1 g weekly. <b>Combination therapy with leucovorin</b>: 9-10 mg/kg for 5 days after leucovorin 5-12 mg/kg for 5 days. Repeat course every 4 weeks. <b>For poor-risk patients</b> - IV injection: Initially 6 mg/kg once a day for 3 days, then 3 mg/kg is given on days 5, 7, and 9 unless toxic reaction occurs before then. Repeat course every 30 days. Max 400 mg/day. IV infusion: 6 mg/kg given once a day over 4 hrs, until toxicity is observed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Poor nutritional state, dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency, depressed bone marrow function, potentially serious infection, management of non-malignant disease. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Discontinue promptly following any signs of toxicity (e.g. stomatitis, esopharyngitis, leukocyte count &lt;3,500/mm<sup>3</sup>, platelet count &lt;100,000 mm<sup>3</sup>, granulocyte count &lt;1,500/mm<sup>3</sup>, intractable vomiting, diarrhea or frequent LBM, hemorrhage, nervous system toxicity. Should not be readministered after a documented CV reaction (e.g. arrhythmia, angina, ST segment changes) or severe neurological toxicity. Patients with heart disease who experience chest pain during treatment course. Patients who undergone recent major surgery (within previous 30 days); have previously received high-dose irradiation therapy to bone marrow-bearing areas or alkylating agents; widespread metastatic involvement of bone marrow. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Elderly &ge;70 yrs. Women. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Nucleoside analogs (e.g. brivudin, sorivudine), cimetidine, clozapine, interferon alfa-2b, leucovorin, levamisole, methotrexate, metronidazole, mitomycin, phenytoin, sorafenib, warfarin. Increase in or false positive in tests for bilirubin (icteric index) and 5-hydroxyindole acetic acid in urine. Diagnostic tests of thyroid function. <b>Incompatibilities</b>: Carboplatin, cisplatin, cytarabine, diazepam, doxorubicin and other anthracyclines, leucovorin, methotrexate, filgrastim, gallium nitrate, metoclopramide, morphine, ondansetron, parenteral nutrition, and vinorelbine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV injection/infusion 50 mg/mL x 10 mL (P197.10)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, famotidine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "H2-Receptor Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Short-term symptomatic relief of heartburn or non-ulcer dyspepsia, relief of hyperacidity and as a daily source of extra calcium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Chew 1 tab daily. Do not use &gt;2 tabs in 24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypermagnesemia may occur, usually in patients with impaired renal function. Reduced absorption of drugs, e.g. ketoconazole, and possibly itraconazole, whose absorption is dependent on acid gastric pH. May occasionally cause constipation. Flatulence from released carbon dioxide may occur in some patients. Hypercalcemia and alkalosis, particularly in patients with renal impairment or after high doses.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Magnesium hydroxide</b>: diarrhea, hypermagnesemia (usually in patients with impaired renal function). <b>Calcium carbonate</b>: constipation, hypercalcemia (patients with renal impairment or after high doses). <b>Famotidine</b>: reported to have little or no anti-androgenic effect, although there are isolated reports of gynecomastia and impotence."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Interaction with many other drugs both by alterations in gastric pH and emptying and by formation of complexes that are not absorbed."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Chewable tablet 800 mg/165 mg/10 mg (P10.00)."

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dapagliflozin propanediol monohydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise, as monotherapy or in combination with other medications, for treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). Prevention of new or worsening heart failure, nephropathy, and cardiovascular death. Treatment of heart failure and chronic kidney disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses taken once daily at any time of day, with or without food. <b>Monotherapy:</b> 10 mg. <b>Add-on combination therapy:</b> 10 mg with metformin (with or without sulfonylurea), thiazolidinedione, sulfonylurea, DPP-4 inhibitor (with or without metformin), GLP-1 receptor antagonist (prolonged-release exenatide), Dapagliflozin (with metformin), or insulin (with or without oral antidiabetic therapy, either metformin plus insulin dual therapy or metformin plus sulfonylurea plus insulin triple therapy). <b>Initial combination therapy:</b> 10 mg plus 500 mg metformin. Dose of metformin may be increased in inadequate glycemic control. <b>eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> Additional glucose-lowering treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM and diabetic ketoacidosis. Patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR < 25 mL/min/1.73 m²); predisposing factors to ketoacidosis include low beta-cell function reserve resulting from pancreatic disorders (e.g. type 1 diabetes, history of pancreatitis or pancreatic surgery), insulin dose reduction, reduced caloric intake or increased insulin requirements due to infections, illness, or surgery and alcohol abuse. Assess signs and symptoms of ketoacidosis, including nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, malaise, and shortness of breath, blood glucose levels < 14 mmol/L (250 mg/dL). Advise patients to seek medical attention if combination of symptoms of pain, tenderness, erythema, or swelling in the genital or perineal area, with fever or malaise is experienced. Discontinue or temporarily interrupt treatment if ketoacidosis is suspected; Fournier’s gangrene. Concomitant use with insulin and insulin secretagogues. Elderly. Childn and adolescents.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Genital infection, UTI; back pain, polyuria, pollakiuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lithium. 1,5-anhydroglucitol assay."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg, 10 mg (P44.00)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and men to prevent fractures, including those of the hip and spine (vertebral compression fractures); help ensure vitamin D adequacy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "One 70 mg/5600 I.U. tablet once weekly, must be taken at least half an hour before the first food, beverage, or medication of the day with plain water only. Special Instructions: Must not lie down for the first 30 minutes of intake. Wait at least 30 minutes after taking Fosavance before taking any other oral medication."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Abnormalities of the esophagus which delay esophageal emptying. Inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 minutes. Hypersensitivity. Hypocalcemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Alendronate- may cause local irritation of the upper gastrointestinal mucosa. Patients with active upper gastrointestinal problems, those requiring invasive dental surgery, hypocalcemia and mineral metabolism disorders (should be corrected prior to therapy). creatinine clearance< 35 mL/min. Causes of osteoporosis other than estrogen deficiency, aging, and glucocorticoid use should be considered. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> may increase the magnitude of hypercalcemia and/or hypercalciuria when administered to patients with diseases associated with unregulated overproduction of calcitriol, monitor urine and serum calcium. Suspected stress fractures should be evaluated, including its causes and risk factors. All patients on bisphosphonate therapy with the need for continued therapy should be reevaluated periodically. Children. Pregnancy and lactation. <a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a> Category: C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [

                  "title": "A",

                },

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."

                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Urticaria, myalgia, malaise, asthenia, nausea, vomiting, esophagitis, esophageal erosions/ulcers, oropharyngeal ulceration, musculoskeletal pain, joint swelling, dizziness, vertigo, dysgeusia, rash, pruritus."
          },

            "content": "<b>Oint</b>: Treatment of skin infections on the skin e.g. infected hair follicles which form pimples containing pus (folliculitis), blistering and crusting (impetigo), or recurring boils (furunculosis). Kills various bacteria which cause other skin infections e.g. staphylococci, streptococci, and <i>E. coli</i>. <b>Cream</b>: Treatment of secondary infected traumatic lesions e.g. small lacerations, sutured wounds or abrasions (up to 10 cm in length or 100 cm<sup>2</sup> in area) due to susceptible strains of <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> and <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Oint</b>: Apply 2-3x a day to the affected area of the skin. Can cover treated area with plaster or suitable dressings. Do not use more than 10 days. <b>Cream – Adults, elderly, childn &ge;1 yr</b>: Apply 3x daily for up to 10 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "<b>Cream</b>: Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not suitable for ophthalmic and nasal use. Avoid contact with eyes. Discontinue treatment if sensitization reactions, severe local irritation, prolonged or significant diarrhea, or abdominal cramps occur. Pseudomembranous colitis. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Burning sensation. <b>Cream</b>: urticaria, pruritus, erythema, contact dermatitis, rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Ointment 2 g/100 g x 5 g (P298.00), 15 g (P664.20). Cream 20 mg/g x 5 g (P343.00), 15 g (P819.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inhaled Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of asthma not adequately controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and as needed; inhaled rapid-acting beta2-agonists; or adequately controlled on both inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta2-agonists. Symptomatic treatment of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and history of repeated exacerbations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Asthma -</b> Maintenance therapy: 1 or 2 inhalations twice daily. Max 4 inhalations/day; Maintenance and reliever therapy: 1 inhalation twice daily, and 1 inhalation as needed. Take additional inhalation if symptoms persist after a few mins. Max 8 inhalations/day. <b>COPD -</b> 2 inhalations twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for initial management of asthma. Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Patients with cardiac arrhythmias (especially 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block and tachyarrhythmias), idiopathic subvalvular aortic stenosis, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, severe heart disease (e.g. acute MI, IHD, CHF), occlusive vascular diseases (e.g. arteriosclerosis, arterial HTN, aneurysm); with known or suspected QTc interval prolongation, thyrotoxicosis, DM, pheochromocytoma, untreated hypokalemia, active or quiescent pulmonary TB, fungal and viral infections in the airways. Monitor blood glucose levels. Use of halogenated anesthetics. Contains a small amount of ethanol. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pharyngitis, hypokalemia, headache, tremor, palpitations, cough, muscle spasms, QTc prolongation, oral fungal infections, oral candidiasis, dysphonia, and throat irritation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Beta-blockers (including eye drops), other beta-adrenergic drugs, quinidine, disopyramide, procainamide, phenothiazines, antihistamines, MAOIs, TCAs, L-dopa, L-thyroxine, oxytocin, alcohol, furazolidone, procarbazine, anesthetics with halogenated hydrocarbons, xanthine derivatives, steroids, diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Metered-dose inhaler 100 mcg/6 mcg per actuation x 120 actuations (P1,290.00)."
          }

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of pulmonary and extrapulmonary aspergillosis in intolerant and refractory to amphotericin B therapy, and blastomycosis. Histoplasmosis (e.g., chronic cavitary pulmonary disease and disseminated, non-meningeal histoplasmosis). Onchomycosis of the toenail, with or without fingernail involvement due to dermatophytes, and fingernail in non-immunocompromised adults. Taken with meal."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Blastomycosis and histoplasmosis:</b> 200 mg once daily, may be increased in 100 mg-increments to max 400 mg if no obvious improvement or there is evidence of progressive fungal disease. Doses >200 mg/day in two divided doses. <b>Aspergillosis:</b> 200-400 mg daily. <b>Life-threatening situations: </b>Loading dose of 200 mg thrice daily for the first 3 days, continued for a minimum of 3 months. <b>Onchomycosis - Toenails with or without fingernail involvement:</b> 200 mg once daily for 12 consecutive weeks; <b>Fingernails:</b> 2 treatment pulses each consist of 200 mg twice daily for 1 week. The pulses are separated by a 3-week period without Funguard."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Present or history of CHF. Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates; colchicine, fesoterodine, and solifenacin in varying degrees of renal or hepatic impairment; eliglustat in poor or intermediate CYP2D6 metabolizers and taking strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors; venetoclax in chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic leukemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, risk factors for CHF, immunocompromised, cystic fibrosis, HIV. Hepatotoxicity (e.g., liver failure and death). Life-threatening cardiac dysrhythmias and/or sudden death in coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors. Transient or permanent hearing loss. Discontinue if signs and symptoms of liver disease or neuropathy appear. Monitor liver function. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Fertility. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Elevated liver enzymes (>2x ULN), rash, hypotension, orthostatic hypotension, headache, malaise, myalgia, vasculitis, vertigo, rhinitis, URTI, UTI, sinusitis, injury, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, abdominal pain, dizziness, rash, cystitis, abnormal liver function, nausea, increased appetite, constipation, gastritis, gastroenteritis, pharyngitis, asthenia, fever, pain, tremor, herpes zoster, abnormal dreaming."
          },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/3q9ht2Lwbx5YmQgSxZk9QE8FLR5aCpo06QX76s3i7phWe4rUFC.jpg",

            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Cryptococcosis. Systemic, mucosal, and genital candidiasis. Deep endemic mycoses. Superficial fungal infections. Prophylaxis of transplant patients. Patients with malignancy who are receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy. Immunosuppressive and radiation therapy. Prophylaxis of HIV or AIDS in patients who are at risk of developing Candida infections and serious fungal infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Cryptococcal meningitis and other cryptococcal infections</b>: 400 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 200-400 mg once daily for 6-8 weeks up to 10-12 weeks. <b>Oropharyngeal candidiasis</b>: 50-100 mg once daily for 7-14 days. <b>Denture-associated atrophic oral candidiasis</b>: 50 mg once daily for 14 days. <b>Esophageal candidiasis</b>: 50-100 mg once daily for 14-30 days, may be increased to 400 mg once daily if necessary. <b>Mucosal candidiasis (except genital candidiasis)</b>: 50-100 mg once daily for 14-30 days. <b>Systemic <i>Candida</i> infections</b>: 400 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 200 mg once daily, may be increased to 400 mg once daily, continue for minimum of 4 weeks and at least 2 weeks after symptoms have resolved. <b>Vaginal candidiasis and candidal balanitis</b>: 150 mg single dose. <b>Recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis</b>: 150 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 150 mg on the 4<sup>th</sup> day, maintenance 100-150 mg once a week for 6 months. <b>Dermatologic infections including tinea pedis, corporis and cruris - <i>Candida</i> infections</b>: 150 mg once a week or 50 mg once daily for 2-6 weeks. <b>Tinea versicolor and capitis</b> : 50 mg once daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>Tinea unguium (onychomycosis)</b>: 150 mg once a week. Duration - fingernails: 3-6 months; toenails: 6-12 months. <b>Deep endemic mycoses</b>: 200-800 mg once daily. Duration - coccidioidomycosis: 11-24 months; paracoccidioidomycosis: 2-17 months; sporotrichosis: 1-16 months; histoplasmosis: 3-17 months. <b>Suppression of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis and cryptococcal infections at other sites in patients with AIDS</b>: 100-200 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of oropharyngeal candidiasis relapse in patients with AIDS</b>: 100-200 mg once a week for 4-9 months. <b>Prevention of fungal infections in patients with HIV</b>: 100-200 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of fungal infections in transplant patients, patients undergoing chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiotherapy and other patients who are at risk of systemic fungal infections</b>: 400 mg once daily. <b>Childn</b> - 3-12 mg/kg once daily. Max 600 mg once daily. <b>Oropharyngeal candidiasis</b>: 6 mg/kg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 3 mg/kg once daily for at least 2 weeks to decrease likelihood of relapse. <b>Esophageal candidiasis</b>: 6 mg/kg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 3 mg/kg once daily, may be increased to 12 mg/kg/day for minimum of 3 weeks and at least 2 weeks after symptoms resolve. <b>Systemic <i>Candida</i> infections</b>: 6-12 mg/kg daily. <b>Cryptococcal meningitis and infections on other sites</b>: 12 mg/kg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 6 mg/kg once daily, may be increased to 12 mg/kg/day for 10-12 weeks. <b>Suppression of cryptococcal meningitis in patient with AIDS</b>: 6 mg/kg once daily for 6 months or longer. <b>Infants</b>: Same doses above but given every other day (for 2-4 weeks old) or once every 3 days (for those &lt;2 weeks old). <b>Renal impairment</b>: For a multiple dosing regimen, initially 50-400 mg followed by a reduced dose. CrCl 11-50 mL/min: 50% of recommended dose; Patients undergoing dialysis: 1 recommended dose after each dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with drugs known to prolong the QT interval and metabolized by CYP34A e.g. astemizole, pimozide, quinidine, and cisapride."

            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Liver disease; may cause dermatologic and hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis, anaphylaxis), overgrowth of non-susceptible strains of <i>Candida</i>, QT prolongation and torsades de pointes. Concomitant use of drugs with narrow therapeutic window metabolized by CYP2C9 and CYP34A should be monitored. Renal and hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Elderly and childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Pregnancy risk</b>: Category C for vaginal candidiasis but D for all other indications.",

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of partial-onset seizures with or without secondarily generalized seizures in patients &ge;4 yrs with epilepsy. Adjunctive treatment of primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients &ge;7 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Partial-onset seizures - Adults, adolescents (&ge;12 yrs), childn (4-11 yrs) &ge;30 kg</b>: Initially 2 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 2 mg/day weekly or every 2 weeks up to maintenance of 4-8 mg/day. May be further increased by increments of 2 mg/day to 12 mg/day if 8 mg/day is tolerated. <b>20-30 kg</b>: Initially 1 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 1 mg weekly or every 2 weeks to a maintenance dose of 4-6 mg/day. May be increased by increments of 1 mg/day to 8 mg/day if 6 mg/day is tolerated. <b>&lt;20 kg</b>: Initially 1 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 1 mg weekly or every 2 weeks to a maintenance dose of 2-4 mg/day. May be increased by increments of 0.5 mg/day to 6 mg/kg, if 4 mg/day is tolerated. <b>Primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures - Adults, adolescents (&ge;12 yrs)</b>: Initially 2 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 2 mg/day weekly or every 2 weeks up to maintenance 8 mg/day. May be further increased by increments of 2 mg/day to 12 mg/day, if 8 mg/day is tolerated. <b>Childn (7-11 yrs) &ge;30 kg</b>: Initially 2 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 2 mg weekly or every 2 weeks to a maintenance dose of 4-8 mg/day. May be increased by increments of 2 mg/day to 12 mg/day if 8 mg/day is tolerated. <b>20-30 kg</b>: Initially 1 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 1 mg weekly or every 2 weeks to a maintenance dose of 4-6 mg/day. May be increased by increments of 1 mg/day to 8 mg/day, if 6 mg/day is tolerated. <b>&lt;20 kg</b>: Initially 1 mg/day, may be increased by increments of 1 mg weekly or every 2 weeks to a maintenance dose of 2-4 mg/day. May be increased by increments of 0.5 mg/day to 6 mg/day, if 4 mg/day is tolerated. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: Initially 2 mg, should be up-titrated using 2 mg doses no faster than every 2 weeks based on tolerability and effectiveness. Max 8 mg. <b>Tab</b>: Tab should not be chewed, crushed, or split. <b>Oral susp</b>: Shake well before use. Use provided adapter and graduated oral dosing syringe."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt discontinuation. May predispose to psychotic disorder (at higher doses), aggressive and hostile behavior, suicidal ideation and behavior. Patients with absence or myoclonic seizures, history of substance abuse; moderate or severe hepatic and renal impairment, on hemodialysis. Concomitant use of progestative-containing hormonal contraceptives, CYP3A-inducing antiepileptic drugs, CYP450 inducers or inhibitors. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential not using contraception. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Tab</b>: Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. <b>Oral susp</b>: Patients on other antiepileptic medications containing sorbitol. Patients with hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI) should not take this medicinal product; contains benzoic acid and sodium benzoate, each mL of perampanel susp contains <0.005 mg benzoic acid and 1.1 mg sodium benzoate. Benzoic acid and benzoates may increase neonatal jaundice which may develop into kernicterus.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, somnolence; decreased/increased appetite, aggression, anger, anxiety, confusional state, ataxia, dysarthria, balance disorder, irritability, diplopia, blurred vision, vertigo, nausea, back pain, gait disturbance, fatigue, weight increase, and fall."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral contraceptives, carbamazepine, phenytoin, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, topiramate, midazolam, rifampicin, hypericum, felbamate, ketoconazole, alcohol."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gabapentin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy in treatment of partial seizures with and without secondary generalization in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs. Adjunctive therapy in treatment of partial seizures with and without secondary generalization in adults and childn &ge;6 yrs. Peripheral neuropathic pain e.g. painful diabetic neuropathy and post-herpetic neuralgia in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs</b> - <b>Initial titration</b>: Day 1: 300 mg once daily; Day 2: 300 mg twice daily; Day 3: 300 mg thrice daily. <b>Epilepsy</b>: Individualized dosage. <b>Childn &ge;6 yrs</b>: 10-15 mg/kg/day for 3 days, may be increased to 25-35 mg/kg/day, up to 50 mg/kg/day in 3 single doses, max time interval should not >12 hrs. <b>Peripheral neuropathic pain</b> - <b>Adults</b>: Initially 900 mg/day given in 3 equally divided doses, can be increased in 300 mg/day increments every 2-3 days up to max 3,600 mg/day. <b>Renal impairment</b> - <b>CrCl >80 mL/min</b>: 900-3,600 mg/day given in 3 divided doses; <b>50-79 mL/min</b>: 600-1,800 mg/day given in 3 divided doses; <b>30-49 mL/min</b>: 300-900 mg/day in 3 divided doses; <b>15-29 mL/min</b>: 150 mg/day (given as 300 mg every other day) to 600 mg/day; <b>&lt;15 mL/min</b>: 150 mg/day (given as 300 mg every other day) to 300 mg/day. <b>Patients undergoing hemodialysis</b>: In addition to maintenance dose, administer an additional 200-300 mg following each 4-hr hemodialysis. <b>Anuric patients undergoing hemodialysis</b>: Loading dose 300-400 mg, then 200-300 mg following each 4-hr hemodialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue use if acute pancreatitis and drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms develops. Abrupt withdrawal may precipitate status epilepticus. Increased seizure frequency or onset of new types of seizures may occur. Not to be used against primary generalized seizure. Patients with mixed seizures including absences. Risk of suicidal ideation and behavior; abuse and dependence. False positive results in semi-quantitative determination of total urine protein by dipstick tests. Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May influence the ability to drive and operate machines. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Viral infection, somnolence, dizziness, ataxia, fatigue, fever. Pneumonia, respiratory infection, UTI, otitis media, leukopenia, anorexia, increased appetite, hostility, confusion and emotional lability, depression, anxiety, nervousness, abnormal thinking, convulsions, hyperkinesias, dysarthria, amnesia, tremor, insomnia, headache, sensations (e.g. paresthesia, hypesthesia), abnormal coordination, nystagmus, reflexes (increased, decreased or absent), visual disturbances (e.g. amblyopia, diplopia), vertigo, dyspnea, bronchitis, pharyngitis, cough, rhinitis, vomiting, nausea, dental abnormalities, gingivitis, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, constipation, dry mouth or throat, flatulence, facial edema, purpura, rash, pruritus, acne, arthralgia, myalgia, back pain, twitching, incontinence, impotence, peripheral or generalized edema, abnormal gait, asthenia pain, malaise, flu syndrome, withdrawal reactions, chest pain, decreased WBC, weight gain, accidental injury, fracture, abrasion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg, 300 mg."
          }

          {
            "title": "Description",
            "content": "The FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus Sensor has a small flexible tip that is inserted just under the skin and can be worn for up to 15 days. Comes in two parts: Sensor Pack and Sensor Applicator."
          },
          {
            "title": "Uses",
            "content": "Intended to be used together with a compatible device to monitor interstitial fluid glucose levels and is designed to replace blood glucose testing in the self-management of diabetes, including dosing of insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Direction",
            "content": "Apply Sensor on the back of the upper arm using the sensor applicator. Avoid areas with scars, moles, stretch marks, or lumps. Scan Sensor at least once every 8 hrs for the most accurate performance. See user’s manual for complete instruction for use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "The Sensor and Sensor Applicator are designed for single use. Contains small parts that may be dangerous if swallowed. Perform a blood glucose test if the readings are inconsistent with how patients feel. Reuse may result in no glucose readings and infection. Not suitable for re-sterilization. Further exposure to irradiation may cause inaccurate results. Some patients may be sensitive to the adhesive that keeps Sensor attached to the skin. Remove and discontinue using Sensor if skin irritation occurs. The sensor should not be taken below 1 meter of water (3 feet), and should not be submerged in water for &gt;30 mins. Childn 2-12 yrs should be supervised by a caregiver &ge;18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {

            "content": "FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus Flash Glucose Monitoring System (Sensor) (P4,120.00)."

            "title": "Uses",
            "content": "Measure glucose in fresh whole blood samples taken from fingers, forearm, upper arm or the base of the thumb. Measure ketone in fresh whole blood samples from fingers only.           },
          {
            "title": "Direction",
            "content": "Wash and dry hands before and after testing. Insert test strip into test port of the meter. Lance test site and apply blood drop to the target area of the test strip. View the result. See user’s manual for complete instructions for use."

            "content": "Not for use in diagnosis of DM. Observe caution when using around childn, small parts may constitute choking hazard. Do not use during xylose absorption testing.         "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Nasal Decongestants, Antiallergics & Related Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of nasal symptoms of seasonal and perennial allergic and non-allergic rhinitis in adults and childn &ge;4 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "50 mcg/0.1 mL (1 actuation). <b>Adults and childn >14 yrs:</b> 2 sprays into each nostril. <b>Childn 4-14 yrs:</b> 1 spray into each nostril. <b>Max:</b> Should not exceed 2 sprays each nostril. <b>Maintenance dose:</b> 1 spray in each nostril. All doses administered once daily, preferably in the morning. Prime pump before first use. Shake well before use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for acute attacks. Avoid abrupt withdrawal and larger than recommended doses. May cause a reduction in growth velocity, monitor height of childn. Transferring patients from systemic steroid treatment. May unmask underlying eosinophilic conditions (e.g. Churg-Strauss syndrome, active or quiescent pulmonary TB). Examine patients periodically for evidence of <i>Candida</i> infection. Childn < 4 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fluconazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used for superficial mucosal (oropharyngeal, oesophageal, or vaginal) candidiasis and for fungal skin infections. For systemic infections including systemic candidiasis, coccidioidomycosis, cryptococcosis, and has been tried in blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, sporotrichosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Superficial mucosal candidiasis: </b>Usual dose 50 mg daily, may be given 100 mg if necessary for 7-14 days, for atrophic oral candidiasis associated with denture 14 days, and for other mucosal candida infections including esophagitis 14-30 days. <b>Genital candidiasis (vaginal candidiasis or candida balinitis): </b>150 mg as a single dose. <b>Infections of the skin: </b>50 mg daily for up to 6 weeks. <b>Systemic candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis and other cryptococcal infections: </b> Initial dose 400 mg, followed by 200 mg to 400 mg daily for at least 6-8 weeks. <b>Immunocompromised patients at risk of fungal infections: </b>Prophylaxis 50 mg to 400 mg daily <b>Renal Impairment- Creatinine clearance >50 mL/min:</b>100 % of the standard recommended dose. <b>CC < 50 mL/min (not on dialysis): </b>50% of the standard recommended dose. <b>Patients on regular haemodialysis:</b> 100% of the standard recommended dose after each dialysis session. No dosage adjustment is needed in patients with renal impairment given single-dose therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cisapride, terfenadine, astemizole, pimozide, quinidine. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired hepatic or renal function, AIDS or malignancy, proarrhythmic conditions.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea and vomiting, taste disturbance, headache, dizziness, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, hyperlipidemia, increased liver enzymes, TEN, SJS, rash, dyspepsia, hepatic disorders, angioedema, anaphylaxis, alopecia, hypokalemia, prolonged QT interval, torsades de pointes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Rifampicin, HCTZ, drugs metabolized by CYP450, CYP3A4, CYP2C9. Selective COX-2 inhibitors, terfenadine, astemizole, cisapride, amitriptyline, theophylline, contraceptive steroids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 150 mg."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ACvNYYo4uV8DxqZjBrVyp4KOiY07LdiXM6xMPpex2VvQUkxAhe.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4P54wpc5VNkxlLyrKiOw0nPqylXJLjJdo6PiUVnwaG3AXgW3bU.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Xjyjgau7EPzDgmlhc3TAfJptYNVyJnV9Y4HhonePNxzmvX12Uk.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levetiracetam",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrrolidine"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy in treatment of partial-onset seizure, with or without secondary generalization in adults &ge;16 yrs. Adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizure, with or without secondary generalization in adults, adolescents and childn &ge;1 month with epilepsy; myoclonic seizures in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in adults and childn &ge;6 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab: Partial-onset seizure</b> - <b>Adults &ge;16 yrs:</b> 250 mg twice daily, increase to 500 mg twice daily after 2 weeks. Dose can be further increased by 250 mg twice daily every 2 weeks. Max 1,500 mg twice daily; <b>Childn and adolescents 4-&lt;16 yrs:</b> 10 mg/kg twice daily, increase every 2 weeks by 20 mg/kg increments to 30 mg/kg twice daily, reduce if patient cannot tolerate the dose. <b>IV: Partial-onset seizure</b> - <b>Adults &ge;16 yrs:</b> 500 mg twice daily, may be increased by 1,000 mg/day every 2 weeks. Max 3,000 mg/day; <b>Childn and adolescents 4-&lt;16 yrs:</b> 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses, increased by 20 mg/kg increments every 2 weeks up to 60 mg/kg/day; <b>Childn 6 months-&lt;4 yrs:</b> 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses, increased by 20 mg/kg increments every 2 weeks up to 50 mg/kg/day; <b>1-&lt;6 months:</b> 14 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses, increased by 14 mg/kg increments every 2 weeks up to 42 mg/kg/day. <b>Tab/IV: Myoclonic seizure in patients &ge;12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy:</b> 500 mg twice daily, increase by 1,000 mg/day every 2 weeks to 3,000 mg/day. <b>Primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures</b> - <b>Adults &ge;16 yrs:</b> 500 mg twice daily, increase by 1,000 mg/day every 2 weeks to 3,000 mg/day; <b>Childn and adolescents 6-&lt;16 yrs:</b> 10 mg/kg twice daily, increase every 2 weeks by 20 mg/kg increments to 30 mg/kg twice daily. <b>Renal impairment</b> - <b>Adults and adolescents &gt;50 kg</b> - CrCl &gt;80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 500-1,500 mg; 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 500-1,000 mg; 30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-750 mg; < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-500 mg. All doses administered every 12 hrs; ESRD patients undergoing dialysis: Loading dose of 750 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day then 500-1,000 mg. Administered every 24 hrs for IV. Give 250-500 mg supplemental dose following dialysis. <b>Childn from 4 yrs and &lt;50 kg BW</b> - CrCl >80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 10-30 mg/kg twice daily; 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 10-20 mg/kg twice daily; 30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 5-15 mg/kg twice daily; < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 5-10 mg/kg twice daily. ESRD patients undergoing dialysis: 15 mg/kg loading dose on 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment then 10-20 mg/kg once daily. Give 5-10 mg/kg supplemental dose following dialysis. <b>Severe hepatic impairment:</b> Reduce daily maintenance dose by 50% when CrCl &lt;70 mL/min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Psychiatric reactions, suicidal behavior and ideation. Somnolence and fatigue. Serious dermatological reactions including SJS, TEN, and DRESS. Withdrawal seizures, hematologic abnormalities, increase in BP. Monitoring of vital signs and observation of clinical status in patients with cases of levetiracetam overdoses (e.g. somnolence, agitation, aggression, depressed level of consciousness, respiratory depression, and coma) upon symptomatic treatment including hemodialysis. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn &lt;4 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infection, viral infection, flu syndrome, otitis media, influenza. Blood and lymphatic disorders. Hypersensitivity, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms. Anorexia, decreased/increased weight, hyponatremia, dehydration. Psychiatric and nervous system disorders. Diplopia, blurred vision, amblyopia, conjunctivitis. Vertigo, ear pain. Respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and SC tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders. UTI, albuminuria, urine abnormality. Asthenia/fatigue, fever, pain, face edema. Injury, head injury, confusion, fall, joint sprain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other antiepileptic drugs (e.g. phenytoin, valproic acid, phenobarbital, lamotrigine, gabapentin, and primidone), carbamazepine, methotrexate, ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 250 mg (P20.08), 500 mg (P39.12), 1 g (P80.89). Concentrate for solution for IV infusion 500 mg/5 mL (P1,590.01)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Drops/Syrup</b>: Prevention and treatment of vitamin B deficiency, macrocytic anemia, megaloblastic anemia, and thalassemia due to folic acid deficiency. Prevention and treatment of folate deficiency states e.g. megaloblastic anemia, chronic hemolytic anemia, gastrointestinal inflammation and malabsorption, alcoholism, and conditions associated with impaired homocysteine metabolism. Prevention of methotrexate toxicity."
          },

            "content": "<b>Drops - Infants &le;1 yr</b>: 500 mcg/kg daily. <b>Syrup - Childn &gt;1 yr</b>: 5 mg daily. <b>Cap</b>: 1 cap daily."
          },

            "content": "Megaloblastic anemia secondary to vitamin B<sub>12</sub> deficiency, not to be given before a diagnosis has been fully established."
          },

            "content": "May mask vitamin B<sub>12</sub> deficiency associated anemia. Patients who may have folate-dependent tumors.",

          },

            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) as: monotherapy; combination therapy with metformin when diabetes is not adequately controlled by diet and exercise alone; combination with antidiabetic drugs (e.g. insulin)."
          },
          {

            "content": "Individualize dosage. 50 mg once daily in the morning; or 50 mg twice daily, in the morning and evening.             "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) not adequately controlled on diet and exercise alone, or who are already treated with the combination of vildagliptin and metformin HCl, as separate tabs. In combination with other antidiabetic drugs (e.g. insulin)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Max 100 mg vildagliptin daily. <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs - Inadequately controlled on vildagliptin monotherapy:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg twice daily, gradually titrated based on therapeutic response; <b>on metformin monotherapy:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1,000 mg twice daily; <b>Switching from combination therapy of vildagliptin + metformin as separate tabs:</b> 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1,000 mg based on dose of vildagliptin or metformin already being taken; <b>Naive patients:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg once daily, gradually titrated to max 50 mg/1,000 mg twice daily based on therapeutic response; <b>Combination with SU or insulin:</b> 50 mg vidagliptin twice daily and metformin dose already being taken. <b>Renal impairment – GFR 60-89 mL/min:</b> Max 3,000 mg/day metformin and max 100 mg/day vildagliptin; <b>45-59 mL/min:</b> Initially &le;1,000 mg with max 2,000 mg/day metformin and max 50 mg/day vildagliptin; <b>30-44 mL/min:</b> Initially &le;500 mg with max 1,000 mg/day metformin and max 50 mg/day vildagliptin. If no adequate strength of vildagliptin + metformin (Galvusmet) is available, individual components should be used instead of fixed dose. Taken with meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min). CHF. Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis or diabetic ketoacidosis, with or without coma)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM or diabetic ketoacidosis. Not recommended in patients with hepatic impairment (e.g. pre-treatment ALT or AST >2.5x ULN) and NYHA functional class IV. Patients with risk factors for lactic acidosis or hypoglycemia, excessive alcohol intake, previously controlled DM developing laboratory abnormalities. Perform liver function tests prior to initiation and during 1<sup>st</sup> yr of therapy at 3-month intervals and periodically thereafter. Monitor renal function before treatment initiation and regularly thereafter. Concomitant use of drugs that may affect renal function. Discontinue if AST or ALT increase &ge;3x ULN; jaundice or other signs suggestive of liver dysfunction developed; dehydration; prior to or at time of imaging or surgical procedures until renal function has been re-evaluated or resumption of oral nutrition, 48 hrs after and found stable; hypoxic states; temporary withheld in case loss of glycemic control.           },

            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, nausea, gastroesophageal reflux disease, diarrhea, flatulence, chills, decreased blood glucose; dizziness, tremor, asthenia, hypoglycemia, hyperhidrosis; decreased appetite, vomiting, abdominal pain."
          },

          {

            "content": "Treatment of gastrointestinal symptoms caused by gastric dysmotility and delayed gastric emptying e.g. sensation of bloating, early satiety, postprandial fullness, upper abdominal pain, anorexia, heartburn, nausea and vomiting, functional (non-ulcer) dyspepsia or chronic gastritis."

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab 3x daily taken before meals. Usually administered up to 8 weeks. Dose may be reduced according to patient’s age and symptoms."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. GI hemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation."
          },

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs with a narrow therapeutic index, sustained-release or enteric-coated formulations. Anticholinergic drugs."
          },
          {

            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of mild to moderate pain due to rheumatoid arthritis (including Still’s disease), soft tissue injuries, other painful musculoskeletal conditions, headache, dental pain, post-op pain, and dysmenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn >12 yrs:</b> Initially 1 tab followed by &frac12; tab every 6 hrs as needed for &le;7 days. Taken preferably with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with aspirin and other NSAIDs. Patients with active PUD, IBD, hepatic and renal impairment, history of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be taken for >7 days. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with plasma-protein-binding drugs and anticoagulants. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dyspepsia, upper GIT discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain."
          },

            "content": "Aspirin, anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin), diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers, corticosteroids, ciclosporin, oral hypoglycemics, lithium, methotrexate, tacrolimus."
