        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Folic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vitamins & Minerals, Maternal"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment and prevention of folate-deficiency state. Used in women of child-bearing potential and pregnant women to protect against neural tube defects in their offspring. Treatment of megaloblastic anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – Folate-deficient megaloblastic anemia; in drug-induced folate deficiency:</b> 5 mg daily for 4 months. Max 15 mg daily for malabsorption states. <b>Prophylaxis in chronic hemolytic state or in renal dialysis:</b> 5 mg every 1-7 days depending on underlying disease. <b>Prevention of neural tube defects in women known to be at risk:</b> 5 mg daily started before conception and continued throughout the 1st trimester. <b>Pregnancy in established folate deficiency:</b> 5 mg daily continued to term. <b>Childn 12-18 yrs – Folate-deficiency anemia:</b> 1 tab (5 mg) daily for 4 months, maintenance dose 5 mg. <b>Hemolytic anemic and metabolic disorder; Prevention of folate deficiency in patient with kidney dialysis:</b> 1-2 tabs (5-10 mg) daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Folate deficiency due to dihydrofolate reductase inhibitors, pernicious, aplastic or normocytic anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be given alone or with inadequate vit B<sub>12</sub> for the treatment of pernicious anemia or undiagnosed megaloblastic anemia and in patients with folate-dependent tumors. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category A.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antiepileptics, oral contraceptives, anti-tuberculosis drugs, alcohol. Folic acid antagonists (e.g. methotrexate, pyrimethamine, triamterene, trimethoprim, and sulfonamides)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 5 mg (P5.60)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

    "detail": {

        "id": 4814,

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Propofol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Parenteral Anesthetics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia. Used in ICU sedation, surgical and diagnostic procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Induction of anesthesia- Adults:</b> 10 mg/mL titrated at 30-40 mg every 10 secs. &lt;55 yrs: 1.5-2.5 mg/kg. Reduce total dose to 1 mg/kg at slower infusion rate (20 mg every 10 secs) in patients in risk groups ASA III & IV esp. in the case of prior cardiac damage & elderly. <b>Childn &ge;1 month:</b> 10 mg/mL titrated slowly. Childn &gt;8 yrs: approx 2.5 mg/kg. 1 month-3 yrs: 2.5-4 mg/kg. <b>Maintenance of anesthesia – Adults:</b> 4-12 mg/kg/hr as continuous IV infusion. <b>Elderly in poor general state of health or with hypovolemia, risk groups ASA III & IV:</b> 4 mg/kg/hr. Repeat bolus inj 25-50 mg subsequent. <b>Childn &ge;1 month:</b> 9-15 mg/kg/hr as IV infusion or repeated bolus inj. <b>ICU sedation &gt;16 yrs:</b> 0.3-4.0 mg/kg/hr by continuous infusion. <b>Sedation for surgical and diagnostic procedures – Adults:</b> 0.5-1 mg/kg for 1-15 mins. Maintenance: 1.5-4.5 mg/kg/hr. Additionally 10-20 mg may be given as bolus. <b>Childn &ge;1 month:</b> 1-2 mg/kg. Maintenance: 1.5-9 mg/kg/hr. Lower doses may be necessary for ASA III & IV patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. ICU sedation for childn &lt;16 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Contains soybean oil. Monitor for the first signs of a decrease in BP, respiratory tract obstruction, and oxygen deficiency. Patients with severe cardiac damage and epilepsy. May impair impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Newborns. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pulmonary edema, bradycardia, spontaneous movements and muscle spasms during the induction of anesthesia, headache during the waking phase, hypotension, hyperventilation and coughing during the induction of anesthesia, temporary apnea during induction of anesthesia, singulation during the induction, nausea and vomiting during the waking phase, hot flushes during the induction of anesthesia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Opiates, rifampicin, valproate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Emulsion for injection 10 mg/mL x 20 mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Vitamins & Minerals, Maternal"

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment and prevention of folate deficiency. Treatment of megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency. Prevention of neural tube defects in the offspring of women planning a pregnancy and known to be at risk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly</b> - <b>Folate deficient megaloblastic anemia</b>: 5 mg daily for 4 months; <b>Chronic hemolytic states</b>: 5 mg every 1 to 7 days depending on underlying disease. <b>Childn < 12 yrs</b>: Consider using a more suitable dosage form. <b>Pregnancy</b>: 5 mg daily continued to term and 3 months after delivery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with untreated cobalamin deficiency including untreated pernicious anemia (long-term therapy). May precipitate cobalamin neuropathy among cobalamin deficient patients (folate administration &ge;3 month)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not give alone or in conjunction with inadequate amounts of vit B<sub>12</sub> for the treatment of pernicious anemia, undiagnosed megaloblastic anemia or other vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency states. May produce hematopoietic response in patients with megaloblastic anemia due to vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency without preventing aggravation of neurologic symptoms which may lead to subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord. Do not use to treat anemia without full investigation of the cause. Patients with folate-dependent tumors.",

          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6dCrztAM24shgDDUeyQXawt02AgNVvaQ7dZdRNkTv8crzTiQeV.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefazolin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "First Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of serious infections due to susceptible organisms, including respiratory tract infections; genitourinary tract (GUT) infections; skin and skin structure infections; biliary tract infections; bone and joint infections; endocarditis. Peri-op prophylaxis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via IM injection, IV injection, or IV infusion (intermittent or continuous). <b>Adults:</b> 500 mg-1 g IM every 8-12 hrs. Max 6 g/day; up to 12 g in severe life-threatening infections. <b>Childn >1 month:</b> 25-50 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses, increased up to max of 100 mg/kg/day in severe infections. <b>Surgical prophylaxis:</b> 1 g 30 mins-1 hr pre-op, followed by 500 mg-1 g during surgery for lengthy procedures. 500 mg-1 g every 6-8 hrs post-op for 24 hrs, or up to 5 days in certain cases. <b>Patients with renal impairment - Severe to very severe infections:</b> CrCl 20-50 mL/min: Initially 500 mg, followed by 250 mg every 6 hrs or 500 mg every 12 hrs; 10-20 mL/min: Initially 500 mg, followed by 250 mg every 12 hrs or 500 mg every 24 hrs; 5-10 mL/min: Initially 500 mg, followed by 250 mg every 24-36 hrs or 500 mg every 48-72 hrs; < 5 mL/min in patients undergoing hemodialysis: Initially 500 mg IV, followed by 500 mg every 72 hrs; <b>Less severe infections:</b> CrCl 20-50 mL/min: Initially 500 mg, followed by 125-250 mg every 12 hrs; 10-20 mL/min: Initially 500 mg, followed by 125-250 mg every 24 hrs; 5-10 mL/min: Initially 500 mg, followed by 75-125 mg every 24 hrs; < 5 mL/min in patients undergoing hemodialysis: Initially 500 mg IV, followed by 50-75 mg every 72 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with penicillins and other cephalosporins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated for meningitis. Patients with renal impairment. Premature and infants < 1 month. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin rash, fever; hematologic and digestive disorders; transient rise in ALT, AST, and alkaline phosphatase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other antibiotics. High MW molecules. False positive Benedict’s and Fehling’s soln, Clinitest, Coomb’s test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 1 g (P398.00)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>Females 9-45 yrs:</b> Prevention of cervical, vulvar, vaginal, and anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18; genital warts (Condyloma acuminata) caused by HPV types 6 and 11; and infections and precancerous or dysplastic lesions caused by HPV types 6, 11, 16, and 18 (e.g. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or 3 and cervical adenocarcinoma <i>in situ</i> (AIS), CIN grade 1, vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) grade 2 and grade 3, vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) grade 2 and grade 3, VIN grade 1 and VaIN grade 1, anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) grade 1, 2 and 3). <b>Males 9-26 yrs:</b> Prevention of anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and external genital lesions and infection caused by HPV types 6, 11, 16, and 18."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "3 separate doses of 0.5 mL IM in the deltoid region of the upper arm or in the higher anterolateral area of the thigh. <b>1<sup>st</sup> dose:</b> At elected date; <b>2<sup>nd</sup> dose:</b> 2 months after the 1st dose; <b>3<sup>rd</sup> dose:</b> 6 months after the 1st dose. <b>Childn 9-13 yrs:</b> 2 separate doses (1<sup>st</sup> dose: At elected date. 2<sup>nd</sup> dose: 6 months or 1 yr after the 1<sup>st</sup> dose).           {
            "title": "Contraindications",

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. GI hemorrhage, mechanical obstruction, or perforation."

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6gmxPuO3BtLNKVacQVSNBawLro8mdbefKOM44OgDxnHv0wZYTK.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kGCk6vgteaoCG0YV8CjCmtawDIcwEww56JIS84x2MOgGNMvJBa.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Omeprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used in conditions where inhibition of gastric acid secretion may be beneficial including aspiration syndromes, dyspepsia, erosive esophagitis, gastroesophageal disease (GERD), benign gastric ulcer, duodenal ulcer and hypersecretory conditions (e.g. Zollinger Ellison syndrome)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Dyspepsia</b>: 20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>GERD</b>: 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks; some may require additional 4 weeks of therapy. <b>Refractory esophagitis</b>: 40 mg daily. Maintenance therapy after healing: 20 mg once daily. Childn: 0.7-1.4 mg/kg BW. Max 40 mg for 4-12 weeks. <b>Peptic ulcer</b>: 20 mg single dose or 40 mg for severe case; continued for 4 weeks for <b>duodenal ulcer</b> and 8 weeks for <b>gastric ulcer</b>. Maintenance 20 mg once daily. <b>NSAID-associated ulceration</b>: 20 mg once daily. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 60 mg once daily. <b>Prophylaxis of acid aspiration during general anesthesia</b>: 40 mg in the evening before the surgery and 40 mg on the day of surgery, 2-6 hrs before the procedure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Possibility of malignancy in patients with gastric ulcer. Hepatic impairment. GI infection. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, diarrhea, skin rashes, pruritus, dizziness, fatigue, abdominal pain, arthralgia, myalgia, dry mouth, bullous eruptions, erythema multiforme, angioedema, anaphylaxis, hepatic encephalopathy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs metabolized by CYP2C19. Diazepam, phenytoin, warfarin, ketoconazole, itraconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Delayed-release capsule 40 mg (P34.50)."
          }

        "id": 4865,
        "brand_name": "Gavrila",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kOJgYyiHGD6COybE52BmPttwBVWJIVUAoaDKFjFeX58c0Io71b.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gHT4RjkrjRaDN4my69fE9A4AjmLzfzTLf6XhN7UD827XUkAb92.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Nijetva8L5tji5dYTVLqCp8P8BdWZQkW1koxmJCgw1tJT6VYgL.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ivabradine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in coronary artery disease adults with normal sinus rhythm and HR &ge;70 bpm. Indicated in adults unable to tolerate or with a contraindication to use beta-blockers or in combination with beta-blocker dose; and in chronic heart failure NYHA class II-IV with systolic dysfunction, in adult in sinus rhythm and whose HR &ge;75 bpm, in combination with standard therapy including beta-blocker therapy or when beta-blocker therapy is contraindicated or not tolerated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris – Adults < 75 yrs:</b> 5 mg twice daily. Maintenance dose: 7.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of chronic heart failure:</b> 5 mg twice daily. After 2 weeks of treatment, may be increased to 7.5 mg twice daily if resting HR is persistently >60 bpm or decreased to 2.5 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Resting HR of < 70 bpm prior to treatment, cardiogenic shock, acute MI, severe hypotension (BP < 90/50 mmHg), severe hepatic insufficiency, sick sinus syndrome, sine-atrial block, pacemaker-dependent, unstable angina, AV block of 3<sup>rd</sup> degree, heart failure. Combination with strong cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with congenital QT syndrome or treated with QT prolonging medicinal products. Moderate hepatic and severe renal insufficiency. Not recommended in patients with atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrythmias that interfere with the sinus node function, AV block 2<sup>nd</sup> degree, stroke. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Luminous phenomena in the visual field (phosphenes), blurred vision, bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, dyspnea, muscle cramps. Hyperuricemia, eosinophilia, and elevated blood-creatinine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, oral erythromycin, nelfinavir, ritonavir, nefazodone, diltiazem, verapamil, fluconazole, rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin, St. John’s Wort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 7.5 mg 28s (P700.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>NSCLC</b> - <b>Monotherapy</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion, repeated once weekly for 3 weeks followed by a 1-week rest period. <b>NSCLC in combination with cisplatin</b>: For 3-week cycle regimen, gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion on days 1 and 8, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle, for 4-week cycle regimen gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given by 30 mins IV infusion on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle. <b>Pancreatic adenocarcinoma</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion, repeated once weekly for 7 weeks, followed by a week rest. <b>Bladder cancer, at invasive stage in combination with cisplatin</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period for a 28-day cycle, recommended dose of cisplatin 70 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 2, then repeat cycle. <b>Breast cancer</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered on day 1 over approx 3 hrs IV infusion, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. <b>Ovarian cancer, in combination with carboplatin</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion, administered on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, after gemcitabine, carboplatin should be given on day 1."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Renal failure. Concomitant use with radiotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform hematological tests before each administration. Impaired bone-marrow function, liver failure. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Myelosuppression, hematological and GI effects, mild proteinuria and hematuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for IV infusion 200 mg, 1 g."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4081,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4081,
        "brand_name": "Gemzar",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gemcitabine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), first-line therapy alone or in combination with cisplatin; cervical cancer in combination with cisplatin; epithelial ovarian carcinoma in combination with carboplatin in patients with relapsed disease following a recurrence-free interval of at least 6 months after platinum-based, first-line therapy; adenocarcinoma of pancreas; 5-FU refractory pancreatic cancer. Treatment of patients with bladder cancer; advanced breast cancer; unresectable, locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who have relapsed following adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy in combination with paclitaxel or following chemotherapy for metastatic disease as monotherapy. Has shown activity in renal cancer, alone or in combination; advanced small cell lung cancer and advanced refractory testicular cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>NSCLC – Monotherapy:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins. Repeat once weekly for 3 weeks, followed by 1-week rest period. Repeat 4-week cycle; <b>Combination with cisplatin (2 dosage schedules) - 3-week cycle:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8, followed by 1 week rest period, then repeat cycle; <b>4-week cycle:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle; <b>With carboplatin:</b> 1,000 or 1,200 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, given by 30-min infusion on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Carboplatin is given on day 1 after gemcitabine. <b>Pancreatic cancer:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins. Repeat once weekly up to 7 weeks, followed by 1 week of rest. On subsequent cycles, give inj once weekly for 3 consecutive weeks out of every 4 weeks. <b>Bladder cancer - Monotherapy:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Repeat 4-week cycle; <b>Combination with cisplatin:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period for 28 day cycle; <b>Cisplatin:</b> 70 mg/m<sup>2</sup> at day 2. Repeat 4-week cycle. <b>Breast cancer – Combination with paclitaxel:</b> Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 1 over approx 3-hr IV infusion, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Patients should have &ge;1,500 x 10<sup>6</sup>/L absolute granulocyte count prior to initiation of combination therapy. <b>Cervical cancer (neoadjuvant treatment and metastatic disease) – Combination with cisplatin:</b> Cisplatin 70 mg/m2 on day 1, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 every 21 days. Repeat 3-week cycle; <b>Combination therapy using radiation – with cisplatin:</b> 40 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, followed immediately by gemcitabine 125 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion once weekly for 6 weeks (days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, and 36), 1-2 hrs before concurrent pelvic radiation therapy. <b>Ovarian cancer – Combination with carboplatin:</b> Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. After gemcitabine, give carboplatin on day 1 to attain target AUC of 4 mg/mL min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; concurrent liver metastases or pre-existing history of hepatitis, alcoholism, liver cirrhosis. Can suppress bone marrow function. Induce hemolytic uremic syndrome, adult respiratory distress syndrome, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Discontinue when capillary leak syndrome, interstitial pneumonitis, pulmonary edema occur. Monitor platelet, leukocyte, and granulocyte counts prior to each dose; renal and hepatic function periodically. Childn. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia. Abnormal liver function tests, nausea, vomiting, mild proteinuria, hematuria, rash, fever, headaches, chills, myalgia, asthenia, anorexia, edema/peripheral edema, alopecia, cough, rhinitis, malaise, sweating, diarrhea, stomatitis, febrile neutropenia, dyspnea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IV) 200 mg, 1 g."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Sulfonylureas"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of non-insulin-dependent (Type 2) diabetes mellitus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Initially 1 or 2 mg once daily with breakfast or the first main meal; <b>Maintenance:</b> 1-4 mg once daily. Max 6 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Type 2 DM patients with ketoacidosis, and those with severe infection, stress, trauma, and other severe conditions where it is unlikely to control hyperglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for Type 1 DM. Perform hepatic and hematological monitoring. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, heartburn, anorexia, diarrhea; skin rashes, pruritus, photosensitivity; altered liver enzyme values, cholestatic jaundice; leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, hemolytic anemia, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, erythema nodosum."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Epinephrine, aminoglutethimide, chlorpromazine, corticosteroids, diazoxide, oral contraceptives, rifamycins and thiazide diuretics. Beta-blockers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 2 mg (P10.00), 3 mg (P11.00)."
          }

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients inadequately controlled on their maximal tolerated dose of metformin alone or those already being treated with the combination of sitagliptin and metformin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dose. Max 100 mg/day of sitagliptin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to sitagliptin and metformin. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis, with or without coma. Patients undergoing radiologic studies involving intravascular administration of iodinated contrast materials. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with type 1 diabetes or for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis. Acute pancreatitis, including fatal and nonfatal hemorrhagic or necrotizing pancreatitis. Hypoxic states, surgical procedures, alcohol intake. Patients with type 2 diabetes who develop laboratory abnormalities or clinical illness. <b>Sitagliptin:</b> Hypoglycemia in combination with sulfonylurea or insulin. Bullous pemphigoid. <b>Metformin:</b> Lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia, use in concomitant medication that may affecting renal function or metformin disposition. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels at 2-3 yr intervals. Child < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, hypoglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Glyburide, furosemide, nifedipine, digoxin, OCT2 or multidrug and toxin extrusion inhibitors (e.g. ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine). Thiazide and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, and isoniazid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P19.50), 100 mg/1 g (P37.50)."
          }

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For management of type 2 diabetes mellitus: Monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone and for whom metformin is inappropriate due to contraindications or intolerance; Dual therapy with metformin, sulfonylurea, or PPAR-gamma (e.g. thiazolidinediones); Triple therapy with metformin and sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "100 mg once daily. Consider lower doses for sulfonylurea or insulin if co-administered. <b>Renal impairment</b> - Moderate (CrCl 30-50 mL/min): 50 mg once daily; Severe (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) or ESRD requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 25 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used in type 1 DM or diabetic ketoacidosis. Risk of acute pancreatitis. Hypoglycemia with other hypoglycemic agents. Renal impairment. Bullous pemphigoid may occur. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, headache."
          },
          {

            "content": "100 mg once daily. <b>In combination with metformin:</b> Given in two divided doses. Lower dose of sulphonylurea when used in combination."

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For type 2 diabetes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 30 mg daily (&frac12; of 60 mg tab) taken at breakfast, may be increased to 60, 90, or 120 mg. Adjust dose according to patient’s metabolic response (blood glucose, HbA1c). Dose increment should be at least 1 month except in patients whose blood glucose has not reduced after 2 weeks of treatment. In such cases, the dose may be increased at the end of the 2<sup>nd</sup> week of treatment. Max 120 mg/day. <b>Switching from gliclazide 80 mg tab and for patients at risk of hypoglycemia:</b> 30 mg/day. <b>In combination with biguanides, alpha glucosidase inhibitors or insulin:</b> 60 mg/day. Tabs may be split in half. Do not crush or chew."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Type 1 DM. Diabetic pre-coma and coma, diabetic ketoacidosis. Severe renal or hepatic insufficiency. Coadministration of miconazole. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients at risk of hypoglycemia. Renal and hepatic insufficiency. Dysglycemia. Patients with G6PD deficiency; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia and adrenergic counterregulation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 966,
        "brand_name": "Glucophage XR",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QuEQQZOjROWTC6XNUAZjO5sSKQieyg8OPaCXvF4hNxcrFrILJu.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QGGk34ivPNFuik5XPOUrIQYMjG3JEGbjMg5ZkjAoU4OtaYl7sf.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xUYVzO7FZ5mpEWjNBKb6ni6VMmzRuG4hOmRTWMRe5TgeDwZkZm.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Biguanides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). Prevention of type 2 DM in patients with pre-diabetes and at least 1 additional risk factor in whom lifestyle modifications alone have not reached adequate glycemic control. 1<sup>st</sup> line therapy in overweight type 2 DM adult patients. Ovulation stimulation to support conception in women with PCOS."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy and combination with other oral antidiabetic agents:</b> Initially 500 or 750 mg once daily with the evening meal. Maintenance: 1 g for patients treated with 1 g or 2 g metformin. Dose adjustment based on blood glucose measurements is recommended after 10-15 days. Recommended dose of 750 mg tab: 2 tabs once daily, may be increased to a max dose of 3 tabs daily.  Max recommended dose of 4 tabs of 500 mg or 2 tabs of 1 g daily. <b>Combination w/ insulin:</b> Initially 500 mg or 750 mg once daily. <b>Ovulation stimulation to support conception in women with PCOS:</b> 1,500-2000 mg once daily for at least 6 months. Max 2,000 mg once daily with the evening meal. <b>Monotherapy for prediabetes:</b> 1,000-1,500 mg once daily. <b>Moderate renal impairment stage 3 (CrCl 30-59 mL/min or eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>):</b> Initially 500 mg or 850 mg daily. Max 1,000 mg. Always take with food. Slow increase of dose may improve GI tolerability."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Any type of metabolic acidosis (e.g., lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma, severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), dehydration, severe infection or shock, diseases that may cause tissue hypoxia (unstable CHF, respiratory failure, recent MI or shock), hepatic insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Intravascular administration of iodinated contrast materials. Discontinue 48 hrs prior to elective major surgical interventions and may not be reinstituted until 48 hrs afterwards. Coadministration with iodinated contrast media."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Lactic acidosis. Not recommended in patients with  mitochondrial diseases e.g., Mitochondrial Encephalopathy with Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke‑like episodes (MELAS) syndrome and Maternal inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD).  Discontinue immediately in case of signs and symptoms suggestive of MELAS syndrome or MIDD after metformin administration. Monitor renal function at least every 3-6 months in patients with CrCl 45-59 mL/min or eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> and in elderly patients; at least every 3 months in patients with CrCl 30-44 mL/min or eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue 48 hrs before iodinated contrast administration in patients with CrCl < 45 mL/min or eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> for IV; CrCl < 60 mL/min or eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> for intra-arterial and prior to elective major surgery. May be reinstituted after 48 hrs if renal function is stable. Patients with heart failure. Perform lab tests for diabetes and monitor regularly. May reduce vit B<sub>12</sub> serum levels. Women of childbearing potential. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, taste disturbances. vit B<sub>12</sub> decrease/deficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol. Glucocorticoids, tetracosactides (systemic and local routes), beta<sub>2</sub>-agonists, danazol, chlorpromazine, diuretics especially loop diuretics. OCT1 inducers (e.g., rifampicin) and inhibitors (e.g., verapamil), OCT2 inhibitors (e.g., cimetidine, dolutegravir, crizotinib, olaparib, daclatasvir, vandetanib)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 500 mg, 750 mg, 1 g."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/T7HKKJgOZ5TMPVNP2DkbSKe22SRb8T4JrUcJ5qF7A5UleOTkiq.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/x8sQEHCNZFd303GdYACXtV4wIiO7mnoNTk1j867mXdBT6JGscx.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ticagrelor",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiplatelets"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of thrombotic events in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) (e.g., unstable angina, ST or non-ST elevation myocardial infarction), including patients managed medically or with percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass graft."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Management of ACS:</b> Initially 180 mg loading dose, then 90 mg twice daily during the first year after ACS event. Give 60 mg twice daily after one year. Use with maintenance dose of 75-100 mg aspirin daily. Tabs may be crushed, mixed with water, and drunk for patients unable to swallow whole tabs. Mixture can also be administered via nasogastric tube. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity (e.g., angioedema). History of intracranial hemorrhage. Active pathological bleeding (e.g., peptic ulcer or intracranial hemorrhage). Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant P2Y12 platelet inhibitor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with moderate hepatic impairment; propensity to bleed; increased risk of bradycardic events. Treatment beyond 1 yr in ACS patients with prior ischemic stroke. Increase risk of bleeding and frequency of asymptomatic ventricular pauses; dyspnea; thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. False negative result in platelet function test for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Discontinue 5 days prior to elective surgery. Premature discontinuation may increase risk of CV death, MI, or stroke. If temporarily discontinued, restart as soon as possible. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Spontaneous hematoma, hemorrhagic diathesis, hyperuricemia, dyspnea, gout, dizziness, syncope, vertigo, hypotension, epistaxis, hemoptysis, diarrhea, nausea, pruritus, increased blood creatinine. GI and post-procedural hemorrhage, subcutaneous or dermal, urinary tract, traumatic bleedings."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, saquinavir, nelfinavir, indinavir, atazanavir, telithromycin), inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), aspirin, opioids, simvastatin, lovastatin, atorvastatin, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 90 mg (P45.00)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/c9wZSIHK2GsKaCDdcA5NLDY0dIK69MNm4MUf3O3HwlwAA4SsO4.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/BWjE05wdhGICgnbZ1qUhBXoKbWOhV7tmWr6CQDxpiGSHx1H0JC.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metformin HCl, glibenclamide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Sulfonylureas"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 DM in adults as 2<sup>nd</sup> line therapy, when diet, exercise and initial treatment with metformin or glibenclamide (or another sulfonylurea) do not result in adequate glycemic control, and as replacement for previous treatment with metformin and glibenclamide in patients whose glycemia is stable and controlled."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult Initial treatment:</b> Initially 1 tab of 500 mg/2.5 mg or 500 mg/5 mg once daily. Initial dose must not exceed the daily doses of glibenclamide (or equiv dose of another sulfonylurea) or metformin already being taken alone. <b>As replacement for previous combination therapy with metformin and sulfonylurea:</b> Initial dose must not exceed the daily dose of glibenclamide (or equiv dose of another sulfonylurea) and metformin already being  taken. Increase dose in increments of not >500 mg/5 mg daily every 2 weeks or longer. Max2,000 mg/20 mg daily. <b>Elderly:</b> Start with lowest available and increase gradually if necessary. Do not titrate to max dose. <b>Debilitated and malnourished patients:</b> Do not titrate to max dose. <b>Renal impairment CrCl30-59 mL/min or eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> Max metformin 1,000 mg daily. Closely monitor renal function every 3-6 months. Take with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Metabolic acidosis (e.g., lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma. Severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m<sup>2</sup>). Kidney insufficiency. Acute conditions with potential to alter renal function e.g. dehydration, severe infection, CV collapse (shock). Acute or chronic disease which may cause hypoxia e.g. cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, CV collapse/shock. Liver insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Porphyria. Miconazole even for local use. Congenital galactosemia, glucose and galactose malabsorption syndrome or lactase deficiency.  Congenital galactosemia, glucose and galactose malabsorption syndrome, and lactase deficiency. Coadministration with miconazole or iodinated contrast media. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Lactic acidosis. Not recommended in patients with known mitochondrial diseases e.g., Mitochondrial Encephalopathy with Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke‑like episodes (MELAS) syndrome and Maternal inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD).  Discontinue immediately in case of signs and symptoms suggestive of MELAS syndrome or MIDD after metformin administration. Hypoglycemia. Blood sugar imbalance. May reduce vit B<sub>12</sub> levels. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, infectious diseases, heart failure, and GCPD deficiency. Monitor renal function at least every 3-6 months in patients with CrCl 45-59 mL/min or eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> and in elderly patients; at least every 3 months in patients with CrCl 30-44 mL/min or eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue treatment 48 hrs before or from the time of IV administration of iodinated contrast media; 48 hrs before elective surgery. May be reinstituted after 48 hrs if renal function is stable. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly &ge;65 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, taste disturbance. Transient visual disturbances may occur at the start of treatment due to a decrease in glycemia levels. Vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Glucocorticoids, tetracosactides, beta-3-agonists, danazol, chlorpromazine, diuretics especially loop diuretics. <b>Glibenclamide:</b> Alcohol, phenylbutazone, bosentan, beta-blockers, clonidine, reserpine, guanethidine, sympathomimetics,  fluconazole, desmopressin, colesevelam, ARBs (e.g., captopril, enalapril). <b>Metformin:</b> OCT1 inhibitors (e.g., verapamil) and inducers (e.g., rifampicin), OCT2 inhibitors (e.g., cimetidine, dolutegravir, crizotinib, olaparib, daclatasvir, vandetanib)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg/5 mg, 500 mg/2.5 mg."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy or in combination with other oral antidiabetic agents or insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Initially 500 mg or 850 mg 2-3x daily, with or after meals; after 10 to 15 days, may be increased by increments of 1 tab. Max 3 g daily in 3 divided doses. <b>Childn &gt;10 yrs</b>: 500 mg. Max 2 g daily in 2-3 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Type 1 DM. Diabetic coma. Ketoacidosis. Renal insufficiency. Stress, trauma, or other severe conditions unlikely to control hyperglycemia. Heart failure. Dehydration. Acute or chronic alcoholism. Conditions predisposing to lactic acidosis. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of lactic acidosis. Determine CrCl before initiating treatment. Discontinue 48 hrs before major surgery and resume 48 hrs post-op or after resumption of oral nutrition, if renal function is normal. Confirm diagnosis of type 2 DM before treating childn and adolescents. Avoid alcohol consumption. Inform physician of any infectious diseases (e.g., influenza, RTI, UTI). Continue diet with regular carbohydrate intake. Overweight patients should maintain energy-restricted diet. Perform regular lab tests for diabetes monitoring. Risk of hypoglycemia when used with insulin or other oral antidiabetics (e.g., sulfonylureas, meglitinides).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, metallic taste or taste disturbance; anorexia, weight loss; lactic acidosis; erythema, pruritus, urticaria; impaired absorption of various substances (e.g., vit B<sub>12</sub>)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that may increase or decrease blood glucose levels, alcohol and alcohol-containing medications, drugs that may impair renal function, cimetidine, diuretics."
          },

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Menotrophin (human menopausal gonadotrophin)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pituitary Hormones & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Patients who have received a GnRH agonist for pituitary suppression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients who have received a GnRH agonist for pituitary suppression</b>: Initially 225 IU IM or SC. Adjust dose not more frequently than once every 2 days and not exceeding 150 IU/adjustment. Max 450 IU/day and 20 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Women with high FSH level indicating primary ovarian failure, uncontrolled thyroid and adrenal dysfunction, organic intracranial lesion e.g. pituitary tumor, sex hormone-dependent tumors of the reproductive tract and accessory organs, abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin, ovarian cysts or enlargement not due to PCOS. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Mild to moderate uncomplicated ovarian enlargement accompanied by abdominal distension and/or pain. Perform thorough gynecologic and endocrine evaluation including an assessment of pelvic anatomy before treatment. Patients with tubal obstruction should receive menotrophin only if enrolled in an IVF program. Careful examination should be made to rule out the presence of early pregnancy. Perform thorough diagnostic evaluation in patients who demonstrate abnormal uterine bleeding or other signs of endometrial abnormalities before starting therapy. Evaluation of the husband’s fertility potential should be included in the workup. Childn. Elderly. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pain/rash at injection site, headache, malaise; nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, bloating; breast tenderness, hot flushes, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (in susceptible individuals)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for solution for IM/SC injection 75 IU x 2 mL."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vaginal Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of candidal vulvovaginitis caused by <i>Candida albicans</i>, bacterial vaginosis caused by <i>Gardnerella vaginalis</i> and anaerobic bacteria, trichomonal vaginitis caused by <i>Trichomonas vaginalis</i>, and mixed vaginal infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Insert 1 suppository, in lying position, high into vagina at night for 3 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Organic neurologic disorders. Current or history of blood dyscrasia. Concomitant use with contraceptive diaphragms, condoms, and other vaginal products (e.g. tampon, douche or spermicide). Virgins and non-sexually mature young girls. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For intravaginal use only. Patients with hepatic failure; CV disorders. May induce transient leukopenia and neutropenia; heart rhythm disorders, difficulty breathing, coma, and death when applied on large skin surfaces under occlusion. Simultaneously treat sexual partners with <i>Trichomonas vaginalis</i>. Do not take alcohol during and 3 days after treatment due to possible disulfiram-like reactions. Breastfeeding can be restarted 72 hrs after treatment. Childn < 12 yrs. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Weakness, fatigue, malaise, headache, dizziness; metallic/bitter taste, nausea, anorexia, loss of appetite, flatulence, dyspepsia, abdominal cramp, epigastric discomfort, vomiting, constipation; darkened urine."

      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 157,
        "brand_name": "H2Bloc",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nsmNtD0Xg4Y0yA5wxfdmLnrJTeZeYlgKxvkMCWeojUhvcXwTks.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/vMyxQoio1qrzbRbkerYkvehejlA8oyb72gTe3j63RpXUZET95o.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DUUZpY5eVSd3kbjPkZ86nYWklxXW975L2uUb4QzyAoYNvyBVvz.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Famotidine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "H2-Receptor Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Short-term treatment of active duodenal ulcer, active benign gastric ulcer, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with or without esophagitis. Maintenance therapy of duodenal ulcer after healing of an active ulcer and GERD. Treatment of pathological hypersecretory conditions (e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, multiple endocrine adenomas). <b>IV/IM</b>: For hospitalized patients with pathological hypersecretory conditions or intractable ulcers. Short-term treatment when oral medication is not feasible; of upper gastrointestinal bleeding due to esophagitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab - Ulcer – Adults</b>: 40 mg once daily at bedtime or 20 mg twice daily for 4-8 weeks; Maintenance: 20 mg/day at bedtime; <b>Childn 1-16 yrs</b>: Initially 0.5 mg/kg/day as single dose at night or in 2 divided dose. Max 40 mg/day. <b>GERD – Adults</b>: 20 mg twice daily (morning and bedtime) for 6-12 weeks. Max 40 mg twice daily if there is esophageal erosion or ulceration; <b>Childn 1-16 yrs</b>: 0.5 mg/kg twice daily. Max 40 mg twice daily. <b>Pathological hypersecretory conditions</b>: 20 mg every 6 hrs, increased as necessary and continued as long as it is clinically indicated; doses up to 800 mg/day have been used. <b>IM/IV</b> - Administered via slow IV injection for &ge;2 mins, slow IV infusion for 15-30 mins, or IM injection. <b>Adults</b>: 20 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Childn 1-16 yrs</b>: Initially 0.25 mg/kg every 12 hrs. Max 40 mg/day. <b>Patients with renal impairment</b>: Reduce dose by 50% or prolong dosing to 36-48 hrs. Patients undergoing dialysis: Reduce dose by 50%. Tabs should be administered at the end of dialysis session or later."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment; duodenal and benign gastric ulcer. Risk of CAP or hospital-acquired pneumonia. Gastric malignancy should be excluded prior to therapy initiation. Monitor blood count and liver function during prolonged high-dose therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids, atazanavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole, probenecid, sucralfate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 20 mg (P23.01). Powder for IM/IV injection 20 mg (P204.33)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KOOB2IDfChEsPkC5nFjPMZ02BjoOwWWurmGbNBk8kvPbGUDt1h.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/1SSy6FkIwNlnr31GwEZJZgfVQK5gOO9S5kroBhTsipbV7Doxct.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gliclazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Sulfonylureas"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Non-insulin dependent type II diabetes in adults when dietary measures, physical exercise and weight loss alone are not sufficient to control blood glucose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 30 mg (half-tab) daily. If blood glucose is not adequately controlled, the dose may be increased to 60, 90, or 120 mg daily, the interval between each dose increment should be at least 1 month. Max: 120 mg daily. <b>Switching from another oral antidiabetic agent to gliclazide MR 60 mg tab:</b> Initially 30 mg daily, followed by a stepwise increase in dose, depending on the metabolic response. <b>Combination treatment with other antidiabetic agents:</b> 60 mg daily. Can be given in combination with biguanides, alpha glucosidase inhibitors or insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to gliclazide, other sulfonylurea or sulfonamides. Type 1 diabetes, diabetic pre-coma and coma, diabetic keto-acidosis. Severe hepatic and renal insufficiency. Treatment with miconazole. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, irregular meal time, imbalance between physical exercise and carbohydrate intake. Renal and hepatic insufficiency. Dysglycemia; concomitant treatment with fluroquinolones, especially with elderly. Patients with G6PD-deficiency. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia. GI disturbances. Rash, pruritus, urticaria, angioedema, erythema, maculopapular rashes, bullous reactions (e.g. SJS and toxic epidermal necrolysis), and exceptionally, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). Raised hepatic enzymes levels (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase). Transient visual disturbances. Cases of erythrocytopenia, agranulocytosis, hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia, allergic vasculitis, hyponatremia, elevated liver enzymes levels and even impairment of liver function (e.g. with cholestasis and jaundice) and hepatitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Miconazole. Phenylbutazone. Alcohol. Insulins, acarbose, metformin, thiazolidinediones, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, beta-blockers, fluconazole, ACE inhibitors (captopril, enalapril), H2-receptor antagonists, MAOIs, sulfonamides, clarithromycin and NSAIDs. Danazol. Chlorpromazine. Glucocorticoids and tetracosactrin. Ritodrine, salbutamol, terbutaline. St. John’s wort. Fluroquinolones. Anticoagulant therapy (e.g. warfarin)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Maintenance for the relief of symptoms and reduction of exacerbations in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Once-daily inhalation of 1 cap using the inhaler at approx same time each day. Max 1 dose/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Caps must not be swallowed or used with other inhalers. Not indicated for asthma and acute episodes of bronchospasm.           },
          {

          },
          {

          },

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment for patients with Type 2 DM as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control or in combination with other antidiabetic agents. Treatment of heart failure in patients with reduced ejection fraction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy:</b> 10 mg once daily. <b>Patients with severe hepatic impairment:</b> 5 mg. May be increased to 10 mg. <b>Patients at risk for volume depletion:</b> 5 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with type 1 DM, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, end-stage renal disease (ESRD), or patients on dialysis. Pregnancy and lactation. Childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Female genital mycotic infections, nasopharyngitis, UTI."

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10 mg/5 mg once daily, may be increased to 25 mg/5 mg once daily in patients requiring additional glycemic control. Lower dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM. Patients with higher risk or history of ketoacidosis; CV disease, on antihypertensive with history of hypotension. Hypoglycemia, pancreatitis. Not recommended for eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue treatment if ketoacidosis, Fournier's gangrene, pancreatitis, or bullous pemphigoid is suspected. Temporary interruption in complicated UTI or until fluid loss is corrected. Assess renal function prior to initiation and periodically during treatment. Monitor ketones, vol status, and electrolytes. Elderly &ge;75 yrs. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "UTI, genital infections, Fournier’s gangrene, nasopharyngitis; angioedema, urticaria; hypoglycemia,  ketoacidosis; increased urination, dysuria; cough; rash, pruritus, bullous pemphigoid; constipation,  pancreatitis, mouth ulceration; vol depletion; thirst; decreased GFR and increased blood creatinine,  lipase, amylase, hematocrit, serum lipids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Insulin, sulfonylureas, thiazide and loop diuretics, lithium, UGT inducers, P-gp, and CYP3A4 inducers  (e.g. rifampicin)."
          },
          {

  {
    "id": 3772,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3772,
        "brand_name": "Gouter",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ukFYmw6BOSCTq8B1nG99ME7nhSks3b7gD7uFRTXFQ6AorBG7aS.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/59wpQUS0nb9KU4FVMArUWyNgdzGruj9DSxOt6L0j4ix5PIPREV.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/RiRZWufZZznrGLpGR7fgGNV7gzeGqyEiT7UP7qQtKetjM69kSa.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Colchicine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antigout Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of acute gout and prophylaxis of acute attacks, particularly during the 1<sup>st</sup> few months of treatment with allopurinol or uricosurics. For Amyloidosis, Behcet’s syndrome, familial Mediterranean fever, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, pericarditis, primary biliary cirrhosis and pyoderma gangrenosum."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute gout attacks:</b> Initially 1 mg, then 0.5 mg every 2-3 hrs until pain relief or if GI adverse effects occur. Max 10 mg. May repeat the course after at least 3 days. Initially 0.5-1.2 mg, then 0.5 or 0.6 mg every 1-2 hrs or 1-1.2 mg every 2 hrs until pain relief or if GI adverse effects occur. <b>Short-term prophylaxis:</b> 500 mcg or 600 mcg 1-3x daily. <b>Mild to moderate renal impairment:</b> Reduce dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Blood dyscrasias. Severe renal (including hemodialysis patients) and hepatic impairment (except in familial Mediterranean fever). Concomitant use with P-gp inhibitors or CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for SC or IM inj. Patients with cardiac, hepatic, renal or GI disease. Elderly and debilitated patients.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain. Bone marrow depression with agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia and aplastic anemia on prolonged treatment, and local reactions (e.g. thrombophlebitis and neuritis). Extravasation may cause tissue necrosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Statins, fibrates, digoxin; cimetidine, tolbutamide; vit B<sub>12</sub>; phenylbutazone; NSAIDs; cytolytic antineoplastic agents; CYP3A4 or P-gp inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin, erythromycin, ritonavir, atazanavir, verapamil, diltiazem, ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, ciclosporin, disulfiram). Grapefruit juice, alcohol. False positive results in urine tests for erythrocytes or HgB levels. May interfere with urinary determination of 17-hydroxycorticosteroids using the Reddy, Jenkins and Thom procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 500 mcg (P4.50)."
          }
        ],

        "id": 3772,
        "brand_name": "Gouter",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ukFYmw6BOSCTq8B1nG99ME7nhSks3b7gD7uFRTXFQ6AorBG7aS.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/59wpQUS0nb9KU4FVMArUWyNgdzGruj9DSxOt6L0j4ix5PIPREV.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/RiRZWufZZznrGLpGR7fgGNV7gzeGqyEiT7UP7qQtKetjM69kSa.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Colchicine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antigout Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of acute gout and prophylaxis of acute attacks, particularly during the 1<sup>st</sup> few months of treatment with allopurinol or uricosurics. For Amyloidosis, Behcet’s syndrome, familial Mediterranean fever, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, pericarditis, primary biliary cirrhosis and pyoderma gangrenosum."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute gout attacks:</b> Initially 1 mg, then 0.5 mg every 2-3 hrs until pain relief or if GI adverse effects occur. Max 10 mg. May repeat the course after at least 3 days. Initially 0.5-1.2 mg, then 0.5 or 0.6 mg every 1-2 hrs or 1-1.2 mg every 2 hrs until pain relief or if GI adverse effects occur. <b>Short-term prophylaxis:</b> 500 mcg or 600 mcg 1-3x daily. <b>Mild to moderate renal impairment:</b> Reduce dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Blood dyscrasias. Severe renal (including hemodialysis patients) and hepatic impairment (except in familial Mediterranean fever). Concomitant use with P-gp inhibitors or CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for SC or IM inj. Patients with cardiac, hepatic, renal or GI disease. Elderly and debilitated patients.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain. Bone marrow depression with agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia and aplastic anemia on prolonged treatment, and local reactions (e.g. thrombophlebitis and neuritis). Extravasation may cause tissue necrosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Statins, fibrates, digoxin; cimetidine, tolbutamide; vit B<sub>12</sub>; phenylbutazone; NSAIDs; cytolytic antineoplastic agents; CYP3A4 or P-gp inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin, erythromycin, ritonavir, atazanavir, verapamil, diltiazem, ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, ciclosporin, disulfiram). Grapefruit juice, alcohol. False positive results in urine tests for erythrocytes or HgB levels. May interfere with urinary determination of 17-hydroxycorticosteroids using the Reddy, Jenkins and Thom procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 500 mcg (P4.50)."
          }
        ],
