  {
    "id": 3900,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3900,
        "brand_name": "Hemactiv",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Epoetin alfa",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hematopoietic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF). Treatment of anemia in patients receiving chemotherapy and to reduce transfusion requirements. To increase the yield of autologous blood in adults in pre donation program (given only to patients with moderate anemia [Hgb 10-13 g/dL or 6.2-8.1 mmol/L], no iron deficiency). Reduce exposure to allogeneic blood transfusions in non-iron deficient adults with anticipated high-risk transfusion complications who will undergo major elective orthopedic surgery (given to patients with moderate anemia and do not have an autologous pre donation program)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients with CRF (available venous access: IV; no available venous access: SC)</b> - <b>Starting dose</b> - Adults: 50-100 IU/kg 3x a week; Childn: 25-50 IU/kg 3x a week. <b>Correction phase:</b> 50 IU/kg 3x a week. Adjust dose in increments or decrements of 25 IU/kg 3x a week at intervals of 4 weeks. Maintenance phase: Desired Hgb levels is 10-12 g/dL (6.2-7.5 mmol/L). Recommended total weekly dose is 75-300 IU/kg. <b>Adult cancer patients with anemia (Hgb < 10 g/dL):</b> Initially, 150 IU/kg SC 3x a week. If after 4 weeks, Hgb increased at least 1 g/dL (0.62 mmol/L) or reticulocytes count increased &ge;40,000 cells/microL above baseline, maintain dosage. Increase to 300 IU/kg 3x a week if Hgb increased < 1mg/dL (<0.62 mmol/L) and the reticulocytes count increased < 4,000 cells/microL. If after an additional 4 weeks with 300 IU/kg 3x a week, Hgb increased &ge;1 g/dL and reticulocytes count increased < 40,000 cells/microL, maintain dosage. If Hgb increased < 1 g/dL and reticulocytes count increased < 40,000 cells/microL, discontinue treatment. <b>Adult surgery patients in an autologous pre-donation program:</b> 300-600 IU/kg IV injection 2x a week for 3 weeks with at least 200 mg of elemental iron. <b>Adults scheduled for elective surgery:</b> 600 IU/kg SC injection weekly for 3 weeks (Days 21, 14, and 7) prior and the day of surgery. If planned time before surgery is shortened to < 3 weeks, administer 300 IU/kg daily for 10 consecutive days prior and the day of surgery and for 4 days immediately after surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to epoetin alfa, and products derived from mammalian cells or albumin. Uncontrolled HTN. Patients scheduled for major elective surgery, not participating in autologous blood pre-donation and not having CAD, PAD, carotid arterial disease or stroke, including patients with recent MI or stroke. Surgical patients who for any reason cannot receive adequate antithrombotic prophylaxis. Patients developing pure red cell aplasia with any erythropoietin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Control BP before initiation and during treatment. Advice patients on importance of compliance with antihypertensive therapy and dietary restrictions. Patients with epilepsy, history of seizures, conditions associated with predisposition to seizure activity as CNS infections or brain metastases. Patients with pure red cell aplasia receiving erythropoietin via SC injection. Patients with gout and chronic liver disease. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased BP or worsening of pre-existing HTN. Increased incidence of thrombotic vascular events. Hypersensitivity reactions, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, pyrexia, chills, injection site reactions, headache and flu-like syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin. Anti-anemia agents. Drugs lowering erythropoiesis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV/SC) 4,000 IU/mL (P900.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 215,
          "name": "The Cathay YSS Distributors Co., Inc."
        },

  {
    "id": 2990,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2990,
        "brand_name": "Hemostan",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OfLDVtu3ZHJFKm3ZrcJpg4QcBgQrEG7rTav68bKiZCu4CrPI2O.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wC6kdnL4xZWqOXN2rsBdWuFyPFMsUi0JuJIOjHunSUgrA1yyc9.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hdAaMd5OIkf8iKrx1J1TE2WBqJmc2q8qln7PD8EchRWfFyjlft.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tranexamic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hemostatics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment and control of excessive bleeding in various surgical and medical conditions including general surgical cases, cardiovascular surgery (e.g. coronary artery bypass graft [CABG], valvular heart surgery, correction of congenital heart disease, thoracic aortic surgery), pulmonary surgery, orthopedic surgery (knee replacement/arthroplasty, total hip replacement/arthroplasty, scoliosis surgery), traumatic injuries, operative procedures on the lungs, bladder, uterus, thyroid, ovaries, adrenals, kidney, liver, brain, lymph nodes, soft tissues; menorrhagia, metrorrhagia, postpartum hemorrhage, conisation of the cervix), epistaxis, gastrointestinal (GI) hemorrhage, hematuria, hereditary angioneurotic edema, tooth extraction, dental surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Adults - General surgical cases</b>: 0.5-1 g (10-15 mg/kg BW) IV every 8-12 hrs for the first few days immediately after surgery then 1-1.5 g orally every 6-8 hrs. <b>CABG</b>: 1 g by IV bolus or 30 mg/kg IV before surgery if treated with aspirin; during surgery 200 mg/hr by IV infusion. <b>Valvular heart surgery</b>: 100 mg/kg IV before surgery. <b>Thoracic aortic surgery</b>: 1 g IV before skin incision, 400 mg/hr by IV infusion during operation and 500 mg in the pump priming. <b>Knee replacement/arthroplasty</b>: 10 mg/kg IV before surgery, another 10 mg/kg IV 3 hrs after surgery. <b>Total hip replacement/arthroplasty</b>: Initially 10 mg/kg IV bolus before surgery, 2<sup>nd</sup> IV bolus of 10 mg/kg 3 hrs later; continuous IV infusion of 1 mg/kg/hr for 10 hrs after surgery. <b>Scoliosis surgery</b>: Initial 10 mg/kg by IV injection and IV infusion of 1 mg/kg/hr. <b>Prostatectomy</b>: 0.5-1 g IV every 8 hrs during surgery up to 3 days after, then orally, 1 to 1.5 g every 6-8 hrs until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. <b>Menorrhagia/metrorrhagia</b>: 1-1.5 g orally every 6-8 hrs for 3-4 days. <b>Post-partum hemorrhage</b>: 1 g IV. If bleeding continues, repeat 1 g after 30 mins, then 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs. <b>Conisation of the cervix</b>: 1.5 g orally every 8 hrs for 12-14 days. <b>Epistaxis</b>: 1.5 g orally every 8 hrs for 4-10 days. <b>GI hemorrhage</b>: 1 g IV every 4 hrs for max of 3 days, then 1.5 g orally every 6 hrs for max of 4 days. <b>Hematuria</b>: 1-1.5 g orally every 8-12 hrs until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. <b>Hereditary angioneurotic edema</b>: 1-1.5 g orally every 8-12 hrs as intermittent or continuous treatment depending on the prodromal symptoms of the patient. <b>Dental surgery in patients with coagulopathies</b>: 10 mg/kg IV immediately before surgery; after surgery 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs for 6-8 days. <b>Renal insufficiency - Serum creatinine of 1.36-2.83 mg/dL</b>: 10 mg/kg IV twice daily or 15 mg/kg orally twice daily; <b>2.83-5.66 mg/dL</b>: 10 mg/kg IV once daily or 15 mg/kg orally once daily. <b>&gt;5.66 mg/dL</b>: 10 mg/kg IV every 48 hrs or 5 mg/kg IV every 24 hrs; 15 mg/kg orally every 48 hrs or 7.5 mg/kg orally every 24 hrs. <b>Childn – IV</b>: 10 mg/kg twice to thrice daily. <b>Oral</b>: 25 mg/kg twice to thrice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active thromboembolic disease (e.g. DVT, pulmonary embolism, cerebral thrombosis). History of thrombosis or thromboembolism (e.g., retinal vein or artery occlusion) or intrinsic risk of thrombosis or thromboembolism (e.g. thrombogenic valvular disease, thrombogenic cardiac rhythm disease, hypercoagulopathy) unless being treated with anticoagulants. Patients receiving thrombin because of increased risk of thrombosis, with acquired color vision disturbances, with subarachnoid hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with high risk of thrombosis, renal insufficiency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, subarachnoid hemorrhage, irregular menstrual bleeding. Indissoluble clots may develop in body cavities due to extravascular clots. May cause convulsions, severe allergic reactions, visual abnormalities (with prolonged use). Concomitant use with hormonal contraceptives, Factor IX complex concentrates or anti-inhibitor coagulant, all-trans retinoic acid (in women with acute promyelocytic leukemia). May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B. <b>IV</b>: Do not mix with blood or solutions containing penicillin.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances e.g. nausea, diarrhea, vomiting."
          },

        "content": "L-Ornithine-L-Aspartate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>IV infusion:</b> Treatment of hyperammonemia as a result of acute and chronic liver disease e.g. liver cirrhosis, fatty liver, hepatitis, especially for the treatment of incipient disturbances of consciousness (pre-coma) or neurological complications (hepatic encephalopathy). <b>Granules for oral solution:</b> Treatment of concomitant disease and sequelae due to impaired hepatic detoxification activity (e.g. cirrhosis of the liver) with symptoms of latent and manifest hepatic encephalopathy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IV infusion:</b> Up to 4 amps/day; <b>Precoma or coma:</b> Up to 8 amps, may be given in 24 hrs. Max infusion rate: 5 g/hr. <b>Granules for oral solution:</b> Dissolve contents of 1-2 sachets in plenty of fluids (e.g. a glass of water, tea or juice) and taken up to 3x daily, with or after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severely impaired renal function (serum Cr >3 mg/100 mL). <b>IV infusion:</b> Not to be administered into artery. <b>Granules for oral solution:</b> Rare hereditary fructose intolerance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "No more than 6 amps should be dissolved per 500 mL infusion. Patients with hepatic impairment. Monitor serum and urine urea levels (at high doses). May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Granules for oral solution:</b> Patients with DM. May cause dental caries in long-term use. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 5 g/10 mL. Granules for oral solution 3 g."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/U0FqqDcOutfvR4X0ZNquWaxH046LIqSxJkKbbE6uGNwgdGmCNL.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Hepatitis B immunoglobulin (human)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatitis A & B Immunoglobulins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prophylaxis against hepatitis B after exposure to HBsAg hepatitis in neonates."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer by IM injection. <b>Following exposure to HBsAg - Adults:</b> 1,000-2,000 IU IM; should be increased or repeated if necessary. <b>Childn:</b> 32-28 IU/kg BW. Administer within 7 days after exposure to HBsAg (preferably within 48 hrs). <b>Neonates - Initial dose:</b> 100-200 IU; first dose administered within 5 days after birth preferably within 48 hrs; for 1 mL doses injections should be done at 2 different sites (0.5 mL per site). <b>Booster dose:</b> 32-48 IU/kg BW; administered between 2 and 3 months after the first administration. Injection should be done at 2 different sites at 0.5 mL per site."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "HBsAg positive individuals (except neonates)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with immunoglobulin A deficiency syndrome. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Local pain, swelling, and induration. Rash, fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Defer for approx 3 months after administration of hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection 100 IU/0.5 mL."
          }

        "content": "Tenofovir alafenamide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For treatment of chronic hepatitis B in adults and adolescents (>12 yrs with BW &ge;35 kg). Patients on hemodialysis: Administer after completion of hemodialysis treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents (>12 yrs with BW >35):</b> 1 tab once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Does not prevent risk of HBV transmission. Patients with decompensated liver disease and who have a Child-Pugh Turcotte (CPT) score >9 (i.e. class C). Exacerbation of hepatitis. Cirrhosis. Patient coinfected with HBV and hepatitis C or D virus. Hepatitis B and HIV coinfection. Patients with lactose intolerance, rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min on dialysis to < 30 mL/min). Nephrotoxicity. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dizziness. Diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, abdominal distention, flatulence. Increase ALT. Rash, pruritus, angioedema, urticaria. Arthralgia. Fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Tenofovir disoproxil, tenofovir alafenamide or adefovir dipivoxil. P-gp inducers (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital or St. John's wort). Carbamazepine. Oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital. Phenytoin. Itrazonazole, ketonazole. Rifapentine."
          },
          {

  {
    "id": 2966,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2966,
        "brand_name": "Hemanex",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Q8RV8WqjqoHFqS2IzXWBtNQ6pvbcW8fFbQZZAkRWnYiRGHAhsI.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Cjr0vLoUHfJvTJDDZyB1khkGpGje3UrwKJc69fCzVJj7uYy466.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/fhr8bDmO63lhZJMSkkkVn6ZpIBfXIYkYfE3oXegc0oEPPm77Ie.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tranexamic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hemostatics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment and control of excessive bleeding in various surgical and medical conditions including general surgical cases, cardiovascular surgery (e.g. coronary artery bypass graft surgery, valvular heart surgery, correction of congenital heart disease, thoracic aortic surgery), pulmonary surgery, orthopedic surgery (e.g. knee replacement, total hip replacement, scoliosis surgery), traumatic injuries, other operative procedures on the prostate, bladder, uterus, thyroid, ovaries, adrenals, kidneys, liver, lymph nodes and soft tissues; menorrhagia/menometrorrhagia, postpartum hemorrhage, abortion, conization of the cervix, epistaxis, hemoptysis, peptic ulcer disease with hemorrhage, hematuria, blood dyscrasias with hemorrhage, hereditary angioneurotic edema; tooth extraction and dental surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>General surgical cases</b>: 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs. <b>Prostatectomy</b>: 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. <b>Menorrhagia/menometrorrhagia</b>: 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs for 3-4 days. <b>Postpartum hemorrhage</b>: 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs. <b>Conization of the cervix</b>: 1.5 g every 8 hrs for 12-14 days after surgery. <b>Epistaxis</b>: 1.5 g every 8 hrs for 4-10 days. <b>Gastrointestinal hemorrhage</b>: 1.5 g every 6 hrs for max of 4 days. <b>Hematuria</b>: 1-1.5 g every 8-12 hrs daily until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. <b>Hereditary angioneurotic edema</b>: 1-1.5 g every 8-12 hrs as intermittent or continuous treatment depending on the prodromal symptoms of the patient. <b>Dental surgery in patients with coagulopathies</b>: 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs for 6-8 days after surgery. <b>Childn</b>: 25 mg/kg/dose twice or thrice daily, depending on the indication. <b>Renal insufficiency</b> - Serum creatinine &gt;5.66 mg/dL: 15 mg/kg every 48 hrs or 7.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs; 2.83-5.66 mg/dL: 15 mg/kg once daily; 1.36-2.83 mg/dL: 15 mg/kg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active or history of thromboembolic disease. Patients receiving thrombin, with acquired disturbances of color vision, subarachnoid hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform ophthalmological examination before and at regular intervals (prolonged treatment). Renal insufficiency. Hematuria caused by disease of renal parenchyma, urinary tract obstruction due to clot formation from severe bleeding in upper urinary tract, high risk for thrombosis, concomitant use of hormonal contraceptives, disseminated intravascular coagulation, irregular menstrual bleeding, indissoluble clots in body cavities. Women taking either factor IX complex or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates. Cerebral edema and cerebral infarction in women with subarachnoid hemorrhage, acute promyelocytic leukemia treated with all-trans retinoic acid. Convulsion.  May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Childn and elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances; anemia; hypersensitivity reactions; nervous system, eye, cardiac and vascular, respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, renal and urinary disorders; fatigue, malaise."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Thrombin, batroxobin, eptacog-alfa, hemocoagulase, hormonal contraceptives, clotting factor complexes, all-trans retinoic acid, tissue plasminogen activators, anticoagulants, fibrinolytic preparations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 500 mg (P37.50)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 591,
          "name": "BioFemme, Inc."
        },

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus: as monotherapy; in combination with metformin and/or a sulfonylurea; with insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "15-30 mg daily, may be increased to max 45 mg daily if necessary."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver function. CV disease. Substitute insulin during peri-op period. Discontinue treatment on morning of surgery and restart when oral administration is possible.   {
    "id": 2970,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2970,
        "brand_name": "Heragest",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Rd4Be6kXYdDhYqKUaqYMKt9G816FxqoxVSiNmrvLI0b4MKKlXl.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NENvpjUV5Y5uPFiE0ASYncLU2csTA0iqvHOZMyFsUOm1jE4Qfe.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DzMLaLBBOw8OGbHSIgw9TcrNrXyfHC9nkMf8o8QdXFArQAiiMj.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Progesterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Infertility and pregnancy: Provides luteal support in luteal phase defects in threatened/recurrent abortion and prevents preterm delivery. Luteal phase insufficiency: Progesterone challenge test in secondary amenorrhea, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, menstrual irregularities due to dysovulation or anovulation, pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), fibrocystic mastopathy, dysmenorrhea, pre-menopause. Postmenopausal women: Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in postmenopausal women with intact uterus receiving estrogen as hormone replacement therapy (HRT)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Oral administration - Threatened/recurrent abortion with luteal phase defect</b>: 200-600 mg daily. <b>Preterm delivery</b>: 400 mg every 6-8 hrs depending on acute phase, then supporting dose of 600 mg daily in 3 divided doses until 36<sup>th</sup> week of pregnancy. <b>Progesterone challenge test in secondary amenorrhea</b>: 400 mg daily at bedtime for 10 days. <b>Dysfunctional uterine bleeding, menstrual irregularities due to dysovulation or anovulation</b>: 200 mg once daily from 17<sup>th</sup> day of cycle for 10 days. <b>PMS, fibrocystic mastopathy, dysmenorrhea, pre-menopause</b>: 200 or 400 mg daily for 10 days (usually from 14<sup>th</sup>-17<sup>th</sup> day to complete 10 days). <b>Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in postmenopausal women with intact uterus receiving estrogen as HRT</b>: 200 mg at bedtime for 12 days sequentially per 28-day cycle. <b>Vaginal administration - Luteal support in assisted reproductive techniques (e.g. in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer)</b>: 200 mg 3x daily from embryo transfer until pregnancy is confirmed. If pregnant, continue up to the 12<sup>th</sup> week of pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Allergy to peanuts. Active liver disease especially of the obstructive type, history of known or suspected estrogen- or progestin-dependent malignant neoplasia (e.g. breast or endometrial cancer). Undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding, active or past history of arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g. stroke, MI, CHD) or VTE (i.e. DVT or pulmonary embolism), active thrombophlebitis, classical migraine, cerebral hemorrhage, partial or complete loss of vision due to ophthalmic vascular disease, missed or incomplete abortion, porphyria. Not for pregnancy test. Childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "In combination with estrogen: Should not to be used for prevention of CV disease or dementia. Patient assessment (including special attention to the breast and pelvic organs) e.g. Pap smear should be done prior to taking HRT. Endometrial biopsy should be done when indicated. Baseline tests should include mammography, measurements of blood glucose, calcium, triglycerides, cholesterol, liver function test. Discontinue if stroke occurs or expected. Possible increased risk of CV morbidity in the 1<sup>st</sup> yr of use. Increased BP. Risk factors of developing VTE. Patients with conditions that might be aggravated by fluid retention. Women with familial hyperlipidemias or porphyria. Diabetics or those with predisposition to diabetes. Patients with metabolic and malignant bone diseases associated with hypercalcemia and renal insufficiency. Increased risk of breast cancer. Women with existing breast cancer or those with a history of the disease, known risk factors associated with the development of breast cancer. Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma. May cause breakthrough bleeding and spotting bleeding during the 1<sup>st</sup>  months of treatment. Increased risk of ovarian cancer in long-term use (at least &ge;5 yrs). Discontinue if visual disturbances, classical migraine, transient aphasia, paralysis or loss of consciousness occurs. Increased risk of probable dementia in women after 65 yrs. Patients with pre-existing mental depression, discontinue if depression recurs to a serious degree. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Women &gt;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infections and infestations, breast carcinoma, jaundice; immune system, endocrine, metabolism and nutrition, psychiatric, nervous system, eye, ear and labyrinth, cardiac and vascular, respiratory, thoracic, mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, renal and urinary, and musculoskeletal and connective disorders. Pregnancy puerperium, and perinatal conditions, reproductive system and breast disorders, congenital, familial, and genetic disorders, general disorders and administration site conditions; altered coagulation tests, lipid profile, breast excisional biopsy, decreased glucose tolerance and weight; increased blood glucose level, BP, liver function tests, weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Liver enzyme inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, griseofulvin, barbiturates, hydantoins, meprobamates, phenylbutazone, rifampicin), CYP450 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole), antidiabetics, bromocriptine, ciclosporin, conjugated estrogens, St. John’s wort; hepatic function tests, coagulation tests, pregnanediol determination, thyroid function tests."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 200 mg (P73.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 591,
          "name": "BioFemme, Inc."
        },

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (acellular component), hepatitis B poliomyelitis (inactivated) and <i>Haemophilus influenzae</i> type B conjugate vaccine (adsorbed)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "DPT & Tetanus Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary and booster vaccination of infants and toddlers from 6 weeks to 24 months against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, poliomyelitis, and invasive disease caused by <i>Haemophilus influenza</i> type B."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary vaccination:</b> Either 2 inj given at an interval of two months or 3 inj given at an interval of 1-2 months (at least 4 weeks apart). <b>Booster:</b> Given at least 6 months after the last dose of the primary vaccination."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active substances, excipients, glutaraldehyde, formaldehyde, neomycin, streptomycin or polymyxin B. Not for IV or SC administration. Patients with acute illness, encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous dose of pertussis vaccine, uncontrolled neurologic disorder or uncontrolled epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with fever and collapse or shock-like state with hypotonic-hyporesponsive episode within 48 hrs, convulsions with or without fever occurring within 3 days of vaccination. Guillain-Barre syndrome, brachial neuritis following receipt of a prior vaccine containing tetanus toxoid. Acute or chronic illness including chronic renal insufficiency. Patients with immunodeficiency condition. Undiagnosed brain illness. Blood problems.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anorexia, somnolence, irritability, fever, prolonged crying, GI distress. Pain, erythema, and swelling at inj site. Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Immunosuppressants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension for injection (IM) 0.5 mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with GI bleeding, obstruction, perforation or conditions where stimulation may be dangerous. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment, significant electrolyte disturbances, conditions where the cardiac conduction intervals are impaired or could be affected and underlying cardiac diseases as congestive heart failure, when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Prolactin-releasing pituitary tumor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "QT prolongation; torsades de pointes. Risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Patients with current or history of cardiac disease; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia; ventricular arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, QTc prolongation, torsades de pointes; somnolence, headache, convulsion, extrapyramidal disorder, depression, dizziness; loss of libido, anxiety, agitation, nervousness, akathisia; dry mouth, diarrhea; anaphylactic reactions; urinary retention; rash, pruritus, urticaria, angioedema; galactorrhea, breast pain, breast tenderness, gynecomastia, amenorrhea, irregular menstruation, breast swelling, lactation disorder; oculogyric crisis; abnormal liver function test, increased blood prolactin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "QTc prolonging drugs; potent CYP3A4 inhibitors; sustained release and enteric-coated formulations; bromocriptine; antacids, antisecretory drugs, opioid analgesics (e.g. morphine, codeine), and anticholinergics; systemic azole antifungals, macrolides, SSRIs, HIV protease inhibitors, CCBs, amiodarone, aprepitant, nefazodone; atropine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P31.05)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in coronary artery disease adults with normal sinus rhythm and HR &ge;70 bpm. Indicated in adults unable to tolerate or with a contraindication to use beta-blockers or in combination with beta-blocker dose; and in chronic heart failure NYHA class II-IV with systolic dysfunction, in adult in sinus rhythm and whose HR &ge;75 bpm, in combination with standard therapy including beta-blocker therapy or when beta-blocker therapy is contraindicated or not tolerated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris – Adults < 75 yrs:</b> 5 mg twice daily. Maintenance dose: 7.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of chronic heart failure:</b> 5 mg twice daily. After 2 weeks of treatment, may be increased to 7.5 mg twice daily if resting HR is persistently >60 bpm or decreased to 2.5 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Resting HR of < 70 bpm prior to treatment, cardiogenic shock, acute MI, severe hypotension (BP < 90/50 mmHg), severe hepatic insufficiency, sick sinus syndrome, sine-atrial block, pacemaker-dependent, unstable angina, AV block of 3<sup>rd</sup> degree, heart failure. Combination with strong cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with congenital QT syndrome or treated with QT prolonging medicinal products. Moderate hepatic and severe renal insufficiency.           },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Luminous phenomena in the visual field (phosphenes), blurred vision, bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, dyspnea, muscle cramps. Hyperuricemia, eosinophilia, and elevated blood-creatinine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, oral erythromycin, nelfinavir, ritonavir, nefazodone, diltiazem, verapamil, fluconazole, rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin, St. John’s Wort."
          },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/aJqkn8sLRbag8WIapmXV5HH9NrTEZkr0iP21ObobzJdyHOxA19.jpg",

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); adults with locally advanced or metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas; patients with 5-fluorouracil refractory pancreatic cancer; bladder cancer at invasive stage. In combination with paclitaxel: Treatment of patients with unresectable, locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who have relapsed following adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy. In combination with carboplatin: Treatment of patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer who have relapse >6 months following platinum-based therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>NSCLC</b> - <b>Monotherapy</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion, repeated once weekly for 3 weeks followed by a 1-week rest period. <b>NSCLC in combination with cisplatin</b>: For 3-week cycle regimen, gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion on days 1 and 8, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle, for 4-week cycle regimen gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given by 30 mins IV infusion on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle. <b>Pancreatic adenocarcinoma</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion, repeated once weekly for 7 weeks, followed by a week rest. <b>Bladder cancer, at invasive stage in combination with cisplatin</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period for a 28-day cycle, recommended dose of cisplatin 70 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 2, then repeat cycle. <b>Breast cancer</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered on day 1 over approx 3 hrs IV infusion, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. <b>Ovarian cancer, in combination with carboplatin</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> given 30 mins IV infusion, administered on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, after gemcitabine, carboplatin should be given on day 1."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Renal failure. Concomitant use with radiotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform hematological tests before each administration. Impaired bone-marrow function, liver failure. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Myelosuppression, hematological and GI effects, mild proteinuria and hematuria."
          },

  {
    "id": 4081,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4081,
        "brand_name": "Gemzar",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gemcitabine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), first-line therapy alone or in combination with cisplatin; cervical cancer in combination with cisplatin; epithelial ovarian carcinoma in combination with carboplatin in patients with relapsed disease following a recurrence-free interval of at least 6 months after platinum-based, first-line therapy; adenocarcinoma of pancreas; 5-FU refractory pancreatic cancer. Treatment of patients with bladder cancer; advanced breast cancer; unresectable, locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who have relapsed following adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy in combination with paclitaxel or following chemotherapy for metastatic disease as monotherapy. Has shown activity in renal cancer, alone or in combination; advanced small cell lung cancer and advanced refractory testicular cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>NSCLC – Monotherapy:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins. Repeat once weekly for 3 weeks, followed by 1-week rest period. Repeat 4-week cycle; <b>Combination with cisplatin (2 dosage schedules) - 3-week cycle:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8, followed by 1 week rest period, then repeat cycle; <b>4-week cycle:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle; <b>With carboplatin:</b> 1,000 or 1,200 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, given by 30-min infusion on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Carboplatin is given on day 1 after gemcitabine. <b>Pancreatic cancer:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins. Repeat once weekly up to 7 weeks, followed by 1 week of rest. On subsequent cycles, give inj once weekly for 3 consecutive weeks out of every 4 weeks. <b>Bladder cancer - Monotherapy:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Repeat 4-week cycle; <b>Combination with cisplatin:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period for 28 day cycle; <b>Cisplatin:</b> 70 mg/m<sup>2</sup> at day 2. Repeat 4-week cycle. <b>Breast cancer – Combination with paclitaxel:</b> Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 1 over approx 3-hr IV infusion, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Patients should have &ge;1,500 x 10<sup>6</sup>/L absolute granulocyte count prior to initiation of combination therapy. <b>Cervical cancer (neoadjuvant treatment and metastatic disease) – Combination with cisplatin:</b> Cisplatin 70 mg/m2 on day 1, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 every 21 days. Repeat 3-week cycle; <b>Combination therapy using radiation – with cisplatin:</b> 40 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, followed immediately by gemcitabine 125 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion once weekly for 6 weeks (days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, and 36), 1-2 hrs before concurrent pelvic radiation therapy. <b>Ovarian cancer – Combination with carboplatin:</b> Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. After gemcitabine, give carboplatin on day 1 to attain target AUC of 4 mg/mL min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; concurrent liver metastases or pre-existing history of hepatitis, alcoholism, liver cirrhosis. Can suppress bone marrow function. Induce hemolytic uremic syndrome, adult respiratory distress syndrome, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Discontinue when capillary leak syndrome, interstitial pneumonitis, pulmonary edema occur. Monitor platelet, leukocyte, and granulocyte counts prior to each dose; renal and hepatic function periodically. Childn. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia. Abnormal liver function tests, nausea, vomiting, mild proteinuria, hematuria, rash, fever, headaches, chills, myalgia, asthenia, anorexia, edema/peripheral edema, alopecia, cough, rhinitis, malaise, sweating, diarrhea, stomatitis, febrile neutropenia, dyspnea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IV) 200 mg, 1 g."
          }

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Cap:</b> Symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhea in adults. <b>Granules for oral susp:</b> Complementary symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhea in infants (&gt;3 months) and childn together with oral rehydration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap:</b> Initially 1 cap regardless of the time of day, then 1 cap 3x daily preferably before the main meals. <b>Granules for oral susp</b> - Childn BW &gt;27 kg: two 30 mg sachets; 13-27 kg: one 30 mg sachet. Infants 9-< 13 kg: two 10 mg sachets; < 9 kg: one 10 mg sachet. All doses to be taken 3x daily. May be added to food or dispersed in a small amount of water (1 tsp), mixed well and administered immediately. Treatment should be continued until 2 normal stools are recorded, and not &gt;7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with angioedema after taking ACE inhibitors. Presence of bloody or purulent stools and fever. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Granules for oral susp:</b> Prolonged or uncontrolled vomiting. Hepatic and renal impairment. Fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome, sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency. Infants &lt;3 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Treatment of antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment. Contains lactose. <b>Granules for oral susp:</b> DM patients.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P56.75). Granules for oral suspension 10 mg (P54.75), 30 mg (P64.00)."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QnlW1qIPzThKLGE5C6lpHmZd9WTZXO1Y8kMtXs2HueAnZ44Rz5.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HFUBjlrpsxSpO7PNGJ2VJhxU2wjfF2dXiv1LyLGIZtzCgpkGtU.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Amoxicillin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of upper and lower respiratory tract infections (URTI and LRTI) including ear, nose & throat (ENT), gastrointestinal and genitourinary tract (GIT and GUT), skin and skin structure, bone, and gallbladder/biliary tract infections; <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> infections; Lyme disease. Adjunct to surgical management of dental abscess. Prophylaxis for endocarditis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 250-500 mg every 8 hrs or 500 mg every 12 hrs. Max 6 g/day in divided doses. <b>Severe or recurrent purulent RTI:</b> 3 g twice daily. <b>ENT, GUT, skin and skin structure infections -</b> Mild to moderate: 250 mg every 8 hrs or 500 mg every 12 hrs; Severe: 500 mg every 8 hrs. <b>Mild, moderate, or severe LRTI:</b> 500 mg every 8 hrs. <b><i>H. pylori</i> to reduce risk of recurrent duodenal ulcer -</b> Triple therapy: Amoxicillin 1 g with clarithromycin 500 mg and omeprazole 20 mg, all given every 12 hrs for 10 days; Dual therapy (with suspected or known clarithromycin-resistance): Amoxicillin 1 g with lansoprazole 30 mg, each given every 8 hrs for 14 days. <b>Lyme disease</b> - Isolated erythema chronicum migrans: 4 g/day; Generalized manifestations: 6 g/day. <b>Endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures:</b> 2 g given 30-60 mins before procedure. <b>Infants >3 months and childn < 40 kg:</b> 25-50 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 8 or 12 hrs. <b>ENT, GUT, skin and skin structure infections -</b> Mild to moderate: 25 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hrs or 20 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 8 hrs; Severe: 45 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hrs or 40 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 8 hrs. <b>Acute otitis media -</b> Mild, moderate, or severe: 80-90 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hrs. <b>LRTI -</b> Mild, moderate, or severe: 45 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hrs. <b>Endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures:</b> 50 mg/kg given 30-60 mins before procedure. <b>Neonates and infants &le;3 months:</b> 20-30 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hrs. <b>Renal impairment - Adults and childn &ge;40 kg -</b> CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 250 mg or 500 mg every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min: 250 mg or 500 mg every 24 hrs; <b>Childn < 40 kg:</b> CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 15 mg/kg/day every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min: 15 mg/kg/day. <b>Adults undergoing hemodialysis:</b> 250 or 500 mg every 24 hrs and an additional dose during and after each dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with infectious mononucleosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "CDAD and colitis. Maintain adequate fluid intake. Patients with renal impairment. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Infants < 3 months. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dermatologic/hypersensitivity reactions. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, black \"hairy\" tongue, tooth discoloration, CDAD, colitis. Agitation, anxiety, behavioral changes, confusion, convulsions, dizziness, reversible hyperactivity, hyperkinesia, insomnia. Anemia including hemolytic anemia. AST/ALT elevations. Acute interstitial nephritis, crystalluria. Tooth discoloration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Allopurinol, anticoagulants, bacteriostatic agents, beta-lactamase inhibitors, digoxin, methotrexate, oral contraceptives, probenecid. False positive reactions (e.g. Clinitest, Benedict’s soln)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for suspension (oral drops) 100 mg/mL x 10 mL (P98.00). Powder for suspension 125 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P114.00), 105 mL (P136.00); 250 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P165.00), 105 mL (P183.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4965,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4965,
        "brand_name": "Hofovir",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4TusF09ZBvAllLlpmkNc2mdVV1ApmgsTMupMhOuyF0byLYa5nw.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cm8M1lRbeGoSqcG4AmfsI5Dy0BTjVGhxhfckOrfAQr7IvwJfPx.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/bJBVqqeRq7iLw9ldtmZXJ8s2O2gOx2Uk1GbwaRnDDgp9EzcuK7.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral medicinal products for adults, infected adolescents 12 to 18 yrs with NRTI resistance or toxicities precluding the use of first line agents. For chronic hepatitis B with adults and adolescents 12 to < 18 yrs with compensated liver disease, with evidence of active viral replication, persistently elevated serum alanine ALT levels and histological evidence of active inflammation and fibrosis; evidence of lamivudine-resistant hepatitis B virus; decompensated liver disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult and adolescents (&ge;12 yrs with BW &ge;35 kg) – HIV-1 or chronic hepatitis B:</b> 300 mg once daily. <b>For renally impaired adult patients – CrCl 30-49 mL/min:</b> 300 mg every 48 hrs. <b>CrCl 10-29 mL/min:</b> 300 mg every 72-96 hrs. <b>Hemodialysis:</b> 300 mg every 7 days or after approx. 12 hrs of dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Does not have been proven to prevent the risk of transmission of HBV to others through sexual contact or contamination with blood. HIV antibody testing should be offered to all HBV infected patients before initiating tenofovir disproxil therapy. Renal impairment, decrease in bone mineral density. Patients with chronic hepatitis B or C, with advance liver disease or cirrhosis. Patients with decompensated live disease and have Child-Pugh-Turcotte (CPT) score &gt;9. Co-administration with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, sofosbuvir/ velpatasvir or sofosbuvir/ velpatasavir/ voxilaprevir.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, flatulence, increased transaminase, rash, asthenia, hypophosphatemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Products containing tenofovir disoproxil or tenofovir alafenamide, adefovir dipivoxil, didanosine. Aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, foscarnet, ganciclovir, pentamidine, vancomycin, cidofovir, interleukin-2, tacrolimus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 300 mg (P47.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualize concentration of albumin solution, dose, and infusion rate based on patient’s size, severity of trauma or illness, and on continuing fluid and protein losses. Administer by IV infusion, either undiluted or after dilution in isotonic solution."

          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not dilute with water for inj. Transmitting infections. Measure adequacy of circulating volume not the plasma albumin levels in determining dose. Monitor arterial BP, pulse rate, central venous pressure, pulmonary artery wedge pressure, urine output, electrolyte, and hematocrit/Hgb, regularly upon administration. Assure adequate hydration when highly concentrated albumin is administered; adequate substitution of other blood constituents if comparatively large volumes are to be replaced. Hypervolemia.   {
    "id": 1961,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1961,
        "brand_name": "Humira",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Adalimumab",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Reduction of signs and symptoms in adults with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who had inadequate response to &ge;2 DMARDs; active arthritis in adults with moderate to severe psoriatic arthritis; active ankylosing spondylitis. Treatment of adults with moderate to severe active Crohn’s disease; active ulcerative colitis; chronic plaque psoriasis; hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) (acne inversa). Treatment of non-infectious intermediate, posterior and panuveitis. <b>Childn</b>: Treatment of active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) in patients &ge;2 yrs who had inadequate response to &ge;2 DMARDs; active enthesitis-related arthritis in patients &ge;6 yrs. Reduction of signs and symptoms in childn &ge;6 yrs with moderate to severe active Crohn’s disease. Treatment of severe chronic plaque psoriasis in childn and adolescents &gt;4 yrs; active moderate to severe HS (acne inversa) in adolescents &gt;12 yrs; chronic non-infectious anterior uveitis in childn &ge;2 yrs; ulcerative colitis in childn &ge;5 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – RA, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis</b>: 40 mg SC as single dose every other week. Patients with RA not taking methotrexate: May be given 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week. <b>Crohn’s disease</b>: Initially 80 mg then 40 mg (2<sup>nd</sup> dose) on day 14. Maintenance: 40 mg on day 28 and continuing every 2 weeks. <b>Ulcerative colitis</b>: 160 mg in week 0 (given as 160 mg in one day or as 80 mg/day for 2 consecutive days); 80 mg in week 2. After induction: 40 mg every other week via SC inj. <b>Plaque psoriasis</b>: Initially 80 mg followed by 40 mg given every other week starting one week after initial dose. Reevaluate continuation of therapy after 16 weeks. <b>HS</b>: Initially 160 mg at day 1 (given as 160 mg in one day or as 80 mg per day for two consecutive days), followed by 80 mg two weeks later at day 15. Two weeks later (day 29), continue with 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week. <b>Uveitis</b>: Initially 80 mg, followed by 40 mg given every other week starting one week after initial dose. <b>Childn – pJIA (from 2 yrs)</b> - &ge;30 kg BW: 40 mg every other week; 10-30 kg BW: 20 mg every other week. Enthesitis-related arthritis (from 6 yrs) – &ge;30 kg BW: 40 mg every other week; 15-30 kg BW: 20 mg every other week. <b>Crohn’s disease</b> (from 6-17 yrs) – &ge;40 kg BW: 80 mg at week 0 and 40 mg at week 2; maintenance: 40 mg every other week. If there is need for more rapid response to therapy: 160 mg at week 0 and 80 mg at week 2. May be increased to 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week; &lt;40 kg BW: 40 mg at week 0 and 20 mg at week 2; maintenance: 20 mg every other week. If there is need for more rapid response to therapy: 80 mg at week 0 and 40 mg at week 2. May be increased to 20 mg every week. <b>Plaque psoriasis (from 4-17 yrs)</b> – &ge;30 kg BW: Initially 40 mg followed by 40 mg every other week starting one week after initial dose; 15-&lt;30 kg BW: Initially 20 mg followed by 20 mg given every other week starting one week after initial dose. Continue therapy beyond 16 weeks if patient is not responding within time period. <b>Adolescent HS (from 12 yrs)</b> – at least &lt;30 kg: 80 mg at week 0 followed by 40 mg every other week starting at week 1 via SC inj. May be increased to 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week. Continue therapy beyond 12 weeks if no improvement within time period. <b>Uveitis (&gt;2 yrs)</b> – &ge;30 kg BW: 40 mg every other week in combination with methotrexate; &lt;30 kg BW: 20 mg every other week in combination with methotrexate. <b>Ulcerative colitis (from 5-17 yrs)</b> – &ge;40 kg BW: 160 mg at week 0 and 80 mg at week 2. Maintenance: 80 mg every other week or 40 mg every week. &lt;40 kg BW: 80 mg at week 0 and 40 mg at week 2. Maintenance: 40 mg every other week or 20 mg every week."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Moderate to severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Active TB or other severe infections (e.g., sepsis, abscess, and opportunistic infections). Hepatitis B reactivation. Patients with history of recurrent infection or with underlying conditions which may predispose patients. Patients with preexisting or recent onset central (e.g., multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis) or peripheral nervous system demyelinating disease (e.g. Guillain-Barre syndrome). Coadministration of anakinra, abatacept, live vaccines. Infants exposed to adalimumab in utero should not receive live vaccines 5 months following mother’s last inj during pregnancy. Childn &lt;2 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

    "id": 3186,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3186,
        "brand_name": "Hytaz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Hydrochlorothiazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Thiazide & Thiazide-like Diuretics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Edema associated with congestive heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, corticosteroid and estrogen therapy. Edema due to various forms of renal dysfunction (e.g. nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and stable chronic renal failure). Diabetes insipidus. Control of essential hypertension (HTN)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Edema – Adults:</b> 25-100 mg daily in 1-3 divided doses; may be reduced to 25-50 mg daily or intermittently. <b>Diabetes insipidus</b> – Adults: 50-100 mg daily in 1-3 divided doses. HTN – Adults: Initially 12.5-25 mg once daily. Usual dose range 12.5-50 mg daily. Max 50 mg daily, another antihypertensive drug may be added or substituted if adequate response is not achieved. <b>Elderly >65 yrs:</b> Initially 12.5 mg once daily, adjust in increments of 12.5 mg if needed. <b>Childn 6 months-12 yrs:</b> 1-2 mg/kg daily in 1-2 divided doses. <b>< 6 months:</b> Up to 3 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses; Max 100 mg daily in children 2-12 yrs; 37.5 mg daily in childn < 2 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Anuria. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Serum electrolytes should be monitored regularly. Fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Hypokalemia, dilutional hyponatremia. May exacerbate SLE and cause idiosyncratic reactions (e.g. acute myopia, acute angle-closure glaucoma) and non-melanoma skin cancer. Patients with hepatic and renal impairment. May impair glucose tolerance. Post-sympathectomy patients. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood and lymphatic system disorders. Anaphylaxis, electrolyte imbalance and other metabolism and nutrition disorders. Insomnia and nervous system disorders. Eye, CV, respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, renal and urinary, breast and reproductive systems disorders. Asthenia, fever, weakness, increased total cholesterol, LDL-C, VLDL-C, and triglycerides."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, amantadine, aminoglycosides, diazoxide, calcium salts, vit D supplements, carbamazepine, cardiac glycosides, cholestyramine, and colestipol resins, corticosteroids, ciclosporin, lithium, pressor amines, NSAIDs (i.e. COX-2 inhibitors), skeletal muscle relaxants, SSRIs, topiramate, and iodinated contrast media. Anticholinergic, antidiabetic, antigout, cytotoxic, and other antihypertensive agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 12.5 mg (P4.93), 25 mg (P6.21)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Per sachet: Sodium chloride 520 mg, trisodium citrate dihydrate 580 mg, potassium chloride 300 mg, anhydrous glucose 2.7 g",

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For fluid and electrolyte replacement and dehydration due to diarrhea and/or vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Dissolve contents of 1 sachet in 200 mL drinking water. <b>Prevention of dehydration -</b> Adults and older childn: As much fluid as tolerated; Childn 2-10 yrs: 100-200 mL; < 2 yrs: 50-100 mL. To be given after every watery stool. <b>Treatment of dehydration -</b> Childn 2-5 yrs (12-19 kg): 900-1,400 mL; 1-2 yrs (10-< 12 kg): 700-900 mL; Infants 4-12 months (6-< 10 kg): 400-700 mL; 4 months (< 6 kg): 200-400 mL. Alternatively, multiply BW (in kg) by 75 mL to obtain approx vol of ORS to be given in the 1<sup>st</sup> 4 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discard remaining soln after 4 hrs upon reconstitution if not refrigerated and after 24 hrs if refrigerated.",

        "content": "Losartan potassium, hydrochlorothiazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN), for patients in whom combination therapy is appropriate. Reduction in the risk of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity and mortality in hypertensive patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b> - Patients who do not respond adequately to losartan/HCTZ 50 mg/12.5 mg: 1 tab once daily. <b>Reduction in the risk of CV morbidity and mortality in hypertensive patients with LVH</b>: Start dose at 50 mg of losartan once daily. If BP goal is not reached with losartan 50 mg, therapy should be titrated using a combination of losartan and a low dose of HCTZ (12.5 mg) and if needed, increased to losartan 100 mg and HCTZ 12.5 mg once daily. If necessary, the dose should be increased to losartan 100 mg and HCTZ 25 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to any component of the drug or other sulfonamide-derived drugs. Patients with anuria, hepatic and renal impairment. Coadministration with aliskiren in diabetic patients. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients who have intravascular vol depletion (e.g. those treated with high-dose diuretics), with renal impairment, bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a solitary kidney, history of hepatic impairment. Increased risk of non-melanoma skin cancer. Fetal toxicity. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C but D in 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, asthenia/fatigue, vertigo. Urticaria. Dose-related orthostatic effects, hypotension and hyperkalemia. Hypersensitivity reactions. GI, CV, hematologic, musculoskeletal, nervous, psychiatric, respiratory and dermatologic effects, neoplasm (basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs including COX2 inhibitors. Losartan: Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes. Lithium salts. Rifampin, fluconazole. HCTZ: Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, antidiabetic drugs, other antihypertensives, cholestyramine, colestipol resins, corticosteroids, ACTH, glycyrrhizin, pressor amines, skeletal muscle relaxants, lithium, aliskiren. Grapefruit Juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg/25 mg (P28.32)."

        "brand_info": [

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
