          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adults with chronic, accelerated, or blast phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) resistant to dasatinib or nilotinib; patients intolerant to dasatinib or nilotinib and for subsequent treatment with imatinib that is not clinically appropriate; or who have T315I mutation. Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) resistant to dasatinib and subsequent treatment with imatinib that is not clinically inappropriate; patients with T315I mutation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 45 mg once daily. Do not crush or dissolve tabs. May be taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Assess CV status including history and physical examination, and CV risk factors should be actively managed before starting treatment. Dose-related arterial occlusive events. Myelosuppression. Arterial occlusion in patients with increasing age, history of ischemia, HTN, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia. Patients with a history of MI, prior revascularization, or stroke. VTE, HTN, aneurysms and artery dissections, CHF, pancreatitis and serum lipase, hepatotoxicity, hemorrhage, hepatitis B reactivation, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Concurrent use with moderate and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers. Risk of bleeding events with anti-clotting agents. QT prolongation. Hepatic and renal impairment (CrCl < 50 mL/min, or ESRD). Concomitant use of moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers; anti-clotting agents. Galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Women of childbearing potential or contraception in males and females. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI; anemia, decreased platelet and neutrophil count; decreased appetite; insomnia; headache, dizziness; HTN; dyspnea, cough; abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, nausea, increased lipase; increased ALT and AST; rash, dry skin, pruritus; bone pain, arthralgia, myalgia, pain in extremity, back pain, muscle spasms; fatigue, asthenia, peripheral edema, pyrexia, pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin, indinavir, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone, nelfinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir, telithromycin, troleandomycin, voriconazole, and grapefruit juice). CYP3A inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifabutin, rifampicin, and St. John’s Wort). P-gp substrates (e.g. digoxin, dabigatran, colchicine, pravastatin) or breast cancer resistance protein substrates (e.g. methotrexate, rosuvastatin, sulfasalazine)."
          },

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/avYlSjY0uMALDnF04IkWOgbdgZA0KfhYy2UWhHmzvpAfTcsjXS.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wjPB2jeOpnBLwuXqy4ejRKTUyHWWYmz4qjP1BACbh6Yi6uCuaD.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/sCdEJeob1RoIj9EWL4L1VmENtulpK9jJMuqPPmSv8kx5aKezK7.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Celecoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For symptomatic relief in treatment of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>OA:</b> 200 mg daily as single dose or in two divided doses, may be increased to 200 mg twice daily if necessary. <b>RA:</b> Initially 200 mg daily in two divided doses, may be increased to 200 mg twice daily. <b>Ankylosing spondylitis:</b> 200 mg daily as single dose or in 2 divided doses, may be increased to 400 mg once daily or in two divided doses. Max 400 mg. <b>CYP209 poor metabolisers, moderate liver impairment with serum albumin of 25-35 g/l:</b> Reduce dose to half the lowest recommended dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active substance, excipients, sulfonamides. Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding. History of asthma, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, angioneurotic edema, urticaria, other allergic-type reactions from aspirin or other NSAIDS. Severe hepatic dysfunction (serum albumin < 25 g/l or Child-Pugh score = 10). CrCl < 30 mL/min. IBS. CHF (NYHA II-IV). Established IHD, PAD, cerebrovascular disease. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild or moderate renal impairment; at risk of developing GI complication or prior history of GI disease; significant risk for CV events or renal toxicity; history of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction or HTN, pre-existing edema, on diuretic treatment; CYP2C9 poor metabolisers. Upper and lower GI complications, CV effects, fluid retention, edema, HTN, skin and systemic hypersensitivity reactions, renal toxicity, fulminant hepatitis, liver necrosis, hepatic failure. May mask fever and other signs of inflammation. Avoid concomitant use with non-aspirin NSAID. Not a substitute for aspirin for prophylaxis of CV thrombo-embolic diseases. Reduce dose of CYP2D6-metabolized drugs if individually titrated. Monitor BP during initiation of therapy. Childn. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "HTN (including aggravated HTN). Sinusitis, URTI, pharyngitis, UTI, hypersensitivity, insomnia, dizziness, hypertonia, headache, MI, rhinitis, cough, dyspnea, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, edema peripheral fluid retention, accidental injury, dysphagia, rash, pruritus (includes pruritus generalized), arthralgia, influenza-like illness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, antihypertensives, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, aspirin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 200 mg (P26.25)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/SP4ebQQ13XRp8YBUL95HMbK93pC3sIoDU7LpgqtD9xKuBRdTU5.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Irbesartan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN); may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents. For treatment of diabetic nephropathy with an increased serum creatinine and proteinuria (>300 mg/day)  in patients with type 2 diabetes and HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> Initially 150 mg once daily. Titrate dose to 300 mg once daily in patients requiring further reduction in BP, may add low dose diuretic. <b>Nephropathy in type 2 diabetic patients:</b> Initially 150 mg once daily; Maintenance dose: 300 once a day. <b>Vol-and salt-depleted patients (e.g. patients treated vigorously with diuretics or on hemodialysis):</b> Initially 75 mg once a day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors in patients with diabetic nephropathy; with aliskiren in patients with DM or GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Vol- or salt-depleted patients. Renal impairment (e.g. patients with unilateral or bilateral renal artery stenosis), kidney transplantation. Hyperkalemia; monitor serum potassium. Patients with aortic and mitral valve stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; primary aldosteronism; ischemic cardiomyopathy or ischemic CV disease. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;4 yrs. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C in 1<sup>st</sup> trimester but D in 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "CV, endocrine and metabolic, GI, genitourinary, hematologic, musculoskeletal, and nervous system effects."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements and salt substitutes. Lithium. NSAIDs (e.g. COX-2 inhibitors, aspirin &gt;3 g/day), ACE inhibitors, aliskiren."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 150 mg (P22.52), 300 mg (P36.86)."
          }

  {
    "id": 4884,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4884,
        "brand_name": "Ifamso PE",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XvQKbbjNuizslgilLyTS3kzuklVq5dq84j71rNlPkwQirziNdj.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mHDncnTKec4QnJ10bSpN5nBwQWPuneeb3dzJwnrHUwrYhM4ZXc.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NZwzUhrq6bWv1EVbbRYsO6VchEKIjHzgWwTg9CGZJt6G4DrhGc.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Tuberculosis & Leprosy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Initial and re-treatment of all forms of tuberculosis in Category I (new smear-positive or severe cases) and Category II (relapse or treatment failures) caused by susceptible mycobacterial strains."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients >71 kg:</b> 5 tabs; <b>55-70 kg:</b> 4 tabs; <b>40-54 kg:</b> 3 tabs. <b>Category I:</b> Given daily during the initial phase (8 weeks) of treatment. If sputum is smear-positive, continue treatment for 4 weeks. <b>Category II:</b> Given daily during the initial phase (12 weeks) of treatment. Streptomycin should be added during the first 8 weeks of the initial phase. If sputum is smear-positive, continue treatment for 4 weeks. Should be given 1 hr before or 2 hrs after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Alcohol, optic neuritis, impaired hepatic function, severe renal insufficiency, hyperuricemia, gouty arthritis, jaundice. Patients with known retrobulbar neuritis, unable to report visual side effects or changes in vision (e.g. childn and patients with mental illness or deficiency). <b>Pyrazinamide:</b> severe hepatic damage, on concomitant therapy with rifampicin, liver disease, history of isoniazid-associated liver injury."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May produce decreases in visual acuity due to optic/retrobulbar neuritis. Not for treatment of latent TB infection.  Patients with pre-existing liver diseases or at increased risk for drug-related hepatitis. Discontinue pyrazinamide if signs of hepatocellular damage appear. All patients should undergo full ophthalmic examination. Pyridoxine deficiency may be observed in adults taking high doses of isoniazid; treatment with high doses of vit B6 may be necessary. Patients with diabetes mellitus, decreased renal function, epileptic, psychotic states characterized by mania or hypomania. Measure liver function before treatment. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 13 yrs. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Ethambutol:</b> leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia; anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reaction, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, eosinophilia; dizziness, hypoesthesia, paresthesia; optic neuritis, atrophy. <b>Rifampicin:</b> thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, eosinophilia, elevations in serum uric acid; headache, drowsiness, fatigue, ataxia, dizziness, inability to concentrate, mental confusion, muscular weakness, generalized numbness, pain in the extremities; visual disturbances, exudative conjunctivitis; GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, renal and urinary system disorders. <b>Isoniazid:</b> Agranulocytosis, eosinophilia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, methemoglobinemia, vasculitis, lymphadenopathy; lupus-like syndrome, rheumatoid syndrome. Peripheral neuropathy, eye disorders; pellagra, hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis, gynecomastia. <b>Pyrazinamide:</b> Thrombocytopenia, sideroblastic anemia with erythroid hyperplasia, vacuolation of erythrocytes, abnormalities in blood clotting mechanisms, porphyria, anorexia, hyperuricemia, increased liver enzymes, serum bilirubin, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, jaundice; acne, photosensitivity, skin rashes; dysuria, interstitial nephritis, arthralgia, gout, myalgia, fever, malaise."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Ethambutol:</b> neurotoxic medicines, antacids containing aluminum hydroxide, phentolamine. <b>Rifampicin:</b> oral contraceptives, aminophylline, theophylline, sulfonylurea, oral antidiabetic agents, phenobarbital, systemic beta-adrenergic blocking agents, chloramphenicol, clofibrate, corticosteroids, cyclosporin, dapsone, diazepam, digitalis glycosides, disopyramide, mexiletine, quinidine, tocainide, estramustine, fluconazole, methadone, phenytoin, trimethoprim, oral verapamil, clofazimine, probenecid. <b>Isoniazid:</b> alfentanil, coumarin, inandione derivative anticoagulants, benzodiazepines, carbamazepine, theophylline, phenytoin, paracetamol, alcohol, rifampicin, aluminum containing antacids, glucocorticoid corticosteroids, cycloserine, disulfiram, false positive reactions with copper sulfate urine glucose tests, other hepatotoxic and neurotoxic medications."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 150 mg/75 mg/400 mg/275 mg."
          }
        ],

      "success": true,

        "id": 2397,
        "brand_name": "Imbruvica",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/q71T4r73As01Ud6hslZTsr3Dg96coTGFcS4WHGaY0lqjQ2dh0a.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DOtg3oJsjTuNhaWiYbeGTlAJ4xJteI7PgY5OSELMr1nNucXMDx.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ot2iDS0fNt0aSPxb1DON7Zqw1fTUp1vK1iw493chXoMh7BwVDN.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ibrutinib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Protein Kinase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of adults with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least 1 prior therapy; chronic or small lymphocytic leukemia (CLL/SLL), CLL/SLL with deletion 17p; Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia (WM)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>MCL:</b> 560 mg (4 caps) once daily. <b>CLL/SLL, WM:</b> 420 mg (3 caps) once daily as monotherapy or in combination with anti-CD20 therapy or bendamustine and rituximab for CLL/SLL; with rituximab for WM. Hepatic impairment - Mild (Child-Pugh class A): 280 mg daily. Moderate (Child-Pugh B): 140 mg daily. Administer with a glass of water approx at same time each day. Swallow whole; do not open, break, or chew caps."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor CBC regularly. Patients in anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy; at increased risk for opportunistic infections, CV diseases, tumor lysis syndrome. Monitor for ILD symptoms, non-melanoma skin cancer.  Concomitant use of moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; fish oil or vit E. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, hemorrhage (bruising), fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, nausea, URTI, cough, and rash. Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, pneumonia, and anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, indinavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir, clarithromycin, telithromycin, itraconazole, nefazodone, cobicistat. Voriconazole, erythromycin, amprenavir, aprepitant, atazanavir, ciprofloxacin, crizotinib, darunavir/ritonavir, diltiazem, fluconazole, fosamprenavir, imatinib, verapamil, amiodarone, dronedarone. Azithromycin, fluvoxamine, grapefruit juice, grapefruit, Seville oranges. Carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenytoin, St. John’s Wort, PPIs, digoxin, methotrexate, rosuvastatin. Dihydroergotamine, ergotamine, fentanyl, ciclosporin, sirolimus, tacrolimus, efavirenz, bupropion, warfarin and other vit K antagonists, fish oil, vit E."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 140 mg (P1,294.44)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 2991,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2991,
        "brand_name": "Inoflox",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/A04qrpRSRtdJ4ds8nwPDSyJW2sX9nXu74q1UIWSXQ97jGVqDsH.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/8qzFGcni1TTtc3Lzu76pHcaLr63QYCMh71tjfoVQ7reNsRI3XZ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/SLYbWj9mnF4NdCqCR6PZqU2kRmq2gIohvJsrfQKCgpXaJOXzNU.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ofloxacin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab/IV</b>: Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections (SSSI), non-gonococcal urethritis and cervicitis, acute pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), uncomplicated cystitis, acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis, complicated urinary tract infection (UTI), prostatitis, enteric infections including typhoid fever and shigellosis. <b>Otic soln</b>: Otitis externa, acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes, chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes. <b>Ophthalmic soln</b>: Blepharitis, hordeolum, dacryocystitis, conjunctivitis, meibomitis, keratitis, trachoma. Prevention of infection following corneal ulceration caused by susceptible organisms. Aseptic treatment during a peri-op period for ocular surgery caused by <i>Staphylococcus</i> spp., <i>Moraxella</i> spp., <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>, <i>Pseudomonas</i> spp., <i>Haemophilus</i> spp., <i>Klebsiella</i> spp., <i>Serratia</i> spp., <i>Proteus</i> spp., <i>Acinetobacter</i> spp., <i>Corynebacterium</i> spp., and anaerobic bacteria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab/IV: Adults - Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, CAP, uncomplicated SSSI</b>: 400 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. <b>Non-gonococcal cervicitis/urethritis due to <i>C. trachomatis</i></b>: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. <b>Acute PID</b>: 400 mg every 12 hrs for 10-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated cystitis</b> - Due to <i>E. coli</i> or <i>K. pneumoniae</i>: 200 mg every 12 hrs for 3 days; Due to other susceptible pathogens: 200 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. <b>Complicated UTI</b>: 200 mg every 12 hrs for 14 days. <b>Acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis</b>: 400 mg every 12 hrs for 14 days. <b>Prostatitis</b>: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 6 weeks. <b>Typhoid fever</b>: 15 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses every 12 hrs for 5-14 days. <b>Shigella</b>: 400 mg single dose or 200 mg every 8 hrs for 1 day. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl of 20-50 mL/min: Give the recommended dose every 24 hrs; &lt;20 mL/min: &frac12; of recommended dose every 24 hrs. <b>Tab</b>: Taken with or without food. <b>IV</b>: Slow IV infusion over 30-60 mins. <b>Otic soln: Otitis externa</b> – Adults and childn &gt;13 yrs: Instill 10 drops into the affected ear once daily for 7 days; Childn 6 months to 13 yrs: 5 drops once daily for 7 days. <b>Acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes</b> – Childn 1-12 yrs: 5 drops twice daily for 10 days. <b>Chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes</b> – Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: 10 drops twice daily for 14 days. <b>Ophthalmic soln</b> - Adults and childn &ge;1 yr: Instill 1-2 drops 3-4 times daily continue until 2 days after the eye/s appear normal. Treatment should not exceed 2 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Tab/IV</b>: History of epilepsy or lowered seizure threshold. G6PD deficiency. History of myasthenia gravis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",

            "content": "Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of systemic aspergillosis and candidiasis, cryptococcosis (including cryptococcal meningitis), histoplasmosis, sporotrichosis, paracoccidiodomycosis, blastomycosis, and other rarely occurring systemic or topical mycoses, onychomycosis, pityriasis versicolor, dermatomycosis, oral candidiasis and vulvovaginal candidosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Vulvovaginal candidosis:</b> 200 mg twice for 1 day or 200 mg once daily for 3 days. <b>Pityriasis versicolor:</b> 200 mg once daily for 7 days. <b>Dermatomycosis:</b> 200 mg once daily for 7 days or 100 mg once daily for 15 days. <b>Tinea pedis, palmar tinea manus:</b> 200 mg twice daily for 7 days or 100 mg daily for 30 days. <b>Onychomycosis [Pulse treatment (1 treatment, 2 capsules twice daily for 1 week)] - Fingernail:</b> 2 pulse treatment. <b>Toenails:</b> 3 pulse treatment. <b>Continuous treatment - toenails with or without fingernail involvement:</b> 2 capsules once daily for 3 months. <b>Aspergillosis:</b> 200 mg once daily for 2-5 months. <b>Candidosis:</b> 100 mg-200 mg once daily for 3 weeks to 7 months. <b>Non-meningeal cryptococcosis:</b> 200 mg once daily for 2 months to 1 year. Cryptococcal meningitis: 200 mg twice daily for 2 months to 1 year. Histoplasmosis: 200 mg once daily for 8 months. Sporotrichosis: 100 mg daily for 3 months. <b>Paracoccidiodomycosis:</b> 100 mg once daily for 6 months. <b>Chromomycosis:</b> 100-200 mg once daily for 6 months. </b>Blastomycosis:</b> 100 mg once daily or 200 mg twice daily for 6 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with terfenadine, astemizole, mizolastine, cisapride, dofetilide, quinidine, pimozide, simvastatin, lovastatin, triazolam, oral midazolam. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to azoles. Neuropathy. Renal and hepatic impairment. Patients developing symptoms suggestive of hepatitis; raised liver enzymes or active liver disease; patients receiving acid neutralizing medicines; patients with achlorhydria, AIDS. Patients with CHF or history of CHF. Concomitant use of CCBs and acid secretion suppressors (e.g. H2-antagonists, proton pump inhibitors). Elderly. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dyspepsia, abdominal pain, nausea, constipation, headache, menstrual disorders, dizziness, allergic reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Rifampicin, rifabutin, phenytoin, clarithromycin, erythromycin, indinavir, ritonavir, terfenadine, astemizole, mizolstine, cisapride, triazolam, oral midazolam, dofetilide, quinidine, pimoxide, CYP3A4 metabolized HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors."

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TX2VP3J2bFwnIEvyU2mFSmLvnqTrq3DoTI4NZr2Y0Hw3YtkdAV.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/R3iqYV9KewCxQAp8xbGApoumehVjWgq4IDABJxHNeLciPqdogW.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Eplerenone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Aldosterone Antagonists and Potassium-Sparing Diuretics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN), alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents. In addition to standard therapy, for reduction of risk for cardiovascular mortality and morbidity in stable patients with left ventricular dysfunction (LVEF &le;40%) and clinical evidence of heart failure (HF) after recent myocardial infarction (MI); and in adults with NYHA class II (chronic) HF and LVEF &le;35%)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: Initially, 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg if BP is not adequately controlled. <b>Post MI and NYHA class II (chronic) HF</b>: Initially, 25 mg once daily and titrated to the target maintenance dose of 50 mg once daily within 4 weeks with consideration of serum potassium level. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl 30-60 mL/min)</b>: Initially, 25 mg every other day, and dose should be adjusted based on potassium level. <b>Concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitors</b>: 25 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with clinically significant hyperkalemia or with conditions associated with hyperkalemia; serum potassium level &gt;5.0 mmol/L at initiation; moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;50 mL/min) in post-MI HF or CrCl &lt;30 mL/min in NYHA Class II (chronic) HF; severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C); concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics, or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, and ritonavir). Hypertensive patients with type 2 diabetes with microalbuminuria; serum creatinine &gt;2.0 mg/dL in males or &gt;1.8 mg/dL in females. Concomitant use of potassium supplement, salt substitutes containing potassium, potassium-sparing diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for hyperkalemia; concomitant use of ACE inhibitors and/or ARBs measure serum potassium before initiating eplerenone therapy and assess periodically thereafter. Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Co-administration with mild to moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers. May cause inability to drive and operate machinery. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Influenza-like illness; hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, dizziness, cough, abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue, albuminuria; increased GGT, ALT."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 25 mg (P23.19), 50 mg (P39.68)."
          }

            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of clinically typical, nonhyperkeratotic, nonhypertrophic actinic keratoses on the face or scalp in immunocompetent patients. Treatment of biopsy-confirmed, primary superficial basal cell carcinoma (sBCC) in immunocompetent adults with a maximum tumor diameter of 2 cm, located on the trunk (excluding anogenital skin), neck or extremities (excluding hands and feet). Treatment of external genital and perianal warts/condyloma acuminata in patients &gt;12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply to the entire treatment area and rub in until the cream is no longer visible. <b>Actinic keratosis</b>: Apply 2x per week for a full 16 weeks to a defined treatment area on the face or scalp (but not both concurrently), applied prior to normal sleeping hrs and left on the skin for approx 8 hrs, after which time the cream should be removed by washing the area with mild soap and water. <b>sBCC</b>: Apply 5x per week for a full 6 weeks, applied prior to normal sleeping hrs and left on the skin for approximately 8 hrs, after which time the cream should be removed by washing the area with mild soap and water. External genital warts: Apply 3x per week for a max of 16 weeks, applied prior to normal sleeping hrs and left on the skin for 6-10 hrs, after which time the cream should be removed by washing the area with mild soap and water."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pre-existing autoimmune conditions. Skin weeping or erosion. May exacerbate inflammatory conditions of the skin including graft versus host disease. Severe local inflammatory reactions of female external genitalia, severe vulvular swelling. Not recommended until skin is completely healed from any various drug or surgical treatment. Malaise, fever, nausea, myalgias and rigor. Avoid exposure to sunlight (including sunlamps). Not for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use.         "brand_status": 1,

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Human Normal Immunoglobulins (HNIg)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary and secondary immunodeficiency (PID and SID), Kawasaki disease, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia, pediatric HIV 1 infection, hemopoietic stem cell transplantation in elderly, allogeneic bone marrow transplantation, Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adjust based on patient body weight and clinical response. <b>Replacement therapy in PID:</b> 0.4-0.8 g/kg (8-16 mL/kg), followed by 0.2-0.8 g/kg (4-16 mL/kg) every 2-4 weeks to obtain IgG trough level of at least 4-6 g/L. <b>Replacement therapy in SID:</b> 0.2-0.4 g/kg (4-8 mL/kg) every 3-4 weeks to obtain IgG trough level of at least 4-6 g/L. <b>Allogeneic bone marrow transplantation</b> - Treatment of infections and prophylaxis of graft versus host disease: 0.5 g/kg (10 mL/kg) every week from day 7 up to 3 months after transplantation. Persistent lack of antibody production: 0.5 g/kg (10 mL/kg) monthly until antibody levels is normal. <b>ITP:</b> 0.8-1 g/kg (16-20 mL/kg) on day 1, possibly repeated once within 3 days, or 0.4 g/kg (8 mL/kg) daily for 2-5 days. <b>Kawasaki disease:</b> 1.6-2 g/kg (32-40 mL/kg) in several doses for 2-5 days in association with aspirin, or 2 g/kg (40 mL/kg) in 1 dose in association with aspirin. <b>Pediatric HIV 1 infection:</b> 0.2-0.4 g/kg (4-8 mL/kg) every 3-4 weeks. <b>GBS:</b> 0.4 g/kg/day (8 mL/kg/day) for 3-7 days. 1<sup>st</sup> infusion should start at initial rate of 0.6-1.2 mL/kg /hr for the 1st 30 mins and can be increased up to 2.4 mL/kg/hr. Subsequent infusion may be increased to 4.8 mL/kg /hr."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with selective IgA deficiency who possess antibody to IgA."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Correct vol depletion before initiation of therapy. Acute renal failure. Patients at risk for developing renal insufficiency. Administration of live attenuated viral vaccines. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "As an immunomodulator for the management of patients with immunodepression suffering from viral infections (e.g. subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), varicella, herpes simplex type 1 and 2). Management of recurrent herpes simplex type 1 and 2. Adjunct in the treatment of genital warts."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – Adults</b>: 2 tabs every 6 hrs for 5-14 days. <b>Herpes simplex</b>: 1 g every 6 hrs for 7-14 days. <b>Genital warts</b>: 1 g every 8 hrs for 14-28 days as an adjunct to standard topical (podophyllin) or surgical (carbon dioxide laser) treatment. <b>SSPE - Adults and childn</b>: 50-100 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 4 hrs continuously, with regular monitoring to evaluate patient status and requirement for extended treatment. <b>Syrup - Adults and elderly</b>: 20 mL every 6-8 hrs for 5-14 days. Usual adult dose of 50 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 6-8 hrs, up to max of 4 g/day. <b>Childn 7-12 yrs</b>: 5 mL; <b>3-6 yrs</b>: 3 mL; <b>1-2 yrs</b>: 2 mL; <b>7-12 months</b>: 1.5 mL; <b>0-6 months</b>: 1 mL. All doses given every 4-6 hrs for 5-14 days. Usual child dose of 50 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 4-6 hrs, up to max of 100 mg/kg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with gout or elevated uric acid blood levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of gout, hyperuricemia, urolithiasis, nephrolithiasis, renal impairment. Transient increase of baseline serum and urine concentration of uric acid in men and elderly. Monitor uric acid levels during therapy. Monitor serum and urine concentrations of uric acid, blood count, and liver and renal function when used continuously for &gt;3 months. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

            "content": "Transient elevation of urine and serum uric acid levels."
          },
          {

          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Irinotecan HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Camptothecins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For patients with metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum whose disease has recurred or progressed after initial fluorouracil-based therapy; as component of 1<sup>st</sup>-line therapy in combination with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy - Regimen 1:</b> 125 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 90 mins on days 1, 8, 15, and 22, then 2-week rest; <b>Regimen 2:</b> 350 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 90 mins on day 1 every 3 weeks. <b>Combination therapy - Regimen 1:</b> 125 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 90 mins with leucovorin 20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV bolus infusion, followed by 5-fluorouracil IV bolus infusion on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 every 6 weeks; <b>Regimen 2:</b> 180 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 90 mins on days 1, 15, and 29 with leucovorin 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 2 hrs, followed by 5-fluorouracil 400 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV bolus infusion, and 5-fluorouracil 600 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 22 hrs on days 1, 2, 15, 16, 29, and 30. Do not administer for 4-5 consecutive days every 4 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients on dialysis. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor and replace fluid and electrolytes. Diarrhea and cholinergic reactions; myelosuppression. Risk of neutropenia in patients with reduced UGT1A1 activity. Patients with vol-depletion, renal and hepatic impairment. Discontinue when interstitial pulmonary disease-like events occur. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, anorexia, mucositis, neutropenia, leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, asthenia, pain, fever, infection, abnormal bilirubin, alopecia; decreased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 20 mg/mL x 4 mL."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ertapenem",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Carbapenems"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of moderate to severe infection caused by susceptible strains of microorganisms. Empiric therapy in adults and childn 3 months-17 yrs for the following infections: Complicated intra-abdominal infection, complicated skin and skin structure infections (e.g. diabetic lower extremity and diabetic foot infections), community-acquired pneumonia, complicated urinary tract infection (e.g. pyelonephritis), acute pelvic infections (e.g. postpartum endomyometritis, septic abortion, and post-op gynecologic infection); bacterial septicemia in adults. Prophylaxis of surgical site infection following elective colorectal surgery in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults >13 yrs:</b> 1 g IV or IM once a day. <b>Infants and childn 3 months-12 yrs:</b> 15 mg/kg twice daily. Max 1 g/day. IV to be infused over 30 mins period. Reconstitute with 1% or 2% lidocaine for IM administration. Usual duration of therapy: 3-14 days depending on type of infection and causative pathogen. <b>Prophylaxis of surgical site infection following elective colorectal surgery:</b> 1 g as single IV dose given 1 hr prior to the surgical incision. <b>Patients with renal insufficiency (CrCl &le;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) including those on hemodialysis:</b> 500 mg daily. When daily dose of 500 mg is given within 6 hrs prior to hemodialysis, administer a supplementary dose of 150 mg following hemodialysis. No supplementary dose is needed if given at least 6 hrs prior to hemodialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients who had anaphylactic reactions to beta-lactam. IM administration in patients with known hypersensitivity to lidocaine or amide-type local anesthesia; Patient with severe shock or heart block. Infants < 3 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, other beta-lactams, other allergens. Patients with CNS disorders or compromised renal function; predisposing factors to convulsions. Concomitant use of valproic acid or divalproex sodium. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms due to prolonged use. Occurrence of mild to life-threatening pseudomembranous colitis. Infants < 3 months. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Diarrhea, infused vein complication, phlebitis/thrombophlebitis, nausea, and headache.  Elevations in ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase and platelet count. <b>Childn:</b> Diarrhea, vomiting, infusion site pain, rash, urticaria, and erythema. Decrease in neutrophil count."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, valproic acid, divalproex sodium. Incompatibilities: Dextrose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection (IV/IM) 1 g (P3,325.00)."
          }

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paliperidone palmitate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia in adults who have been adequately treated with the 1-month paliperidone palmitate injectable product for at least 4 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IM only. The last 2 doses of 1-month injection be the same dosage strength before starting Invega Trinza. Initiate Invega Trinza at time when next 1-month paliperidone palmitate dose was to be scheduled with an Invega Trinza dose based on the previous 1-month injection dose (using 3.5 as multiplier for the 1-month dose to get Invega Trinza dose). May be administered up to 7 days before or after the monthly time point of next scheduled paliperidone palmitate 1-month dose. Following the initial Invega Trinza dose, this should be administered every 3 months. Dose adjustment can be made every 3 months in increments within the range of 175-525 mg if needed. <b>Patients with mild renal impairment:</b> Max 350 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to paliperidone, any component of the formulation, and risperidone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not administer SC, IV, or in divided doses. Consider discontinuing if NMS, tardive dyskinesia or EPS develops. Patients with history of cardiac arrhythmias, congenital long QT syndrome, and in concomitant use with drugs known to prolong the QT interval; known CV disease, cerebrovascular disease or conditions that predispose the patient to hypotension; seizures. Hyperglycemia, DM and exacerbation of pre-existing DM. Weight gain. May induce orthostatic hypotension.  History of clinically low WBC count or drug-induced leukopenia/neutropenia. Cases of VTE. Parkinson’s disease or dementia with Lewy bodies. Body temp regulation disruption. Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome during cataract surgery. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Elderly with dementia. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, weight increased, headache, anxiety, akathisia, Parkinsonism, UTI, injection site reaction, hyperglycemia, nausea, hyperinsulinemia, dyskinesia, dystonia, somnolence, tachycardia, amenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Centrally acting drugs, alcohol, levodopa, and other dopamine agonists, carbamazepine, divalproex sodium, risperidone, psychostimulants (e.g. methylphenidate)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Prolonged-release suspension for injection (IM) 263 mg (P27,297.32), 350 mg (P27,297.32), 525 mg (P27,297.32)."
          }

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prophylaxis of Japanese encephalitis in childn &ge;9 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC inj. <b>Primary vaccination - Childn &ge;9 months:</b> Single dose 0.5 mL; <b>Booster vaccination - Adults:</b> Not needed for up to 5 yrs after single dose. <b>Childn and adolescents &le;18 yrs:</b> One 0.5 mL given 1-2 yrs (preferably 1 yr) after 1<sup>st</sup> vaccination; <b>Childn previously given with inactivated Japanese encephalitis vaccine:</b> One 0.5 mL dose."

          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Febrile or acute disease.           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Wait for &ge;1 month until immune function has recovered after treatment of high doses of systemic corticosteroids given for &ge;14 days, before vaccination. Do not mix with any other injectable vaccines or medicinal products.",

          },

        "id": 51,
        "brand_name": "Inderal",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/oyDS384ztX5fQNCdkjMIA6HHjy2sb9WOzCc1HNrAJzQvov25D2.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kcKkgy0cJ0Qyds5OvYIn3EaTKxsDdjmZJ5M8A29j0jUfkBTTrP.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5nA31IJqy3k1YzeLGUSeCMQSqvuF8r9QJDdn6U95qs2p8oF9A0.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Propranolol HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN), cardiac arrhythmias, anxiety and anxiety tachycardia. Management of angina pectoris, essential tremor, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, pheochromocytoma. Adjunct in management of thyrotoxicosis and thyrotoxic crisis. Prophylaxis of migraine, long-term prophylaxis after recovery from acute myocardial infarction (MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – HTN</b>: Initially 80 mg twice daily, may be increased to 160-320 mg at weekly intervals. Max: 640 mg/day (in divided doses). <b>Angina, anxiety, migraine, essential tremor</b>: Initially 40 mg 2-3x daily, may be increased by same dose at weekly intervals. Max daily dose of 240 mg for migraine; 480 mg for angina. <b>Arrhythmias, anxiety tachycardia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and thyrotoxicosis</b>: 10-40 mg 3-4x daily. Max: 240 mg/day. <b>Post-MI</b>: Start treatment between days 5 and 21 after MI. Initially 40 mg 4x daily for 2 or 3 days. Max 80 mg twice daily. <b>Pheochromocytoma (used only with effective alpha blockade – Pre-op</b>: 60 mg daily for 3 days; <b>Non-operable malignant cases</b>: 30 mg daily. <b>Childn – Arrhythmias, pheochromocytoma thyrotoxicosis</b>: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg 3 or 4x daily. <b>Migraine – &gt;12 yrs</b>: Adult dose; <b>&lt;12 yrs</b>: 20 mg 2-3x daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of bronchial asthma or bronchospasm. Patients with bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, hypotension, metabolic acidosis, severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances, 2<sup>nd</sup>- or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree block, sick sinus syndrome, untreated pheochromocytoma, uncontrolled heart failure of Prinzmetal’s angina. Patients with hypoglycemia i.e. after prolonged fasting or with restricted counter-regulatory reserves e.g. due to malnutrition, starvation, chronic liver disease, diabetes, use of drugs which blocks catecholamine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal and hepatic impairment. Patients with poor cardiac reserve, 1<sup>st</sup> degree heart block, decompensated cirrhosis; diabetes. May mask signs of thyrotoxicosis. Avoid abrupt discontinuation in patients with IHD. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fatigue, bradycardia, Raynaud’s phenomenon, sleep disturbances, nightmares."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Hypoglycemic agents, rizatriptan. Disopyramide, amiodarone, digitalis glycosides, verapamil, diltiazem, nifedipine, IV epinephrine, cimetidine, hydralazine, clonidine, ergotamine and related compounds. Ibuprofen, indomethacin, chlorpromazine, anesthetics agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg, 40 mg."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 2182,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2182,
        "brand_name": "Indirin",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KUBaIcxNeNMSWM7gKwF5qLOsMGm7NZK5jCWvX0OQppGcopvwpb.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jAgaMlPPIwoXVDsku1bXwrfZunjROaSMwzuo57H6ccxhOXoMmT.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/z12kjwbgh8ncKy94Srq4jrzcovA9PgJzCDzhDN3qQLBNLsDWWp.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Propranolol HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of hypertension (HTN), cardiac arrhythmias, anxiety and anxiety tachycardia. Management of pheochromocytoma (should only be started in the presence of effective alpha-blocker), angina pectoris, essential tremor, and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Adjunctive management of thyrotoxicosis and thyrotoxic crisis. Long-term prophylaxis after recovery from acute myocardial infarction (MI). Prophylaxis of migraine. Prophylaxis of upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding in patients with portal HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – HTN</b>: Initially 40 mg twice or thrice daily, may be increased by 80 mg/day at weekly intervals. Usual dose: 160-320 mg/day. <b>Angina, migraine, and essential tremor</b>: Initially 40 mg twice to thrice daily, may be increased by same amount at weekly intervals. Usual dose for migraine: 80-160 mg/day; for angina and essential tumor: 120-140 mg/day. <b>Arrhythmia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and thyrotoxicosis</b>: 10-40 mg 3-4 times daily. <b>Portal HTN</b>: 40 mg twice daily, may be increased to 80 mg up to max 160 mg twice daily depending on heart rate response. <b>Pheochromocytoma (used only in the presence of effective alpha-blocker) - Pre-op</b>: 60 mg daily for 3 days. <b>Non-op malignant cases</b>: 30 mg daily. <b>Post-MI</b>: Start treatment between days 5 and 21 after MI, with initial dose of 40 mg 4 times daily for 2-3 days. Total daily dose of 80 mg twice daily may be given in order to improve compliance. <b>Hyperthyroidism</b>: Adjust dose according to clinical response. <b>Severe liver disease</b>: Max 20 mg thrice daily. <b>Childn – Arrhythmias</b>: 250-500 mcg/kg 3-4 times daily. <b>Migraine - Childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: Adult dose; <b>Childn < 12 yrs</b>: 20 mg twice or thrice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of bronchial asthma, bronchospasm, COPD. Inadequately treated cardiac decompensation, severe bradycardia, hypotension; cardiogenic shock; 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree heart block; sick sinus syndrome; uncontrolled heart failure; metabolic acidosis; severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances; untreated pheochromocytoma; Prinzmetal's angina. Patients at risk of hypoglycemia; asthma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with poor cardiac reserve, less severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances, 1<sup>st</sup>-degree heart block, decompensated cirrhosis, hepatic and renal impairment. Concomitant use with hypoglycemic therapy (e.g. insulin) in patients with DM. Concomitant use with CCBs with negative inotropic effects (e.g. diltiazem, verapamil) in patients with impaired ventricular function and/or SA or AV conduction abnormalities. May mask signs of thyrotoxicosis. May induce or aggravate myasthenia gravis. May deteriorate liver function and develop hepatic encephalopathy in patients with portal HTN. Avoid abrupt discontinuation in patients with IHD. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fatigue and/or lassitude, bradycardia, Raynaud’s phenomenon, sleep disturbances, nightmares; thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, angioedema, hypoglycemia, arthralgia, reduced renal flow, impotence, dizziness; nervous system and psychiatric, eye, CV, respiratory, thoracic, mediastinal, GI, skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Hypoglycemic therapy, rizatriptan, Class I anti-arrhythmic drugs (e.g. disopyramide), amiodarone, digitalis glycosides, CCBs with negative inotropic effects (e.g. verapamil, diltiazem), DHP CCBs (e.g. nifedipine, nisoldipine, nicardipine, isradipine, lacidipine), sympathomimetic agents (e.g. adrenaline), lidocaine, cimetidine, hydralazine, alcohol, clonidine, ergot alkaloids, PG synthetase inhibitors (e.g. ibuprofen and indomethacin), chlorpromazine, anesthetic agents, quinidine, propafenone, rifampicin, theophylline, warfarin, thioridazine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P12.75), 40 mg (P17.75)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/rvHDxdHk12omJr5SDXPEVVzaprm0cpfwzMjfDqm0IWJeqJoTnj.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefuroxime sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections e.g. community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, complicated urinary tract infections (UTI) (e.g. pyelonephritis), soft-tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas and wound infections), intra-abdominal infections in adults and childn including neonates (from birth). Prophylaxis against infection in gastrointestinal (GI), orthopedic, cardiovascular (CV), and gynecological surgery (including caesarian section)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;40 kg</b> – CAP, acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, soft tissue infections, intra-abdominal infections: 750 mg IM/IV every 8 hrs. Complicated UTI: 1.5 g IM/IV every 8 hrs. Severe infections: 750 mg IV every 6 hrs or 1.5 g IV every 8 hrs. Surgical prophylaxis for GI, gynecological surgery and orthopedic operations: 1.5 g with induction of anesthesia; may be supplemented with two 750 mg IM after 8 and 16 hrs. Surgical prophylaxis for CV and esophageal operations: 1.5 g with induction of anesthesia followed by 750 mg IM every 8 hours for further 24 hrs. <b>Childn &lt;40 kg BW and infants &gt;3 weeks</b> – CAP, complicated UTI, soft-tissue infections, intra-abdominal pain: 30-100 mg/kg/day IV given as 3 or 4 divided doses; usual dose is 60 mg/kg/day. <b>0-3 weeks</b>: 30-100 mg/kg/day IV given as 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>Renal impairment</b> – CrCl 10-20 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 750 mg twice daily; &lt;10 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:750 mg twice daily. <b>Patients on hemodialysis</b>: An additional 750 mg IM/IV at end of each dialysis. <b>Patients in renal failure on CAVH or HF in intensive therapy units</b>: 750 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Overgrowth of <i>Candida</i> and other non-susceptible microorganisms e.g. enterococci and <i>Clostridium difficile</i>. Antibacterial-associated pseudomembranous colitis may develop. Not suitable for the treatment of infections caused by G(-) non-fermenting bacteria. Concomitant use with potent diuretics or aminoglycosides. Patients on controlled sodium diet. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neutropenia, eosinophilia, decreased Hgb concentration. Transient rise in liver enzymes. Skin rash, urticaria, pruritus. Injection site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral contraceptives, probenecid. Furosemide, aminoglycoside, oral anticoagulants. Positive Coombs’ test, copper reduction methods (e.g. Benedict’s, Fehling’s, Clinitest). False-negative result in ferricyanide test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 750 mg."
          }

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of mild to moderate pain (e.g., musculoskeletal pain, dysmenorrhea, dental pain)."

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "25 mg every 8 hrs. Max 75 mg. Take at least 30 mins before meals. <b>Renal and hepatic dysfunction:</b> 50 mg total daily dose."

            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with drugs that induce asthma attacks, bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, urticaria, or angioneurotic edema.           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",

            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia."
          },

          },

  {
    "id": 4801,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4801,

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Irinotecan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Camptothecins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and folinic acid for treatment of advanced colorectal cancer without prior chemotherapy for advanced disease; monotherapy if 5-FU-containing treatment regimen failed. In combination with cetuximab for EGFR-expressing RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer not receiving prior treatment for metastatic disease or after failure of irinotecan-including cytotoxic therapy. Combination with 5-FU, folinic acid, and bevacizumab is 1<sup>st</sup>-line for metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum. Combination with capecitabine with or without bevacizumab is 1<sup>st</sup>-line for metastatic colorectal carcinoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion single use only into peripheral or central vein. <b>Monotherapy (for previously treated patient):</b> 350 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 30-90 mins every 3 weeks or weekly when need a closer follow-up or at risk of severe neutropenia. <b>In combination with 5-FU and folinic acid (for previously untreated patient):</b> 180 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once every 2 weeks over 30-90 mins, followed by 5-FU and FA. <b>In combination with capecitabine for elderly &ge;65 yrs:</b> Reduce dose of capecitabine to 800 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 2x daily. <b>Impaired hepatic function - BiIirubin 1.5-3x ULN:</b> 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; <b>&le;1.5x:</b> 350 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Give prophylactic antiemetics prior to each treatment. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and dilution."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Chronic inflammatory bowel disease and/or bowel obstruction. Bilirubin >3x ULN. Severe bone marrow failure. WHO performance status >2. Concomitant use with St. John’s wort and live attenuated vaccines. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid contact with skin and eyes; extravasation. Patients with impaired renal function; previous abdominal/pelvic radiotherapy, baseline hyperleukocytosis, WHO performance status &ge;2 and women; severe diarrhea; Gilbert's syndrome; asthma; risk factors of respiratory disorders; extensive prior radiation (e.g. >25% of bone marrow irradiated and within 6 weeks prior to start of treatment); underlying cardiac disease, previous cytotoxic chemotherapy; hereditary fructose intolerance. Risk of delayed diarrhea for >24 hrs; neutropenia (e.g. febrile neutropenia); nausea and vomiting; acute cholinergic syndrome; interstitial lung disease; increased serum creatinine or BUN, acute renal failure; thromboembolic events; renal insufficiency, hypotension or circulatory failure. Monitor CBC weekly for patients with impaired hepatic function and bilirubin 1.5-3x ULN; infusion site. Perform liver function tests. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. May consider preservation of gametes prior to therapy. Childn. Elderly. Women should use contraception during and 3 months after last dose; men during and 3 months after. Women of childbearing potential.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infection; neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia; decreased appetite; cholinergic syndrome; delayed diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, constipation; decreased appetite; alopecia; mucosal inflammation; pyrexia; asthenia; increased blood creatinine, blood bilirubin, transaminases (ALT and AST), and blood alkaline phosphatase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 and /or UGT1A1 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, apalutamide); inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole, protease inhibitors, clarithromycin, erythromycin, telithromycin). UGT1A1 inhibitors (e.g. atazanavir, ketoconazole, regorafenib). Vitamin K antagonists. Immunodepressant agents (e.g. ciclosporin, tacrolimus). Neuromuscular blocking agents (e.g. suxamethonium and non-depolarizing). Crizotinib, idelalisib."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 1.5 mg/mL x 180 mL, 200 mL, 210 mL, 220mL, 240 mL."
          }
        ],

    "detail": {
      "success": true,

        "id": 4458,

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gemcitabine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment of locally advanced (non-resectable stage II or III) or metastatic (stage IV) pancreatic adenocarcinoma; for patients previously treated with fluorouracil. In combination with carboplatin as treatment for advanced ovarian cancer that has relapsed at least 6 months after completion of platinum-based therapy. In combination with paclitaxel as 1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment for metastatic breast cancer after failure of prior anthracycline-containing adjuvant chemotherapy, unless anthracyclines were clinically contraindicated. In combination with cisplatin as 1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment for inoperable locally-advanced (stage IIIa or IIIB) or metastatic (stage IV) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses infused IV over 30 mins. <b>Ovarian cancer:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, administered after with carboplatin AUC 4 on Day 1. <b>Breast cancer:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, administered prior with paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs on day 1. <b>NSCLC - 28-day:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle, administered after with cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 1; <b>21-day:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle after cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 1. <b>Pancreatic cancer:</b> 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; Weeks 1-8: Weekly dosing for the 1st 7 weeks, followed by 1 week rest; After week 8: Weekly dosing on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity, infusion bag selection, and administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not exceed >60 mins infusion time nor more frequently than weekly dosing. Patients with concurrent liver metastases or preexisting history of hepatitis, alcoholism, or liver cirrhosis. Concomitant use with other cytotoxic drugs and radiation therapy. Myelosuppression; pulmonary toxicity including interstitial pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis or edema, adult respiratory distress syndrome; hemolytic uremic syndrome including fatalities from renal failure or requirement for dialysis; hepatotoxicity including liver failure and death; life-threatening mucositis, esophagitis, pneumonitis; capillary leak syndrome; posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Perform CBC with a differential and platelet count prior each dose and renal function before treatment initiation. Assess renal and hepatic function prior to therapy initiation and periodically during treatment. Use contraception during and for 3 months after treatment. May impair male fertility. Childn. Female patients, especially elderly. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, anemia, increased ALT and/or AST, neutropenia, increased alkaline phosphatase, proteinuria, fever, hematuria, rash, thrombocytopenia, dyspnea, edema. Diarrhea, hemorrhage, infection, increased BUN, alopecia, hyperbilirubinemia, stomatitis, somnolence, paresthesia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 10 mg/mL x 120 mL (P15,000.00), 140 mL (P17,000.00), 160 mL (P19,000.00), 180 mL."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {

            "content": "In combination with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and folinic acid for treatment of advanced colorectal cancer without prior chemotherapy for advanced colorectal cancer; monotherapy if 5-FU-containing treatment regimen failed; combination with cetuximab for treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (KRAS wild-type) with EGFR expression, without prior treatment or after failure of irinotecan-including cytotoxic therapy; combination with 5-FU, folinic acid (FA), and bevacizumab as 1st-line treatment of metastatic carcinoma of colon or rectum; combination with capecitabine with or without bevacizumab as 1st-line treatment of metastatic colorectal carcinoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion over 30-90 mins. <b>Monotherapy (previously treated patient):</b> 350 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks. <b>Combination therapy (previously untreated patient):</b> 180 mg/m<sup>2</sup>once every 2 weeks, followed by infusion with FA and 5-FU. <b>Combination with capecitabine for elderly &ge;65 yrs:</b> Reduce dose of capecitabine to 800 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice daily. <b>Impaired hepatic function - Starting doses for weekly regimen:</b> Serum ALT/AST concentration &le;5.0 x IULN: Total bilirubin 1.5-3.0 x IULN: 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; 3.1-5.0 x IULN: 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; Serum ALT/AST concentration 5.1-20.0 x IULN: Total bilirubin &lt;1.5 x IULN: 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; 1.5-5.0 x IULN: 40 mg/m<sup>2</sup>.             "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not administer &lt;1 hr after the end of cetuximab infusion. Avoid extravasation. Patients with impaired renal function, WHO performance status grade 2, asthma, risk for diarrhea, respiratory disorders, or MI, and who previously received pelvic/abdominal irradiation. Delayed diarrhea, febrile neutropenia, dizziness, myelosuppression, MI events. Renal dysfunction, hypotension, or circulatory failure in patients experiencing dehydration associated with diarrhea, vomiting, or sepsis. Concomitant use with live-attenuated vaccines. May diminish response to killed or inactivated vaccine. Not recommended for childn and patients with total bilirubin &gt;3.0 x IULN. Give high doses of loperamide for 12 hours after the last liquid stool in patients experiencing diarrhea. Give atropine sulfate 0.25 mg SC if acute and severe cholinergic syndrome appears. Monitor CBC weekly; liver function tests at baseline and before each cycle of administration. Use effective contraception during and up to 1 month (women) and 3 months (men) after treatment. Elderly. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neutropenia, anemia, decreased appetite, cholinergic syndrome, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, alopecia (reversible), mucosal inflammation, pyrexia, asthenia, thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia, constipation, increased blood creatinine, SGPT, SGOT, bilirubin, and blood alkaline phosphatase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Neuromuscular blockers, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, ketoconazole, rifampicin, atazanavir sulfate, vit K anticoagulants, live attenuated vaccines, phenytoin, cyclosporine, tacrolimus. Yellow fever vaccine, St. John’s Wort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solutions for IV infusion 20 mg/mL x 2 mL, 5 mL."
          }
        ],

          },

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - CAD, paroxysmal SVT, atrial flutter/fibrillation:</b> 120-480 mg in 3 or 4 divided doses. <b>HTN:</b> 120-480 mg in 3 divided doses. <b>Childn</b> - 6-14 yrs: 80-360 mg in 2-4 divided doses; up to 6 yrs: 80-120 mg in 2-3 divided doses."

            "content": "Angina pectoris, congestive heart failure."

            "content": "Angina pectoris – Sublingual tablet: 5-10 mg every 2-3 hours for the prophylaxis of acute angina, may be supplemented by 5-10 mg prior to stressful situations likely to provoke an attack of angina; Oral tablet: 5-30 mg 4x daily, preferably on an empty stomach.           {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Cutaneous vasodilation with flushing, vascular headache, transient episodes of dizziness and weakness, nausea, vomiting, weakness, restlessness, pallor, perspiration."
