        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Bdnm8oChMLMWV79SZLxMJ7ipTdY4T6m94QKkOmIO8pHORqumyg.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LSP4WMC3vXdCcGnNqyaQGOqqIfmV1Jv0OOCLZ2wI9UdknZguyL.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gHOBzDL0UPgwnv2lBzUfjcKXFZyPcUUxL41BXQA9IOfydeI3cA.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Isoxsuprine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Uterine Relaxants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Uterine hypermotility disorders e.g. threatened abortion and uncomplicated premature labor. Adjunct in the treatment of peripheral vascular disease, e.g. arteriosclerosis obliterans, thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger’s disease), Raynaud’s disease. Relief of symptoms associated with cerebrovascular insufficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Uterine hypermotility – IV</b>: 100 mg (20 mL) in 500 mL infusion fluid (normal saline or dextrose solution) at a rate 0.5 mL/min (10 drops/min), increase rate in increments of 10 drops/min at 10-min intervals until control of uterine motility is obtained. <b>IM</b>: 10 mg (2 mL) every 3 hrs for 24 hrs, then every 4-6 hrs for a further 48 hrs. <b>Tab</b>: 20 mg (2 tabs) 3-4x daily when uterine contractions have ceased for at least 12 hrs with parenteral isoxsuprine. <b>Circulatory disturbances – IM</b>: 5-10 mg (1-2 mL) 3x daily. <b>Tab</b>: 20 mg (2 tabs) 3-4x daily after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Following recent arterial hemorrhage, patients with known heart disease, severe anemia. Childn. <b>IM/IV</b>: Hypotension, tachycardia, premature detachment of placenta, immediately post-partum, premature labor if there is infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue if rash develops. Monitor state of hydration, cardiac, and respiratory function. Keep fluid infusion vol to the minimum. For infusion, hypotonic dextrose is preferred over isotonic saline solution. Discontinue immediately and institute diuretic therapy when signs of pulmonary edema develop. Elderly. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Trembling, nervousness, weakness, dizziness, flushing, transient palpitation, tachycardia, chest pain, hypotension, abdominal distress, nausea vomiting, intestinal distension, severe rash, slight increase in fetal heart rate (as IV infusion in premature labor)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other vasodilators, antihypertensives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg (P27.00). Solution for injection (IV/IM) 5 mg/mL x 2 mL (P200.00)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases. Pregnancy and lactation."

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of vulvovaginal candidosis, pityriasis versicolor, dermatophytoses caused by organisms susceptible to itraconazole (<i>Trichophyton</i> spp., <i>Microsporum</i> spp., <i>Epidermophyton floccosum</i>) e.g. tinea pedis, tinea cruris, tinea corporis, tinea manuum; oropharyngeal candidosis, onychomycosis caused by dermatophytes and/or yeasts. Treatment of histoplasmosis, aspergillosis and candidosis, cryptococcosis (including cryptococcal meningitis) in immunocompromised patients with cryptococcosis and in all patients with cryptococcosis in the CNS. Maintenance therapy in AIDS patients to prevent relapse of underlying fungal infection. Prevention of fungal infection during prolonged neutropenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Vulvovaginal candidosis</b>: 200 mg twice daily for 1 day. <b>Pityriasis versicolor</b>: 200 mg once daily for 7 days. <b>Tinea corporis, tinea cruris</b>: 100 mg once daily for 15 days or 200 mg once daily for 7 days. <b>Tinea pedis, tinea manuum</b>: 100 mg once daily for 30 days. <b>Oropharyngeal candidosis</b>: 100 mg once daily for 15 days, may be increased to 200 mg once daily for 15 days in AIDS or neutropenic patients due to impaired absorption. <b>Onychomycosis (toenails with or without fingernail involvement)</b>: 200 mg once daily for 3 months. <b>Aspergillosis</b>: 200 mg once daily. <b>Candidosis</b>: 100-200 mg once daily. Doses may be increased to 200 mg twice daily. <b>Histoplasmosis</b>: 200 mg once daily to 200 mg twice daily. <b>Maintenance in AIDS:</b> 200 mg once daily. <b>Prophylaxis in neutropenia</b>: 200 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. QT prolongation and ventricular tachyarrhythmias e.g. torsade de pointes. Patients with ventricular dysfunction e.g. CHF. Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates, CCBs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to azoles. Renal and hepatic impairment. Neuropathy. Transient or permanent hearing loss. Patients with CHF; reduced gastric acidity from disease (achlorhydria) or concomitant medication (drugs that reduce gastric acidity), immunocompromised patients (e.g. neutropenic, AIDS, or organ transplant patients), patients with immediately life-threatening systemic fungal infections, AIDS.  Concomitant use of CCBs. Childn. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, abdominal pain, nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that reduce gastric acidity e.g. aluminum hydroxide or H2-receptor antagonist and PPIs. INH, rifabutin, rifampicin; carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin; efavirenz, nevirapine. Ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin, erythromycin; ritonavir-boosted darunavir, fosamprenavir, indinavir. meloxicam."
          },

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with cyclophosphamide as a conditioning regimen prior to allogeneric hematopoietic progenitor cell transplantation for chronic myelogenous leukemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Premedicate patients with anticonvulsants, administer 12 hrs before or 24 hrs after the last dose of busulfan. Administer antimimetics prior to first dose and continue on a fixed schedule throughout therapy. <b>In combination with cyclophosphamide as a conditioning regimen prior to bone marrow or peripheral blood progenitor cell replacement</b> - Patients weighing &gt;12 kg: 0.8 mg/kg IV via a central venous catheter as a 2-hr infusion every 6 hrs for 4 consecutive days for a total of 16 doses (Days 7, 6, 5, and 4); Cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg IV as 1-hr infusion on each of 2 days beginning no sooner than 6 hrs following the 16<sup>th</sup> dose of busulfan (IV Busulfex) (Days 3 and 2). Administer hematopoietic progenitor cells on Day 0."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Myelosuppresion, seizures, hepatic veno-occlusive diseases (HVOD), embryo-fetal toxicity, cardiac tamponade in childn with thalassemia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, cellular dysplasia. Patients with history of seizure disorder, head trauma, or receiving potentially epileptogenic drugs. Rapid infusion is not recommended. Patients who have received prior radiation therapy, greater than or equal to 3 cycles of chemotherapy, or a prior progenitor cell transplant. Childn. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {

            "content": "Fever, headache, asthenia, chills, pain, general edema, allergic reaction, chest pain, inflammation at injection site, back pain; tachycardia, HTN, thrombosis, vasodilation; nausea, stomatitis (mucositis), vomiting, anorexia, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, constipation, dry mouth, rectal disorder, abdominal enlargement; hypomagnesemia, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, hyperbilirubinemia, edema, serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase elevation, increased creatinine; insomnia, anxiety, dizziness, depression; rhinitis, lung disorder, cough, epistaxis, dyspnea; rash, pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Itraconazole, metronidazole, fluconazole, acetaminophen; phenytoin. Incompatibility: polycarbonates."

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adrenocortical insufficiency, shock, hypersensitivity reactions e.g. anaphylactic shock and angioedema, inflammatory bowel disease, hemorrhoids, rheumatic disease, ophthalmic and other conditions requiring immediate metabolic and anti-inflammatory actions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IV</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 100-500 mg 3-4x daily, depending on severity of condition and patient response. <b>Childn 6-12 yrs:</b> 100 mg; <b>1-5 yrs:</b> 50 mg; <b>up to 1 yr:</b> 25 mg. <b>Intra-articular:</b> 5-50 mg depending on size of joint."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infection. Administration of live or live attenuated vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal in patients who had repeated courses of systemic corticosteroids (&gt;3 weeks), reasons for adrenocortical insufficiency other than exogenous corticosteroid therapy; receiving &gt;160 mg hydrocortisone; repeatedly taking doses in the evening; short course prescribed within 1 yr of cessation of long-term therapy. Administration of killed or inactivated vaccines. Not used to treat traumatic brain injury or stroke. Avoid exposure to measles. Patients with ocular herpes simplex, CHF, osteoporosis, HTN, existing or history of severe affective disorders, DM, glaucoma, liver failure or cirrhosis, renal insufficiency, epilepsy or seizure disorders, peptic ulceration, fresh intestinal anastomoses, predisposition to thrombophlebitis, abscess or other pyogenic infections, ulcerative colitis, diverticulitis, myasthenia gravis, recent MI; history of TB; previous corticosteroid-induced myopathy. Concomitant use with aspirin and NSAIDs, digoxin. Post-menopausal women. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anaphylactoid reactions, dyspepsia, peptic ulcer with perforation and hemorrhage, abdominal distention, esophageal ulceration and candidiasis, acute pancreatitis, bowel perforation, increased AST, ALT and alkaline phosphatase, increased susceptibility and severity of infections with suppression of clinical signs and symptoms, opportunistic infections, suppressed reaction to skin tests, recurrence of dormant TB, proximal myopathy, osteoporosis, vertebral and long bone fractures, avascular osteonecrosis, tendon rupture, aseptic necrosis, muscle weakness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenobarbitone, phenytoin, primidone, aminoglutethimide. CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. cimetidine, erythromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, diltiazem, mibefradil). Anticholinesterases, hypoglycemic agents, anti-hypertensives, diuretics. Acetazolamide, loop and thiazide diuretics, carbenoxolone."
          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy in the treatment of partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in patients from 16 yrs with newly diagnosed epilepsy. Adjunctive therapy in the treatment of: partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in adults and childn from 1 month with epilepsy; myoclonic seizures in adults and adolescents from 12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in adults and childn from 12 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab/Syr: Adults and adolescents >16 yrs - Monotherapy</b>: Initially 250 mg twice daily, increased to 500 mg twice daily after 2 weeks. Can be further increased by 250 mg twice daily every 2 weeks. Max 1,500 mg twice daily. <b>Adults (&gt;18 yrs) and adolescents (12-17 yrs) weighing &ge;50 kg - Add-on therapy</b>: Initially 500 mg twice daily, increased up to 1,500 mg twice daily. Dose changes can be made in 500 mg twice daily increases or decreases every 2-4 weeks. <b>Adolescents (12-17 yrs) and childn (4-11 yrs) weighing &lt;50 kg</b>: Initially 10 mg/kg twice daily, can be increased up to 30 mg/kg daily. Dose changes should not exceed increases or decreases of 10 mg/kg twice daily every 2 weeks. <b>Adolescents, childn and infants 6 months - Weighing &le;50 kg</b>: 500 mg twice daily, max 1,500 mg twice daily; <b>25 kg</b>: 250 mg twice daily, max 750 mg twice daily; <b>20 kg</b>: 200 mg twice daily, max 600 mg twice daily; <b>15 kg</b>: 150 mg twice daily, max 450 mg twice daily; <b>10 kg</b>: 100 mg twice daily, max 300 mg twice daily; <b>6 kg</b>: 60 mg twice daily, max 180 mg twice daily. <b>Infants &lt;6 months – weighing 7 kg</b>: 49 mg twice daily, max 147 mg twice daily; <b>5 kg</b>: 35 mg twice daily, max 105 mg twice daily; <b>4 kg</b>: 28 mg twice daily, max 84 mg twice daily. <b>Renal Impairment - Adults and adolescents weighing &gt;50 kg – CrCl &gt;80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 500-1,500 mg twice daily; <b>50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 500-1,000 mg twice daily; <b>30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 250-750 mg twice daily; <b>&lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 250-500 mg twice daily; <b>ESRD patient undergoing dialysis</b>: 500-1,000 mg once daily. Loading dose: 750 mg on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment. Supplemental dose: 250-500 mg following dialysis. <b>Adolescents, childn &lt;50 kg and infants 6-23 months - CrCl >80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 10-30 mg/kg twice daily; <b>50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 10-20 mg/kg twice daily; <b>30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 5-15 mg/kg twice daily; <b>< 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 5-10 mg/kg twice daily; <b>ESRD patient undergoing dialysis:</b> 10-20 mg/kg once daily. Loading dose: 15 mg/kg on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment. Supplemental dose: 5-10 mg/kg following dialysis. <b>IV: Partial onset seizures – Adults &ge;16 yrs</b>: Initially 1,000 mg/day (500 mg twice daily). Max 3,000 mg/day; <b>Childn 4 to &lt;16 yrs</b>: Initially 20 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses (10 mg/kg twice daily), increase to 60 mg/kg daily (30 mg/kg twice daily) every 2 weeks. Max 3,000 mg/day; <b>6 months to &lt;4 yrs</b>: Initially 20 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses (10 mg/kg twice daily), increase to 50 mg/kg daily (25 mg/kg twice daily) every 2 weeks; <b>1-&lt;6 months</b>: Initially 14 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses (7 mg/kg twice daily), increase to 42 mg/kg daily (21 mg/kg twice daily) every 2 weeks. <b>Myoclonic seizures in patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy</b>: Initially 1,000 mg/day (500 mg twice daily), increase to 3,000 mg daily every 2 weeks. <b>Primary generalized tonic-clonic seizure – Adults &ge;16 yrs</b>: Initially 1,000 mg/day (500 mg twice daily), increase to 3,000 mg daily every 2 weeks; <b>Childn 6 to &lt;16 yrs</b>: Initially 20 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses (10 mg/kg twice daily), increase to 60 mg/kg daily (30 mg/kg twice daily) every 2 weeks. <b>Renal impairment – CrCl &gt;80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 500-1,500 mg every 12 hrs; <b>50-80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 500-1,000 mg every 12 hrs; <b>30-50 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 250-750 mg every 12 hrs; <b>&lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup></b>: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs; <b>ESRD using dialysis:</b> 500-1,000 mg every 24 hrs."

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin phosphate, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control when diet and exercise do not provide adequate glycemic control. Adjunct to diet and exercise: (1) In patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM on metformin or sitagliptin (alone or in combination); (2) as part of triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma agonist (e.g. thiazolidinediones) in patients inadequately controlled with any 2 of 3 drugs (metformin, sitagliptin, or sulfonylurea/PPAR-gama agonist); or (3) in combination with insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Taken with food. <b>Initial therapy:</b> 50 mg sitagliptin/500 mg metformin tab 2x daily, may be titrated gradually up to 2,000 mg metformin daily. <b>Inadequately controlled on metformin monotherapy:</b> 50 mg sitagliptin 2x daily with dose of metformin already taken; <b>on sitagliptin monotherapy:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg 2x daily, may be titrated up to 50 mg/1 g 2x daily. <b>As part of combination therapy with a sulfonylurea, thiazolidinedione or insulin:</b> 50 mg sitagliptin 2x daily with metformin dose based on current dose and glycemic control level. <b>Switching from co-administration of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs:</b> Initiate dose of sitagliptin and metformin already being taken."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (e.g. diabetic ketoacidosis) with or without coma. Type 1 DM. Hepatic disease. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Switching from other oral hypoglycemics. Patients exposed to stress, with excessive alcohol intake, risks for hypoglycemia, previously controlled DM developing laboratory abnormalities. Not recommended for patients with eGFR < 45-30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Concomitant use of cationic drugs. May require lower sulfonylurea or insulin doses to reduce risk of hypoglycemia. Discontinue prior to or at the time of iodinated contrast imaging in patients with eGFR &ge;30-< 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, history of liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure, or IV/intra-arterial administration of iodinated contrast, until eGFR has been re-evaluated 48 hrs after and found acceptable; pancreatitis; bullous pemphigoid; condition associated with hypoxemia, dehydration, or sepsis; suspected lactic acidosis; surgical procedures until resumption of oral intake and renal function is stable. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels at 2-3 yr intervals in patients with inadequate vit B<sub>12</sub> or calcium intake or absorption. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, hypoglycemia, abdominal pain, acute pancreatitis, worsening renal function, URTI, fungal skin infection, peripheral edema, nasopharyngitis, constipation, arthralgia, myalgia, pain in extremity and back."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Nifedipine, ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine, thiazide and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid drugs, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P30.31), 50 mg/850 mg (P32.14), 50 mg/1,000 mg (P32.55)."
          }

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), in whom diet and exercise do not provide adequate glycemic control. Adjunct to diet and exercise in patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM: (1) on metformin or sitagliptin (alone or in combination); (2) as part of triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea; (3) as part of triple combination therapy with a PPAR-gamma agonist (e.g. thiazolidinedione); or (4) in combination with insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Single tab once daily with meals, preferably in the evening. Tabs must not be split, broken, crushed, or chewed before swallowing. <b>Type 2 DM inadequately controlled with diet and exercise:</b> 100 mg/1 g, titrate gradually to reduce GI side effects. Max 2 g of metformin. <b>Patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM on metformin monotherapy:</b> 100 mg sitagliptin + metformin (current dose); <b>On sitagliptin monotherapy:</b> 100 mg/1 g. <b>As part of combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or a thiazolidinedione or insulin:</b> 100 mg total daily dose of sitagliptin. May require lower doses to reduce risks of sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycemia. Consider the patient's level of glycemic control and current metformin dose in determining the starting dose of metformin. <b>Patients switching from co-administration of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs:</b> Initiate previously prescribed dose of sitagliptin and metformin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis with or without coma, and radiologic studies involving IV administration of iodinated contrast materials. Patients with an eGFR &ge;30-< 45 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pancreatitis, liver disease, hypoxic states, surgical procedures, alcohol intake. Hypoglycemia in combination with sulfonylureas or insulin. Lactic acidosis in the elderly and in patients with significant renal insufficiency, impaired hepatic function. Monitor renal function before initiation of therapy. Discontinue if bullous pemphigoid or hypersensitivity reactions occur. Concomitant use of cationic drugs eliminated by renal tubular secretion. Discontinue at the time of or prior to iodinated contrast imaging in patients with eGFR &ge;30-< 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, history of liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure, or those who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast. Re-evaluate eGFR 48 hrs after the imaging procedure and restart Janumet if renal function is acceptable. Decreased vit B<sub>12</sub> levels. Patients susceptible to hypoglycemia (e.g. elderly, debilitated, or malnourished; adrenal or pituitary insufficiency, alcohol intoxication, taking adrenergic blockers). Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, pemphigoid, hypoglycemia, abdominal pain, pancreatitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, glyburide, furosemide, nifedipine, OCT2 inhibitors or MATE inhibitors (e.g. ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine), thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release film-coated tablet 100 mg/1 g (P62.50)."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/lpLhWqbviaU9yuFisGhSwsy37JVZ3UK9avDqYVSONZFiVYRzLE.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7E9jNk257jNOug30uAQzzopZOPomyXL8zgCESgxFGEqASwWuwL.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Empagliflozin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control in adults as monotherapy, when diet and exercise alone do not provide adequate glycemic control when use of metformin is inappropriate  due to intolerance, or add-on combination therapy with other glucose-lowering drugs (e.g. insulin). Used  in conjunction with other measures in line with the current standard of care in patients with type 2 DM and established cardiovascular (CV) disease to reduce the risk of CV death. For adults with heart failure  (NYHA class II-IV) independent of LVEF, with or without type 2 DM: to reduce risk of CV death and  hospitalization for heart failure, to slow kidney function decline. Chronic kidney disease (CKD): to reduce  the risk of kidney disease progression or CV death and all-cause hospitalization."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Type 2 DM:</b> Initially 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 25 mg once daily for eGFR &ge;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> and requiring additional glycemic control. <b>Heart failure and CKD:</b> 10 mg once daily. Consider lowering dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy. <b>Renal impairment -  eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 10 mg with additional glucose-lowering treatment if needed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Rare hereditary conditions (e.g. galactose intolerance) incompatible with excipients. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM. Patients with higher risk or history of ketoacidosis; CV disease, on antihypertensive with history of hypotension. Not recommended to initiate in patients on dialysis. Discontinue if ketoacidosis and Fournier’s gangrene is suspected. Temporary interruption in complicated UTI Assess renal function prior to initiation and periodically during treatment. Monitor ketones, vol status, and electrolytes. Elderly &ge;75 yrs. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia (when used with sulfonylurea or insulin); vol depletion; UTI, vaginal moniliasis,  vulvovaginitis, balanitis, and other genital infections, Fournier’s gangrene; constipation; increased urination, dysuria; thirst; Increased blood creatinine, hematocrit, and serum lipids, decreased GFR."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Thiazide and loop diuretics, insulin and insulin secretagogues (e.g. sulfonylurea), lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P48.28), 25 mg (P60.53)."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/G9arRq7AuNXK3qnGmXk0ymyJ6fhDK1AvcxPvjnEGONZ7tuw0La.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KzODWMKAMFu6FnuvzyKCvjadXEo1ouBFORbsGYzaG1GDLhYUxp.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Empagliflozin, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and childn &ge;10 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). For adults with type 2 DM and established cardiovascular (CV) disease, to reduce the risk of CV death; in conjunction with other measures to prevent CV death."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dose. Max 25 mg empagliflozin/2,000 mg metformin daily. Take 1 tab 2x daily with meals. <b>Patients inadequately controlled on metformin alone or in combination with other products including insulin:</b> Initially 5 mg empagliflozin 2x daily with dose of metformin already being taken, may be increased to total 25 mg empagliflozin daily if total 10 mg daily can be tolerated. <b>Patients already treated with empagliflozin:</b> Continue with the same daily dose. <b>Switching from individual monocomponents to combination therapy:</b> Continue with the same daily dose or the nearest therapeutically appropriate dose of metformin. Lower dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy. <b>Renal impairment – GFR 60-89 mL/min:</b> Max 3,000 mg metformin daily (may reduce in relation to declining renal function), max 25 mg empagliflozin daily; <b>45-59 mL/min:</b> Max 2,000 mg metformin daily (starting dose: most &frac12; max dose), no dose adjustment for empagliflozin; <b>30-44 mL/min:</b> Max 1 g metformin daily (starting dose: most &frac12; max dose), no dose adjustment for empagliflozin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidoses). Diabetic pre-coma. Severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function (e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock, IV iodinated contrast agents). Diseases which may cause tissue hypoxia, especially acute disease, or worsening of chronic disease (e.g. decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent MI, shock). Hepatic insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM. Patients with higher risk or history of ketoacidosis; CV disease, on antihypertensive with history of hypotension; childn with eGFR < 60 mL/min. Inform patients for risk of lactic acidosis (e.g. acidotic dyspnea, abdominal pain, muscle cramps asthenia, hypothermia followed by coma). Discontinue if pancreatitis, dehydration, ketoacidosis, Fournier’s gangrene is suspected; prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure or surgery under general, spinal, or epidural anesthesia until &ge;48 hrs after surgery or resumption of oral nutrition and, provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable. Temporary interruption in complicated UTI or until fluid loss is corrected. Assess GFR prior to initiation of treatment and at least annually; more frequently in patients with increased risk of further progression of renal impairment and elderly. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels periodically in patients with risk factors for vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency, ketones, vol status, and electrolytes. May be used with regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function in patients with stable chronic heart failure. Elderly &ge;75 yrs. Childn < 10 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia; nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, constipation; lactic acidosis, vit B<sub>12</sub> decreased/deficiency, ketoacidosis; UTI, vaginal moniliasis, vulvovaginitis, balanitis and other genital infections; hepatitis, liver function tests abnormalities; taste disturbance; increased urination, dysuria; vol depletion; thirst; increased blood creatinine, hematocrit, and serum lipids, decreased GFR; pruritus, allergic skin reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, thiazide and loop diuretics, insulin and insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas), lithium, iodinated contrast agents, NSAIDs, COX-2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonist, verapamil, rifampicin, cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, isavuconazole, crizotinib, olaparib."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg/500 mg (P23.33), 5 mg/1 g (P34.25), 12.5 mg/500 mg (P31.64), 12.5 mg/1 g (P34.31)."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qwd8pFT9KizTKpUWPRQR4w9jkvC8PVxNclC329SGIruQdFhIHM.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adult patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus indicated to improve glycemic control as monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone and for whom metformin is inappropriate due to contraindications or intolerance. As dual therapy in combination with: metformin when diet and exercise plus metformin alone do not provide adequate glycemic control; sulfonylurea when diet and exercise plus maximal tolerated dose of sulfonylurea alone do not provide adequate glycemic control and when metformin is inappropriate due to contraindications or intolerance; PPAR-gamma agonist (i.e. thiazolidinedione) when use of PPAR-gamma agonist is appropriate and when diet and exercise plus PPAR-gamma agonist alone do not provide adequate glycemic control. As triple oral therapy in combination with sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma and metformin when diet and exercise plus dual therapy with these medicinal products do not provide adequate glycemic control. As add-on to insulin (with or without metformin) when diet and exercise plus stable dose of insulin do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "100 mg once daily. <b>In combination with metformin and/or a PPAR-gamma agonist:</b> Dose of metformin and/or PPAR-gamma agonist should be maintained, and sitagliptin tab administered concomitantly. <b>In combination with a sulfonylurea or with insulin:</b> A lower dose of the sulfonylurea or insulin may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia. <b>Moderate renal impairment (CrCl < 30 to < 50 mL/min):</b> 50 mg once daily. <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or with ESRD requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis:</b> 25 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used in type I DM or for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis. Severe hepatic impairment. Risk of acute pancreatitis or history of pancreatitis. Hypoglycemia. Hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. anaphylaxis, angioedema, and exfoliative skin conditions (i.e. SJS). Discontinue if bullous pemphigoid is suspected. Renal impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia. Headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid. Ciclosporine. Digoxin. Quinolone antibiotics (e.g. ofloxacin)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P34.90), 100 mg (P35.59)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Symptomatic relief of hyperacidity associated with peptic ulcer, gastritis, esophagitis, and dyspepsia.             "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 1-2 tabs 1 hr after each meal and at bedtime. Tab may be chewed then swallowed without water or swallowed whole with water."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with kidney disease, intestinal obstruction, appendicitis, fecal impaction, gastric outlet obstruction, constipation, phosphate depletion and low serum phosphate, osteomalacia."

          {

            "content": "Patients at risk of aluminum and magnesium accumulation and toxicity (advanced kidney disease). Phenylketonurics. Pregnancy.",

          },
          {

            "content": "Diarrhea and constipation. Excessive doses may result in high aluminum and magnesium levels in the blood of patients with kidney impairment."
          },

            "content": "Tetracyclines, iron and iron-containing preparations; oral digoxin, indomethacin, isoniazid, quinolones (e.g. ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin), ketoconazole; salicylates e.g. aspirin; weakly basic drugs e.g. quinidine, chlorpromazine, propranolol, diazepam; weakly acidic drugs e.g. phenytoin, pentobarbital, warfarin; dicumarol and pseudoephedrine; chlordiazepoxide, bisphosphonates."
          },

    "id": 4574,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4574,
        "brand_name": "Jinarc",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/shsq2Y5Viq37u7nG6j3JnNJiac8KPrBWBoTeuICYEyau1zlFSn.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HCwayMYVF8aSbWZyIWeuzRWKlkrgXBLuno9Q8ZRfp47SGox3be.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KsDLtliGAsGfiL5iDVkCPBqiw0irz6gC2TbbdJL2YPiUOWm91Z.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tolvaptan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vasopressin antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "To slow progression of cyst development and renal insufficiency of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in adults with chronic kidney disease stage 1 and 4 at initiation of treatment with evidence of rapidly progressing disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 60 mg/day as split-dose regimen (i.e. 45 mg taken upon waking and before the morning meal + 15 mg taken 8 hrs later). May be increased to a split-dose regimen of 90 mg/day (60 mg + 30 mg), up to 120 mg/day (90 mg + 30 mg), with at least weekly intervals between titrations. <b>Patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors</b> - Daily split-dose 60 mg + 30 mg or 90 mg + 30 mg: Reduce to 30 mg once daily, further reduce to 15 mg if not well tolerated; 45 mg + 15 mg: Reduce 15 mg once daily. <b>Patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors</b> - Daily split-dose 90 mg + 30 mg: Reduce to 45 mg + 15 mg; 60 mg + 30 mg: Reduce to 30 mg + 15 mg; 45 mg + 15 mg: Reduce to 15 mg + 15 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Elevated liver enzymes or signs or symptoms of liver injury before initiation of treatment that meet requirements for permanent discontinuation; anuria, vol depletion, hypernatremia. Patients who cannot perceive or respond to thirst. Concomitant use of grapefruit juice. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal (eGFR &lt;20) and severe hepatic impairment, DM. Monitor liver enzymes regularly; uric acid concentrations. Instruct patients to drink water or other aqueous fluids at 1<sup>st</sup> sign of thirst. Drink 1-2 glasses of fluid before bedtime. Patients with or at risk of dehydration, urinary outflow obstruction. Monitor fluid and electrolyte status. Correct serum sodium abnormalities before treatment. Childn. Elderly &gt;50 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Polydipsia; headache, dizziness; diarrhea, dry mouth; nocturia, pollakiuria, polyuria; fatigue, thirst. Dehydration, hypernatremia, decreased appetite, hyperuricemia, hyperglycemia, gout; insomnia; palpitations; dyspnea; abdominal pain and distention, constipation, dyspepsia, GERD; abnormal hepatic function; rash, pruritus; muscle spasms; asthenia; increased ALT and AST, decreased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers. Hypertonic sodium chloride soln, oral sodium formulations, and other medicinal products that increase serum sodium concentration. Diuretics, vasopressin analogues. Digoxin, dabigatran, rosuvastatin, pitavastatin, methotrexate, ciprofloxacin, sulfasalazine, metformin. Grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 15 mg (P371.00), 30 mg (P371.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 105,
          "name": "Otsuka (Philippines) Pharmaceutical, Inc."
        },

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD), social anxiety disorder (SAD) or social phobia, generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), panic disorder with or without agoraphobia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>MDD:</b> 10 mg up to max 20 mg once daily for at least 6 months. <b>SAD, GAD, OCD:</b> 10 mg up to max 20 mg once daily. <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia:</b> 5 mg once daily for 1<sup>st</sup> week, increase to 10 mg once daily for &ge;3 months.             "content": "N-Acyl-Alpha Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of partial onset seizures (monotherapy or adjunctive therapy) and as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients &ge;4 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults &ge;17 yrs – Monotherapy</b>: Initially 100 mg twice daily (for partial onset seizures), increase by 50 mg twice daily every week. Maintenance: 150 mg-200 mg twice daily (for partial onset seizures); Adjunctive therapy: Initially 50 mg twice daily, increase by 50 mg twice daily every week. Maintenance: 100 mg-200 mg twice daily; Alternative initial dosage: 200 mg single loading dose, followed 12 hrs later by 100 mg twice daily; <b>Loading dose</b>: 200 mg, followed 12 hrs later by 100 mg twice daily for 1 week. <b>Childn &ge;50 kg</b>: 50 mg twice daily, increase by 50 mg twice daily every week. Maintenance - Monotherapy: 150 mg-200 mg twice daily (for partial onset-seizures); Adjunctive therapy: 100 mg-200 mg twice daily. <b>30-&lt;50 kg</b>: Initially 1 mg/kg twice daily, increase by 1 mg/kg twice daily every week. Maintenance: 2-4 mg/kg twice daily. <b>11-&lt;30 kg</b>: Initially 1 mg/kg twice daily, increase by 1 mg/kg twice daily every week. Maintenance: 3-6 mg/kg twice daily. <b>Converting from a single antiepileptic (AED) to lacosamide monotherapy for partial-onset seizures</b>: Achieve therapeutic dose for at least 3 days before AED withdrawal. Gradually withdraw the concomitant AED over at least 6 weeks. <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min in adults, &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> in childn) or ESRD</b>: Reduce by 25% of max dosage. Hemodialysis: Administer a supplemental dose up to 50% after dialysis. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: Reduce by 25% of max dosage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Known 2<sup>nd</sup>- or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor patients for signs of suicidal ideation and behaviors. Patients with known conduction problems, severe cardiac disease (e.g. history of MI or heart failure), phenylketonuria.           },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache, nausea, and diplopia. Depression, confusional state, insomnia, balance disorder, abnormal coordination, memory impairment, cognitive disorder, somnolence, tremor, nystagmus, hypoesthesia, dysarthria, attention disturbance, paraesthesia, blurred vision, vertigo, tinnitus, vomiting, constipation, flatulence, dyspepsia, dry mouth, diarrhea, pruritus, rash, muscle spasms, gait disturbance, asthenia, fatigue, irritability, feeling drunk, fall, skin laceration, contusion."
          },

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: Monotherapy and adjunctive treatment of partial seizures with or without secondary generalization. Adjunctive therapy of myoclonic seizures and primarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures. <b>IV/Oral soln</b>: Treatment of partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalisation; Monotherapy in adults &ge;16 yrs with newly diagnosed epilepsy and as adjunctive therapy in adults and childn (IV: Childn &ge;4 yrs, Oral soln: Childn &ge;1 month) with epilepsy. Adjunctive therapy in patients &ge;12 yrs for myoclonic seizures in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab - Adults &ge;16 yrs and childn &gt;50 kg</b>: Initially 500 mg twice a day, may be increased in steps of 1 g every 2-4 weeks until effective antiepileptic control is achieved. Max 3 g/day. <b>Childn &lt;50 kg</b>: 20 mg/kg daily, may be increased in steps of 20 mg/kg every week. Max 60 mg/kg daily. <b>Monotherapy</b>: 500 mg daily, may be increased to 1 g daily after 2 weeks. May further be increased in steps of 500 mg every 2 weeks. Max 3 g daily. <b>IV - Monotherapy - Adults and adolescents &ge;16 yrs</b>: Initially 250 mg twice daily, increased to 500 mg twice daily after 2 weeks. May be further increased by 250 mg twice daily every 2 weeks. Max 1,500 mg twice daily. <b>Add-on therapy - Adults &ge;18 yrs and adolescents 12-17 yrs weighing &ge;50 kg</b>: Initially 500 mg twice daily, dose increases or decreases can be made every 2-4 weeks by 500 mg twice daily. Max 1,500 mg twice daily. <b>Adolescents and childn 4-11 yrs weighing &lt;50 kg</b>: Initially 10 mg/kg twice daily, increases or decreases should not exceed 10 mg/kg twice daily every 2 weeks. Max 30 mg/kg twice daily; <b>Renal impairment - Adults and adolescents weighing &gt;50 kg</b> - CrCl &ge;80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 500-1,500 mg twice daily; 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 500-1,000 mg twice daily; 30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-750 mg twice daily; &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-500 mg twice daily; ESRD, patients on dialysis: 750 mg loading dose then 500-1,000 mg once daily followed by 250-500 mg supplemental dose after dialysis. <b>Adolescents and childn &ge;4 yrs weighing &lt;50 kg</b> - CrCl &ge;80 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 10-30 mg/kg twice daily; 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 10-20 mg/kg twice daily; 30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 5-15 mg/kg twice daily; &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 5-10 mg/kg twice daily; ESRD or patients undergoing dialysis: 15 mg/kg loading dose then 10-20 mg/kg once daily followed by 5-10 mg supplemental dose after dialysis. <b>Severe hepatic impairment (CrCl &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>)</b>: Reduce to 50% of daily maintenance dose. <b>Oral soln - Monotherapy - Adults and adolescents &ge;16 yrs</b>: Initially 250 mg twice daily, increased to 500 mg twice daily after 2 weeks and can be further increased by 250 mg twice daily every 2 weeks depending upon response. Max 1,500 mg twice daily. <b>Add-on therapy - Adults (18 yrs) and adolescents (12-17 yrs) weighing &ge;50 kg</b> : Initially 500 mg twice daily and can be started on 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment. Dose can be increased up to 1,500 mg twice daily; changes can be made in 500 mg increases or decreases every 2-4 weeks. <b>Severe hepatic impairment (with CrCl < 60 mL/min/m<sup>2</sup>)</b>: Reduce by 50% of daily maintenance dose. <b>Add-on therapy - Infants (6-23 months), childn (2-11 yrs), and adolescents (12-17 yrs) weighing &lt;50 kg</b>: Initially 10 mg/kg twice daily, can be increased up to 30 mg/kg twice daily and should not exceed increases/decreases of 10 mg/kg twice daily every 2 weeks; <b>Infants (1-6 months)</b>: Initially 7 mg/kg twice daily, can be increased up to 21 mg/kg twice daily and should not exceed increases/decreases of 7 mg/kg twice daily every 2 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },

            "title": "Precautions",

May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Elderly. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",

              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },

                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {

                },

          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, headache, fatigue/asthenia, dizziness. <b>Tab</b>: CNS, dermatologic, ENT, GI, genitourinary, hematologic-lymphatic, hepatic, metabolic, musculoskeletal, respiratory disorders; accidental injury, infection, pain, influenza, flu syndrome, face edema. <b>IV</b>: Nasopharyngitis; anorexia, depression, hostility/aggression, anxiety, insomnia, nervousness/irritability, convulsion, balance disorder, lethargy, tremor, vertigo, cough, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, vomiting, nausea, rash. <b>Oral soln</b>: Increased seizure frequency, postural dizziness."

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of peripheral and central neuropathic pain in adults. Adjunctive therapy in adults with partial seizures with or without secondary generalization. Treatment of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "150-600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>Neuropathic pain</b>: Initially 150 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 3- to 7-day interval, and if needed up to max 600 mg/day after an additional 7-day interval. <b>Epilepsy</b>: Initially 150 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>GAD</b>: 150-600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. Initially 150 mg/day, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week. May be increased to 450 mg/day following an additional week. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Diabetic patients. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema occur. Increase occurrence of accidental injury (fall) in elderly. Vision-related effects. Patients with CHF, history of substance abuse, underlying conditions that may precipitate encephalopathy; rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Increased CNS adverse reactions in the treatment of central neuropathic pain due to spinal cord injury. Monitor for signs of suicidal ideation and behavior. Reduced lower GIT function. Concomitant use with opioids. Monitor for symptoms of misuse, abuse or dependence. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Childn &lt;12 yrs and adolescents. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, somnolence, headache. Nasopharyngitis; increased appetite; ataxia, abnormal coordination, tremor, dysarthria, amnesia, memory impairment, attention disturbance, paresthesia, hypoesthesia, sedation, balance disorder, lethargy; blurred vision, diplopia; vertigo; vomiting, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, abdominal distention, dry mouth; erectile dysfunction; peripheral edema, edema, abnormal gait, fall, feeling drunk, abnormal feeling, fatigue; increased weight. Muscle cramps, arthralgia, back pain, pain in limb, cervical spasm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ethanol and lorazepam, opioids and other CNS depressants, oxycodone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 75 mg (P34.38)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7694hKgfxITbhyxe82cFlUFTB29Yjii6kq0jX75thf4ECwjwyC.png",

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dexmedetomidine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Alpha-2 Selective Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>ICU sedation</b>: Indicated for sedation of initially intubated and mechanically ventilated patients during treatment in an intensive care setting. <b>Procedural sedation</b>: Indicated for sedation of non-intubated patients prior to and/or during surgical and other procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer using a controlled infusion device. Dexmedetomidine concentration after dilution should be 4 mcg/mL. <b>Initiation of ICU sedation – Adults</b>: Loading infusion of 1 mcg/kg over 10 mins; <b>For less invasive procedures</b>: Loading infusion of 0.5 mcg/kg given over 10 mins. <b>Patients &gt;65 yrs</b>: Loading infusion of 0.5 mcg/kg over 10 mins. <b>Maintenance of procedural sedation – Adults</b>: Initiated at 0.6 mcg/kg/hr and titrated to achieve desired clinical effect with doses ranging from 0.2 to 1 mcg/kg/hr. <b>Awake fiberoptic intubation patients</b>: Maintenance infusion of 0.7 mcg/kg/hr is recommended until the endotracheal tube is secured. <b>Elderly, patients with impaired renal or hepatic function</b>: Reduce dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with preexisting severe bradycardia disorders (e.g. advanced heart block), or ventricular dysfunction (e.g. ejection fraction &lt;30%) including CHF and cardiac failure. Hypotension in hypovolemic patients, elderly &gt;65 yrs, and diabetic patients. Should not be administered for greater than 24 hrs. Abrupt discontinuation may result in clonidine-like withdrawal symptoms (e.g. nervousness, agitation and headache, accompanied or followed by a rapid rise in blood pressure and elevated catecholamine concentrations in the plasma). Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypotension, hypertension, bradycardia, dry mouth, and nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anesthetics, sedatives, hypnotics, opioids; vasodilators, negative chronotropic agents; propofol or midazolam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for infusion 100 mcg/mL x 2 mL vial (P8,145.00)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Urinary Alkalinizers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of renal tubular acidosis with calcium stones, hypocitraturic calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis of any etiology, and uric acid lithiasis with or without calcium stones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Severe hypocitraturia (urinary citrate < 150 mg/day):</b> Initially 60 mEq/day (20 mEq 3x a day or 15 mEq 4x a day with meals or within 30 mins after food). <b>Mild to moderate hypocitraturia (>150 mg/day):</b> Initially 30 mEq/day (10 mEq 3x a day with meals)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with or conditions predisposing hyperkalemia i.e. chronic renal failure, uncontrolled DM, acute dehydration, strenuous physical exercise in unconditioned individuals, adrenal insufficiency, extensive tissue breakdown or administration of potassium-sparing agents. Patients for whom there is cause for arrest or delay in tab passage through the GIT e.g. suffering from delayed gastric emptying, esophageal compression, intestinal obstruction or stricture or those taking anticholinergic medication. Patients with PUD and renal insufficiency (GFR <0.7 mL/kg/min)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hyperkalemia and cardiac arrest. Discontinue immediately and investigate possibility of bowel perforation or obstruction if there is severe vomiting, abdominal pain or GI bleeding. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Isotretinoin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Acne Agents & Cell Stimulants & Proliferants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of severe acne not responding to other measures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 0.5 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks. <b>Maintenance dose:</b> 0.1-1.0 mg/kg/day. Max 1 mg/kg/day within a limited duration. Usual duration of therapy is 16 weeks. If cystic acne persists, a second course of therapy may be initiated. <b>Patients with severe renal impairment:</b> Initially 10 mg/day, gradually increase up to 1 mg/kg/day. <b>Intolerant patients:</b>10 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic impairment, hypervitaminosis A, and hyperlipidemia. Concomitant use with tetracyclines. Childn < 12 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of depression, intestinal and musculoskeletal disorder. Increase risk of fetus deformity. Control elevations of serum triglycerides. Benign intracranial hypertension.  Monitor liver function/enzymes before use and 1 month after starting treatment, and subsequently at 3 months. Concomitant use with epidermolysis/keratolysis treatment and UV therapy. Monitor blood glucose of patients with diabetes or taking antidiabetics. Do not donate blood during therapy and for 1 month following discontinuance of the drug. Concomitant use with epidermolysis/keratolysis treatment and UV therapy. Monitor blood glucose of patients with diabetes or taking antidiabetics. Do not administer progesterone as contraceptive method during therapy. May impair night vision.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypervitaminosis A, cheilitis, muscle pain, arthralgia, arthritis, neurological, visual disturbances, vomiting and IBD, bronchospasm, anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, hypertriglyceridemia or alterations in blood sugar levels, edema, fatigue, weight loss."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Vit A supplements and tetracyclines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 10 mg."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/476O1OnGQCgHymbpayXRleoMzYY67R8V92oV2oK5bwfwJpzeuK.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/lQqY4ApbHOG8hsFa3iBlTKjwyTzKUHycz4Hbi0qUEuqijt07fG.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dabigatran etexilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients who have undergone elective total hip replacement surgery or total knee replacement surgery. Treatment of VTE and prevention of recurrent VTE in pediatric patients from birth to &lt;18 yrs of age."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults- Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with NVAF with &ge;1 risk factors (SPAF):</b> 150 mg twice daily. <b>VTE prevention after elective orthopedic surgery: Begin treatment 1-4 hrs post-surgery:</b> Initially 100 mg, followed by 110 twice daily. Duration- knee replacement: 10 days; hip replacement: 28-35 days. Delay treatment if hemostasis is not secured. If treatment is not started on the day of surgery, initiate with 110 mg twice daily. <b>Dose reduction:</b> Moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-50 mL/min), concomitant treatment with verapamil, amiodarone, quinidine, and early &ge;75 yrs: Initially 75 mg, followed by 150 mg once daily. <b>Childn- Primary prevention of VTE:</b> Total daily dose in 2 divided doses, 12 hrs apart: 11 to &lt;13 kg (8 to &lt;9 yrs): 150 mg: 13 to &lt;21 kg (8 to &lt;14 yrs): 220 mg; 21 to &lt;31 kg (8 to &lt;18 yrs): 300 mg; 3 to &lt;41 kg (8 to &lt;18 yrs): 370 mg; 41 to 51 kg (8 to &lt;18 yrs): 440 mg; 51 to &lt;61 kg (8 to &lt;18 yrs): 520 mg;  &ge;61 kg (8 to &lt;18 yrs): 600 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) in adult patients, eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> in pediatric patients, active clinically significant bleeding, lesion or conditions considered at risk for major bleeding. Concomitant treatment with any other anticoagulant, heparin derivatives, ketoconazole, ciclosporin, itraconazole, dronedarone, glecaprevir/pibrentasivir. Hepatic impairment/liver disease. Prosthetic heart valve requiring anticoagulant treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Assess renal function prior to and during treatment. Hemorrhagic risk. Surgery and interventions, emergency surgery, subacute surgery, elective surgery. Spinal anesthesia, epidural anesthesia, lumbar puncture. Pedriatriic cancer pafients. Patients with antiphospholipid syndrome. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, decreased hgb, epistaxis, hemorrhage (GI, genitourological, rectal, skin), abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, hepatic function abnormalities."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Unfractionated heparin (UHF), low molecular weight heparins (LMWH), heparin derivatives (e.g., fondaparinux, desirudin). thrombolytic medicinal products, vitamin K antagonists, rivaroxaban, P-gp inhibitors and inducers, protease inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 75 mg (P28.00), 110 mg (P38.00), 150 mg (P48.00)."
          }
        ],

      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3082,
        "brand_name": "Karvil",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hYHqIeNg6PjMLEgqXJkj9jCrY4sRT23LsCuE4Gdcl3IliVGgnu.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hYHqIeNg6PjMLEgqXJkj9jCrY4sRT23LsCuE4Gdcl3IliVGgnu.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/oV8IMifI2wSSioIi0NDzSVOLwOtGkyyc3eIZt3QLwW9BMuvURW.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Carvedilol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of essential hypertension (HTN) and angina pectoris, and as an adjunct to standard therapy in symptomatic heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: Initially 6.25 mg twice daily, maintain for 7-14 days if tolerated then increase to 12.5 mg twice daily and may further be increased to 50 mg once daily or in divided doses at intervals of at least 2 weeks. <b>Elderly</b>: 12.5 mg once daily. <b>Heart failure</b>: Initially 3.125 mg twice daily, increased to 6.25 mg after 2 weeks and then increased gradually at intervals not &lt;2 weeks to max tolerated dose (patients with severe heart failure weighing &lt;85 kg: Max 25 mg twice daily; mild to moderate heart failure weighing &gt;85 kg: Max 50 mg twice daily). <b>Angina pectoris</b>: Initially 12.5 mg twice daily, increase to 25 mg twice daily after 2 days. <b>Left ventricular dysfunction following myocardial infarction</b>: Initially 6.25 mg twice daily, increase to 12.5 mg twice daily after 3-10 days  then to target dose 25 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hepatic impairment. Patients with NYHA class IV decompensated cardiac failure requiring IV inotropic therapy, bronchial asthma or related bronchospastic conditions, 2<sup>nd</sup>-or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block, sick sinus syndrome (unless permanent pacemaker is in place), cardiogenic shock or severe bradycardia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with COPD with bronchospastic component who are not receiving oral or inhaled medication; peripheral vascular disease. Use with anesthesia known to depress myocardial function. Diabetic patients receiving insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents. Patients with ischemic heart disease, pheochromocytoma, Prinzmetal’s angina.         "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Drugs for Hyperkalemia and Hyperphosphatemia"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the control of hyperphosphatemia in adult patients receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis; patients with chronic kidney disease not on dialysis with serum phosphorus &gt;1.78 mmol/L."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initial dose - Serum phosphorus level - of 1.78-2.42 mmol/L (5.5-7.5 mg/dL): 2.4 g/day; &gt;2.42 mmol/L (7.5 mg/dL): 4.8 g/day. Titration and maintenance: Titrate dose every 2-4 weeks until an acceptable serum phosphorus level is reached. Swallow whole. Do not crush, chew, or break into pieces prior to administration. Sevelamer carbonate should be used with calcium supplements, vitamin D, or its analogs to control the development of renal bone disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hypophosphatemia. Bowel obstruction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with CKD not on dialysis with serum phosphorus &lt;1.78 mmol/L. Patients with dysphagia, swallowing disorders, severe GI motility disorder e.g. untreated or severe gastroparesis, retentions of gastric contents and abnormal or irregular bowel motion, active IBD, major GI tract surgery. Intestinal obstruction and ileus or subileus. May develop low levels of vitamins A, D, E, and K; folate deficiency; hypocalcemia or hypercalcemia; metabolic acidosis; peritonitis. Patients with hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine; hyperparathyroidism; lactose intolerance (hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption). Patients taking anti-arrhythmic or anti-seizure medicinal products. Possible accumulation in long-term chronic treatment (&gt;1 yr). Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, and abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciprofloxacin, ciclosporin, mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, levothyroxine, anti-arrhythmics, anti-seizure medicinal products, and folic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 800 mg x 30s (P930.00)."

  {
