    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3865,
        "brand_name": "Kefsyn",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ZqLX4l8Yc0JHAqGWgjzRRs9Z4YL7bgD9y0KTXoURgdr8uadejq.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/IkbjvrtS2letHKiCvdAaKSQ1afdKzt51L4dpSoEE3RobL0KUrG.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/uZ6loel2L8Omo1JP0h1hTFelXrAWkcJ73IxnAf2yZvy4A8RAdA.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefuroxime (Oral: Axetil; IM/IV: Sodium)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of susceptible infections e.g. bone and joint infections, bronchitis and other lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI), gonorrhea, meningitis, otitis media, peritonitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, skin infections (e.g. soft tissue infections), and urinary tract infections (UTI). Prophylaxis to surgical infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – Adults – Uncomplicated UTI:</b> 125 mg twice daily. <b>RTI:</b> 250-500 mg twice daily. <b>Pneumonia or exacerbations of chronic bronchitis:</b> 1.5 g twice daily or 750 mg twice daily, respectively, in parenteral route followed by oral 500 mg twice daily. <b>Lyme disease:</b> 500 mg twice daily for 20 days. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 1 g single dose. <b>Childn >2 yrs with otitis media:</b> 250 mg or 15 mg/kg, twice daily. Max 500 mg daily. <b> >3 months:</b> 125 mg or 10 mg/kg, twice daily. Max 250 mg daily. <b>IM/IV - Adults:</b> 750 mg three times daily. <b>Severe infections:</b> 1.5 g thrice daily, may be increased to total dose 3-6 g daily given every 6 hrs. <b>Infants and childn</b>: 30-60 mg/kg/day, may be increased to 100 mg/kg given in 3-4 divided doses. <b>Most infections:</b> 60 mg/kg/day. <b>Renal impairment – CrCl < 20 mL/min:</b> Reduce dose. <b>10 mL/min:</b> 750 mg once daily. <b>Hemodialysis:</b> A further 750 mg given at the end of dialysis. <b>Continuous peritoneal dialysis:</b> 750 mg twice daily. <b>Susp – Adults – Uncomplicated UTI:</b> 250 mg (1 tsp) twice daily. <b>RTI:</b> 250-500 mg twice daily. <b>Childn >3 months:</b> 250 mg or 10 mg/kg twice daily, max: 250 mg daily. <b>Childn >2 yrs with otitis media:</b> 250 mg or 15 mg/kg twice daily, max: 500 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cross-sensitivity in patients allergic to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics, history of hypersensitivity to other beta-lactam agents, renal impairment. May cause Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions following treatment of Lyme disease, overgrowth of <i>Candida</i> and other non-susceptible microorganisms (e.g. <i>Enterococci</i> and <i>Clostridium difficile</i>), mild to life-threatening pseudomembranous colitis. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>IM/IV:</b> Patients receiving concurrent treatment of potent diuretics. Superinfection. <b>Susp:</b> Patients with renal impairment. Monitor renal and hematological status.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances e.g. diarrhea, nausea, vomiting. Overgrowth of <i>Candida</i>. Pseudomembranous colitis. <b>Tab:</b> Erythema multiforme, SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis. Mild to moderate hearing loss. <b>IM/IV:</b> Pain in IM injection site. Hypersensitivity reactions e.g. skin rashes (maculopapular, urticaria), drug fever, anaphylaxis. Decreased hemoglobin concentration and/or eosinophilia, leukopenia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. High levels of SGOT, SGPT and bilirubin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Tab and Susp:</b> Probenecid. <b>IM/IV:</b> Diuretics e.g. furosemide and aminoglycoside."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P63.72). Powder for injection (IM/IV) 750 mg (P362.88). Granules for oral suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 50 mL (P444.67)."
          }

          "original": null,

          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ceftazidime pentahydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of nosocomial pneumonia, bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis, bacterial meningitis, chronic suppurative otitis media, malignant otitis externa; complicated urinary tract (UTI), skin and soft tissue, intra-abdominal, bone and joint infections; peritonitis associated with dialysis in patients on CAPD; bacteremia. Management of neutropenic patients with fever suspected due to a bacterial infection; peri-op prophylaxis of UTI for patients undergoing trans-urethral resection of the prostate (TURP)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn weighing &ge;40 kg</b> - Intermittent administration - <b>Bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis:</b> 100-150 mg/kg/day every 8 hrs. Max 9 g/day. <b>Febrile neutropenia, nosocomial pneumonia, bacterial meningitis, bacteremia:</b> 2 g every 8 hrs. <b>Bone and joint, complicated skin and soft tissue, intra-abdominal infections, peritonitis associated with dialysis in CAPD patients, chronic suppurative otitis media, malignant otitis media:</b> 1-2 g every 8 hrs. <b>Complicated UTI:</b> 1-2 g every 8 or 12 hrs. <b>Peri-op prophylaxis for TURP:</b> 1 g at induction of anesthesia, and 2<sup>nd</sup> dose at catheter removal. Continuous infusion: Loading dose of 2 g, followed by 4-6 g continuous infusion every 24 hrs. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl 50-31 mL/min: 1 g every 12 hrs (intermittent administration), loading dose of 2 g followed by 1-3 g continuous infusion every 24 hrs; 30-16 mL/min: 1 g every 24 hrs (intermittent administration), loading dose of 2 g followed by 1 g continuous infusion every 24 hrs; 15-6 mL/min: 0.5 g every 24 hrs; &lt;5 mL/min: 0.5 g every 48 hrs. <b>Infants and toddlers &gt;2 months and childn weighing &lt;40 kg</b> - Intermittent administration - <b>Most infections:</b> 100-150 mg/kg/day given in 3 divided doses. Max 6 g/day. <b>Neutropenia, bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis, bacterial meningitis, bacteremia:</b> 150 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. Max 6 g/day. Continuous infusion: Loading dose of 60-100 mg/kg followed by 100-200 mg/kg/day continuous infusion. Max 6 g/day. <b>Neonates and infants &le;2 months:</b> 25-60 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl 50-31 mL/min: 25 mg/kg every 12 hrs; 3-16 mL/min: 25 mg/kg every 24 hrs; 15-6 mL/min: 12.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs; &lt;5 mL/min: 12.5 mg/kg every 48 hrs. Hemodialysis: 1 g daily as single dose or in divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not used as single agent for treatment of some types of infections. Discontinue if severe hypersensitivity reactions, and diarrhea occur. Patients with renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Eosinophilia, thrombocytopenia, phlebitis or thrombophlebitis, diarrhea, transient elevations of hepatic enzymes, maculopapular or urticarial rash, pain and inflammation, positive Coombs’ test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, furosemide, chloramphenicol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 1 g."
          }

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ethinylestradiol, levonorgestrel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Contraception, for treatment of menstrual disorders e.g. dysmenorrhea, premenstrual syndrome, and menorrhagia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Take 1 pill daily, beginning on the first day of menstrual bleeding or any day as long as not pregnant for 28 days. Start with the pill marked number '1' and follow the arrows indicated on the pack. The interval between 2 pills should be 24 hrs. Should be taken at the same time every day, preferably at the time of the evening meal. A pack is good for 28 days. Start a new pack after taking the last white pill."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Liver disorders, clotting disorders, breast and cervical cancer, sickle-cell anemia, hormone-active tumors, hyperlipidemia, severe CV diseases, previous or existing thromboembolic diseases, idiopathic jaundice. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "DM, high BP, varicose veins, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, migraine, ophthalmological problems and tetany. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headaches, gastric upsets, nausea, vomiting, change in appetite, breast tenderness, slight changes in body weight and libido, depressive moods, or interference with liver functions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Analgesics, anti-migraine and tranquilizer. Ampicillin, chloramphenicol, neomycin, penicillin V, nitrofurantoin, sulfonamides, tetracycline and isoniazid. Clarithromycin, erythromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir, grapefruit juice. Carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, felbamate, topiramate, phenytoin, griseofulvin, troglitazone, phenylbutazone, rifampicin and troleandomycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "<b>Each blister pack - 21 beige tablet:</b> Ethinylestradiol 30 mcg, levonorgestrel 150 mcg; <b>Each 7 white tablet:</b> Lactose 40 mg x 28s."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wAWzvRQKtdzSJLfZQGwxCBjWRAhJhb6gSjjpGQktaytbPflY44.jpg"
        },

        "content": "Furosemide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Loop Diuretics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of edema associated with heart failure including pulmonary edema, and renal and hepatic disorders. In high doses, used for management of oliguria due to renal failure or insufficiency. Treatment of hypertension (HTN) alone or in combination with other anti-hypertensives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Edema:</b> Initially 40 mg once daily. In mild cases, dose may be adjusted to 20 mg daily or 40 mg on alternate days. Dose of &ge;80 mg given once or twice daily, or intermittently in some patients. Severe cases may require gradual titration up to 600 mg/day. <b>Childn:</b> 1-3 mg/kg daily. Max 40 mg daily. <b>HTN:</b> 40-80 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Anuria or renal failure caused by nephrotoxic or hepatotoxic drugs (high doses) or in association with hepatic coma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pre-coma states associated with hepatic cirrhosis. Patients with prostatic hyperplasia or impairment of micturition. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fluid and electrolyte imbalance (hyponatremia, hypokalemia, hypochloremic alkalosis). Increased urinary excretion of calcium, hyperuricemia and precipitation of gout attacks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Digitalis glycosides; drugs that prolong QT-interval prolongation e.g. astemizole, terfenadine, halofantrine, pimozide, sotalol. Atracurium. Corticosteroids, corticotropin, beta2-agonists (e.g. salbutamol), carbenoxolone, amphotericin B, reboxetine. Alpha blockers, ACE inhibitors. Alcohol, barbiturates, opioids. Lithium. Allopurinol. Tetracyclines. NSAIDs, pressor amines, oral hypoglycemics, cephalosporins, aminoglycoside antibacterials and other ototoxic drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 40 mg (P6.50)."
          }
        ],

          {

            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg daily in one or two divided doses. <b>Intravascular vol depletion (e.g. treated with high-dose diuretics) and elderly >75 yrs:</b> Initially 25 mg daily. <b>Diabetic nephropathy:</b> Initially 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg once daily.             "content": "Dizziness, asthenia/fatigue, vertigo."

            "content": "Rifampicin, fluconazole; potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements or salt-containing potassium; indomethacin."

  {
    "id": 3699,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3699,
        "brand_name": "Kepreptol",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/z8kuzjUNBCQvJNkbtG7Td7IBzy2BcSGvyxpVZtTZ0yTMiKOjyk.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xLj704YfxuYN56bgBP0w4JQv49OoLXX1GTeh9tnS8a2aA8zkzI.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MiarZMuaGF7XeEf66OdZpafufzC2vAzgbd23sjwvsRDZxnBHoX.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levetiracetam",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrrolidine"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy in the treatment of partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in adults and adolescents &ge;16 yrs with newly diagnosed epilepsy. Adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in adults and childn &ge;4 yrs with epilepsy; myoclonic seizures in adults, adolescents and childn &ge;12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in adults and adolescents &ge;4 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy – Adults and adolescents &ge;16 yrs:</b> Initially 250 mg 2x daily, increased to 500 mg 2x daily after 2 weeks. Can be further increased by 250 mg 2x daily every 2 weeks depending on clinical response. Max 1,500 mg 2x daily. <b>Add-on therapy – Partial seizures - Adults &ge;18 yrs, adolescents 12-17 yrs and childn 4-11 yrs weighing &ge;50 kg:</b> Initially 500 mg 2x daily, increased up to 3,000 mg/day. Dose changes can be made in 1,000 mg/day increments or decrements every 2-4 weeks; <b>adolescents 12-17 yrs and childn 4-11 yrs weighing < 50 kg:</b> Initially 10 mg/kg 2x daily, increased up to 30 mg/kg 2x daily. Dose increments or decrements should not exceed 10 mg/kg 2x daily every 2 weeks. <b>Myoclonic seizures - Childn &ge;12 yrs:</b> Initially 500 mg 2x daily, increased by 1,000 mg/day every 2 weeks to 3,000 mg daily. <b>Primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures - Adults &ge;18 yrs and adolescents 12-17 yrs weighing >50 kg:</b> Initially 500 mg 2x daily, may give additional 1,000 mg/day increments every 2 weeks to max 3,000 mg daily; <b>adolescents 12-17 yrs weighing < 50 kg:</b> Initially 10 mg/kg 2x daily, may give additional 20 mg/kg/day increments every 2 weeks to max 60 mg/kg/day. <b>Impaired renal function - Adults - CrCl 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 500-1,000 mg every 12 hrs; <b>30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 250-750 mg every 12 hrs; <b>< 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 250-500 mg every 12 hrs; <b>ESRD patients using dialysis:</b> 500-1,000 mg every 24 hrs, 750 mg/kg loading dose on 1<sup>st</sup> day and 250-500 mg supplemental dose after dialysis. <b>Childn and adolescents < 60 kg -</b> 15 mg/kg on 1<sup>st</sup> day. <b>CrCl 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 10-20 mg/kg 2x daily; <b>30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 5-15 mg/kg 2x daily; <b>< 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 5-10 mg/kg 2x daily; <b>ESRD patients using dialysis:</b> 10-20 mg/kg/day, 5-10 mg/kg supplemental dose after dialysis. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increase risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior. Patients with renal/hepatic impairment. Childn < 4 yrs. Elderly >65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Avoid abrupt withdrawal.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, fatigue; somnolence, choreoathetosis, dyskinesia, paresthesia, lethargy, amnesia, ataxia, convulsion, dizziness, headache, hyperkinesia, tremor, balance disorder, attention disturbance, memory impairment; agitation, depression, emotional lability/mood swings, hostility/aggression, insomnia, nervousness/irritability, personality disorders, abnormal thinking, suicide, suicide attempt and ideation, psychotic disorder, abnormal behavior, hallucination, anger, confusional state, panic attack, agitation, anger; abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting; anorexia, weight increase; vertigo; diplopia, blurred vision; myalgia; accidental injury; infection, nasopharyngitis; increased cough; eczema, pruritus, rash; thrombocytopenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P34.00)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute musculoskeletal pain, dysmenorrhea, toothache, and post-op pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: 12.5 mg every 4-6 hrs or 25 mg every 8 hrs. Max 75 mg/day. Take on an empty stomach (30 mins before meal). <b>IV/IM</b>: 50 mg/mL every 8-12 hrs. Max 150 mg/day. Mild renal and mild to moderate hepatic impairment: 50 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF NYHA II-IV. Crohn's disease/ulcerative colitis, severe cardiac failure, moderate to severe renal dysfunction, severe liver dysfunction, hemorrhagic diathesis, coagulation disorders. Anticoagulant therapy. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>IV/IM</b>: Intrathecal or epidural administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of allergic conditions, esophagitis, gastritis and peptic ulcer. Patients with hematopoietic disorders, SLE or mixed-type connective tissue diseases.           },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs, anticoagulants, heparin, ticlopidine, lithium, methotrexate, hydantoin, sulfonamide, diuretics, beta-blockers, pentoxifylline, thrombolytics, zidovudine, sulfonylureas, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, probenecid, cardiac glycosides, mifepristone, quinolones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 25 mg (P34.75). Solution for injection (IV/IM) 50 mg/2 mL (P578.75)."

            "content": "<b>Adults 70 kg:</b> 1 tab/5 kg BW/day or 4-8 tabs 3x daily with meals. Swallow whole; do not chew or crush. <b>Treatment duration:</b> Given as long as GFR is 5-15 mL/min; food should contain 40 g/day protein or less in adults."

            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypercalcemia, disturbed amino acid metabolism, and hereditary phenylketonuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor serum calcium level regularly. Ensure sufficient calorie intake. Decrease vit D intake if hypercalcemia occurs. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy and adjunctive treatment of partial seizures and primary and secondary generalized tonic-clonic seizures, seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Prophylaxis of bipolar disorder in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy – Monotherapy – Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: Initially 25 mg once daily for 2 weeks followed by 50 mg once daily for 2 weeks, may be increased by 50 mg/day every 1-2 weeks to maintenance dose of 225-375 mg daily in 2 divided doses; <b>Childn 2-12 yrs</b>: Initially 300 mcg/kg BW daily in 1 or 2 divided doses for 2 weeks followed by 600 mcg/kg BW in 2 divided doses for 2 weeks, may be increased by 600 mcg/kg BW daily every 1-2 weeks to maintenance dose of 4.5-7.5 mg/kg BW daily. Maintenance dose may need to be increased by as much as 50% in patients &lt;30 kg. Max 300 mg/day in 2 divided doses. <b>Add-on therapy (without valproate) – Adults</b>: 50 mg once daily for 2 weeks followed by 50 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, may be increased by 100 mg/day every 1-2 weeks to maintenance dose of 300-500 mg daily in 2 divided doses; <b>Childn 2-12 yrs</b>: Initially 600 mcg/kg BW daily in 2 divided doses for 2 weeks followed by 1.2 mg/kg BW in 2 divided doses, may be increased by a max 1.2 mg/kg BW every 1-2 weeks to maintenance dose of 5-15 mg/kg BW in 2 divided doses. Maintenance dose may need to be increased by as much as 50% in patients &lt;30 kg. Max 400 mg/day. <b>Add-on therapy (with valproate) – Adults</b>: Initially 25 mg every other day for 2 weeks followed by 25 mg once daily for 2 weeks, may be increased by 25-50 mg/day every 1-2 weeks to maintenance dose of 100-200 mg daily; <b>Childn</b>: Initially 150 mcg/kg once daily for 2 weeks followed by 300 mcg/kg once daily for 2 weeks, may be increased by 300 mcg/kg every 1-2 weeks to maintenance of 1-5 mg/kg BW once daily or 2 divided doses. Maintenance dose may need to be increased by as much as 50% in patients &lt;30 kg. Max 200 mg/day in 1 or 2 divided doses. <b>Bipolar disorder – Monotherapy</b>: Initially 25 mg once daily, gradually increased to 200 mg daily over 6 weeks. <b>Patients taking valproate</b>: 25 mg every other day and the target dose is 100 mg/day from week 6. <b>Patients receiving carbamazepine or other enzyme-inducing drugs</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily, gradually increased up to 400 mg/day from week 7. Dosage &gt;50 mg/day can be given once daily or in 2 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue at the 1<sup>st</sup> sign of rash. Multiorgan hypersensitivity reactions. Monitor for signs of anemia, unexpected infection or bleeding; emergence or worsening of depression, suicidal thoughts or behavior, and/or any unusual changes in mood or behavior; signs and symptoms of meningitis. Multidrug regimen that includes valproate. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin rashes, severe skin reactions including SJS, TEN. Angioedema, photosensitivity, diplopia, blurred vision, conjunctivitis, dizziness, drowsiness, insomnia, headache, ataxia, nystagmus, tremor, tiredness, nausea, vomiting, irritability, aggression, hallucinations, agitation, confusion, somnolence, rhinitis, pharyngitis, infection, diarrhea, abdominal pain, back pain and xerostomia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, valproate; rifampicin; lopinavir/ritonavir, atazanavir/lopinavir; dofetilide; estrogen-containing oral contraceptives. OCT2 substrates."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 50 mg (P31.00), 100 mg (P50.20)."
          }

Impulse control or compulsive behaviors; hallucinations or psychotic-like behavior. Monitor for melanomas frequently and regularly. Avoid abrupt discontinuation.           },
          {

          },

Disseminated or localized mycobacterial infections due to <i>Mycobacterium avium</i> or <i>M. intracellulare</i>. Localized infections due to <i>M. chelonae</i>, <i>M. fortuitum</i>, or <i>M. kansasii</i>. <b>Granules for susp:</b> Acute otitis media. <b>Tab:</b> Prevention of <i>M. avium</i> complex (MAC) in HIV-infected patients with CD4 lymphocyte counts &le;100/mm<sup>3</sup>. Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i> in the presence of acid suppression. Treatment of odontogenic infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: One 250 mg tab twice daily. <b>Severe infections:</b> 500 mg twice daily.   {
    "id": 2858,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2858,
        "brand_name": "Klaryth",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clarithromycin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Macrolides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of respiratory tract infections e.g. pharyngitis/tonsillitis caused by <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i>, acute maxillary sinusitis, chronic bronchitis, pneumonia, and otitis media. Skin and soft tissue infections caused by <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i>, <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i>. Prophylaxis and treatment of opportunistic mycobacterial infections commonly caused by <i>Mycobacterium kansasii</i>, <i>M. avium</i> or <i>M. intracellulare</i> and for the treatment of leprosy. Prevention of disseminated infection due to <i>M. avium complex</i> in patients with advanced HIV infection. Protozoal infections, including toxoplasmosis. May be given to eradicate <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> in the treatment regimens for peptic ulcer disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Childn 30-40 kg (10-12 yrs)</b>: 10 mL; <b>20-29 kg (7-9 yrs)</b>: 7.5 mL; <b>12-19 kg (3-6 yrs)</b>: 5 mL; <b>8-11 kg (1-2 yrs)</b>: 2.5 mL; <b>< 8 kg</b>: approx 7.5 mg/kg. All doses are given twice daily. Duration of treatment: 5-10 days depending on the pathogen involved and severity of condition. May be taken with or without meals and may be taken with milk. Shake well until the contents are evenly suspended."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of astemizole, cisapride, and terfenadine. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired renal or hepatic function. Possible cross-resistance between clarithromycin and other macrolide drugs, lincomycin and clindamycin. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances (e.g. nausea, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea). Taste disturbance, stomatitis, glossitis, and tooth discoloration. Transient elevations of liver enzyme values, cholestatic jaundice, and hepatitis. Headache, and rashes. Transient CNS effects e.g. anxiety, dizziness, insomnia, hallucinations, and confusion. Thrombocytopenic purpura, corneal opacities, pseudomembranous colitis, acute psychoses, pancreatitis, QT prolongation, and torsades de pointes, fever and leukocytoclastic vasculitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Rifabutin, fluoxetine, ritonavir, efavirenz, zidovudine, cimetidine, omeprazole, ethambutol, INH, pyrazinamide and rifampicin, theophylline, carbamazepine, fluconazole, oral anticoagulants, digoxin, colchicine, drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A, quinidine, disopyramide, ergotamine or dihydroergotamine, triazolam, alprazolam and midazolam, lovastatin and simvastatin, sildenafil, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, alfentanil, methylprednisolone and cilostazol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Granules for suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 35 mL (P540.50), 70 mL (P1,046.50)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Treatment of upper (e.g. streptococcal pharyngitis, tonsillitis, acute maxillary sinusitis, acute otitis media) and lower (e.g. bronchitis, pneumonia) respiratory tract infections; uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections (e.g. impetigo, folliculitis, cellulitis, abscesses); disseminated or localized mycobacterial infection due to <i>Mycobacterium avium</i> or <i>M. intracellulare</i>; localized infections due to <i>M. kansasii</i>, <i>M. chelonae</i>, and <i>M. fortuitum</i>; <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> infections (in combination with other drugs); odontogenic infections. Prevention of disseminated <i>M. avium</i> complex (MAC) infection in patients with advanced HIV infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Susp - Non-mycobacterial infections:</b> Usual pediatric dose: 15 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses; <b>125 mg/5 mL:</b> Childn 7-12 yrs: 7.5-10 mL; 2-6 yrs: 5 mL; 6 months-1 yr: 2.5 mL; <b>250 mg/mL:</b> Childn 7-12 yrs: 5 mL; 2-6 yrs: 2.5 mL; 6 months-1 yr: 1.25 mL. All doses given every 12 hrs for 5-10 days; <b>Treatment of disseminated or localized mycobacterial infections:</b> 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hrs; treatment should be continued as long as clinical and mycobacterial improvements are observed; <b>Prevention of disseminated MAC infection in patients with advanced HIV infection:</b> 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hrs; treatment should be continued while CD4 count is < 100 mm<sup>3</sup>. <b>Renal impairment:</b> Reduce dose by &frac12;; treatment duration should not exceed 14 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with prior use of clarithromycin; QT prolongation or ventricular cardiac arrhythmia. Concomitant use with simvastatin or lovastatin; ticagrelor or ranolazine; clarithromycin or colchicine in patients with renal/hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cross-sensitivity to other macrolides, lincomycin, and clindamycin. Not indicated for CAD. QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity, CDAD, myasthenia gravis. Patients with HIV, hepatic/renal impairment, mild to moderate skin and soft tissue infections caused by <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> or <i>S. pyogenes</i>. Patients receiving ototoxic drugs (e.g. aminoglycosides); monitor vestibular and auditory function during and after treatment. Concomitant use with quetiapine, oral hypoglycemic agents (e.g. sulfonylureas), insulin, oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin), triazolobenzodiazepines (e.g. triazolam, alprazolam), other benzodiazepines (e.g. IV midazolam), CCBs metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g. verapamil, diltiazem, amlodipine, nifedipine), colchicine; ranitidine bismuth citrate in patients with CrCl < 25 mL/min and history of acute porphyria. Absence of proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection or prophylactic indication is unlikely to be beneficial and increases risk of the development of drug-resistant microorganisms. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms (prolonged use). Perform susceptibility testing when prescribing clarithromycin for CAP. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly 65-81 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abnormal taste, dyspepsia, abdominal pain/discomfort, rash, headache."
          },

            "content": "Drugs metabolized by hepatic microsomal enzymes, tolterodine, atypical antipsychotics (e.g. quetiapine), anti-retroviral agents, oral hypoglycemic agents, insulin, anticoagulants, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, triazolobenzodiazepines and other benzodiazepines, CCBs, colchicine."

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mQCwmxJhJaODXNimFHzaDUtMkJlFFGUusfzuQM2JOPueUzdsHc.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clindamycin (Cap: HCl; IV/IM: Phosphate)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Lincosamides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Cap</b>: Lower respiratory tract infections (RTI) (e.g. bronchitis, pneumonia, empyema, lung abscess), URTI (e.g. tonsillitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, otitis media, scarlet fever), skin and skin structure infections (e.g. inflammatory acne vulgaris, furuncles, cellulitis, impetigo, abscesses, contaminated wounds, erysipelas, paronychia), gynecological infections (e.g. endometritis, pelvic cellulitis, post-op vaginal cuff infection, nongonococcal tubo-ovarian abscess, salpingitis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), cervicitis due to <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>), intra-abdominal infections (e.g. peritonitis, abdominal abscess), bone and joint infections (e.g. acute hematogenous osteomyelitis, septic arthritis), septicemia, endocarditis, dental infections (e.g. periodontal abscess, periodontitis), <i>Pneumocystis jiroveci (carinii)</i> pneumonia (PJP) in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) (in combination with primaquine in patients who are intolerant to or do not respond to conventional treatment). Alternative treatment of multi-drug resistant <i>Plasmodium falciparum</i> in combination with quinine or amodiaquine. <b>IV/IM</b>: Acute and chronic bacterial infections caused by clindamycin-sensitive pathogens, e.g., infections of bones and joints, ear, nose, throat, dental and maxillary area, deep respiratory tract, pelvic and abdominal area, female genitalia, skin and soft tissues. Scarlet fever, septicemia, endocarditis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap – Adults – Serious infections</b>: 150-300 mg every 6 hrs. <b>More severe infections</b>: 300-450 mg every 6 hrs. Duration of treatment for beta-hemolytic streptococcal infections: &ge;10 days. <b>Acne</b>: 150 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Bacterial vaginosis</b>: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. <b>Cervicitis due to <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i></b>: 450 mg every 6 hrs for 10-14 days. <b>PID (inpatient treatment)</b>: Initially 900 mg IV every 8 hrs + IV antibiotic with G(-) aerobic spectrum for &ge;4 days and &ge;48 hrs after the patient improves. Continue with 450 mg orally every 6 hrs to complete duration of 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of bacterial endocarditis in penicillin-allergic patients</b>: 600 mg 30-60 mins before procedure as single dose. <b>PJP in AIDS patients</b>: 300-450 mg every 6-8 hrs + primaquine for 21 days; reduce dose if serious hematologic adverse effects develop. <b>Alternative treatment of multidrug-resistant <i>Plasmodium falciparum</i></b>: 5-10 mg/kg twice daily + quinine or amodiaquine for &ge;5 days. <b>IV/IM</b> – For IV infusion or IM injection. <b>Adults and adolescents &gt;14 yrs – Moderately severe infections</b>: 8-12 mL daily (equiv to 1.2-1.8 g) in 2-4 single doses. <b>Severe infections</b>: 16-18 mL daily (equiv to 2.4-2.7 g) in 2-4 single doses. Max 32 mL/day (equiv to 4.8 g) in 2-4 single doses. <b>Infants &gt;4 weeks and childn &le;14 yrs</b> – 20-40 mg/kg BW in 3-4 single doses. <b>Patients with severe hepatic or renal insufficiency or anuria</b>: Reduce dose or prolong interval (8-12 hrs for patients with renal insufficiency or anuria). <b>IM injection</b>: Max of 600 mg single dose. <b>IV infusion</b>: Max of 12 mg/mL diluted solution. Max infusion rate: 30 mg/min or 1,200 mg/hr as single infusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>IV/IM</b>: Neonates especially premature infants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use for meningitis. May cause overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (e.g. fungi), <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea, serious allergic reactions. Atopic individuals. Patients with history of GI disease (particularly colitis), G6PD deficiency, severe renal or hepatic impairment with severe metabolic aberrations. Concomitant use with neuromuscular blocking agents. Perform liver and kidney function tests and blood counts during prolonged therapy. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B. <b>IV/IM</b>: Infants, childn up to 3 yrs. <b>Cap</b>: Childn &lt;16 yrs. Elderly &gt;60 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "CDAD, pseudomembranous colitis, and other GI diseases, dermatologic and hypersensitivity reactions, hepatobiliary and renal, and hematologic effects. Vaginal infection/vaginitis, polyarthritis, dysgeusia, lymphadenitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Neuromuscular blocking agents, aminoglycosides, ampicillin, erythromycin, neostigmine and physostigmine, estrogens, oral typhoid vaccine, vit K antagonists (e.g. warfarin, acenocoumarol, fluindione), liver function tests."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 300 mg (P85.16). Solution for injection (IV/IM) 150 mg/mL x 4 mL."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1736,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1736,
        "brand_name": "Lavida",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MViVayJrysQhui2IchB1qad5rVPqZ3I31Bwqb9OIHNA2lLnrsE.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MViVayJrysQhui2IchB1qad5rVPqZ3I31Bwqb9OIHNA2lLnrsE.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/c7izzkDEtmWCMlUq384aUqkscsCExSWKuCh4eYijUXKP0pZ2bR.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levodopa, carbidopa",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of Parkinson's disease and syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients not receiving levodopa</b> - <b>Initial:</b> 100 mg/25 mg thrice daily, may be increased by 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg daily or every other day. Max 2 g/200 mg; <b>Maintenance:</b> Individualized dosage. At least 70-100 mg of carbidopa/day should be provided. When more levodopa is required, 250 mg/25 mg should be substituted at a dosage of 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg given 3 or 4x daily. If necessary, the dose of 250 mg/25 mg may be increased by &frac12;-1 tab 100 mg/25 mg every other day. Max 8 tabs daily. <b>Patients receiving levodopa alone:</b> Discontinue levodopa at least 12 hrs before starting therapy. Levodopa + carbidopa should be given as the 1<sup>st</sup> morning dose after a night without any levodopa. The dose should be approx 20% of the previous daily dose of levodopa. <b>Levodopa requirement</b> - &gt;1,500 mg/day: 250 mg/25 mg 3 or 4x daily; &lt;1,500 mg/day: 100 mg/25 mg 3 or 4x daily. <b>Patients receiving levodopa with another decarboxylase inhibitor:</b> Discontinue levodopa at least 12 hrs before starting therapy. Start with the same amount of levodopa as with the other levodopa + decarboxylase inhibitor combination. <b>Patients receiving other antiparkinsonian agents:</b> Dose adjustment of levodopa + carbidopa may be necessary."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with non-selective MAOIs, sympathomimetic amine (e.g. epinephrine, norepinephrine or isoproterenol). Clinical or lab evidence of uncompensated CV, endocrine, hematologic, hepatic, pulmonary, renal disease. Narrow-angle glaucoma. Severe psychoses. Suspicious undiagnosed skin lesions or a history of melanoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended for the treatment of medicine-induced extrapyramidal reactions. MI, dyskinesia, mental disturbance, somnolence, NMS, behavioral disturbances, glaucoma, melanoma. Peri-op considerations. Severe CV or pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, renal, hepatic or endocrine disease, peptic ulcer, seizure. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Orthostatic hypotension; anorexia; nausea, vomiting; involuntary movements (e.g. grimacing, bruxism, gnawing, chewing, twisting and protrusion of the tongue, rhythmic opening and closing of the mouth, bobbling and wave-like motions of the head with or without gesticulations, slow rhythmic movements of the neck, hands or feet, jerky movements of the shoulder or pelvic girdle, and opisthotonos or ballismus), intermittent myoclonic body jerks during sleep; dyskinesia, increased hand tremor, ataxia, agitation, anxiety, euphoria; dream abnormalities including nightmares, insomnia, drowsiness; blepharospasm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anesthetic, anticholinergic, antihypertensives, TCAs, selegiline, D<sub>2</sub>-receptor antagonists, isoniazid, dopamine-depleting agents and other drugs depleting monoamine stores, phenytoin and papaverine, iron salts, metoclopramide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg/25 mg (P24.53), 250 mg/25 mg (P38.59)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 87,
          "name": "Medichem Pharmaceuticals, Inc."
        },
        "class": "human",
        "form_class": "3",

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Laxatives & Enemas"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Constipation: Regulation of the physiological rhythm of the colon. It is where a soft stool is considered of medical benefits (hemorrhoids, post colonic/anal surgery). Hepatic Encephalopathy: Treatment and prevention of hepatic coma or pre-coma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Constipation, or where a soft stool is considered of medical benefits – Adults:</b> Starting dose 15-45 mL/day, maintenance dose 15-30 mL/day. May be given as single daily dose or in 2 divided doses. <b>Childn 7-14 yrs:</b> Starting dose 15 mL/day, maintenance dose 10-15 mL/day. <b>1-6 yrs:</b> Starting dose and maintenance dose 5-10 mL/day. <b>Infants < 1 yr:</b> Starting dose and maintenance dose up to 5 mL. <b>Hepatic encephalopathy – Adults:</b> 30-45 mL (20-30 g) 3-4x daily, may be adjusted to produce soft stool 2-3x daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Galactosemia, GI obstruction, digestive perforation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Lactose intolerant. Patients with rare hereditary problem of galactose or fructose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Childn < 18 yrs with hepatic encephalopathy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, flatulence, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Syrup 3.33 g/5 mL (P320.88)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Protein Kinase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of unresectable thyroid cancer (TC). In combination with pembrolizumab, for the 1st-line treatment of patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC). In combination with everolimus, for the treatment of patients with advanced RCC following 1 prior antiangiogenic therapy. Treatment of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In combination with pembrolizumab, for the treatment of patients with advanced endometrial carcinoma (EC) who have disease progression following prior systemic therapy in any setting and are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>TC</b>: Initially 24 mg once daily (two 10 mg cap and one 4 mg cap). <b>RCC</b>: 20 mg (two 10 mg cap) once daily in combination with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks; or 18 mg (one 10 mg cap and two 4 mg cap) once daily in combination with everolimus 5 mg at the same time each day. <b>HCC - Patients</b> &ge;60 kg: 12 mg (three 4 mg cap) once daily; < 60 kg: 8 mg (two 4 mg cap) once daily. <b>EC</b>: 20 mg once daily in combination with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks. <b>Severe hepatic (Child-Pugh C) or severe renal (CrCl < 30 mL/min) impairment – TC</b>: 14 mg once daily. <b>RCC, EC</b>: 10 mg once daily. Take at the same time each day. Caps are swallowed whole with water. Alternatively, add the caps (without breaking or crushing) to 1 tbsp of water or apple juice in a small glass to produce a suspension. Leave caps in the liquid for at least 10 mins. Stir for at least 3 mins and drink the mixture. After drinking, add the same amount of water or apple juice (1 tbsp) to the glass, swirl the contents and swallow the additional liquid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid repeat exposure to contents of the caps. Patients with or at risk for renal impairment (renal failure, proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome); GI impairment (fistula formation or GI perforation); CV events (cardiac failure and decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, QT interval prolongation, hemorrhage, arterial thromboembolism); hepatic impairment (hepatic encephalopathy, failure); thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, TSH suppression impairment); wound healing complications. Risk for fertility impairment for men. Childn. Pregnancy and Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, neutropenia, cardiac failure, QT interval prolongation, hypothyroidism, abdominal pain, amylase increased, constipation, diarrhea, dry mouth, dyspepsia, flatulence, GI perforation and fistula, lipase increased, nausea, oral pain, pancreatitis, stomatitis, vomiting, asthenia, peripheral edema, fatigue, malaise, impaired wound healing, cholecystitis, hepatotoxicity, hepatic failure, hepatic encephalopathy, UTI, weight decreased, decreased appetite, dehydration, hypercholesterolemia, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, arthralgia, back pain, musculoskeletal pain, myalgia, pain in extremity, ONJ, dizziness, dysgeusia, headache, reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome, insomnia, nephrotic syndrome, proteinuria, renal failure/impairment, cough, dysphonia, pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, alopecia, hyperkeratosis, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome, rash, arterial thromboembolic events, hemorrhage, HTN, hypotension, aortic dissection."
          },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9sTaVsRwHLugJ1x7UOgqdWeU5UzY0DACKYI0Aiu1jGhRYaqb7i.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WGrLRREAs1bObiGx29F30WTZLWnbdBQw2QUYv1hEPIkOIQCS1w.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levetiracetam",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrrolidine"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab/Oral soln:</b> Monotherapy in treatment of partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in patients &ge;16 yrs with newly diagnosed epilepsy. Adjunct therapy in partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in adults and childn &ge;4 yrs (oral soln: &ge;1 month) with epilepsy; myoclonic seizures in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; primary generalized tonic, clonic seizure (PGTCS) in patients &ge;4 yrs (oral soln: &ge;12 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy). <b>IV:</b> Alternative when oral administration is temporarily not feasible. Adjunct therapy in partial onset seizures in patients &ge;1 month with epilepsy; myoclonic seizures in patients &ge;12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; PGTCS in patients &ge;6 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses taken 2x daily with or without food. Oral soln may be diluted in glass of water. <b>Tab/Oral soln - Monotherapy - Adults and adolescents &ge;16 yrs:</b> Initially 250 mg, increased to 500 mg after 2 weeks. May be further increased by 250 mg every 2 weeks, max 1,500 mg depending on the clinical response. <b>Add-on therapy - Adults, adolescents &ge;12 yrs, and childn weighing &ge;50 kg:</b> Initially 500 mg on 1st day of therapy. May be increased/decreased by 500 mg every 2-4 weeks, max 1,500 mg; <b>Infants 6-23 months, adolescents and childn 4-17 yrs weighing < 50 kg:</b> Initially 10 mg/kg. May be increased/decreased by 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks, max 30 mg/kg. <b>Oral soln - 6 kg:</b> 0.6-1.8 mL or 60-180 mg; <b>10 kg:</b> 1-3 mL or 100-300 mg; <b>15 kg:</b> 1.5-4.5 mL or 150-450 mg; <b>20 kg:</b> 2-6 mL or 200-600 mg; <b>Tab - 15 kg:</b> 150-450 mg; <b>20 kg:</b> 200-600 mg; <b>25 kg:</b> 250-750 mg; <b>Infants 1-< 6 months:</b> Initially 7 mg/kg. May be increased/decreased by 7 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Max 21 mg/kg. <b>4 kg:</b> 0.3-0.85 mL or 28-84 mg; <b>5 kg:</b> 0.35-1.05 mL or 35-105 mg; <b>7 kg:</b> 0.5-1.5 mL or 49-147 mg. <b>IV - Partial onset seizures - Adults &ge;16 yrs:</b> Initially 500 mg. May be increased by 500 mg every 2 weeks. Max 1,500 mg; <b>Childn 4-< 16 yrs:</b> 10 mg/kg, increased by 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks to a recommended dose of 30 mg/kg. Max 1,500 mg; <b>6 months-< 4 yrs:</b> 10 mg/kg, increased by 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks to a recommended dose of 25 mg/kg; <b>Infants 1-< 6 months:</b> 7 mg/kg, increased by 7 mg/kg every 2 weeks to a recommended dose of 21 mg/kg. <b>Myoclonic seizures:</b> Initially 500 mg, increased by 500 mg every 2 weeks to a recommended dose of 1,500 mg. <b>PGTCS - Adults &ge;16 yrs:</b> 500 mg, increased by 500 mg every 2 weeks to a recommended dose of 1,500 mg; <b>Childn 6-< 16 yrs:</b> 10 mg/kg, increased by 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks to a recommended dose of 30 mg/kg. <b>Switching from oral:</b> Initial total IV daily dose should be equivalent to total oral daily dose and frequency. <b>Switching to oral:</b> Oral dose should be equivalent to IV daily dose and frequency. <b>Renal impairment:</b> 750 mg loading dose on 1<sup>st</sup> day of therapy. <b>CrCl 50-80 mL/min:</b> 500-1,000 mg; <b>30-49 mL/min:</b> 250-750 mg; <b>< 30 mL/min:</b> 250-500 mg; <b>ESRD, undergoing dialysis:</b> 500-1,000 mg once daily, then a 250-500 mg supplemental dose after dialysis. <b>Severe hepatic impairment:</b> 50% dose reduction in CrCl < 70 mL/min. See product insert for preparation and administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with moderate and severe renal impairment. Increased seizure frequency; somnolence, other CNS-related symptoms; suicide, suicidal attempts, ideation, and behavior; emergence or worsening of symptoms of depression, unusual changes in mood or behavior (e.g. aggression, agitation, anger, anxiety, apathy, depression, hostility, irritability); anaphylaxis, angioedema; hematological and hepatic abnormalities; SJS, TEN; coordination difficulties. Not recommended for patients with rare hereditary fructose intolerance (oral soln). Monitor childn < 4 yrs for increased diastolic BP; seizure control during pregnancy.  May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 4 yrs. Elderly. Planning of pregnancy. Pregnancy. <b>Pregnancy risk:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },

        "content": "Clozapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For treatment-resistant schizophrenia patients. Indicated to reduce the risk of recurrent suicidal behavior or psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson’s disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Treatment resistant schizophrenia – Initial dose:</b> 12.5 mg once or twice on the 1 <sup>st</sup> day, followed by one or two 25 mg tabs on the 2<sup>nd</sup> day. May be increased slowly in increments of 25-50 mg in order to achieve a dose level of up to 300 mg/day within 2-3 weeks. May be further increased in increments of 50-100 mg at weekly intervals. <b>Therapeutic dose:</b> 300 to 450 mg/day given in divided doses. Max 900 mg/day in divided doses. <b>Maintenance: </b>Careful downward titration. Treatment should be maintained for at least 6 months. If dose ≤200 mg, give once a day in the evening. <b>Ending therapy:</b> Withdraw gradually over 1-2 weeks period. <b>Psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson’s disease – Initial dose: </b> ≤12.5 mg once daily in the evening, subsequent increase to 12.5 mg, up to 2 increases each week, 50 mg should not be reached before the end of 2<sup>nd </sup>week. <b>Therapeutic dose:</b> 25-37.5 mg daily, may be increased to 50 mg at weekly intervals. Max 100 mg daily. <b>Maintenance:</b> 12.5 mg, max 100 mg daily, as single dose or 2 divided doses. <b>Ending therapy:</b> gradual reduction in dose by steps of 12.5 mg over a period of at least 1 week. <b>Elderly: </b>12.5 mg once daily on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, with subsequent dose increments of 25 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with uncontrolled epilepsy, alcoholic or other toxic psychoses, drug intoxication, comatose conditions, circulatory collapse, CNS depression of any cause, impaired bone marrow function, history of toxic or idiosyncratic granulocytopenia/agranulocytosis (with the exception of granulocytopenia/agranulocytosis from previous chemotherapy), severe renal or cardiac disorders, active liver disease associated with nausea, anorexia or jaundice, progressive liver disease, hepatic failure, and paralytic ileus. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, thromboembolism, cardiovascular disorder, MI, QT interval prolongation, hyperglycemia, metabolic changes, dyslipidemia, weight gain, seizures, fever, anticholinergic effects. Monitoring of WBC counts and absolute neutrophil count; 10 days prior to starting treatment, weekly monitoring for 18 weeks, and thereafter at least every 4 weeks throughout treatment and 4 weeks after complete discontinuation. Women of child-bearing potential. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tachycardia, constipation, hypersalivation, drowsiness, sedation, dizziness, leukopenia, decreased WBC, neutropenia, eosinophilia, leukocytosis, weight gain, dysarthria, blurred vision, syncope, postural hypotension, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, headache, seizures, convulsions, myoclonic jerks, extrapyramidal symptoms, akathisia, tremor, rigidity, elevated liver enzymes, urinary retention or incontinence, benign hyperthermia, disturbances in sweating, temperature regulation, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lithium, alcohol, MAO inhibitors, narcotics, antihistamines, benzodiazepines, carbamazepine,\nphenytoin, rifampicin, cimetidine, erythromycin, fluvoxamine, perazine, ciprofloxacin, oral contraceptives, SSRIs (e.g. paroxetine, sertraline, fluoxetine, citalopram), omeprazole, CYP 450 inhibitors or inducers."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",

    "detail": {

        "brand_name": "Litcab",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kP9qgISIMgLZLgNandhp4wXBtjwKvIuZJQF1uFBkesDc0hVGyx.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/eu0rPkjs25IDBQusYfQzRvBApsClF8yq6FiiaW5lVEvbj3SGDj.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NMArSydRJhH34dzqoy2W3hadveu4Qg3qeIDG7qxmnes5V0qJ5f.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Lithium carbonate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Lithium Antipsychotic"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of manic episodes of bipolar disorder. Prevents or diminishes the intensity of subsequent episodes in those with bipolar disorder with a history of mania as maintenance therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute treatment of mania and hypomania:</b> 1.5-2 g daily may be given for the 1<sup>st</sup> 5-7 days. <b>Mania, bipolar disorder, recurrent depression, and aggressive or self-harming behavior</b> - <b>Treatment:</b> Initially 450-675 mg twice daily. <b>Prophylaxis:</b> Initially 450 mg twice daily. Adjust dose to achieve a serum lithium concentration of 0.4-1 mmol/L 12 hrs after a dose on days 4-7 of treatment then every week until dosage has remained constant for 4 weeks and every 3 months thereafter."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with severe CV or renal disease, severe debilitation or dehydration, sodium depletion, brain damage. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Conditions that cause sodium depletion (loss of salt and fluids e.g. vomiting, diarrhea, perspiration, use of diuretics). Pregnancy. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, thirst, dryness of mouth, abdominal pain. General muscle weakness, ataxia, tremor, muscle hyperirritability. Slurred speech, blurring of vision, headache, seizures, psychomotor retardation, somnolence, restlessness. Arrhythmia, hypotension, cardiac collapse. Albuminuria, polyuria, glycosuria. Dryness and thinning of the hair, leg ulcers, skin rash. Anemia, leucopenia, leucocytosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Metronidazole, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, steroids, tetracyclines. Xanthines, sodium bicarbonate-containing products, urea, calcitonin. Haloperidol, flupentixol, diazepam, thioridazine, fluphenazine, chlorpromazine, clozapine, methyldopa, triptan derivatives, CCBs, carbamazepine. Class IA and III antiarrhythmic agents, cisapride, erythromycin, amisulpride, SSRIs, TCAs, anesthetics, theophylline, phenytoin, indomethacin, other prostaglandin-sythetase inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sustained-release tablet 450 mg (P13.50)."
          }
        ],

        },

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the improvement of hypoalbuminemia in patients with decompensated hepatic cirrhosis presenting with hypoalbuminemia despite adequate dietary intake."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 1 sachet three times a day. To be taken with liquid (e.g. water) after meals, not to be reconstituted."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with congenital branched-chain amino acid metabolic abnormality e.g. MSUD, advanced hepatic cirrhosis (stage III or more in the severity of coma due to hepatic encephalopathy. total bilirubin level of &ge;3 mg/dL, markedly depressed hepatic function for protein synthesis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients on restricted protein intake, with abnormal BUN or blood ammonia levels. Long-term use. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal distension/discomfort, diarrhea, inappetence, thirst."
          },

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Valproic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fatty Acid Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of patients with complex partial seizures (CPS) that occur either in isolation or in association with other types of seizures. Sole and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of simple and complex absence seizures, and adjunctively in patients with multiple seizure types that include absence seizures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10-15 mg/kg/day, increasing at 1-week intervals by 5-10 mg/kg/day until seizures are controlled or side effects preclude further increases. Max 60 mg/kg/day. If the total daily dose exceeds 250 mg, it should be given in divided doses. May be taken with food to avoid GI irritation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic dysfunction; POLG-related disorders e.g. Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome; urea cycle disorders; porphyria. Use in prophylaxis of migraine headaches in pregnant women. Childn < 2 yrs who are suspected of having POLG-related disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform liver function tests prior to therapy. Patients with history of hepatic diseases, hepatic dysfunction. Risk of pancreatitis, suicidal behavior and ideation, somnolence in the elderly, thrombocytopenia, hyperammonemia, hypothermia. Patients with DM, fructose intolerance, glucose and galactose malabsorption, or sucrose-isomaltase insufficiency. May be harmful to teeth and contains methylhydroxybenzoate and sorbitol. Concomitant use of carbapenem antibiotics, topiramate. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &le;2 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, asthenia, fever, back pain, chest pain, malaise. CV, GI, hematologic, lymphatic, metabolic, nutritional, musculoskeletal, respiratory, skin, special senses, and urogenital effects."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ritonavir, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, antidepressants, aspirin, carbapenem antibiotics, felbamate, rifampin, amitriptyline, nortriptyline, clonazepam, diazepam, ethosuximide, lamotrigine, primidone, tolbutamide, topiramate, warfarin, and zidovudine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Syrup 250 mg/5 mL x 100 mL (P412.50)."
          }
        ],

Adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalization in adults, adolescents, and childn &ge;4 yrs with epilepsy; myoclonic seizures in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs with idiopathic generalized epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "15-min IV infusion. <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs, adolescents 12-17 yrs and childn 4-11 yrs weighing &ge;50 kg:</b> Initially 500 mg twice daily starting on day 1. Initial 25 mg twice daily may be given, then increased to 500 mg twice daily after 2 weeks. Max 1,500 mg twice daily. Dose can be increased or decreased in 250 or 500 mg twice daily every 2-4 weeks. <b>Add-on therapy - Adolescents 12-17 yrs and childn 4-11 yrs weighing < 50 kg:</b> Initially 10 mg/kg twice daily, may be increased up to 30 mg/kg twice daily. Max 10 mg/kg twice daily increase or decrease every 2 weeks; <b>25 kg:</b> Initially 250 mg twice daily, max 750 mg twice daily; <b>20 kg:</b> 200 mg twice daily, max 600 mg twice daily; <b>15 kg:</b> 150 mg twice daily, max 450 mg twice daily. <b>Renal impairment - Adults and adolescents >50 kg - CrCl 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 500-1,000 mg twice daily; <b>30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 250-750 mg twice daily; <b>< 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 250-500 mg twice daily; <b>ESRD patients undergoing dialysis:</b> 750 mg loading dose on 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment, then 500-1,000 mg once daily. Give supplemental 250-500 mg following dialysis; <b>Childn &ge;4 yrs and adolescents < 50 kg - CrCl 50-79 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 10-20 mg/kg twice daily; <b>30-49 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 5-15 mg/kg twice daily; <b>< 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> 5-10 mg/kg twice daily; <b>ESRD patients undergoing dialysis:</b> 15 mg/kg loading dose on 1<sup>st</sup> day of treatment, then 10-20 mg/kg once daily. Give supplemental 250-500 mg following dialysis. <b>Severe hepatic impairment with CrCl < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> Reduce daily dose by 50%."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, prolonged QTc interval, concomitant QT prolonging drugs, pre-existing cardiac disease, electrolyte disturbances, controlled sodium-diet. Acute kidney injury, decreased blood cell counts, suicide, suicidal attempt, ideation, and behavior, psychotic symptoms, behavioral abnormalities (e.g. irritability and aggressiveness), worsening of seizures, ECG QT interval prolongation. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 4 yrs (add-on therapy) or < 16 yrs (monotherapy). Pregnancy planning. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, somnolence, headache, anorexia, depression hostility/aggression, anxiety, insomnia, nervousness/irritability, convulsion, balance disorder, dizziness, lethargy, tremor, vertigo, cough, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, rash, asthenia/fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Methotrexate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate for solution for IV infusion 100 mg/mL x 5 mL."
          }
        ],
