  {
    "id": 3674,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3674,
        "brand_name": "Lixiana 30 mg",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ArYbB3pmaD60kBLUmcszV5Xmj43jd7tEMzADXNsqTgnYMK4odp.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/seT3kcuM9K6Gh2UCcDFULXSriykTYSdXGCyvxAP2YdXrQKr6JO.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/76AngAbLeSqyWWlJiQC7c2HC3H7yB6efoXgotVMKtecJTKSNAM.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Edoxaban tosilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with one or more risk factor e.g. congestive heart failure, hypertension, age &ge;75 yrs, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients with renal insufficiency – Mild (CrCl &gt;50-80 mL/min)</b>: 60 mg once daily; <b>Moderate or severe (CrCl 15-50 mL/min)</b>: 30 mg once daily. <b>Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: 60 mg once daily. Take with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Clinically significant active bleeding. Patients with hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk. Lesion or condition, if considered to be a significant risk for major bleeding. Uncontrolled severe HTN. Concomitant treatment with any other anticoagulants e.g. unfractionated heparin, LMWH (enoxaparin, dalteparin), heparin derivatives (fondaparinux), oral anticoagulants (warfarin, dabigatran, etexilate, rivaroxaban, apixaban) except under specific circumstances of switching oral anticoagulant therapy or when unfractionated heparin is given at doses necessary to maintain an open central venous or arterial catheter. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hemorrhagic risk. Discontinue use if severe hemorrhage occurs. Not recommended in patients with ESRD (CrCl &lt;15 mL/min) or in dialysis, and severe hepatic impairment. Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST &gt;2x ULN) or total bilirubin &ge;1.5x ULN. Discontinue use at least 24 hrs before the procedure and interventions. Concomitant use of medicines affecting hemostasis. Not recommended in patients with mechanical heart valves, during the first 3 months after implantation of a bioprosthetic heart valve, with or without atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe mitral stenosis. Not recommended as an alternative to unfractionated heparin in patients with PE who are hemodynamically unstable or may receive thrombolysis or pulmonary embolectomy. Patients with active cancer. Not recommended in patients with history of thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome. Adolescents and childn &lt;18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with one or more risk factor, such as congestive heart failure, hypertension, age &ge;75 yrs, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients with renal insufficiency</b> – Mild (CrCl &gt;50-80 mL/min): 60 mg once daily; Moderate or severe (CrCl 15-50 mL/min): 30 mg once daily. <b>Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: 60 mg once daily. Take with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Clinically significant active bleeding. Patients with hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk. Lesion or condition, if considered to be a significant risk for major bleeding. Uncontrolled severe HTN. Concomitant treatment with any other anticoagulants e.g. unfractionated heparin, LMWH (enoxaparin, dalteparin), heparin derivatives (fondaparinux), oral anticoagulants (warfarin, dabigatran, etexilate, rivaroxaban, apixaban) except under specific circumstances of switching oral anticoagulant therapy or when unfractionated heparin is given at doses necessary to maintain an open central venous or arterial catheter. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hemorrhagic risk. Discontinue use if severe hemorrhage occurs. Not recommended in patients with ESRD (CrCl &lt;15 mL/min) or in dialysis, and severe hepatic impairment. Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST &gt;2x ULN) or total bilirubin &ge;1.5x ULN. Discontinue use at least 24 hrs before the procedure and interventions. Concomitant use of medicines affecting hemostasis. Not recommended in patients with mechanical heart valves, during the first 3 months after implantation of a bioprosthetic heart valve, with or without atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe mitral stenosis. Not recommended as an alternative to unfractionated heparin in patients with PE who are hemodynamically unstable or may receive thrombolysis or pulmonary embolectomy. Patients with active cancer. Not recommended in patients with history of thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome. Adolescents and childn &lt;18 yrs.",

        "content": "Allopurinol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antigout Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of signs and symptoms of primary and secondary gout (recurrent acute attacks, arthropathy, tophi, radiographic changes of gout, or associated uric acid nephrolithiasis); subsequent hyperuricemia in patients undergoing chemotherapy; recurrent calcium oxalate renal calculi in males and females patients whose urinary urate excretion exceeds 800 mg/day and 750 mg/day, respectively."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Management of gout - Initial dose:</b> 100 mg/day 2 weeks after pain and swelling of acute gouty arthritis have subsided. Titrate dose by 50-100 mg/day every 2-4 weeks to achieve serum uric acid < 6 mg/dL. Max 300/day. <b>Chemotherapy-associated hyperuricemia:</b> 600-800 mg/day for 2-3 days. Ensure adequate hydration. <b>Recurrent calcium oxalate renal calculi:</b> Initially 200-300 mg/day in divided doses or as single dose. Adjust subsequent doses depending on control of hyperuricosuria assessed by 24-hour urinary urate excretion determination. <b>Renal impairment - Initial doses</b> - CrCl 10-20 mL/min: Not >200 mg/day; < 10 mL/min: Not >100 mg/day. <b>Maintenance doses</b> - CrCl 80 mL/min: 250 mg/day; 60 mL/min: 200 mg/day; 40 mL/min: 150 mg/day; 20 mL/min: 100 mg/day; 10 mL/min: 100 mg every 2 days; 0 mL/min: 100 mg every 3 days. <b>Dialysis:</b> If dialysis is required 2-3x a week, 300-400 mg immediately after each dialysis with none in the interim. Preferably after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue immediately at first appearance of rash or any sign that may indicate an allergic reaction. Intolerance. Not for asymptomatic hyperuricemia. Patients under treatment for HTN or cardiac insufficiency, with diuretics or ACE inhibitors; reversible clinical hepatotoxicity. Impaired renal or thyroid function. Patients with impaired renal or thyroid function; hemochromatosis; genetic disorders of purine metabolism (i.e. Lesch-Nyhan syndrome). Bone marrow depression with cytotoxic drugs. Ensure adequate fluid intake. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, skin reactions (e.g. pruritic maculopapular rash) and alterations in liver function test results."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ampicillin/amoxicillin, anticoagulants, ACE inhibitors, antacids, chlorpropamide, ciclosporin, didanosine, diuretics, mercaptopurine or azathioprine, phenytoin, theophylline, vidarabine, uricosurics and salicylates, drugs that increase serum urate concentrations, cyclophosphamide and other cytotoxic agents."
          },
          {

  {
    "id": 3472,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3472,
        "brand_name": "Liverprime HD",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gdIdNqmUoopB2OV3RhXS7eLNDKkYdvH5oIW7TsytDII2DFMmnD.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WCJxiYplHtW42PfmzWbROYYVsIIRVb9SubsHop3R9bJC1Zfmyl.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NRcRHLaSAVdjK8dVk56Kv5JnPKRu7gSsiD9lTu2kMZG4Pp0M1a.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Silibinin, phosphatidylcholine, multivitamins, zinc",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Helps maintain liver health. Adjunct in the management of a variety of liver disorders including: Acute and chronic viral hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, alcohol-related liver disease, liver damage from certain drugs (e.g. phenothiazine and butyrophenone), fatty liver (e.g. non-alcoholic fatty liver disease or non-alcoholic steatohepatitis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 1 cap 1-3x a day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with diabetes or hypoglycemia, or taking medicines or supplements that affect blood sugar levels, malabsorption problems, antiphospholipid-antibody syndrome, gallbladder disease or history of jaundice or liver disease, DM, gout, peptic ulcer or allergy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Silybin, phosphatidylcholine</b>: Hyperbilirubinemia, increased ALT, possible laxative effect (high doses). Abdominal pain or discomfort, flatulence/gassiness, diarrhea, loss of appetite, dizziness, urticarial (hives), eczema and allergic/hypersensitivity and anaphylactic reactions. <b>Nicotinic acid</b>: Nausea, heartburn, headache, fatigue, sore throat, dry hair, dry skin, tightness of the face, hives and blurred vision (chronic administration). Elevated liver function tests and liver damage including jaundice, cholestatic hepatitis and portal fibrosis (large doses). Dizziness, diarrhea, vomiting, moderate increase in gastric secretion and bile flow, abnormal prothrombin time and hypoalbuminemia. <b>Zinc</b>: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, GI discomfort, metallic taste, headache, and drowsiness (high doses). Low HDL levels. UTI and kidney stones (long-term)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Silybin</b>: Clopidogrel, erythromycin, fexofenadine, nifedipine, tamoxifen, warfarin; hypoglycemics; metronidazole; oral contraceptives; statins. <b>Nicotinic acid</b>: Carbamazepine. <b>Zinc</b>: Bisphosphonates; cholesterol medicines; copper or iron; penicillamine; quinolones; tetracyclines; foods containing high amounts of phosphorus, calcium (dairy), or phytates (e.g. bran, brown bread)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule (P59.84)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>Acute sinusitis</b>: 500 mg/day for 10-14 days or 750 mg/day for 5 days. <b>Acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis</b>: 500 mg/day for 7 days. <b>Community-acquired pneumonia</b>: 500 mg/day for 7-14 days or 750 mg/day for 5 days. <b>Nosocomial pneumonia</b>: 750 mg/day for 7-14 days. <b>UTI and prostatitis</b>: 250 mg/day for 3 days. <b>Complicated UTI and acute pyelonephritis</b>: 250 mg/day for 10 days or 750 mg/day for 5 days. <b>Chronic prostatitis</b>: 500 mg for 28 days. All doses to be given once every 24 hrs. <b>Postexposure prophylaxis to anthrax</b> - Adults: 500 mg once daily. Childn &ge;6 months with &gt;50 kg BW: 500 mg once daily; &lt;50 kg: 8 mg/kg, not to exceed 250 mg/dose. To be given every 12 hrs. <b>Chlamydial infections</b>: 500 mg once daily for 7 days. <b>Uncomplicated or disseminated gonorrhea</b>: 250 mg single dose. <b>Epididymitis</b>: 500 mg once daily for 10 days. <b>Nongonococcal urethritis</b>: 500 mg once daily for 7 days. <b>Pelvic inflammatory disease</b>: 500 mg once daily for 14 days with or without oral metronidazole. <b>Travelers’ diarrhea</b>: 500 mg once daily for 1-3 days. <b>Renal impairment - CrCl 10-49 mL/min</b>: No dose adjustment if for uncomplicated UTI. <b>20-49 mL/min</b> - Complicated UTI or acute pyelonephritis: No dose adjustment; Other infections: 500 or 750 mg initially then 250 mg every 24 hrs or 750 mg every 48 hrs, respectively. <b>10-19 mL/min</b>: 250 mg every 48 hrs or initially 500 or 750 mg then 250 or 500 mg every 49 hrs, respectively. <b>Hemodialysis or CAPD patients</b>: 500 or 750 mg initially then 250 or 500 mg every 48 hrs, respectively. No supplemental dose required."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with positive family history of aneurysm disease, or in patients diagnosed with pre-existing aortic aneurysm and/or aortic dissection, or in the presence of other risk factors or conditions predisposing for aortic aneurysm and dissection (e.g. Marfan syndrome, vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Takayasu arteritis, giant cell arteritis, Behcet’s disease, HTN, atherosclerosis). Tendinopathy and tendon rapture. Discontinue at 1<sup>st</sup> sign of rash. Hepatic or renal impairment. Patients with known or suspected CNS disorders or other risk factors to predispose to seizures or lowers seizure threshold. Peripheral neuropathy. Superinfection, <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea and colitis. History of prolonged QT interval, uncorrected electrolyte disorders, patients receiving class IA or III antiarrhythmic agents. Blood glucose disturbances. Resistance in <i>N. gonorrhoeae</i>. Elderly &gt;60 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that prolong QT interval, antiarrhythmic agents, antacids, antidepressants, antidiabetic agents, cimetidine, corticosteroids, ciclosporin and tacrolimus, didanosine, digoxin, iron, multivitamins, mineral supplements, NSAIDs, probenecid, sucralfate, theophylline, warfarin."
          },

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Subdermal use. For three years of use. May be inserted at any time during menstrual cycle."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Current or history of breast cancer. Other diagnosed or suspected sex hormone-dependent neoplasia. Severe liver disease, infection, or tumor. Thromboembolic disease. Unexplained vaginal bleeding. SLE with positive or unknown antiphospholipid antibodies."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with undiagnosed, persistent, or recurrent vaginal bleeding; family history of breast cancer or benign breast nodules or mastopathy; history of thromboembolic disease; predisposition to arterial disease; hepatic impairment; history of, development of, or worsening focal or crescendo-type migraine; DM; conditions that may worsen by fluid retention. Contact lens wearers with loss of vision or changes in lens tolerance. May alter serum lipoprotein levels or glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity in oral glucose tests; decrease total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides. May induce stroke, MI, pulmonary embolism, and DVT; thrombophlebitis and superficial phlebitis; mild or moderate transient rise in total serum bilirubin at initiation of implant; slight increased risk of cholelithiasis; ectopic pregnancy; scleroderma, lupus erythematosus disseminate, RA. Remove implants if thrombotic or embolic disease, cholestatic hepatitis or jaundice, idiopathic intracranial HTN, or pregnancy occurs.       "data": {
        "id": 4670,
        "brand_name": "Levostrat",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/R6h0rJgrA4w0qVygTOCMudBLTLq4MXI3oKlZ8JH3DItiY0eySe.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Bg1LZ9CmuKeMYzoSDtYzZVxYAFFr1x1o9GqIOjYCxxrxYjI8N6.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/zmVFz1oLiHVxeZpAGV5vqUomMVEkSGcS9RcSVxgTHMKj30j92J.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levothyroxine sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-Hypothyroidism Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of hypothyroidism, congenital hypothyroidism in infants, acquired hypothyroidism in childn. Juvenile myxedema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: Initially 50-100 mcg daily, adjust at 3-4 wk intervals by 50 mcg until normal metabolism is steadily maintained. Elderly >50: final daily dose may be up to 50-200 mcg. <b>Childn:</b> Maintenance dose is generally 100-150 mcg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA. <b>Congenital hypothyroidism in infants:</b> Initially 10-15 mcg/kg/day for the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months. <b>Acquired hypothyroidism in childn:</b> Initially 12.5-50 mcg per day, increased gradually every 2-4 weeks according to the clinical findings and thyroid findings and TSH values. <b>Juvenile myxedema in childn:</b> Initially 25 mcg daily. Daily dose may be increased by 25 mcg at intervals of every 2-4 weeks until mild symptoms of hyperthyroidism is seen. Childn &lt;5 yrs: Oral soln is preferred. Avoid administration of whole, crushed, or dispersed tabs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Thyrotoxicosis. Acute MI, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Treatment in patients with panhypopituitarism or other causes predisposing to adrenal insufficiency may cause reactions, including dizziness, weakness, malaise, weight loss, hypotension, adrenal crisis. Patients with cardiac symptoms, DM Should not be used for the treatment of obesity or weight loss. Larger doses may produce serious or even life threatening manifestations of toxicity when given in association with sympathomimetic amines. Patients with myxedema have an increased sensitivity for thyroid hormones. In women, long- term levothyroxine sodium therapy has been associated with increased bone resorption. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased appetite; abnormal weight loss, hyperthyroidism, abdominal cramps; nausea; vomiting; diarrhea, headache; tremors; seizure, anginal pain; cardiac arrhythmias; palpitations; tachycardia; increased blood pressure; heart failure; MI, dyspnea, sweating; alopecia, flushing, cramps in the skeletal muscle; muscular weakness, craniosynostosis in infants, anxiety; emotional lability; nervousness; excitability; insomnia; restlessness, menstrual irregularity; impaired fertility, fatigue; heat intolerance; fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Increase effect of anticoagulants. May increase phenytoin levels. Enhanced the metabolism of thyroid hormones with anticonvulsants e.g. carbamazepine and phenytoin. Cardiac glycosides. Enhanced effects of sympathomimetic agents. Decreased the absorption of thyroxin with cholestyramine, calcium-, aluminum-, magnesium-, iron supplements, aluminum hydroxide, polystyrene sulfonates, sucralfate, lanthanum, bile acid sequestrants e.g. colestipol, anion/cation exchange resins e.g. kayexalate, sevelamer, calcium carbonate, ferrous sulphate, PPI. Soy-containing compounds and high-fiber diets can decrease the intestinal absorption of thyroxine. Increase dosage requirement w/ oral contraceptives. Statins may increase thyroid hormone requirements in patients receiving thyroxine therapy. Use of sertraline can reduce serum levels of thyroxine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 50 mcg."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TlX2tFs9fnExvmFhBLqh5ntnOtEovnJiEHXOVTG4hVVyIeMneI.jpg"

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of adults &ge;18 yrs with mild, moderate, or severe infections caused by susceptible strains of the designated microorganisms for the following conditions: Acute bacterial sinusitis; acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis; community-acquired pneumonia (CAP); healthcare-associated pneumonia (HCAP); complicated skin and skin structure infections (SSSI); uncomplicated SSSI (mild to moderate) including abscesses, cellulitis, furuncles, impetigo, pyoderma, wound infections; complicated and uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI); acute pyelonephritis; chronic bacterial prostatitis. Reduce the incidence or progression of inhalational anthrax in adults and childn &ge;6 months, following exposure to aerosolized <i>Bacillus anthracis</i>. Treatment of plague, including pneumonic and septicemic plague due to <i>Yersinia pestis</i> and prophylaxis for plague in adults and childn &ge;6 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: 500 or 750 mg tab once daily. <b>IV infusion</b>: 250 or 500 mg by slow IV infusion over 60 mins once every 24 hrs. <b>Tab/IV infusion - Adults - Acute bacterial sinusitis</b>: 500 mg for 10-14 days or 750 mg for 5 days. <b>Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis</b>: 500 mg for 7 days or 750 mg for 5 days. CAP: 500 mg for 7-14 days or 750 mg for 5 days. <b>HCAP, complicated SSSI</b>: 750 mg for 7-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated SSSI</b>: 500 mg for 7-10 days. <b>UTI, acute pyelonephritis</b>: 250 mg for 10 days or 750 mg for 5 days. <b>Chronic bacterial prostatitis</b>: 500 mg for 28 days. <b>Uncomplicated UTI</b>: 250 mg for 3 days. <b>Inhalational anthrax (post-exposure)</b>: 500 mg for 60 days. <b>Plague</b>: 500 mg for 10-14 days.<b>Renal impairment - CrCl 20-49 mL/min</b>: 750 mg every 48 hrs; or 500 mg initial dose then 250 mg every 24 hrs. <b>10-19 mL/min</b>: 750 mg initial dose then 500 mg every 48 hrs; or 500 mg initial dose then 250 mg every 48 hrs; or 250 every 48 hrs (no dosage adjustment required if treating uncomplicated UTI). <b>Hemodialysis or CAPD</b>: 750 mg initial dose then 500 mg every 48 hrs; or 500 mg initial dose then 250 mg every 48 hrs. <b>Childn &ge;50 kg</b>: 500 mg once every 24 hrs for 60 days (for inhalational anthrax post-exposure) or 10-14 days (for plague). <b>&lt;50 kg and &ge;6 months old</b>: 8 mg/kg BW /dose (not to exceed 250 mg/dose) to be given every 12 hrs for 60 days (for inhalational anthrax post-exposure) or 10-14 days (for plague)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of myasthenia gravis.  hepatotoxicity, peripheral neuropathy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "<i>C. difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture; peripheral neuropathy. Avoid direct exposure to excessive sunlight or UV radiation. Patients with known or suspected CNS disorder that may predispose to seizures or lower seizure threshold; prolongation of the QT interval, uncorrected hypokalemia, significant bradycardia, cardiomyopathy, myocardial ischemia; diabetes; G6PD deficiency. Not for the treatment of syphilis or gonorrhea.Renal and hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Infants and childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms including fungi. CV, CNS, dermatologic and sensitivity reactions, endocrine and metabolic, GI, hepatic, hematologic, musculoskeletal, reproductive/urogenital, and respiratory effects."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antidiabetic agents, fluoxetine, imipramine, corticosteroids, NSAIDs, theophylline, warfarin. False positive urine screening test results for opiates. May give false negative results in bacteriological diagnosis of TB. <b>Tab</b>: Antacids, sucralfate, metal cations, and zinc-containing multivitamin preparations. <b>IV infusion</b>: Solution containing multivalent cations (e.g. magnesium) through the same IV line."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P214.46), 750 mg (P280.49). Solution for IV infusion 5 mg/mL x 50 mL (P1,000.24), 100 mL (P1,951.10), 150 mL (P2,135.69)."
          }

    "detail": {

      "data": {
        "id": 556,

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Losartan potassium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN), heart failure, diabetic nephropathy with elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria (urinary albumin to creatinine ratio &ge;300 mg/g) in type 2 diabetes and history of HTN. Decreases risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in hypertensive patients with left ventricular hypertrophy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN - Adults:</b> 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg once daily. <b>Intravascular volume depletion:</b> Initially 25 mg once daily. <b>Childn &ge;6 yrs:</b> Initially 0.7 mg/kg once daily; <b>&ge;50 kg:</b> 50 mg once daily, max 100 mg daily. <b>&ge;20-< 50 kg:</b> 25 mg once daily, max 50 mg daily. <b>Renal impairment - Moderate to severe, undergoing dialysis:</b> 25 mg once daily. <b>Hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy:</b> Initially 50 mg once daily. Added with HCTZ 12.5 mg or increased losartan to 100 mg once daily followed by increase in HCTZ to 25 mg once daily. <b>Heart failure:</b> Initially 12.5 mg once daily, titrated at weekly intervals to 50 mg once daily. <b>Nephropathy in type 2 DM:</b> Initially 50 once daily, may be increased to 100 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Women trying to get pregnant. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of liver impairment. Fetal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. Correct hypotension and electrolyte/fluid imbalance before therapy. Changes in renal function are RAAS-dependent. Oliguria, progressive azotemia, acute renal failure, and/or death, acute hypotension. May increase BUN and serum creatinine in patients with unilateral or bilateral renal artery stenosis. Risk of MI or stroke in ischemic cardiopathy or cerebrovascular disease. Monitor serum potassium levels in type 2 DM with nephropathy. Childn with GFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> or hepatic impairment. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C (1st trimester) and D (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters). Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, chest pain, edema, facial edema, fatigue, fever, infection, influenza-like disease, orthostatic effects, syncope, trauma, abdominal pain, anorexia, constipation, dental pain, diarrhea, dry mouth, dyspepsia, flatulence, gastritis, nausea, vomiting, vertigo, anemia, orthostatic hypotension, increased BUN and serum creatinine, hypoglycemia, dizziness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lithium, potassium-sparing diuretics/supplements/salt substitutes, NSAIDs, rifampicin, fluconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P24.06), 100 mg (P30.33)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of fungal infections affecting up to 2 nails and the upper half or sides of the nail."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply once or twice weekly to affected nails. Once weekly for up to 6 months for finger nails and 9-12 months for toe nails. See patient leaflet for complete instructions for use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used alone if fungal infection is in the lunula (base of nail). Patients with diabetes, weak immune system, poor circulation in hands and feet; severely damaged or infected nails. Discontinue immediately when allergic reaction occurs. Avoid contact with eyes, ears or mucous membranes (e.g. mouth and nostrils). Do not inhale. Wear impermeable gloves when handling organic solvents (e.g. acetone, ethanol). Do not use nail varnish or artificial nails during treatment.",

            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply 1 patch to the affected area once daily. Max 2 patches/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with PUD, severe blood abnormality, severe hepatic or renal impairment, severe cardiac dysfunction, severe HTN, current or history of aspirin-induced asthma. Concomitant use with enoxacin hydrate, lomefloxacin, norfloxacin, or prulifloxacin. Pregnancy (late)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be applied to damaged skin or membrane, areas of eczema or rash. Patients with peptic ulcer induced by long-term use of NSAID analgesics who need long-term use of Locoa and are being treated with agents (e.g. misoprostol); history of peptic ulcer; blood abnormality; bleeding tendency; hepatic disorder; renal disorder or reduced renal blood flow; abnormal cardiac function; HTN; bronchial asthma; ulcerative colitis; Crohn’s disease. Prolonged use may result in temporary infertility in women. Elderly. Low-birth-weight infants. Childn. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dermatitis, erythema, pruritus, eczema, rash; increased blood urea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "New quinolone antibiotics (e.g. ofloxacin), coumarin anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin), methotrexate, lithium products (e.g. lithium carbonate), thiazide (e.g. HCTZ) and loop (e.g. furosemide) diuretics, corticosteroids (e.g. methylprednisolone), CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g. fluconazole)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Transdermal patch 40 mg x 7s (P350.00)."
          }

          {

          {

  {
    "id": 2524,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2524,
        "brand_name": "Linelid",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WfgPqlxD7i8Shung0lFG3ReWesRqyVNYSw1T1AGvBPrWKkPWJm.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WfgPqlxD7i8Shung0lFG3ReWesRqyVNYSw1T1AGvBPrWKkPWJm.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/aefYHt3tYfZJPipuumpThZQuMEoXaMW1133JgeU00BHs4oYYbr.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Linezolid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Oxazolidinones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of nosocomial and community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), skin and soft tissue infections, enterococcal infections i.e. vancomycin-resistant strains and forms accompanied by bacteremia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn >12 yrs - Nosocomial pneumonia and CAP, skin and soft tissue infections:</b> 600 mg every 12 hrs for 10-14 days. <b>Enterococcal infections:</b> 600 mg every 12 hrs for 14-28 days. <b>Childn 0-11 yrs - Nosocomial pneumonia and CAP, skin and soft tissue infections:</b> 10 mg/kg every 8 hrs for 10-14 days. <b>Enterococcal infections:</b> 10 mg/kg every 8 hrs for 14-28 days. Infusion should be administered within 30-120 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with uncontrolled arterial HTN, pheochromocytoma, carcinoid, thyrotoxicosis, bipolar depression, schizophrenia, acute dizziness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Tyramine-enriched foods. Patients with DM or impaired glucose tolerance, on restricted sodium diet; renal failure, pre-existing anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, liver injury. Monitor complete blood count parameters. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Candidiasis, headache, taste perversion, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, changes in liver function and hematological findings."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "SSRIs, TCAs, serotonin 5-HT1 receptor agonists, directly and indirectly acting sympathomimetics (i.e. adrenergic bronchodilators, pseudoephedrine, phenylpropanolamine), vasopressors, dopaminergic compounds, pethidine, or buspirone. MAOIs. Tyramine-rich food. <b>Incompatibilities:</b> Amphotericin B, chlorpromazine HCl, diazepam, pentamidine isethionate, phenytoin sodium, erythromycin lactobionate, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and ceftriaxone sodium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 2 mg/mL x 300 mL."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 69,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 69,
        "brand_name": "Lipanthyl",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fenofibrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fibric Acid Derivatives & Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia alone or combined (types IIa, IIb, III, IV, V dyslipidemia) in patients unresponsive to dietary and other non-drug therapeutic measures (e.g. weight reduction or increased physical activity), particularly when there is evidence of associated risk e.g. hypertension, smoking. Secondary hyperlipoproteinemias (if hyperlipoproteinemia persists despite effective treatment of underlying disease)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 3 caps/day, may be increased up to 4 caps if required."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hepatic insufficiency, gallbladder disease, severe CKD, chronic or acute pancreatitis, photoallergy or phototoxic reaction. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Treat secondary causes of hyperlipidemia before therapy. Elevation of transaminase levels. Discontinue if creatinine levels &gt;50% ULN, AST and ALT levels increase &gt;3x ULN, and symptoms indicative of hepatitis occur. Measure creatinine during the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months after initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Patients with pre-disposing factors for myopathy and/or rhabdomyolysis. Renal and hepatic impairment. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood homocysteine level increase, GI symptoms (abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, flatulence), transaminases increase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, other fibrates and HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, ciclosporin, glitazones. Drugs metabolized by CYP2C19, CYP2A6, and CYP2C9 with a narrow therapeutic index."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 67 mg (P37.75)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

          "name": "Abbott Laboratories"

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XyPgTcXthSYcGOlEnnvmIc0K5kVcz4RzMrngjklUMVMihjppYR.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/rcnsW72YFAvcHqvgBtTjjCM765rNTCR1wvFM2CzlDgsgmdnQJu.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fenofibrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fibric Acid Derivatives & Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia alone or combined (types IIa, IIb, III, IV, V dyslipidemia) in patients unresponsive to dietary and other non-drug therapeutic measures, particularly when there is evidence of associated risk e.g. hypertension, smoking. Secondary hyperlipoproteinemias (if hyperlipoproteinemia persists despite effective treatment of underlying disease)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once daily. Patients taking one 200 mg cap (or one 145 mg tab) can change to one 160 mg tab without dose adjustment. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl 30-60 mL/min):</b> Dose reduction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active substance, excipients, peanut, or soy. Hepatic insufficiency, gallbladder disease, severe CKD, chronic or acute pancreatitis, photoallergy or phototoxic reaction. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Treat secondary causes of hyperlipidemia before therapy. Elevation of transaminase levels. Discontinue if creatinine levels &gt;50% ULN, AST and ALT levels increase &gt;3x ULN, and symptoms indicative of hepatitis occur. Measure creatinine during the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months after initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Patients with pre-disposing factors for myopathy and/or rhabdomyolysis. Renal and hepatic impairment. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood homocysteine level increase, GI symptoms (abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, flatulence), transaminases increase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, other fibrates and HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, ciclosporin, glitazones. Drugs metabolized by CYP2C19, CYP2A6, and CYP2C9 with a narrow therapeutic index."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 160 mg (P101.75)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3176,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3176,
        "brand_name": "Lipitor",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mXINMdd8qISAhA9V8QbGHiIDIioFos0u2Rkq21O4YTGVv6bjpM.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GuNoJWIP5GkM49c64Qufu4FS7jSleOXbyilhQAxbFvj8r0tdMZ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/VNoOs0E0egztBwYen0UIvq8RxmiFI4l2EkVMRdPDAAmEKnJbhx.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Atorvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "As adjunct to diet for treatment of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides (TG) and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and nonfamilial hypercholesterolemia), combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson Types IIa and IIb), elevated serum TG levels (Fredrickson Type IV), and for patients with dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson Type III) who do not respond adequately to diet. For reduction of total-C and LDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduce risk for fatal coronary heart disease (CHD) and non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI); stroke; revascularization procedures and angina pectoris in patients without clinically evident cardiovascular disease (CVD), and with or without dyslipidemia, but with multiple risk factors for CHD. Reduce the risk for non-fatal MI; fatal and non-fatal stroke; revascularization procedures; hospitalization for congestive heart failure; angina. As adjunct to lifestyle changes to halt the progression of atherosclerosis (total atheroma or plaque volume) in patients with CAD and other individuals who are at high risk for CVD. Adjunct to diet to reduce total cholesterol, LDL-C, and apolipoprotein B levels in boys and post-menarchal girls, age 10-17 yrs, and with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduce the risk of CV disease in patients with diabetes with moderately decreased eGFR. Reduce the risk of major CV events including stroke in patients with clinically evident CHD and chronic kidney disease (CKD) not requiring dialysis. Reduce the rate of GFR decline and progression of CKD in patients with clinically evident CHD and/or diabetes with microalbuminuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "10-80 mg once daily. Starting and maintenance dosage should be individualized according to baseline LDL-C levels, the goal of therapy, and patient response. After initiation and/or upon titration of atorvastatin, lipid levels should be analyzed within 2-4 weeks, and dosage adjusted accordingly. <b>Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia</b>: 10 mg once daily. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b>: 80 mg. <b>Severe dyslipidemias in childn &ge;10 yrs</b>: 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 80 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases &gt;3x ULN. Concomitant use with letermovir wtih ciclosporin. Women of childbearing potential not using contraceptive measures. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Moderate elevations of serum transaminases. Perform liver function tests before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Patients who consume substantial amounts of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease. Discontinue if markedly elevated creatine phosphokinase occur or if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected. Temporarily withhold or discontinue in patients with acute, serious condition suggestive of myopathy or with risk factor predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Increased risk for recurrent hemorrhagic stroke. Increase in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, hyperglycemia, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, arthralgia, myalgia, musculoskeletal pain, muscle spasms, pain in extremity, joint swelling, abnormal liver function test and increase in blood creatine phosphokinase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors, protease inhibitors, diltiazem grapefruit juice, itraconazole, ciclosporin, erythromycin and clarithromycin, glecaprevir, pibrentasvir, elbasvir, grazoprevir and letermovir; colchicine; fusidic acid; fibric acid derivatives, erythromycin, immunosuppressive drugs, azole antifungals, or niacin. Oral contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg (P13.00), 20 mg (P16.50), 40 mg (P22.75), 80 mg (P28.00)."
          }
        ],

        },

            "content": "<b>HTN – Adults</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily. Patients with possible depletion of intravascular vol or history of hepatic impairment: 25 mg once daily. Add HCTZ 12.5 mg daily and/or increase losartan to 100 mg once daily followed by an increase HCTZ to 25 mg once daily based on BP response. <b>Nephropathy in type 2 diabetes patients</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily, increased to 100 mg once daily based on BP response.             "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>20 mg</b>: Treatment of reflux esophagitis, acid peptic ulcer disease (PUD), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. As adjunct to antibiotics in duodenal ulcer associated with <i>Helicobacter pylori</i>. Prophylaxis of acid aspiration before surgery. Prevention and treatment of NSAID-associated ulcer. <b>40 mg</b>: Treatment of PUD, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), heartburn, and other symptoms associated with GERD, severe erosive esophagitis and eradication of <i>H. pylori</i> in patients with active duodenal ulcer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>GERD or erosive esophagitis</b>: 20 mg/day for 4-8 weeks. <b>Pathological hypersecretory conditions</b>: 60 mg once daily to start doses up to 120 mg thrice daily. Administered daily doses &gt;80 mg in divided doses. <b><i>H. pylori</i></b>: 20 mg twice daily in combination with bismuth subsalicylate, tetracycline, and clarithromycin or with clarithromycin alone. <b>Gastric ulcers</b>: 40 mg/day for 4-8 weeks. <b>Refractory esophagitis</b>: 40 mg daily. Maintenance: 20 mg once daily. Childn: 0.7-1.4 mg/kg BW daily. Max 40 mg for 4-12 weeks. <b>PUD</b>: 20 mg or 40 mg in severe cases. Continue for 4 weeks for duodenal and 8 weeks for gastric ulcer. Maintenance: 20 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, skin rashes, and headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Nelfinavir, atazanavir, digoxin, clopidogrel, posaconazole, erlotinib, ketoconazole, itraconazole. R-warfarin, other vit K antagonists, cilostazol, diazepam, phenytoin, saquinavir/ritonavir, tacrolimus, methotrexate."

          {

  {
    "id": 972,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 972,
        "brand_name": "Mepraz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Omeprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of peptic ulcer disease (PUD), duodenal ulcer associated with <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> infection, gastric ulcer, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), hypersecretory conditions e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, reflux esophagitis and dyspepsia. Prophylaxis of acid aspiration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>PUD:</b> 20 mg once a day, and 40 mg for severe case. Healing usually occurs within 4 weeks for patients with duodenal ulcer and 8 weeks for gastric ulcer. Maintenance: 10-20 mg once a day. <b>Duodenal ulcer:</b> 20 mg once a day for 4-8 weeks. <b>Duodenal ulcer associated with <i>H. pylori</i></b> - <b>Triple therapy:</b> 20 mg + clarithromycin 500 mg + amoxicillin 1,000 mg each given twice daily for 10 days; or 20 mg + clarithromycin 250 mg + metronidazole 500 mg or tinidazole each given twice daily for 1 week; or 20 mg cap once a day + amoxicillin 500 mg + metronidazole 500 mg both thrice daily for 1 week. <b>Dual therapy:</b> 40 mg + clarithromycin 500 mg thrice daily for 14 days or 40 mg once a day + amoxicillin 750 mg twice a day for 2 weeks. <b>Gastric ulcer:</b> 20 mg once a day for 4 weeks; for patients with poorly responsive gastric ulcer: 40 mg once a day for 8 weeks. <b>GERD:</b> 20 mg-40 mg once a day for 4-12 weeks; Maintenance: 20 mg once a day. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome:</b> 60 mg once a day up to 120 mg thrice daily. <b>Prophylaxis of acid aspiration:</b> 40 mg in the evening before surgery followed by 40 mg on the day of surgery given 1-4 hrs before the procedure. <b>Reflux esophagitis:</b> 20 mg daily for 4 weeks; Severe: 40 mg once a day for 8 weeks. <b>Dyspepsia:</b> Initially 10 mg daily; <b>for patients with epigastric pain with or without heartburn:</b> 20 mg for 4 weeks. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Max 10-20 mg once a day. <b>Renal impairment:</b> Adjust dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Rule out malignancy. Hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

    "id": 4532,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4532,
        "brand_name": "Mepresone 40",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Methylprednisolone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Dermatological disease:</b> Severe erythema multiforme (Stevens-Johnson syndrome). <b>Allergic states:</b> Bronchial asthma, severe seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, angioneurotic edema, anaphylaxis. <b>Gastrointestinal diseases:</b> Ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease. <b>Respiratory diseases:</b> Aspiration of gastric contents, fulminating or disseminated tuberculosis (TB). <b>Neurological disorders:</b> Cerebral edema secondary to cerebral tumor acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis superimposed on a relapsing-remitting background. <b>Miscellaneous:</b> TB meningitis transplantation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV or IM. IV (high dose) should be given over a period of at least 30 mins and 5 mins for doses up to 250 mg. <b>Adults</b> - <b>Graft rejection reactions following transplantation:</b> 1 g/day; For acute rejection: 500 mg-1 g. Administer for 48-72 hrs. <b>Status asthmaticus:</b> 40 mg IV. <b>Edema due to brain tumor</b> - Schedule A - Pre-op: 20 mg IM every 3-6 hrs; During surgery: 20-40 mg IV hourly; Post-op: Administered by IM; taper dose every 24 hrs in regular intervals. Schedule B - Pre-op: 40 mg IM every 6 hrs for 2-3 days; Post-op: Initially 40 mg IM every 6 hrs for 3-5 days, then switch to oral. Aim to discontinue therapy after 10 days. <b>Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis:</b> 500 mg or 1 g/day for 3 days IV given over at least 30 mins. <b>Other indications:</b> 10-500 mg depending on clinical problem being treated. <b>Childn</b> - <b>Graft rejection reactions:</b> 10-20 mg/kg/day for up to 3 days. Max 1 g/day; <b>Status asthmaticus:</b> 1-4 mg/kg/day for 1-3 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections, cerebral edema in malaria. Use by intrathecal route. Administration of live or live attenuated vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May increase susceptibility and mask signs of infections, and new infections may appear. Avoid exposure to chickenpox, herpes zoster or measles. Patients with known or suspected parasitic infections (e.g. <i>Strongyloides</i> infestation). Use in active TB is restricted to cases of fulminating or disseminated TB. Monitor patients with latent TB or tuberculin reactivity; during prolonged corticosteroid therapy, these patients should receive chemoprophylaxis. Not used in treating septic shock, or traumatic brain injury. Prolonged use may result in HPA suppression. Acute adrenal and drug-induced secondary adrenocortical insufficiencies, and steroid withdrawal syndrome may occur if withdrawn abruptly. Avoid abrupt withdrawal in patients who had repeated courses of systemic corticosteroids (&gt;3 weeks), reasons for adrenocortical insufficiency other than exogenous corticosteroid therapy; receiving &gt;32 mg/day methylprednisolone; repeatedly taking doses in the evening; short course prescribed within 1 yr of cessation of long-term therapy. Patients with Cushing’s disease, hypothyroidism, DM, existing or previous history of severe affective disorders, seizure disorders, myasthenia gravis, ocular herpes simplex, existing CV risk factors, CHF, recent MI, HTN, predisposition to thromboembolic disorders, ulcerative colitis, perforation, abscess or other pyogenic infections, diverticulitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, peptic ulceration, osteoporosis, renal insufficiency, pheochromocytoma. Concomitant use with digoxin, NSAIDs, aspirin. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Troleandomycin, isoniazid, rifampin, phenobarbital, phenytoin, aprepitant, fosaprepitant, itraconazole, ketoconazole, HIV-protease inhibitors, diltiazem, ethinylestradiol/norethisterone, ciclosporin, erythromycin, carbamazepine, cyclophosphamide, tacrolimus; anticoagulants, neuromuscular blockers, anticholinesterases, antidiabetic agents, aminoglutethimide, NSAIDs, high-dose aspirin; grapefruit juice. <b>Incompatibilities:</b> Allopurinol sodium, doxapram HCl, tigecycline, diltiazem HCl, calcium gluconate, vecuronium bromide, rocuronium bromide, cisatracurium besylate, glycopyrrolate and propofol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IV/IM) 40 mg (P373.00)."
          }

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Telmisartan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN). Reduction of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity in adults with manifested atherothrombotic CV disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) with documented target organ damage in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Essential HTN:</b> 40 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. Max: 80 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of CV disease:</b> 80 mg once daily. <b>Renal impairment:</b> 20 mg initially. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Should not exceed 40 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with biliary obstructive disorders, cholestasis, or severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use of aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor potassium and creatinine serum levels. Intravascular hypovolemia. Increase risk of hypotension. Patients with severe CHF or underlying renal disease including renal artery stenosis, primary aldosteronism, aortic and mitral valve stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic CV disease. Diabetic patients treated with insulin or antidiabetics. Hyperkalemia.  Black hypertensive population. May affect ability to drive or operate machines. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For essential hypertension and whose BP is not adequately controlled on telmisartan alone in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individual dose titration with each of the two components is recommended before changing to the fixed dose combination. <b>Adults whose BP is not adequately controlled by telmisartan alone:</b> 1 tab (40 mg/12.5 mg or 80 mg/12.5 mg or 80 mg/25 mg) once daily. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Should not exceed 40 mg/12.5 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active substances, any of the excipients, or other sulfonamide-derived substances. Patients with cholestasis, biliary obstructive disorders, severe hepatic and renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Concomitant use of aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Refractory hypokalemia, or hypercalcemia. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of severe hypotension and renal insufficiency. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), hepatic impairment, severe CHF or underlying renal disease including renal artery stenosis; primary aldosteronism; aortic or mitral stenosis or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic CV disease. Intravascular hypovolemia. Dual blockade of RAAS with ACE inhibitors or aliskiren. May impair glucose tolerance. Electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, hyperchloremic alkalosis, hypercalcemia). Patients with fructose intolerance, galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Hypertensive Black patients. Photosensitivity reactions. Risk factor for acute myopia and angle-closure glaucoma. May affect ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lithium, kaliuretic diuretics, laxatives, corticosteroids, ACTH, amphotericin, carbenoxolone, penicillin G Na, salicylic acid derivatives, ACE inhibitors, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, cyclosporine, heparin sodium, class Ia and III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics (e.g. thioridazine, chlorpromazine, levomepromazine, trifluoperazine, cyamemazine, sulpiride, sultopride, amisulpride, tiapride, pimozide, haloperidol, droperidol), bepridil, cisapride, diphemanil, erythromycin IV, halofantrine, pentamidine, sparfloxacin, terfenadine, vincamine IV, digitalis glycosides, digoxin, other antihypertensive agents, oral antidiabetics, insulin, metformin, cholestyramine, colestipol resins, NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin, COX-2 inhibitors, and non-selective NSAIDs), noradrenaline, tubocurarine, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, allopurinol, calcium salts, beta-blockers, diazoxide, atropine, biperiden, amantadine, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, baclofen, amifostine, alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, or antidepressants."

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Carbapenems"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI) in adults and childn &ge;3 months; complicated intra-abdominal infections e.g. complicated appendicitis and peritonitis in adults and childn; bacterial meningitis in childn &ge;3 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>SSSI:</b> 500 mg every 8 hrs; <b>cSSSI caused by <i>P. aeruginosa</i> and intra-abdominal infections:</b> 1 g every 8 hrs. Administered by IV infusion over 15-30 mins. Doses of 1 g may be given as IV bolus injection (5-20 mL) over 3-5 mins. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl >50 mL/min: 500 mg every 8 hrs (cSSSI) and 1 g every 8 hrs (intra-abdominal infections); 26-50 mL/min: 500 mg every 12 hrs (cSSSI) and 1 g every 12 hrs (intra-abdominal infections); 10-25 mL/min: 250 mg every 12 hrs (cSSSI) and 500 mg every 12 hrs (intra-abdominal infections); &lt;10 mL/min: 250 mg every 24 hrs (cSSSI) and 500 mg every 24 hrs (intra-abdominal infections). <b>Childn weighing &gt;50 kg</b> - <b>cSSSI:</b> 500 mg every 8 hrs; <b>cSSSI caused by <i>P. aeruginosa</i> and intra-abdominal infections:</b> 1 g every 8 hrs; <b>Meningitis:</b> 2 g every 8 hrs. <b>Childn &ge;3 months</b> - <b>cSSSI:</b> 10 mg/kg every 8 hrs. Max 500 mg; <b>cSSSI caused by <i>P. aeruginosa</i>:</b> 20 mg/kg every 8 hrs; <b>Complicated intra-abdominal infections:</b> 20 mg/kg every 8 hrs. Max 1 g; <b>Meningitis:</b> 40 mg/kg every 8 hrs. Max 2 g. <b>Infants &lt;3 months</b> - <b>Complicated intra-abdominal infections</b> - &lt;32 weeks gestational age and &lt;2 weeks postnatal age: 20 mg/kg every 12 hrs; &lt;32 weeks gestational age and &ge;2 weeks postnatal age: 20 mg/kg every 8 hrs; &ge;32 weeks gestational age and &lt;2 weeks postnatal age: 20 mg/kg every 8 hrs; &ge;32 weeks gestational age and &ge;2 weeks postnatal age: 30 mg/kg every 8 hrs. Given as IV infusion over 30 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to beta-lactams."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue if hypersensitivity reaction occurs. Patients with CNS disorders (e.g. brain lesions or history of seizures), bacterial meningitis and/or compromised renal function. Risk of breakthrough seizures due to drug interaction with valproic acid. <i>C. difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Development of drug-resistant bacteria. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Thrombocytopenia in patients with renal impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain; liver function tests disturbance; thrombocytopenia, positive Coomb’s test, eosinophilia, leukopenia, neutropenia; headache, paresthesia; hypersensitivity reactions; convulsions, SJS and TEN; local irritation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, valproic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IV) 500 mg, 1 g."
          }
        ],

    "id": 2564,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2564,
        "brand_name": "Medgyl Solution for Injection",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Q8m26G7WcRYhJtU4PUUDsr5JwKLpozQv5TvbGzQboZj6Oayc9H.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Q8m26G7WcRYhJtU4PUUDsr5JwKLpozQv5TvbGzQboZj6Oayc9H.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/axYhZtR90TrSGU1WtA3w25HJCBtrLSkSRp1897jyemGixP0Brl.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metronidazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-protozoals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections in which anaerobic bacteria have been identified or are suspected pathogens, particularly <i>Bacteroides fragilis</i> and other species of <i>Bacteroides</i> and including other species for which metronidazole is bactericidal. Prevention of post-op abdominal and pelvic infections due to anaerobic bacteria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment - Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: 100 mL IV infusion every 8 hrs at a rate of 5 mL/min for 7 days. <b>Childn &lt;12 yrs</b>: Single IV dose based on 1.5 mL/kg BW. <b>Prophylaxis - Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: 100 mL IV infusion immediately pre-op, during and post-op, followed by the same dose every 8 hrs until oral medication can be given to complete 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with blood dyscrasias, active CNS disease. Short high dose regimen during pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Convulsive seizures, peripheral neuropathy. GI disorders (nausea, headache, anorexia, vomiting, diarrhea, epigastric distress, abdominal cramping and constipation). Sharp, unpleasant metallic taste, furry tongue, glossitis and stomatitis. Reversible neutropenia, T-wave flattening. Dizziness, vertigo, incoordination, ataxia, confusion, irritability, depression, weakness and insomnia. Urticaria, erythematous rash, flushing, nasal congestion, dryness of mouth (or vagina or vulva) and fever. Dysuria, cystitis, polyuria, incontinence and sense of pelvic pressure. Proliferation of <i>Candida</i> in the vagina, dyspareunia, decreased libido, proctitis and fleeting joint pain (resembling serum-sickness)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection 5 mg/mL x 100 mL (P250.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Infections caused by microorganisms susceptible to metronidazole: Amebiasis; urogenital trichomoniasis; non-specific vaginitis; giardiasis; curative treatment of medico-surgical infections due to susceptible anaerobic pathogens; prophylaxis against infections caused by susceptible anaerobic pathogens in high risk surgical contexts; conversion from prophylactic or curative injectable treatment of infections due to susceptible anaerobic pathogens."

          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis, erythema multiforme."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

        "id": 1261,
