        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/91DHSHrigFX0Hw6LSaJmUdSkGyLeg1xEWv48BubIGA6qBOOyhj.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/91DHSHrigFX0Hw6LSaJmUdSkGyLeg1xEWv48BubIGA6qBOOyhj.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/3uHXZJlPxAOtJaTdhFDFrQfC2Wbb1L5vUp2hReeePWdu0xwegW.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ibuprofen",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For relief of mild to moderate to intense aches and pains due to dental pain, headache (including migraine and neuralgia), muscular aches (including sprains and strains, minor arthritis pain, back ache, and shoulder pain), common cold or flu, menstrual cramps; other types of pain e.g. earache, or pain after vaccination or surgery; inflammation from arthritis, non-serious arthritic conditions, and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis; fever reduction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs - 200 mg</b>: 1 softgel cap every 6-8 hrs as needed. Max 4 caps/24 hrs. <b>400 mg</b>: 1 softgel cap up to 3 times a day with at least 4 hrs between each dose or every 8 hrs. Max 1,200 mg/24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to ibuprofen, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Patients with active bleeding or blood-clotting disorder e.g. hemophilia; severe renal disease (CrCl < 30 mL/min); hepatic disease; SLE; connective tissue disease; dengue fever; GI problems e.g. heartburn, IBD (Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis), stomach ulcers. Patients with history or at risk for stroke, HTN, dyslipidemia, DM; undergoing heart surgery; conditions associated with bronchospasm, angioedema, nasal polyps, dehydration (vomiting, diarrhea). Pregnancy (last 3 months) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not take longer than 10 days. Concomitant use of aspirin, other NSAIDs, anticoagulants, or steroids. Patients with severe or persistent sore throat. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Risk for fertility impairment in women. Childn 7-12 yrs. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Constipation, decreased appetite, diarrhea, dizziness, dyspepsia, otitis media, fever, fluid retention, bloating or flatulence, headache, heartburn, indigestion, itching, stomatitis, nausea, nervousness, rash, tinnitus, pharyngitis, stomach cramps or pain, swelling, vertigo, and vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aspirin; aminoglycosides; antacids; antihypertensives (e.g. captopril, enalapril, losartan, telmisartan); diuretics (e.g. furosemide); cardiac glycosides (e.g. digoxin); cholestyramine; ciclosporin, tacrolimus; <I>Ginkgo biloba</i>; lithium, methotrexate; drugs affecting liver enzymes; hypoglycemic agents; probenecid; quinolone antibiotics; zidovudine; alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 200 mg (P7.00), 400 mg (P12.25)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of conditions in which corticosteroid therapy is indicated except in adrenocortical-deficiency states where hydrocortisone with supplementary fludrocortisone is preferred."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b> Adults</b>: 4-48 mg daily in single or multiple doses. <b>Multiple sclerosis</b>: 160 mg for 1 week, then 64 mg every 2 days for 1 month. <b>Childn - Adrenocortical insufficiency</b>: 0.117 mg/kg BW or 3.33 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA per day in 3-4 divided doses. <b>Other indications</b>: 0.417-1.67 mg/kg BW or 12.5-50 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA per day in 3-4 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections. Long-term treatment in patients with duodenal and peptic ulcer, severe osteoporosis, and those with a history of mental disease, herpes. Patients currently receiving vaccines. Premature infants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concomitant administration of smallpox vaccination or other immunization procedures during treatment. Patients with hypothyroidism or cirrhosis, ocular herpes simplex.           },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fluid and electrolyte disturbances, muscle weakness, impaired wound healing, increased BP, posterior subcapsular cataracts, growth suppression in childn, adrenal insufficiency, Cushing's syndrome, osteoporosis, and peptic ulcer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs, antirheumatic and antidiabetic drugs, smallpox vaccine, and other immunizations. Barbiturates, phenytoin, rifampicin, anticholinesterase agents, and potassium-depleting drugs."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Meropenem trihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Carbapenems"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections caused by single or multiple susceptible bacteria and as empiric therapy prior to identification of causative organisms: Lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), urinary tract infections (including complicated infections), intra-abdominal infection, gynecological infections (including postpartum infections), skin and skin structure infections, septicemia, meningitis, polymicrobial infections. Empiric treatment including initial monotherapy for presumed bacterial infections in host-compromised neutropenic patients. Effective in patients with cystic fibrosis and chronic LRTI either monotherapy or in combination with other antibacterial agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV bolus inj over approx 5 mins or IV infusion over approx 15-30 mins. <b>Adults and childn >50 kg:</b> 500 mg-1 g every 8 hrs depending on type and severity of infection, known or expected susceptibility of pathogen and condition of patient. <b>Childn >3 months-12 yrs:</b> 10-40 mg/kg every 8 hrs. <b>Febrile episodes in neutropenic patients - Adults:</b> 1 g every 8 hrs; <b>Childn:</b> 20 mg/kg every 8 hrs. <b>Meningitis/cystic fibrosis - Adults:</b> 2 g every 8 hrs; <b>Childn:</b> 40 mg/kg every 8 hrs. <b>Infections caused by <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i> - Adults:</b> at least 1 g every 8 hours (max 6 g daily in 3 divided doses); <b>Childn:</b> at least 20 mg/kg every 8 hrs (max 120 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses). <b>Renal impairment – CrCl 26-50 mL/min:</b> 1 unit dose every 12 hrs; <b>10-25 mL/min:</b> &frac12; unit dose every 12 hrs; <b>< 10 mL/min:</b> &frac12; unit dose every 24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of hypersensitivity to carbapenems, penicillins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Patients with renal insufficiency; liver disease; pre-existing liver disorder. Discontinue if severe cutaneous adverse reactions (e.g. SJS, TEN, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, erythema multiforme, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis) occurs. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms; pseudomembranous colitis. Positive Coombs’ test. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Infants < 3 months. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thrombocythemia, headache, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, increased ALT and AST, blood alkaline phosphatase, blood lactate dehydrogenase, and gamma-glutamyltransferase, rash, pruritus, inflammation, pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, valproic acid/sodium valproate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection 1 g."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Glycopeptide Antibiotic"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of potentially life-threatening infections caused by susceptible G(+) organisms which cannot be treated by other less toxic antimicrobial drugs (e.g. penicillins, cephalosporins): Severe staphyloccocal infections, treatment and prophylaxis against endocarditis in patients at risk from dental or surgical procedures; other staphylococci infections e.g. osteomyelitis, pneumonia, septicemia, soft tissue infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via IV infusion over at least 60 mins. Max rate: 10 mg/min. Recommended diluted soln concentration &le;5 mg/mL. <b>Adults:</b> 500 mg every 6 hrs or 1 g every 12 hrs. Duration of treatment - Staphylococcal endocarditis: &ge;3 weeks. <b>Childn:</b> 10 mg/kg/dose every 6 hrs. <b>Infants and neonates:</b> Initially 15 mg/kg, followed by 10 mg/kg every 12 hrs (neonates 1<sup>st</sup> week of life), and every 8 hrs (neonates up to 1 month). <b>Elderly, patients with renal impairment:</b> Adjust dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of shock."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for IM injection. Patients with hearing loss due to peptide antibiotics or aminoglycosides, renal (e.g. acute urinary retention) and hepatic impairment, history of renal disorder, impaired vestibular organ or cochlea. Concomitant use with aminoglycosides. Discontinue if symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis by <i>Clostridium difficile</i>, and superinfection occurs. Monitor leukocyte count periodically. Premature infants and neonates. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, tinnitus, hearing loss; increased bilirubin, AST and ALT, BUN and creatinine; exfoliative and bullous dermatitis, SJS and TEN; rash, erythema, flushing, hypotension, wheezing, dyspnea, urticaria and pruritus. Red-man’s syndrome, chest and abdominal pain, muscle spasm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anesthetic agents, amphotericin B, aminoglycosides, bacitracin, polymyxin B, colistin, viomycin, cisplatin, nedaplatin, anticoagulants. <b>Incompatibility:</b> Alkaline solutions, beta-lactam antibiotics."
          },

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses to be administered every 8 hrs via IV infusion over 15-30 mins; alternatively, doses up to 1 g (adults, adolescents, childn >50 kg) or 20 mg/kg (childn 3 months-11 yrs and up to 50 kg) can be given IV bolus over 5 mins. <b>Pneumonia including community-acquired and nosocomial pneumonia; complicated UTI, intra-abdominal infection, and skin and soft tissue infections:</b> Adults and adolescents, childn >50 kg: 500 mg or 1 g; Childn 3 months-11 yrs and up to 50 kg: 10 or 20 mg/kg. <b>Intra- and post-partum infections -</b> Adults and adolescents: 500 mg or 1 g. <b>Bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis, acute bacterial meningitis -</b> Adults and adolescents, childn >50 kg: 2 g; Childn 3 months-11 yrs and up to 50 kg: 40 mg/kg. <b>Management of febrile neutropenia -</b> Adults and adolescents, childn >50 kg: 1 g. Childn 3 months-11 yrs and up to 50 kg: 20 mg/kg. <b>Adults and adolescents with renal impairment -</b> CrCl 26-50 mL/min: 1 dose every 12 hrs; 10-25 mL/min: &frac12; dose every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min: &frac12; dose every 24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g. penicillins, cephalosporins, other carbapenems)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with liver disease; on a controlled-sodium diet. Concomitant use with drugs that inhibit peristalsis, valproic acid/sodium valproate, probenecid. Antibiotic-associated colitis, pseudomembranous colitis; hepatotoxicity (hepatic dysfunction with cholestasis and cytolysis) may develop. Monitor hepatic function closely during therapy. Childn < 3 months or with renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thrombocythemia; headache; diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain; increased transaminase, blood alkaline phosphatase, blood lactate dehydrogenase; rash, pruritus; inflammation, pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, valproic acid, oral anticoagulants. False positive direct or indirect Coombs test."
          },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/h2opHw1Zn5WUOVeFGnpBr85H0Vxoua6DguVdb1KkPGQGhTJrgg.png",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/UFntmuvN1YQEdcXECxeLxKEZNWLaPfvUk15QdW9PsGHHUDvrkE.png"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Methylprednisolone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary or secondary adrenocortical insufficiency; in conjunction with mineralocorticoids; congenital adrenal hyperplasia; non-suppurative thyroiditis; hypercalcemia associated with cancer. Adjunct therapy for short-term administration in management of acute episode or exacerbation of rheumatic disorders: Psoriatic arthritis; acute gouty arthritis; rheumatoid arthritis (RA), including juvenile RA; post-traumatic osteoarthritis (OA); synovitis OA; ankylosing spondylitis; acute and subacute bursitis; acute non-specific tenosynovitis; epicondylitis. Maintenance therapy of collagen disease: Systemic lupus erythematosus; systemic dermatomyositis; acute rheumatic carditis; polymyalgia rheumatica; giant cell arteritis. Dermatological diseases: Pemphigus; bullous dermatitis herpetiformis; severe erythema multiforme (SJS); exfoliative dermatitis; mycosis fungoides; severe psoriasis; severe seborrheic dermatitis. To control severe or incapacitating allergic conditions intractable to adequate trials of conventional treatment: Seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis; serum sickness; bronchial asthma; drug hypersensitivity reactions; contact dermatitis; atopic dermatitis. Severe acute and chronic allergic and inflammatory processes involving the eye: Allergic corneal marginal ulcers; herpes zoster ophthalmicus; anterior segment inflammation; diffuse posterior uveitis and choroiditis; sympathetic ophthalmia; allergic conjunctivitis; keratitis; chorioretinitis; optic neuritis; iritis and iridocyclitis. Respiratory disease: Symptomatic sarcoidosis; berylliosis; Loeffler’s syndrome; fulminating or disseminated pulmonary tuberculosis; aspiration pneumonitis. Hematologic disorder: Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura in adults; secondary thrombocytopenia in adults; acquired hemolytic anemia; erythroblastopenia; congenital hypoplastic anemia. Palliative management of: Leukemias and lymphomas in adults; acute leukemia of childhood. To manage patients over a critical period of gastrointestinal diseases: Ulcerative colitis; regional enteritis. Nervous system: Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis; management of edema associated with brain tumor. Edematous states (induce a diuresis or remission of proteinuria in the nephrotic syndrome, without uremia). Others: Organ transplantation. Tuberculosis meningitis with subarachnoid block; trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Cerebral edema:</b> 200-1,000 mg/day. <b>Organ transplantation:</b> up to 7 mg/kg/day. <b>Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis:</b> 500 mg/day for 5 days. Maintenance dose should be determined by decreasing dose in small decrements. Discontinue treatment gradually after long-term therapy. Alternate day therapy: Twice the usual daily dose is administered every other morning to provide patient requiring long-term dose treatment while minimizing certain undesirable effects including pituitary-adrenal suppression, Cushingoid state, corticoid withdrawal symptoms, and growth suppression in childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients who have systemic fungal infections. Administration of live attenuated vaccine in patients receiving immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May increase susceptibility and mask signs of infection, and new infections may appear during use. May decrease resistance and inability to localize infection when used. Monitor patients with latent TB or tuberculin reactivity, during prolonged corticosteroid therapy, these patients should receive chemoprophylaxis. Kaposi's sarcoma. Septic shock. Allergic reactions. Prolonged periods may result in HPA suppression. Acute adrenal and drug-induced secondary adrenocortical insufficiencies. Steroid \"withdrawal syndrome\". Patients with Cushing's disease, hypothyroidism, pre-existing diabetes, psychic derangements, seizure disorders, myasthenia gravis, ocular herpes simplex (possible corneal perforation), existing CV risk factors, patients who have or may be predisposed to thromboembolic disorders, HTN, GI ulcer and acute pancreatitis, liver disease, osteoporosis, renal insufficiency. Elevation of BP, salt and water retention, and increased excretion of potassium. Should not be used to treat traumatic brain injury. Pheochromocytoma crisis. Intracranial pressure and pancreatitis in childn and infants in high doses. Should not drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

                  "title": "X",

            "content": "Injection site infection or pain, or reactions, increased appetite, irritability, insomnia, nausea, dizziness, skin hyperpigmentation, hyperhidrosis, muscular weakness, GI disorders."

CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin). Neuromuscular blockers, anticholinesterases, antidiabetics, aminoglutethimide, aspirin, potassium-depleting agents."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefuroxime sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "LRTI; ears, nose and throat infections; bone and joint infections; gonorrhea, meningitis, otitis media, peritonitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, skin infections, UTI and prophylaxis for surgical infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 750 mg IM/IV every 8 hrs. <b>More severe cases</b>: 1.5 g 3-4 times daily IV. <b>Infant and childn</b>: 30-60 mg/kg BW in equally divided doses every 8 or 12 hrs. <b>Neonates</b>: 30-100 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses every 8 or 12 hrs. <b>Gonorrhea</b>: 750 mg divided in 2 inj sites. <b>Pre-op infection prophylaxis - Abdominal region, pelvis and orthopedic surgery</b>: 1.5 g IV and then two 750 mg IM 8 and 16 hrs after. <b>Heart, lung, esophagus and blood vessel op</b>: 1.5 g IV. <b>Meningitis – Adults</b>: 3 g three times daily by IV inj. <b>Infant and childn</b>: 200-240 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses every 6-8 hrs by IV inj, may be reduced to 100 mg/kg/day if clinical symptoms are improved or 3 days after beginning of therapy. <b>Neonates</b>: 100 mg/kg/day, reduced to 50 mg/kg/day upon improvement."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "History of shock and hypersensitivity. Severe renal disorders, bronchial asthma, eruption, urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Anaphylactic reaction to penicillins. Renal impairment. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions. Renal disorders. Decrease hemoglobin concentration. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea or anorexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Furosemide, aminoglycosides."
          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jMDhcGxLQdbL82oT1JkTyIuOOqCQQbXpSBTxXv4xhqlIxTMTT1.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tenecteplase",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Thrombolytic/Fibrinolytic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute ischemic stroke within 4.5 hrs of symptom onset and after exclusion of intracranial hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>&ge;90 kg:</b> 25 mg (5,000 U); <b>&ge;80 to < 90 kg:</b> 22.5 mg (4,500 U); <b>&ge;70 to < 80 kg:</b> 20 mg (4,000 U); <b>&ge;60 to < 70 kg:</b> 17.5 mg (3,500 U); <b>< 60 kg:</b> 15 mg (3,000 U). Given as single IV bolus over approx 5-10 secs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Significant bleeding disorder (present or within past 6 months). With effective anticoagulation (e.g., INR >1.3). History or suspected intracranial hemorrhage. Symptoms suggestive of subarachnoid hemorrhage, even with normal CT-scan. Severe stroke (e.g., NIHSS >25). Acute ischemic stroke without disabling neurological deficit, or symptoms rapidly improving before start of inj. History of CNS damage (e.g., neoplasm, aneurysm, intracranial or spinal surgery). Hemorrhagic diathesis. Severe uncontrolled arterial HTN. Major surgery, biopsy of parenchymal organ, or significant trauma within past 2 months. Recent head or cranium trauma. Prolonged CPR (>2 mins) within past 2 weeks. Acute pericarditis and/or subacute bacterial endocarditis. Acute pancreatitis. Severe hepatic dysfunction (e.g., HF, cirrhosis, portal HTN, and active hepatitis). Active peptic ulceration. Arterial aneurysm and arterial/venous malformation. Neoplasm with increased bleeding risk. Symptoms of ischemic attack beginning >4.5 hrs before inj or unknown onset time. Seizure at onset of stroke. Administration of heparin within previous 48 hrs and thromboplastin time exceeding the ULN for laboratory. History of prior stroke and concomitant diabetes. Prior stroke within last 3 months. Platelet count < 100,000/mm<sup>3</sup>. >185 mmHg SBP or >110 mmHg DBP, or aggressive management (IV pharmacotherapy) to reduce BP. Blood glucose < 50 mg/dL or >400 mg/dL (< 2.8 mM or >22.2 mM)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid administration of IV heparin or platelet aggregation inhibitors (e.g., aspirin) in the first 24 hrs after treatment. Bleeding. Cerebral edema. Hypersensitivity (e.g., angioedema). Discontinue concomitant heparin immediately if serious bleeding occurs. Consider protamine if heparin was given within 4 hrs before bleeding. Recent IM inj or small recent traumas, puncture of major vessels or cardiac massage for resuscitation. Conditions with increased hemorrhage risk. Patients receiving anticoagulants. Monitor BP for 24 hrs after treatment. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >80 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Vascular, GI (e.g., hematemesis, melena, gastric, gastric ulcer, rectal, and mouth hemorrhage), urogenital (e.g., hematuria, urinary tract hemorrhage), inj/puncture site, and Intracranial (e.g., cerebral hemorrhage or hematoma, hemorrhagic stroke, hemorrhagic transformation stroke, intracranial hematoma, subarachnoid hemorrhage) hemorrhage, somnolence, aphasia, hemiparesis, convulsion, epistaxis, ecchymosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs affecting coagulation/platelet function, ACE inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for solution for IV injection 25 mg (5,000 U) (P67,179.24)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NKYxMiYddyvrnc7AUcS0f2gR8Oo7u4m2uwXcTmp1O3MHIKovbd.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Methylprednisolone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of endocrine, dermatological, ophthalmic, GI, respiratory, hematologic, nervous system diseases; tuberculosis (TB) meningitis with subarachnoid or impending block when used concurrently with appropriate anti-TB chemotherapy; trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement. Adjunct therapy for short-term administration in rheumatic disorders. Treatment of exacerbation or as maintenance in selected cases of collagen diseases. Control of severe or incapacitating allergic conditions intractable to adequate trials of conventional treatment. Palliative management of neoplastic diseases. Induction of diuresis or remission of proteinuria in nephrotic syndrome without uremia of the idiopathic type, or due to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Organ transplantations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 4-48 mg daily in 4 divided doses, may be increased to &ge;100 mg in acute severe diseases. <b>Rheumatoid arthritis -</b> Moderate and childn: 4-8 mg/day; Moderately severe: 8-12 mg/day; Severe: 12-16 mg/day; <b>Systemic dermatomyositis:</b> 48 mg; <b>SLE:</b> 20-100 mg/day; <b>Acute rheumatic fever:</b> 48 mg/day until ESR normal for 1 week; <b>Allergic and ophthalmic diseases:</b> 12-40 mg; <b>Bronchial asthma:</b> Up to 64 mg single dose or up to max 100 mg on alternate days; <b>Hematological disorders, leukemias, malignant lymphoma:</b> 16-100 mg/day; <b>Ulcerative colitis:</b> 16-60 mg/day; <b>Crohn's disease:</b> Up to 48 mg/day in acute episodes; <b>Organ transplantation:</b> Up to 3.6 mg/kg/day; <b>Pulmonary sarcoid:</b> 32-42 mg on alternate days; <b>Giant cell arteritis/polymyalgia rheumatic:</b> 64 mg/day; <b>Pemphigus vulgaris:</b> 80-360 mg/day; <b>Multiple sclerosis:</b> 200 mg/day; <b>Cerebral edema:</b> 200-1,000 mg/day; <b>Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis:</b> 200 mg/day for 1 week, followed by 80 mg every other day for 1 month. <b>Childn:</b> Initially 0.117-1.66 mg/kg/day (3.3-50 mg/m2/day) in 3 or 4 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic infections including fungal infections. Concomitant use with live or live attenuated vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Not indicated for traumatic brain injury. Patients with recent MI, HTN, predisposition to thrombophlebitis, renal insufficiency; history of DM; active or latent PUD, diverticulitis, abscess or other pyogenic infections, fresh intestinal anastomoses, nonspecific ulcerative colitis; liver failure, cirrhosis; myasthenia gravis; postmenopausal stage, debilitated patients; Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy, history of steroid myopathy; active ocular herpes simplex; seizure disorders; existing or history of severe affective disorders. Suppression of inflammatory response and immune function, increased susceptibility to and/or mask symptoms of infections (e.g. viral infections, special pathogens, TB); allergic (e.g. angioedema) and anaphylactoid reactions (e.g. bronchospasm); HPA suppression; sodium retention resulting in edema, potassium loss, hypokalemic alkalosis, and HTN; acute myopathy; posterior subcapsular and nuclear cataract (particularly in childn), exophthalmos, increased IOP; mental disturbances, aggravation of emotional instability or psychotic tendencies. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI, musculoskeletal, skin and subcutaneous tissue, endocrine-metabolic, psychiatric, nervous system, ophthalmic, CV, immune system, reproductive system and breast, ear and labyrinth effects. Fluid and electrolyte disturbances. Elevated serum liver enzyme levels, hypokalemia, increased calcium excretion/urine calcium; hiccups, leukocytosis, malaise, withdrawal symptoms, moon face."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. barbiturates, phenytoin, primidone, rifampicin, rifabutin, aminoglutethimide, carbamazepine), inhibitors (e.g. antifungals, antiemetics, immunosuppressants, macrolides, HIV protease inhibitors, diltiazem, grapefruit juice), and substrates (e.g. mibefradil, cimetidine, contraceptives, CCBs). Sympathomimetics, antivirals, antacids, oral contraceptives and estrogen, aspirin and other NSAIDs, warfarin, diuretics, mifepristone, amphotericin B, anticholinergics, insulin and oral antidiabetics, digitalis glycosides, toxoids, live or inactivated vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 4 mg (P10.75), 16 mg (P36.75)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Reduction in the risk or delay of the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus- in adult, overweight patients adjunct to diet, exercise, and lifestyle changes. May be used as monotherapy or in combination with other oral antidiabetic agents, or with insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 500 mg once daily with evening meal, may be increased in 500 mg increments every 10-15 days. Max 2,000 mg once daily. May be given as 1,000 mg twice daily with food if glycemic control is not achieved on 2,000 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma, severe renal failure (GFR < 30 mL/min).           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Lactic acidosis. Patients with heart failure are more at risk of hypoxia and renal insufficiency. Administration of iodinated contrast agents.             "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Taste disturbances, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite."
          },

            "content": "NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptors, diuretics. Verapamil, rifampicin, cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, isavuconazole, crizotinib, olaparib. Alcohol. Iodinated contrast agents."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Epilepsy, porphyria, severe hepatic impairment. Alcohol intake during and 3 days after the treatment. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For vaginal use only, not to be swallowed or applied by other routes. Patients with alteration of hematopoietic function, CNS and peripheral nervous system disorders. Avoid sexual contact during treatment. Simultaneous treatment of sexual partner is recommended (i.e. administration of systemic medicinal products e.g. oral metronidazole) if used as prophylaxis for reinfection or in case of trichomonal vaginitis. Change in transaminases and glycemic values during treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Itching, burning, pain and irritation of vaginal mucosa. Dark brown urine, abdominal pain and spasm, metallic taste, xerostomia, constipation, diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, ataxia, vertigo, psycho-emotional disorders, peripheral neuropathy (long-term use), cramps. Leukopenia, allergic reactions (urticaria, prurigo of teguments, eruptions)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenytoin, carbamazepine, ciclosporin, astemizole, terfenadine. <b>Metronidazole</b>: Alcohol, disulfiram, fluorouracil, lithium, oral anticoagulants, cimetidine. <b>Miconazole</b>: Acenocoumarol, anisindione, dicumarol, phenindione, phenprocoumon, warfarin, cisapride, fosphenytoin, fentanyl, glimepiride, oxybutynin, oxycodone, pimozide, tolterodine, trimetrexate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Vaginal suppository 500 mg/100 mg (P98.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of moderate to severe Alzheimer’s disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Treatment initiation</b> - Week 1: 5 mg/day for 7 days; Week 2: 10 mg/day for 7 days; Week 3: 15 mg/day for 7 days; Week 4: 20 mg/day for 7 days. Max 20 mg/day. <b>Elderly &gt;65 yrs</b>: 20 mg/day. <b>Renal impairment</b> - Moderate (CrCl 30-49 mL/min): 10 mg/day, can be increased up to 20 mg/day after at least 7 days if tolerated well; Severe (CrCl 5-29 mL/min): 10 mg/day. All doses are taken once daily, at the same time every day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with, or predisposing factors for, epilepsy; history of convulsions; recent MI, uncompensated CHF (NYHA III-IV), uncontrolled HTN.             "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache, constipation, somnolence, HTN; balance disorders, dyspnea, elevated liver function test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Levodopa, dopaminergic agonists, anticholinergics, barbiturates, neuroleptics, antispasmodics, dantrolene, baclofen, amantadine, ketamine, dextromethorphan, phenytoin, cimetidine, ranitidine, procainamide, quinidine, quinine, nicotine, HCTZ, warfarin and other oral anticoagulants."
          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/bK0eUHfEYbmcakaotgRh3tlysRobgA8pIbv08S3QYFvHMcgJal.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Biguanides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. May be used concomitantly with sulfonylureas or insulin to improve glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy and combination with other oral antidiabetic agents</b>: Initially 500 mg once daily, may be increased by increments of 500 mg every 10-15 days based on blood glucose measurements. Max 2,000 mg once daily given with evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on 2,000 mg once daily, consider 1,000 mg twice daily or switch to standard tab to max dose of 3,000 mg daily. <b>Combination with insulin</b>: Initially 500 mg once daily, while insulin is adjusted based on blood glucose measurements."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Diabetic ketoacidosis, diabetic pre-coma. Renal failure or renal dysfunction (CrCl &lt;60 mL/min). Acute conditions with potential to alter renal function e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock. Acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia e.g. cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, shock. Hepatic insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of lactic acidosis. Determine CrCl or serum creatinine levels before treatment and regularly thereafter. Discontinue prior to or at the time of iodinated contrast media administration, or 48 hrs before elective surgery with general spinal or peridural anesthesia and not reinstituted until 48 hrs afterwards and only after re-evaluation to normal renal function. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery when used in combination with other antidiabetic agents. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disorders e.g. nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain and loss of appetite. Taste disturbance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, iodinated contrast agents, glucocorticoids, sympathomimetics, loop diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 500 mg (P10.90)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>In combination with cisplatin:</b> 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA IV infusion over 10 mins on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of each 21-day cycle + cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA infused over 2 hrs approx 30 mins after completion of the pemetrexed infusion on the 1<sup>st</sup> 2 days of each 21-day cycle. <b>As single agent in patients treated for NSCLC after prior chemotherapy:</b> 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA IV infusion over 10 mins on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of each 21-day cycle. <b>Pre-medication regimen (corticosteroids):</b> Dexamethasone 4 mg orally twice daily, should be given the day prior to, on the day of, and the day after pemetrexed administration to reduce the incidence and severity of skin reactions. <b>Vitamin supplementation to reduce toxicity:</b> Oral folic acid or multivitamins containing folic acid (350-1,000 mcg) on a daily basis at least 5 doses of folic acid must be taken during the 7 days preceding the 1<sup>st</sup> dose of pemetrexed, continue during the full course of therapy and for 21 days after the last dose of pemetrexed + IM injection of vitamin B<sub>12</sub> (1,000 mcg) in the week preceding the 1<sup>st</sup> dose of pemetrexed and once every 3 cycles thereafter, subsequent vitamin B<sub>12</sub> injection may be given on the same day as pemetrexed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant yellow fever vaccine. Childn. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Myelosuppression. Use of NSAIDs in patients with CrCl 45-79 mL/min 2 days before and after pemetrexed administration. MI, CV and cerebrovascular events. Patients treated with radiation. Renal and hepatic impairment. Sexually active male. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bone marrow suppression, anemia, neutropenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and GI toxicities, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, pharyngitis, mucositis, and stomatitis. Renal toxicities, increased transaminases, alopecia, fatigue, dehydration, rash, infection/sepsis, neuropathy. SJS and TEN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection (IV) 100 mg, 500 mg."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "<b>Per 100 mL MG TNA-Peri (3-chamber bag) - Glucose 11%:</b> glucose monohydrate 7.44 g. <b>Amino acids 11.3% with electrolytes:</b> L-alanine 0.33 g, L-arginine 0.24, L-aspartic acid 0.071, L-glutamic acid 0.12 g, glycine 0.16 g, L-histidine 0.14 g, L-isoleucine 0.12 g, L-leucine 0.16 g, L-lysine HCl 0.24 g, L-methionine 0.12 g, L-phenylalanine 0.16 g.         "brand_info": [

            "content": "Rx"
          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Supply water, electrolytes, amino acids, and calories to patients if enteral nutrition is impossible, insufficient, or contraindicated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Mix contents of each chamber before use. Administer by drip infusion. <b>Adults and childn >10 yrs - Patients with normal nutritional state or under mild catabolic stress:</b> 0.7-1 g/kg (0.10-0.15 g of nitrogen/kg) daily of amino acids. <b>Moderate to high catabolic stress:</b> 1-2 g/kg (0.15-0.30 g of nitrogen/kg) daily of amino acids. <b>General dose:</b> 0.7-1 g/kg of daily total amino acids are administered into peripheral or central veins which corresponds to 27-40 mL/kg of MG TNA-Peri.           },

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute pulmonary edema, hyperhydration, decompensated heart failure, hypotonic dehydration. Hemophagocytic syndrome, unstable conditions e.g. post-traumatic conditions, decompensated diabetes, acute MI, metabolic acidosis, severe hyperosmolar coma. Hypokalemia. Childn < 2 yrs."

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults, prevention of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity and mortality in patients &ge;55 yrs at high risk of CV disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily, swallowed whole with or without food. Max antihypertensive effect is attained 4-8  weeks after treatment starts. <b>Essential HTN:</b> 40 mg, may increase to max 80 mg If target BP is not achieved. Alternatively, may be used in combination with thiazide-type diuretics or CCBs. <b>Severe HTN:</b>  Max 160 mg alone and with 12.5-25 mg HCTZ. <b>Prevention of CV morbidity and mortality:</b> 80 mg. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Max 40 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Biliary obstructive disorders. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with vol and/or sodium depletion; hepatic insufficiency; renal impairment, kidney transplant;  bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney; whose vascular tone and renal function depend largely on RAAS; suffering from aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Hyperkalemia, renovascular HTN, hypotension, changes in renal function, hyperazotemia, oliguria; risk of fatal MI and unexpected CV death in concomitant use with ARBs or ACE inhibitors in DM patients with additional CV risk; MI or stroke in excessive BP reduction in patients with ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic CV disease. Not recommended in patients with primary aldosteronism; dual blockade of RAAS. Black hypertensive people. Monitor BP, serum creatinine, and potassium. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Planning pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infections and infestations; disorders of blood and lymphatic system, immune system, metabolism and nutrition, psychiatric, nervous system, eye, ear and labyrinth, cardiac, vascular, respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous, musculoskeletal, renal, urinary."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other antihypertensives, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium, NSAIDs, ramipril and ramiprilat, heparin, digoxin, lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 40 mg (P24.30), 80 mg (P42.08)."

          {

            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in patients whose BP is not adequately controlled on telmisartan or hydrochlorothiazide alone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily. <b>BP not adequately controlled by telmisartan 40 mg or HCTZ:</b> 40 mg/12.5 mg; <b>telmisartan 80 mg or telmisartan + HCTZ 40 mg/12.5 mg:</b> 80 mg/12.5 mg; <b>telmisartan + HCTZ 80 mg/12.5 mg or previously stabilized on telmisartan and HCTZ given separately:</b> 80 mg/25 mg. <b>Severe HTN:</b> Telmisartan up to 160 mg alone and in combination with HCTZ 12.5-25 mg daily. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Max 40 mg/12.5 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cholestasis and biliary obstructive disorders. Severe hepatic impairment, coma  hepaticum, hepatic precoma. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or serum creatinine >1.8 mg/100 mL), anuria, acute glomerulonephritis. Refractory hypokalemia, hypercalcemia. Therapy refractory hyponatremia. Hypovolemia. Symptomatic hyperuricemia/gout. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Rare hereditary galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment or progressive liver disease; vol and/or sodium depletion; bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney; renal impairment, kidney transplant; whose vascular tone and renal function depend largely on RAAS; suffering from aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; renal insufficiency, heart failure; DM and coexistent CAD; with liver cirrhosis, experiencing brisk diuresis, receiving inadequate oral intake of electrolytes and concomitant therapy with corticosteroids or adrenocorticotropic hormone;  history of sulfonamide or penicillin allergy. Hyponatremia with neurological symptoms; renovascular HTN; hyperazotemia, oliguria, acute renal failure; risk of fatal MI and unexpected CV death in concomitant use with ARBs or ACE inhibitors; MI or stroke in excessive BP reduction in patients with ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic CV disease; increase cholesterol, triglyceride; hyperuricemia; gout; fluid or electrolyte imbalance; hypercalcemia, hypomagnesemia; choroidal effusion, acute myopia, secondary angle-closure glaucoma; non-melanoma skin cancer. Not recommended in patients with primary aldosteronism; dual blockade of RAAS; hereditary fructose intolerance. Discontinue before parathyroid function tests; if photosensitivity occurs and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Monitor serum creatinine, potassium, serum electrolytes. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, syncope, paresthesia, sleep disorders, headache; visual impairment, vision blurred, angle closure glaucoma, choroidal effusion; vertigo; diarrhea, dry mouth, flatulence, abdominal pain and discomfort, constipation, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, gastritis, pancreatitis; infections and infestations;  neoplasms benign, malignant and unspecified (incl cysts and polyps); blood and lymphatic system, immune system, metabolism, nutrition, psychiatric, cardiac, respiratory, thoracic, mediastinal, hepatobiliary, skin, subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal, connective, renal, urinary, reproductive, breast, general disorders and administration site conditions."

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 drop in the affected eye 3x for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For external use only. Not for injection. Do not inject subconjunctivally nor introduce directly into the anterior chamber of the eye. Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms (e.g. fungi). Discontinue treatment at the first sign of a rash or allergic reaction or if superinfection occurs. Do not wear contact lenses in signs and symptoms of bacterial conjunctivitis. Infants < 1 yr. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

            "content": "Conjunctivitis, decreased visual acuity, dry eye, keratitis, ocular discomfort, hyperemia, pain and pruritus, subconjunctival hemorrhage, tearing. Fever, increased cough, infection, otitis media, pharyngitis, rash, and rhinitis."
          },

            "content": "Treatment of ocular infections caused by susceptible microorganisms. Prevention of post-op ocular inflammation and bacterial infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of post-op ocular inflammation and infection:</b> 1 drop 4x daily in the eye to be operated, given 1 day pre-op until 15 days post-op; <b>Cataract surgery:</b> Instill immediately post-op; <b>Refractive surgery by LASIK:</b> Instill within 15 mins post-op. <b>Treatment of ocular infections caused by susceptible organisms:</b> 1 drop 4x daily for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Herpes simplex keratitis, vaccinia, varicella, other corneal or conjunctival viral infections; mycobacterial and fungal ocular infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for injection. Do not inject subconjunctivally nor introduce directly into the anterior chamber of the eye. Prolonged use may cause ocular HTN or glaucoma with optic nerve damage, reduced visual acuity, visual field defects, and posterior subcapsular cataract formation; increased hazard of secondary ocular infections; thinning or cornea or sclera, perforations; reduction of resistance to and development of non-susceptible bacterial, fungal, or viral infections; tendon inflammation and rupture; delayed corneal wound healing; overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (e.g. fungi). Discontinue treatment at first sign of tendon inflammation and superinfection. May mask clinical signs of infection. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn.         },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Desogestrel, ethinylestradiol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Oral contraception."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab daily, starting with the large tab for 21 consecutive days followed by small (placebo) tab for 7 days. Each subsequent pack is started immediately following the last placebo tab. Take tabs in the order directed on the package every day at about the same time."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Venous or arterial thrombotic or thromboembolic events, TIA, angina pectoris, arterial thrombosis (MI, CVA), activated protein c resistance, antithrombin-III deficiency, protein C deficiency, protein S deficiency, hyperhomocysteinemia and antiphospholipid antibodies. History of migraine with focal neurological symptoms, DM with vascular involvement, pancreatitis, severe hepatic disease, liver tumors, sex steroid-influenced malignancies, and undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Known or suspected pregnancy and lactation. Hepatitis C virus combination drug regimen ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir with or without dasabuvir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "MI, DVT, pulmonary embolism, risk factors for cervical cancer, hypertriglyceridemia. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Depressed or altered mood, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, breast pain, breast tenderness, increased weight, venous and arterial thromboembolic disorders, HTN, hormone-dependent tumors, chloasma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP450 enzyme inducers, ciclosporin, lamotrigine. HIV protease inhibitors (e.g. nelfinavir), non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (e.g. nevirapine), hepatitis c virus combination drug regimen (e.g. boceprevir, telaprevir, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir with and without dasabuvir), strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin), moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. fluconazole, diltiazem, erythromycin)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 150 mcg/30 mcg x 28’s (P119.20)."
          }

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4403,
        "brand_name": "Maxcort",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/61geiRGLkYZDZhhdaTjH3qBVjE1trASPXPOfYBW223dmznKCWN.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KdLteEeoLElnWeO4sUM3BgjDLqKEGpVfkU5Y0qRxh6ZdVsp5Ys.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QCUXgaAwDC9AER5Z7SUa2euDhr75ClBnlGQ6ZzwO9n1i8iS3WJ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clobetasol propionate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Topical Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Short-term treatment of more resistant inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of steroid-responsive dermatoses unresponsive to less potent corticosteroids e.g. psoriasis (excluding widespread plaque psoriasis), recalcitrant dermatoses, lichen planus, discoid lupus erythematosus, other skin conditions unresponsive to less potent steroids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply enough amount to cover the entire affected area 1-2 times daily until improvement occurs, then reduce frequency of application or change treatment to less potent preparation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Untreated cutaneous infections (e.g. rosacea, acne vulgaris, pruritus without inflammation, perianal and genital pruritus, perioral dermatitis). Dermatoses (dermatitis and nappy eruptions) in childn &lt;1 yr."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Topical steroids withdrawal. Long-term use beyond recommended dose. Consider less potent corticosteroids if to be used for &gt;4 weeks. Patients with history of local hypersensitivity to other corticosteroids. Hypercortisolism (Cushing’s syndrome) and HPA axis suppression, leading to glucocorticosteroid insufficiency. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Use on occluded skin areas (e.g. intertriginous areas or under occlusive dressings), thin skin areas (e.g. face), broken skin or other conditions where skin barrier is impaired. Use in psoriasis. Concomitant infections. If used on face, treatment should be limited to 5 days. Contains propylene glycol and cetostearyl alcohol. Infants. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pruritus, local skin burning or skin pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir and itraconazole)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Cream 500 mcg/g (0.05%) x 5 g, 15 g."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Leuprorelin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Endometriosis, uterine leiomyomata, palliative treatment for prostate cancer, central precocious puberty (CPP)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Endometriosis</b>: 3.75 mg via IM/SC injection, alone or in combination with norethindrone, every month for 6 months only. Initial dose should be given on the 1<sup>st</sup> 5 days of menstrual cycle. <b>Uterine leiomyomata</b>: Up to 3 months. For endometrial preparation prior to intrauterine surgery, give 3.75 mg via IM/SC injection, 5-6 weeks before surgery. <b>Prostate cancer</b>: 3.75 mg via IM (depot) every month. <b>Central precocious puberty</b>: Individualize dosage for each child. Starting dose of 0.3 mg/kg every 4 weeks (minimum 7.5 mg) as single IM or SC injection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "CV diseases, urinary obstructions, metastatic vertebral lesions. Hyperglycemia and diabetes. Causes suppression of pituitary-gonadal system and decrease in bone density.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hot flushes, nausea, malaise, fatigue and transient local irritation at the injection site. Convulsions, hepatic dysfunction, jaundice, spinal fracture, paralysis, and hypotension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for solution for injection (IM/SC) 3.75 mg."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

  {
    "id": 16,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 16,
        "brand_name": "Luprolex",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Leuprorelin acetate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For endometriosis and uterine fibroids (myoma). Treatment of central precocious puberty in girls < 9 yrs, boys < 10 yrs. <b>3.75 mg and 11.25 mg:</b> Premenopausal breast cancer, prostate cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Single IM/SC inj. 1.88 mg or 3.75 mg once a month, or 11.25 mg once every 3 months. <b>Uterine fibroids/endometriosis - Patients >50 kg BW or with markedly large uterus:</b> 3.75 mg; <b>< 50 kg:</b> 1.88 mg. Treatment duration:  Max 6 months, may extend to 12 months (endometriosis) if given with 5 mg norethindrone acetate. <b>Childn - &ge;20 kg BW:</b> Initially 3.75 mg; <b>< 20 kg:</b> 1 or 2 mL of 1.88 mg SC once a month. May be increased if inadequately suppressed. Administration interval is 30± 2 days (1.88 mg and 3.75 mg) or 90± 2 days (11.25 mg) to prevent recurrence of precocious puberty."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Undiagnosed abnormal uterine/vaginal bleeding. Postmenopausal women. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for prevention of relapse after curative operation. Patients with a history of seizures, epilepsy and CV disorders, CNS anomalies or tumors, progressive brain tumors; congenital long QT syndrome, CHF, frequent electrolyte abnormalities, or taking QT-prolonging drugs; prostate cancer. Concomitant use with drug-induced convulsions. Retreatment is not advisable in patients with major risk factors for loss of bone mineral content. Temporary increase of sex steroids; development or worsening of depression, memory disorders; emotional lability in childn; convulsions; hypoestrogenism; stop of menstruations; decrease of bone mass; severe bleeding in women with submucous fibroids; urethral obstruction, spinal cord compression; hyperglycemia, development of DM; prolonged QT interval; vaginal bleeding, spotting, discharge; slipped femoral epiphysis after discontinuation. Discontinue if pseudotumor cerebri/idiopathic intracranial HTN occurs. Monitor bone age during therapy with 6-12 months intervals; hormonal parameters at 2-week intervals if sterile abscess occurs; blood glucose and glycosylated Hgb; ECG and electrolytes. Use non-hormonal contraceptives. Infants.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin, subcutaneous, appendages, musculoskeletal system, autonomic, central, and peripheral nervous system, vision, psychiatric, reproductive, general, GI, liver, administration site, flare phenomenon, endocrine, cardiovascular, immune system disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "QT-prolonging drugs or drug-induced Torsade de pointes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/SC) sustained-release 1.88 mg, 3.75 mg. Lyophilized powder for injection (IM/SC) sustained-release 11.25 mg."
          }
        ],

      "data": {
        "id": 4945,
        "brand_name": "Lurasitor",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/8oW91y9AsKGJ8LHj2CAU8vlXS6JnZ7NHB4OawotpoKYjA2GxNp.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/iUoqxPLG3mWxWoExA5epd5ybiaTDDqpa5T2FPRiKIdXqiG5PGX.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Lurasidone HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia in adults and adolescents 13-17 yrs. Monotherapy of major depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults and childn 10-17 yrs. Adjunct treatment with lithium or valproate in adults with major depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia - Adults:</b> 40 mg once daily. Max 160 mg daily; <b>Adolescents 13-17 yrs:</b> 40 mg once daily. Max 80 mg daily. <b>Depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder - Adults:</b> 20 mg once daily as monotherapy or adjunct therapy with lithium or valproate. Max 120 mg daily; <b>Childn 10-17 yrs:</b> 20 mg once daily as monotherapy, may be increased after 1 week. Max 80 mg daily. <b>Concomitant use with CYP3A4 inducers:</b> Increase dose after chronic treatment (&ge;7 days) with CYP3A4 inducer. <b>Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors, moderate (CrCl 30-< 50 mL/min) and severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min):</b> Initially 20 mg daily. Max 80 mg daily. <b>Moderate (Child-Pugh B) and severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C):</b> Initially 20 mg daily; Child-Pugh B: Max 80 mg daily; Child-Pugh C: Max 40 mg daily. Taken with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Angioedema. Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, voriconazole, mibefradil), inducers (e.g., rifampin, avasimibe, St. John’s wort, phenytoin, carbamazepine), grapefruit or grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for treatment of dementia-related psychosis; childn with depression. Increased mortality and cerebrovascular adverse reactions (e.g., stroke) in elderly with dementia-related psychosis. Patients with DM; history of seizures or conditions that lower the seizure threshold; risk for aspiration pneumonia; Parkinson’s disease or Lewy body dementia. Worsening and emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors; metabolic changes (hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, weight gain) that may increase CV risk; hyperprolactinemia; orthostatic hypotension, syncope; body temperature dysregulation; manic or hypomanic episode; esophageal dysmotility, aspiration. Perform fasting blood glucose testing at the beginning and periodically during therapy in patients with risk factors for DM. Discontinue if NMS, tardive dyskinesia, severe neutropenia, and first sign of WBC decline occur. Monitor CBC during the first few months in patients with pre-existing low WBC or history of drug-induced leukopenia/neutropenia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, akathisia, EPS, nausea, omitting, anxiety, tachycardia, blurred vision, abdominal pain, diarrhea, increased CPK, decreased appetite, HTN, rash, pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 40 mg (P90.00), 80 mg (P130.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct treatment to diet and exercise in the glycemic control of adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 2.5 mg once daily before or after breakfast, can be increased to 5 mg once daily when effect is insufficient."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Type 1 DM. Patients with severe renal impairment or ESRD undergoing dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal or severe hepatic impairment; at risk for vol depletion; UTI or genital infection. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Cystitis; hypoglycemia; constipation; pollakiuria; increased blood ketone body, increased beta-2 microglobule in urine, WBC urine positive, albumin in urine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other antidiabetic drugs (e.g. sulfonylureas, biguanides, thiazolidinediones, DPP-4 inhibitors, alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, glinide, insulin preparations, GLP-1 agonists, insulin); diuretics (e.g. loop or thiazide diuretics). False positive urine glucose test; decreased serum 1,5-AG."
          },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduce LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides, and increase HDL-C in the management of hyperlipidemias, including primary hypercholesterolemia (type IIa), mixed dyslipidemia (type IIb), hypertriglyceridemia (type IV), and homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduce the progression of atherosclerosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Hypercholesterolemia:</b> 5 or 10 mg once daily, may be adjusted to the next dose after 4 weeks. Max 40 mg is only considered in severe hypercholesterolemia at high CV risk, particularly familial hypercholesterolemia, who do not achieve treatment goal on 20 mg and require routine follow up. <b>Prevention of CV events:</b> 20 mg daily. <b>Elderly >70 yrs:</b> Initially 5 mg. <b>Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia - Childn and adolescents:</b> Initially 5 mg daily; <b>10-17 yrs:</b> 5-20 mg once daily; <b>6-9 yrs:</b> 5-10 mg once daily. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevated liver function tests. Childn < 6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform liver function tests prior and at 12 weeks after initiation of treatment then periodically thereafter. Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis with or without acute renal failure secondary to myoglobinuria. Childn < 6 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "DM, headache, dizziness, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, myalgia, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aluminum-magnesium hydroxide antacids, bile acid sequestrants, ciclosporin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

          }
