            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Contraception, menorrhagia and secondary amenorrhea, mild to moderate endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Contraception and menorrhagia:</b> Given as single dose 150 mg/mL within the 1<sup>st</sup> 7 days of cycle or within 1<sup>st</sup> 4 weeks after giving birth (delay 6 weeks after giving birth if breastfeeding). Can also be administered any day as long as the patient is not pregnant and use a back-up method (e.g. condoms) for the next 7 days to avoid pregnancy. <b>Secondary amenorrhea:</b> 5-10 mg daily IM for 5 to 10 days until 2 days before expected onset of menstruation. <b>Mild to moderate endometriosis:</b> 50 mg weekly or 100 mg every 2 weeks IM for at least 6 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding and history or current high risk of arterial disease, hormone-dependent neoplasms, hepatic impairment, porphyria, after recent evacuation of hydatidiform mole. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "CV or renal impairment, DM, asthma, epilepsy, migraine, or other conditions which may be aggravated by fluid retention, history of depression, susceptible to thromboembolism, past ectopic pregnancy, HTN, ability to cause significant decrease in bone mineral density that may lead to osteoporotic fractures. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, changes in appetite, weight and libido, fluid retention, edema, acne, chloasma (melasma), allergic skin rashes, urticaria, mental depression, breast changes (e.g. discomfort or occasionally gynecomastia), hair loss, hirsutism, fatigue, drowsiness or insomnia, fever, headache, premenstrual syndrome-like symptoms, altered menstrual cycles or irregular menstrual bleeding, anaphylaxis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension for injection (IM) 150 mg/mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Adjunct to diet for treatment of primary hypercholesterolemia as substitute in adults adequately controlled with rosuvastatin and ezetimibe given concurrently but as separate products."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab with or without food. Not suitable for initial therapy. Take &ge;2 hrs before or &ge;4 hrs after administration of bile acid sequestrant."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity.           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Use in elderly &gt;70 yrs, patients with renal impairment (CrCl < 60 mL/min), Asian, or have predisposing factors to myopathy should use monocomponent preparations. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic insufficiency, history of liver disease or consumption of alcohol, acute and serious conditions suggestive of myopathy or predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Monitor patients at risk for DM. Concomitant use with protease inhibitors, fibrates, and anticoagulants, fusidic acid. Childn < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {

            "content": "Increased hepatic transaminases, GI problems, muscle pain."
          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Progesterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in non-hysterectomized post menopausal women who are receiving conjugated estrogen tabs and secondary amenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia:</b> 200 mg as single dose orally for 12 days sequentially per 28 day cycle. <b>Secondary amenorrhea:</b> 400 mg as single dose for 10 days. <b>Premenstrual syndrome, benign mastopathies, menstrual irregularities, premenopause:</b> 200-300 mg daily. 10 days per cycle usually from 14<sup>th</sup> day until onset of menstruation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe liver disease, hepatic cell tumors, rotor syndrome and Dubin-Johnson syndrome. Thrombophlebitis, thromboembolic disorders, cerebral hemorrhage, or history of these conditions. Breast carcinoma. Suspected or confirmed breast or genital organ neoplasia. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "HTN, cardiac disease, renal disease, epilepsy, migraine, asthma. Patients with history of depression, diabetes, mild to moderate hepatic dysfunction, migraine, photosensitivity. Not for treatment of premature labor. Intended to be co-prescribed with an estrogen product as HRT. DVT or pulmonary embolism. VTE. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Should only be used in pregnancy during the first trimester and only by vaginal route.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Breakthrough bleeding, change in menstrual flow, amenorrhea, changes in cervical erosion and secretions, breast changes, edema, weight gain, catabolism, cholestatic jaundice, allergic reaction and rashes, acne, chloasma, mental depression, pyrexia, insomnia, somnolence, nausea, alopecia, hirsutism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Bromocriptine, ciclosporin, rifampicin, ketoconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 200 mg."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of cardiovascular risk due to concomitant hypertension and dyslipidemia. Angina."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Amlodipine:</b> Initially 5 mg/day. Max 10 mg/day. In small adults, fragile, elderly, hepatic insufficiency and childn >6 yrs: 2.5 mg/day. Angina, coronary artery disease: 5-10 mg/day. Childn 6-17 yrs: 2.5-5 mg/day. <b>Atorvastatin:</b> 10- 80 mg/day. Hyperlipidemia and mixed dyslipidemia: 10-20 mg/day. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 10-80 mg/day. Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia in childn 10-17 yrs: Initially 10 mg. Usual dose range 10-20 mg/day. Adjustments at intervals of 4 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Active liver disease. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Risk factors predisposing to development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Liver dysfunction. Worsening angina and acute MI in patients with severe obstructive CAD. Symptomatic hypotension particularly in with severe aortic stenosis. Increase in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Concomitant use with ciclosporin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, HIV protease inhibitors, colchicine. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rhabdomyolysis, myopathy, and liver enzyme abnormalities."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers; sildenafil; immunosuppressants, fibric acid derivatives, niacin, clarithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors and itraconazole; hepatitis C protease inhibitor, grapefruit juice, gemfibrozil, digoxin, oral contraceptives, and colchicine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg/5 mg."
          }

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Thrombolytic/Fibrinolytic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of thromboembolic disorders, e.g. acute myocardial infarction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Two 10 U IV bolus injections, each administered over 2 mins. 2nd bolus is given 30 mins after the initial bolus injection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active bleeding, history of CVA, recent intracranial or intraspinal surgery or trauma, intracranial neoplasm, arteriovenous malformation, aneurysm, known bleeding diathesis, severe uncontrolled HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Internal and superficial bleeding may occur. Other venipunctures, concomitant anticoagulant therapy. Recent major surgery e.g. CABG, obstetrical delivery, organ biopsy; previous puncture of noncompressible vessels, cerebrovascular disease; recent GI or genitourinary bleeding; HTN (SBP >180 mmHg and/or DBP >110 mmHg); subacute bacterial endocarditis, hemostatic defects including those secondary to severe hepatic or renal disease; severe hepatic or renal dysfunction; diabetic hemorrhagic retinopathy or other hemorrhagic ophthalmic conditions; septic thrombophlebitis or occluded AV cannula at an infected site; patients taking oral coagulants; coronary thrombolysis. Elderly >75 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hemorrhage, intracranial bleeding (higher risk for patients with systolic BP >160 mmHg)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Heparin, vit K antagonists, drugs altering platelet function e.g. aspirin, dipyridamole, abciximab."
          },
          {

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/fVad4zNVRvyay0hv6ASVU5u6SIOAeFyIrIwJDJS4mnvqY6qxWm.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pregabalin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of neuropathic pain, including neuropathic pain associated with spinal cord injury; generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). As adjunctive therapy with partial seizures, with or without secondary generalization. Management of fibromyalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "150-600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses; may be increased based on response and tolerability. <b>Neuropathic pain</b>: Initially 150 mg/day, may be increased to 300 mg/day after an interval of 3-7 days, and if needed, to max 600 mg/day after an additional 7 days interval. <b>Fibromyalgia</b>: 300-400 mg/day in 2 divided doses. Begin at 75 mg 2 times a day; may be increased to 150 mg 2 times a day within 1 week; may be further increased to 225 mg 2 times a day if no sufficient benefit experienced with 300 mg/day to max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>Epilepsy</b>: Initially 150 mg/day; may be increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week to 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>GAD</b>: Initially 150 mg/day; may be increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week; may be further increased to 450 mg/day after an additional week to max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl &ge;60 mL/min: 150 mg/day 2 or 3 divided doses. Max 600 mg/day; &ge;30 to < 60 mL/min: 75 mg/day 2 or 3 divided doses. Max 300 mg/day; &ge;15 to < 30 mL/min: 25-50 mg/day single dose or 2 divided doses, max 150 mg; < 15 mL/min: 25 mg/day single dose. Max 75 mg/day; supplementary dose following hemodialysis: 25 mg/day single dose. Max 100 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinuation of pregabalin should be done gradually over a minimum of 1 week. Patients with DM, CHF; history of substance abuse. Risk for fall in the elderly; loss of consciousness, confusion, and mental impairment; transient visual blurring and other changes in visual acuity; CNS depression and GI impairment with concomitant use of opioids. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Women of childbearing potential or contraception. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness and somnolence. Nasopharyngitis; increased appetite; euphoric mood, confusion, irritability, depression, disorientation, insomnia, libido decreased; ataxia, coordination abnormal, tremor, dysarthria, amnesia, memory impairment, disturbance in attention, paresthesia, hypoesthesia, sedation, balance disorder, lethargy; vision blurred, diplopia; vertigo; vomiting, constipation, flatulence, abdominal distension, dry mouth; muscle cramp, arthralgia, back pain, pain in limb, cervical spasm; edema peripheral, edema, gait abnormal, fall, feeling drunk, feeling abnormal, fatigue; increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ethanol and lorazepam; oxycodone; CNS depressants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 25 mg,  50 mg, 75 mg, 150 mg."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Measles, mumps and rubella virus vaccines, live [with recombinant hemagglutinin (rHA)]",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Measles, Mumps, Rubella Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Simultaneous vaccination against measles, mumps and rubella in people >12 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC or IM 0.5 mL, preferably into the anterolateral area of the thigh in younger childn and the deltoid area in older childn, adolescents, and adults. SC in patients with thrombocytopenia or any coagulation disorder. <b>Recommended vaccination schedule - 1<sup>st</sup> dose:</b> 12-15 months old; <b>2<sup>nd</sup> dose:</b> 4-6 yrs. <b>Measles outbreak - If 1<sup>st</sup> dose:</b> 6-12 months old; <b>2<sup>nd</sup> dose:</b> 12-15 months; <b>Revaccination:</b> 4-6 yrs or of age for individuals first vaccinated at 12 months or older. <b>Post-exposure vaccination:</b> Within 72 hrs of exposure. <b>Use with other vaccines:</b> Given one month before or after administration of other live viral vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to vaccine components, including gelatin. Anaphylactic or anaphylactoid reactions to neomycin. Any febrile respiratory illness or active febrile infection; active untreated TB; Patients receiving immunosuppressive therapy (except those receiving corticosteroids as replacement therapy, e.g. Addison's disease); with malignant neoplasms affecting the bone marrow or lymphatic systems (e.g. blood dyscrasias, leukemia, lymphoma of any type). Primary and acquired immunodeficiency states, including immunosuppressed patients with HIV or AIDS, cellular immune deficiencies, hypogammaglobulinemia and dysgammaglobulinemia. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to eggs. Thrombocytopenia. Patients with history of convulsions, cerebral injury or any other condition in which stress due to fever should be avoided. Thrombocytopenia. Tuberculin test should be administered either before or simultaneously with M-M-R II. Infants < 6 months. Avoid pregnancy for 3 months following vaccination. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Burning and/or stinging at the injection site for a short duration, fever, rash, or measles-like rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Immune globulins (Ig), blood or plasma transfusions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection (SC) 0.5 mL (P945.75)."
          }

            "content": "Treatment of symptoms of seasonal allergic or perennial rhinitis in adults and childn >2 yrs. Prophylactic treatment in patients who have a history of moderate to severe symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis. Treatment of nasal polyps in adults >18 yrs; acute rhinosinusitis without severe bacterial infection in adults and childn >12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Each actuation delivers approx 50 mcg mometasone furoate. Initial priming: 10 actuation until a uniform spray is observed. Reprime with 2 actuation if not used for 14 days or longer. <b>Seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis - Adults and childn >12 yrs:</b> 2 actuations in each nostril daily. Once symptoms are controlled, dose reduction to 1 actuation in each nostril may be effective for maintenance. Dose may be increased to max daily dose of 4 actuation in each nostril if symptoms are inadequately controlled. <b>Childn 6-11 yrs:</b> 1 actuation in each nostril once daily. <b>Nasal polyposis:</b> Initially 2 actuations in each nostril once daily; dose may be increased to 2 actuations in each nostril twice daily if symptoms are inadequately controlled after 5-6 weeks. Dose should be titrated to lowest dose at which effective control symptoms is maintained. Alternatives should be considered if no improvement seen after 5-6 weeks. <b>Acute rhinosinusitis:</b> Initially 2 actuations in each nostril twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Untreated localized infection involving the nasal mucosa. Patients with recent nasal surgery or trauma until healing is completed."
          },

            "content": "First line chemotherapy of ovarian cancer for the treatment of advanced disease or a residual disease (>1 cm) after initial laparotomy, in combination with cisplatin. 2<sup>nd</sup> line in the treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of standard platinum-based therapy. Initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer either in combination with an anthracycline or in combination with trastuzumab, or in patients over expressed HER-2 at a 3+ level for whom an anthracycline is not suitable. Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>First-line treatment of ovarian cancer:</b> 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over a period of 3 hrs or 135 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over a period of 24 hrs followed by 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> of cisplatin, therapy is repeated at 3-week interval. <b>2nd-line treatment of ovarian cancer:</b> 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, with a 3 weeks interval between courses. <b>Adjuvant chemotherapy in breast carcinoma:</b> 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over a period of 3 hrs every 3 weeks for 4 courses. Following AC therapy. <b>1st-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma with combination with doxorubicin (50 mg/m<sup>2</sup>):</b> Recommended dose 220 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs, with a 3-week interval between courses, should be administered 24 hrs after doxorubicin. <b>1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma with combination with trastuzumab:</b> Recommended dose 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs, with 3-week interval between courses, infusion may be started the day following the 1<sup>st</sup> dose of trastuzumab or immediately after the subsequent dose of trastuzumab. <b>2<sup>nd</sup>- line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma:</b> 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hrs, with a 3-week interval between courses. <b>Advanced NSCLC:</b> 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered 3 hrs followed by 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup> of cisplatin, with a 3-week interval between courses. <b>Treatment of AIDS-related KS:</b> Recommended dose 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 3 hrs IV infusion every 2 weeks."

            "title": "Precautions",

            "content": "Nausea, vomiting diarrhea, URTI, UTI, myelosuppression, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, bleeding, flushing, rash, hypotension, alopecia, transient and mild nail and skin changes, arthralgia, myalgia, mucosal inflammation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers."
          },
          {

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qiv5m63Jk7kQN45RgTlENQ5Nw4H0NtK0Vpj1cGrDlFPjI3U4hl.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qiv5m63Jk7kQN45RgTlENQ5Nw4H0NtK0Vpj1cGrDlFPjI3U4hl.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/L5LPEEYt68iBXuKs6U4DkwTpYEatr2SZOVodYVFXWSFWkERAwp.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefixime trihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of susceptible infections i.e. gonorrhea, otitis media, pharyngitis, lower respiratory tract infections (RTI) e.g. bronchitis and urinary tract infection (UTI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b> Cap - Adults:</b> 200-400 mg daily as single dose or in 2 divided doses. <b>Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment:</b> Reduce dose. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 400 mg as a single dose. <b>Susp - Adults and childn >10 yrs:</b> 200-400 mg daily in 1-2 divided doses. <b>Childn:</b> 8 mg/kg/day as single dose or in 2 divided dose; <b>5-10 yrs:</b> 10 mL daily; <b>1-4 yrs:</b> 5 mL daily; <b>6 months-1 yr:</b> 3.75 mL daily. <b>Lower RTI:</b> 400 mg/day. <b>Upper RTI and uncomplicated UTI:</b> 200 mg/day. <b>Treatment course:</b> 5-7 days up to 14 days if required. <b>Patients with renal impairment - CrCl >60 mL/min:</b> standard dosing; <b>21-60 mL/min or patients on hemodialysis:</b> 75% standard dosing; <b>>20 mL/min CAPD patients:</b> 50% standard dosing. All doses are at standard dosing intervals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B. <b>Cap:</b> Patients with a history of allergy. May produce falsely high values with the Jaffe’s method of measuring creatinine. Positive results to the direct Coombs’ test. False positive reaction for glucose using copper reduction reactions. Penicillin-sensitive patients. Avoid alcohol-containing medications. Patients with renal impairment. Monitor renal and hematological status during prolonged and high dose therapy. <b>Susp:</b> Patient with previous hypersensitivity to cephalosporins, history of cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia. False positive reactions with nitroprusside test, Coombs’ test, Clinitest, Benedict’s solution, Fehling’s solution.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Cap:</b> Skin rash, urticaria, eosinophilia, fever, reactions resembling serum sickness, and anaphylaxis. GI disturbances i.e. diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants; probenecid. <b>Cap:</b> Ethacrynic acid, furosemide, gentamicin and vancomycin; alcohol; high dose heparin. <b>Susp:</b> Platelet aggregation inhibitors e.g. NSAIDs, salicylates, sulfinpyrazone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for oral suspension 100 mg/5 mL x 60 mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of hypertension (HTN) in patients who develop cough with ACE inhibitors. Reduction of risk of stroke in patients with left ventricular hypertrophy. Treatment of diabetic nephropathy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN – Adults</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily. Patients with possible depletion of intravascular vol or history of hepatic impairment: 25 mg once daily. Taken once or twice daily. Total daily dose: 25-100 mg. <b>Childn &ge;6 yrs</b>: Initially 0.7 mg/kg once daily (up to 50 mg total). <b>Patients with left ventricular hypertrophy</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily. Add HCTZ 12.5 mg daily and/or increase losartan to 100 mg once daily followed by an increase HCTZ to 25 mg once daily based on BP response. <b>Nephropathy in type 2 diabetes patients</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily, increased to 100 mg once daily based on BP response. May be administered with insulin and other hypoglycemic agents (e.g. sulfonylureas, glitazones and glucosidase inhibitors)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired liver and renal function. Symptomatic hypotension may occur in patients with intravascular vol depletion. Electrolyte imbalances in patients with renal impairment. Childn &lt;6 yrs or with GFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Elderly. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C for 1<sup>st</sup> trimester and D for 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters.",

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of mild to moderate hypertension in case of inadequate control with monotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially, 1 tab daily; increase to 2 tabs daily if necessary."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hypotension, poor cardiac reserve and heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, renal artery stenosis and vol depletion, hepatic and renal impairment. May induce hypotension, hyperkalemia. Concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics. Do not use in cardiogenic shock, patients who recently suffered MI, or in acute unstable angina. Not be used to treat an angina attack in chronic stable angina. Discontinue in patients with ischemic pain following administration. Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Elderly. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, flushing, headache, hypotension, peripheral edema, tachycardia and palpitations, nausea and other GI disturbances, increased micturition frequency, lethargy, eye pain and mental depression, paradoxical increase in ischemic chest pain, rashes (e.g. erythema multiforme), fever and abnormalities in liver function e.g. cholestasis; impaired renal function, hyperkalemia, myalgia, RTI, back pain, fatigue, neutropenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Rifampicin, fluconazole, drugs that increase serum potassium, lithium, NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/5 mg (P15.00)."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity.           },

            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, primary hyperaldosteronism, ischemic CV and cerebrovascular disease, heart failure, aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes or other drugs that may increase serum potassium. Monitor serum electrolytes regularly. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D. <b>HCTZ:</b> Patients with history of allergy or bronchial asthma.                 },

                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV/IM. <b>Adults:</b> 1 g or 2 g every 8 hrs. <b>Uncomplicated infections:</b> 1 g every 6-8 hrs; <b>Moderately severe or severe:</b> 2 g every 6-8 hrs; <b>Infections generally needing antibiotics in higher dose:</b> 2-3 g every 4-6 hrs. <b>Renal impairment and undergoing hemodialysis:</b> Initially 1-2 g. Severe infections: 200 mg/kg/day. Max 12 g/day. <b>Prophylactic dose:</b> 30-40 mg/kg 30 mins-1 hr before initial incision, 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> doses given every 8-12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",

          },

            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concurrent therapy with PDE-5 inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated for acute attacks of angina pectoris. Not recommended in angina with acute MI or CHF.             "content": "Acute bacterial cystitis, acute episodes in relapsing bacterial cystitis, acute bacterial urethrovesical syndrome, non-specific bacterial urethritis.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 1 sachet (3 g) single dose regimen. <b>More clinically problematic cases (e.g. elderly, bedridden patients, recurrent infections):</b> 2 doses administered at 24-hr interval. <b>Prophylaxis of UTI following surgery and transurethral diagnostic maneuvers:</b> 2 doses, 1<sup>st</sup> dose is administered 3 hrs before the intervention and the 2<sup>nd</sup> dose 24 hrs after surgery. <b>Acute lower UTI</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 3 g. Take on an empty stomach, 2-3 hrs apart from meals, preferably at bedtime, after emptying bladder. Dose must be dissolved in a glass of water (50-75 mL)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal failure (CrCl &lt;10 mL/min), hemodialysis. Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency."
          },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Detoxifying agent for antineoplastic treatment"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of advanced colorectal cancer in combination with fluorouracil (5-FU); megaloblastic anemias due to folate deficiency; and megaloblastic anemias of pregnancy and infancy. For reduction of methotrexate toxicity after high-dose therapy. Management of folic acid antagonists overdosage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Advanced colorectal cancer in combination with 5-FU - Bimonthly regimen</b>: 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 2 hrs, followed by IV bolus injection of 5-FU 400 mg/m<sup>2</sup> and 22-hr infusion of 5-FU 600 mg/m<sup>2</sup> for 2 consecutive days, every 2 weeks on days 1 and 2. <b>Weekly regimen</b>: 20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> by IV bolus injection or 200-500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as IV infusion over 2 hrs plus IV bolus injection of 5-FU 500 mg/m2 in the middle or end of folinic acid infusion. <b>Monthly regimen</b>: 20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as IV bolus injection or 200-500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as IV infusion over 2 hrs immediately followed by IV bolus injection of 5-FU 425 or 370 mg/m<sup>2</sup> during 5 consecutive days. <b>Folinic acid rescue after chemotherapy with &gt;500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> methotrexate:</b> Start rescue therapy within 24 hrs of methotrexate administration. Dosage schedule: 10 mg/m<sup>2</sup> parenterally followed by 10 mg/m<sup>2</sup> orally (if there is adequate GI function) every 6 hrs until serum methotrexate concentration has declined to &lt;10<sup>-8</sup> M. If at 24 hrs after methotrexate administration, serum creatinine has increased to &ge;50% or the serum creatinine is &gt;5x10<sup>-6</sup> M, or if at 48 hrs after methotrexate administration, the serum methotrexate concentration is &lt;9x10<sup>-7</sup> M: May increase to 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 hrs until serum methotrexate &gt;10<sup>-8</sup>M. <b>Antidote to methotrexate toxicity</b>: Up to 75 mg IV infusion within 12 hrs followed by 12 mg IM every 6 hrs for 4 doses. When average methotrexate doses appear to have an adverse effect: 6-12 mg IM every 6 hrs for 4 doses. <b>Antidote to trimetrexate toxicity</b>: 20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 6 hrs, should be given orally or IV (over 5-10 mins) and continued for at least 72 hrs after last trimetrexate dose. Total daily dose: 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Recommended course: 21 days trimetrexate therapy and 24 days folinic acid. Overdosage with trimetrexate &gt;90 mg/m<sup>2</sup> without concomitant folinic acid: 40 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV every 6 hrs for 3 days. <b>Antidote to pyrimethamine toxicity</b>: 3-9 mg per day IM for 3 days or until platelet and leukocyte counts reach safe levels. <b>Antidote to trimethoprim toxicity</b>: 3-10 mg per day until recovery of blood cell counts. <b>Megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency</b>: Up to 1 mg IM daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Not to be used for treatment of undiagnosed anemia, pernicious anemia, vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency or other megaloblastic anemias secondary to vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not administer intrathecally. Do not mix with 5-FU in same IV injection or infusion. Administration of folinic acid after methotrexate in patients with aciduria, ascites, dehydration, GI obstruction, pleural or peritoneal effusions. Patients with renal impairment; advanced colorectal cancer when used in combination with 5-FU. Concomitant administration of folinic acid and 5-FU in elderly or debilitated patients; anticonvulsant therapy in childn. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, severe mucosal toxicity, diarrhea, dehydration. <b>With 5-FU</b>: leukopenia, diarrhea, stomatitis, lethargy, malaise, fatigue, alopecia, dermatitis, anorexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Folic acid antagonists, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fluoropyrimidines, anticonvulsants, direct or indirect DNA synthesis inhibitors, glucarpidase. <b>Incompatibilities</b>: Droperidol, 5-FU, foscarnet, methotrexate."
          },

  {
    "id": 941,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 941,
        "brand_name": "Loxeva",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levofloxacin hemihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute maxillary sinusitis, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, community acquired-pneumonia (CAP), complicated and uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTI), acute pyelonephritis, uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections (SSSI). Tab: Nosocomial pneumonia, complicated skin and skin structure infections, chronic bacterial prostatitis, inhalational anthrax (post-exposure) in childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IV infusion</b>: 500 mg over 60 mins every 24 hrs. <b>Duration of treatment - Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis</b>: 7 days. CAP: 7-14 days. <b>Acute maxillary sinusitis</b>: 10-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated SSSI</b>: 7-10 days. <b>Renal impairment in above mentioned indications - CrCl 50-80 mL/min</b>: Reduce subsequent doses; <b>20-49 mL/min</b>: Initially 500 mg then 250 mg once daily; <b>10-19 mL/min, hemodialysis and CAPD</b>: Initially 500 mg then 250 mg once every 2 days. <b>UTI</b>: 250 mg once daily, increased in severe infections for 10 days (complicated) or 3 days (uncomplicated). <b>Acute pyelonephritis</b>: 250 mg once daily for 10 days. <b>Renal impairment in above mentioned indications - CrCl 20 mL/min</b>: Reduce subsequent doses; <b>10-19 mL/min</b>: Initially 250 mg then 250 mg every 2 days. <b>Tab - Adults</b>: 250-500 mg once or twice daily and 750 mg once daily depending on the type of infection. <b>Renal impairment - CrCl &lt;50 mL/min</b>: Reduce dose. <b>Inhalational anthrax (post-exposure) - Childn (&ge;6 months) &gt;50 kg</b>: 500 mg every 24 hrs for 60 days; <b>&lt;50 kg</b>: 8 mg/kg twice daily for 60 days. Max 250 mg/dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with epilepsy, history of tendon or CNS disorders related to fluoroquinolone administration. Childn or growing adolescents. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Disturbances of blood glucose including symptomatic hyper- or hypoglycemia in diabetic patients receiving concomitant treatment with an oral hypoglycemic agent or with insulin. Possible photosensitivity reactions during and for several days following therapy. Avoid exposure to excessive sunlight. Increases risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture in all ages but higher in elderly &gt;60 yrs, patients taking corticosteroids and patients with kidney, heart or lung transplants. <b>IV infusion</b>: Not the optimal therapy in most severe cases of pneumococcal pneumonia. Patients with known or suspected CNS disorders or renal dysfunction. Patients predisposed to seizures; with G6PD deficiency, renal impairment. Childn &lt;18 yrs. <b>Tab</b>: May induce collagen degradation causing tendinopathy that may cause or aggravate aortic aneurysm and dissection. Myasthenia gravis may interfere with diagnostic tests. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; dizziness, headache, insomnia; tremor. <b>IV infusion:</b> Constipation; arthralgia. <b>Tab:</b> Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, pseudomembranous colitis, pancreatitis and dysphagia; confusion, restlessness; drowsiness, nightmares, hallucinations, psychotic reactions, depression, convulsion, intracranial HTN, paresthesia and peripheral neuropathy; rash, pruritus, vasculitis, erythema multiforme, SJS and TEN; eosinophilia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia, hemolytic anemia or agranulocytosis; tachycardia, hypotension, edema, syncope, hot flushes and sweating; photosensitivity or phototoxicity, burning, erythema, exudation, vesicles, blistering and edema; crystalluria, transient increase in serum creatinine or BUN, elevated liver enzyme values, jaundice, hepatitis, and acute renal failure secondary to interstitial nephritis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, NSAIDs. <b>IV infusion</b>: Antineoplastic agents; cimetidine. Incompatible with heparin or alkaline solutions. <b>Tab</b>: Fluoroquinolones, oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin), glibenclamide, methotrexate, probenecid, metal ions (e.g. aluminum, calcium, magnesium or iron), H2-antagonist, phenytoin, antiarrhythmic drugs (e.g. quinidine, procainamide, amiodarone, and sotalol), antihistamine, astemizole, terfenadine, cisapride, erythromycin, pentamidine, phenothiazines or TCAs, antacids, sucralfate, metal cations and zinc-containing multivitamin preparations, drugs that alter blood-glucose concentrations. False positive screening results for opiates using immunoassay kits."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 5 mg/mL x 100 mL (P1,088.08). Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P56.84), 750 mg (P84.69)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 214,

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used for the dissolution of cholesterol-rich gallstones in patients with functioning gallbladders. Management of cholestatic liver disease, such as primary biliary cirrhosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "6-12 mg/kg daily as single bedtime dose or in 2-3 divided doses. Obese patients: 15 mg/kg daily. <b>Primary biliary cirrhosis:</b> 13-15 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses with food. <b>Prevention of gallstones:</b> 300 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patient with complete biliary obstruction of extrahepatic origin, with widespread intrahepatic obstruction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patient with variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, or in need of an urgent liver transplant. Monitor serum liver function tests and bilirubin level every month for 3 months after start of therapy, and every 6 months thereafter. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Estrogenic hormones, cholesterol-lowering drugs (e.g. clofibrate), antacids, charcoal, cholestyramine, colestipol, smectite, ciclosporin, ciprofloxacin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 300 mg. Film-coated tablet 500 mg."
          }
